label: 103 Venning Street
request: 103 Venning Street - —Conceptual Comment for Accessory Structure

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Losse Knight, architect representing the applicant, stated that they are proposing to remove the existing shed structure and replace with garage structure. He stated that the lot is an irregular shape and are trying to propose a new footprint for the carport relative to some of the setback requirement for grand trees and turning radiuses for getting in and out of the property. They wanted to demonstrate that although they are asking for this structure to be within 3 feet of the setback, it is fairly consistent when you view the accessory structures that are already in the general area. He showed the existing structure they are proposing to take down. They would like to propose a simple open air, structure with columns in the front with a small storage area in the back, which will also function as an entryway into the home. He stated that the area along the side property line is where they are asking for a 3 foot setback and the typical accessory setback is 6 feet. The building is turned so as you move away from the corner they are 5 feet off the setback on both sides and along the rear, they are 4.7 feet. Mr. Keenan asked what the building’s current setbacks are. Mr. Knight said that it is 6 feet on both sides. They are attempting to have a dual carport and entry. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Dickson asked if they took the storage element away, would they have their 6 feet. Mr. Knight stated that likely on that area, but one of the purposes of this is to pick up some storage. He stated that there are allowances in the guidelines to have a 12 x 12 structure in other areas on the site; however, when you look at turning radius and setbacks for tree protection, there was no other place to put the structure. The roofline is set at 18 feet and trying to keep with the architectural character of the existing roof. Ms. Dickson asked if there was room under the eaves for storage. Mr. Knight stated that there is, but very little. The original intent was to think about a full height space, but realized that they were exceeding 18 foot threshold. Their goal is to review height, scale and mass, but also would like to receive feedback on the footprint of the structure. Ms. Dickson asked if Mr. Knight has talked to the neighbors about backing right up to their property line. Mr. Knight stated that they have not. Mr. Keenan stated that they are basically asking for a 3 foot encroachment variance from this commission. Ms. Dickson asked if they needed it on both sides. Mr. Knight stated that on the rear side, they are encroaching roughly 18 inches, so it is 4’7” off the rear setback. One side will be 3 feet and the rear side would be 18 inches. Mr. Keenan stated that everything on those lots are very tight and this lot is very complicated. Mr. Bennett stated that what Mr. Knight has drawn is consistent with what was discussed over the last several weeks in terms of design and the more modest height of accessory structures. He applauds what Mr. Knight has done; however, has reservations that given the way the lot is situation and the fact that the applicant already has some encroachment to the rear anyway, is a 3 foot variance meaningful. Ms. Rowe asked how large the storage area is. Mr. Knight said 6’10 in one direction and 14 feet in the other. Mr. Knight stated that the initial study was a 2 car garage and realize that this would not work. They tried to study other buildings around and decided to go to an open carport and have a little bit of storage in the back. They could potentially consider pulling it forward to move it away from the rear accessory setback. However, it would detract from the hierarchy of the main house and make the carport front and center. Ms. Rowe asked if they thought about doing something similar to the house on Bennett Street with the storage on the side and the open front and back. This would accomplish storage. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Knight stated that they did like that one; however, it was setup for a width of approximately 22 to 24 feet in order to make this work. This lot is a really irregular site. Mr. Keenan stated this his thoughts are consistent with Mr. Bennett’s and appreciates the 18 foot height and likes the open air aspect and understands this is a function of storage and being able to cover their vehicle. Is 3 feet that big of an issue? He does not believe so. Ms. Dickson stated that she would like to know what the neighbors think, because it may be an issue for them. Claudia Coker, homeowner, stated that the storage is important because they have bicycles, paddles for kayaks, skateboards, basketballs, and are not storing tools. She stated it is a very unique lot and this is all the way back in the corner where her neighbor to the right, his building is actually blocking his house from this structure. The neighbor behind, it is in the very corner of his lot where his kids play back there, but they have a full yard and also have an accessory building up against her property that is within the setback. She said she is asking for some leeway, because the neighbors’ buildings are within the setback and because of the uniqueness of her lot, there is no other way to do this. She does not think the neighbors would have an issue. Ms. Dickson stated that granting a variance is easier when they know that the neighbors are okay with it, because you are asking for relief from the rules as they stand. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the reservation he has is the nature of the lot and the continuum of houses in that area are shoehorned in. To add an additional structure that is in excess of the setbacks it pushes the envelope further, especially without property feedback from the neighbors. He stated that it feels that too much is being put into a space that has already surpassed its utility. Mr. Knight stated that he understands that they have not addressed the neighbors, but thought that this was a platform for it to be publically addressed where it is put on the internet, with the yellow sign out in front of the home. He stated that in the future, do they need to be knocking on the doors of neighbors. Mr. Keenan stated that this is that platform and the Commission will not make decisions based on what the neighbors are thinking, but based on the guidelines. However, supportive letters always help. Mr. Bennett stated that the Commission cannot require letters of support from an applicant; however, they are helpful. Mr. Knight asked if their preference which they thought would be the best option is to sit the structure back and ensure they are not overwhelming the house. Given that this is an open air type of colonnade and it does have a porch like feel, if they were to move it so they are at least not in the rear setback, they could completely get out of that. At that point, the front corner is out of it and they just have approximately 30% of the back corner. Old Village Historic District Commission

They have a hip roof that was intentionally designed to pitch away from the neighbor’s property instead of something that projects out. Would something like this be acceptable to be able to maintain a similar footprint? Mr. Bennett stated that this is a sample he would be more comfortable with, because then you are asking for inches instead of feet. The debate the Commission is having is adding another setback variance in this restrained tight space, which is already happening with some of the neighbors, or because the other variances have already been granted either explicitly or by default with the way things were built years ago, does the Commission just accept this for this particular tract and grant another 3 feet for another accessory structure. This is the dilemma that the Commission faces. For the applicant to make that concession towards the rear, he could be more comfortable with the setback variance on the other dimension. Ms. Rowe agreed. Mr. Bennett stated that the other issue is the setback ordinances are there for a reason and some of that is to provide separation and not impose on neighbors. The other is more practical as a matter of maintenance. Are you able to get back between those spaces to property paint and repair them and provide reasonable drainage. He stated that the Commission has been faced with this on a number of occasions.

label: Confederate Cemetery
request: Confederate Cemetery- — After-the-Fact Approval for Free Standing Sign for Mary-Julia Royall Park

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Miles Beach, stated that Mary-Julia Royall was President of the Confederate Memorial Association for 20 years or more. This association dwindled to 2 individuals, Mary-Julia Royall and one other. He stated that she asked the Moultrie Camp Son of Confederate Veterans if they would take title to Carr Street Cemetery. He stated that Carr Street Cemetery includes a lot more than just that piece that is enclosed with wrought iron, which now needs some repair. He stated that 5 or 6 years ago, they were happy to take title to the cemetery and their attorney drew up the property documents and they have been registered and filed with the courts. Moultrie Camp 27 of the Sons of Confederate Veterans does own this property. Mr. Bennett stated that his understanding is it goes all the way through back to Royall. Mr. Beach stated that the block that Carr Street Cemetery is in probably has a fairly large number of graves there that they know nothing about. They had a state archeologist come from the State to do a scan of the entire property, which would indicate where unmarked graves are located. From the back of the fenced in portion, coming towards Carr Street, on the right hand side, from the oak tree forward, there are 11 unmarked graves. Their intent is not to do anything with this area. He does live in the OVHD; Old Village Historic District Commission

however, Mary-Julia Royall, to maintain the cemetery over the years, they felt that she needed some recognition for all that she has done for that cemetery. Before they put the sign up, the new house next to the property, has a driveway the ends before you get to the back of the house, and they have a stack of everything there, which is very visible. They removed all the barbed wire, vines, trash trees, etc., and opened it up and have come back in and planted camellias, azaleas, encore azaleas and several other to help hide some of the items that are at the new house. He showed an area that had become a trash area and they wanted to do away with the trash area. Another issue they had was with a resident who had a heating and cooling system that is down on the ground and uses the temperature of the ground to heat and cool the system. His overflow drain pipe goes out onto the cemetery property, which causes some issues. He stated that the sign in question is approximately 6 feet x 3 feet and is done is Charleston green and is set in concrete and they would like to recognize Mary-Julia Royall and this would be a very honorable way of doing so. Their request, although after the fact, is to allow them to leave the sign in place. Mr. Bennett stated that he applauds what the SVC BB – applaud what SCV is doing and to assume responsibility for this parcel. He stated that Mary-Julia Royall is a Town treasurer and to acknowledge her for her years of commitment is wonderful. His reservation about the sign itself is that it emphasizes a park and not clear what the park is and does not represent that it is a confederate cemetery. Mr. Beach stated that there is a sign on the fence that states Confederate Cemetery and has also put 2 signs from the Boy Scouts who are working on their Eagle Project. What they should recognize is the War of 1812 monument which is there. He stated that there are only 2 War of 1812 monuments in the in the State of South Carolina, and they have one, which is inside the fence. He believes the cemetery sign sets it aside. The entire property has underground irrigation from street to street and their intent is to make it a landscaped park with different trees and flowers. Mr. Keenan thought the sign placement was odd. Mr. Beach stated that they put it there to keep people from dumping their trash there. Out of respect for those graves, they wanted to stop the dumping of trash and it has worked. Ms. Rowe asked if the sign was level. Mr. Beach stated that it was and that the property has a slight slope to it that makes it look like it is not level. Ms. Rowe stated that it is a lovely monument to a lovely person. Ms. Dickson asked Mr. Beach if he has had discussions with the Preservation Society about putting up a property sign that tells the public what is there, such as the 1812 monument and the confederate cemetery. Mr. Beach stated that the 1812 monument is there already on the street side. He stated that they raise all the funds to maintain this cemetery, so Old Village Historic District Commission

funding is sometimes an issue. He stated that they do want one of the signs indicating that it is a Confederate Cemetery. Mr. Keenan made a motion to approve the ex post facto application for the Confederate Cemetery as submitted; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

label: 102 Middle Street
request: 102 Middle Street (HISTORIC 6018)- —Final Approval for Addition

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phil Clark, Clark Design Group, and stated that they were here previously. This is a historic structure, built in 1887 – 1891 in Charleston and brought by barge. He stated that they have the storefront glass on 2nd floor porch that was never really a porch and would like to bring it back to be more in line with the original historical character with the eyebrow around and windows above. He stated that the existing site plan has a lot of paving and they would like to clean some of it up and take it away in order to keep the lot coverage down. Everything they are doing is staying inside the setbacks. They are going to take up the unnecessary walkways and do a pervious paver from the front walk from the gate to the front porch. He stated that Mr. Hirshorn made some comments previously about the size of side porch and they went back and studied it. They have tightened up the fireplace and pulled in the porch slightly and is not quite as heavy. Mr. Bennett stated that what he is struggling with is the sighting of the fireplace and the historic context for this kind of addition which is essentially a porch, but it is the location of the fireplace. He asked if it would be possible to locate the fireplace adjacent to the main structure’s wall, which he feels would be more consistent with history. Mr. Clark stated that with the floorplan layout, the fireplace works out on the porch, because they wanted the porch to connect to the inside. They would hate to lose the window. Having the fireplace outside on the porch makes it part of the house. He stated that one of the main concerns Mr. Hirshorn had with the porch was the location next to the neighbor. He showed the distance from the edge of the proposed new side porch to the property line. Ms. Balzac stated that to put the fireplace up against the house with take away from the original historic structure. She stated that where the fireplace is proposed has the least amount of impact. Mr. Keenan stated that he has a slightly different opinion, because of the impact of losing an original window and what it would do to the siding and roofline of the house to move the fireplace. He stated that he likes what is shown, as well as the hardscape plan and appreciates scaling it back. He stated that the chimney, especially the width is a much better proportion. Mr. Juan asked what the distance is of the chimney to the side corner. Mr. Clark stated that is more than 10 feet, which is the code. Ms. Rowe stated that it looks great. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan made a motion to approve the application at 102 Middle Street as submitted; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

label: 124 Mary Street
request: 124 Mary Street – (HISTORIC 6253) – Final Approval for Hardscape Alteration of Existing patio/driveway

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. JR Cramer, 5256 East Alton St, North Charleston, landscape architect for the applicant. He stated that there are two lots with the main house, guest house and pool on one lot, and a garage and driveway on the other lot. He stated that the main reason they were hired is to re-do the swimming pool and hardscape and correct some drainage issues. He stated that they were not proposing to go over any existing impervious coverage, but to add in more permeable coverage as needed. He stated that there are a great deal of trees on site so they would like to use care with the tree roots. The swimming pool will be built within the existing pool and they will add in to the existing hardscape on top, which will be travertine. The existing spa area will remain with the existing bluestone and all of the other hardscape surfaces will be the travertine. They will be incorporating permeable hardscape in where possible and also increase drainage features. He indicated on the plans a high area where the water comes down and goes underneath the house. He stated that the actual house has a basement, which is unusual. He stated that what they are trying to create is a terraced vegetable garden and the existing driveway, which is gravel, they will add in a French drain on the edge of the driveway so it collects down, and another feature, the dry creek bed is going to be another French drain element. There is another rain garden that is going to step back into the entertaining area. He stated that what they are asking for is approval for the improvements of the hardscape, but with that, they are trying to add in more permeable coverage. He stated that when they surveyed the property, they had given up property on the right hand side, so they are proposing to shift their fence onto the property line. They were proposing a 6 foot privacy fence; however, the existing picket fence was previously approved by the Commission and they would like for it to go back in. He stated that it would aesthetically tie in better with the house. Ms. Rowe asked if the concrete is already in front of the garage and if they are leaving that as it is. Mr. Cramer responded in the affirmative to both questions. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Rowe stated that this is a lot of concrete. Mr. Cramer stated that the existing driveway is gravel and they are proposing to enhance that. Ms. Dickson asked Mr. Cramer to explain a French drain. Mr. Cramer stated that it is an underground trench filled with gravel or rock, or a perforated pipe that redirects water away. He stated that all the water coming off the existing concrete is going to be going into a tiered rain guards system. Mr. Juan asked if Mr. Cramer has had discussions with Kevin Mitchell, Engineer with the Town, regarding the drainage designs. Mr. Cramer stated that it should not be necessary, as they cannot tie into anything, so everything they are doing is much improved. Ms. Dickson stated that it looks very nice. Where does the water go after it has been through the rain garden? Mr. Cramer stated that it infiltrates into the ground. Ms. Dickson asked if it will impact the neighbors. Mr. Cramer stated that what they are doing will be beneficial to all the neighbors. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the house is in a divot and most of the water comes straight in. He stated that he is concerned about the home behind the second lot, which is the garage. Mr. Cramer stated that the water goes from the existing concrete to the first tier rain guard, then to the 2nd tier rain guard on the lower level which ties into underneath the patio area. Mr. Keenan thanked the homeowners for their attention to the drainage, although the OVHDC does not have purview over drainage. He stated that he likes the design and what the architects have developed. Ms. Rowe made a motion to accept the plans for 124 Mary Street, as submitted; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

label: 205 Queen Street
request: 205 Queen Street—(HISTORIC 6099) —Final Approval for Outdoor Fireplace

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Bob Fleming, Classic Remodeling, representing the homeowners, stated that there are wrap around porches and are proposing to install an exterior fireplace on the porch. He stated that they would be matching all the existing brick that is there as outlined in the guidelines. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he does not have an issue with the plan. Ms. Dickson stated that it appears large and out of scale. Mr. Fleming stated in order to get the minimum sizes on the firebox and follow the code, this is how big it must be built in order to achieve a 42” firebox. He stated that they are not doing a false fireplace, but doing Old Village Historic District Commission

actual masonry. He stated that they tried to taper to get the upper component smaller. Ms. Rowe stated that her concern was seeing it when you come down Queen Street. Mr. Fleming stated that you would have to go to the end of Queen Street in order to see it. Ms. Wilson stated that it is too deep and an unusual relationship and could slip so that it aligns with the heated portion of the house, as opposed to it being partially outside so that you would see it less from Queen Street. Mr. Fleming stated that they did have it in further, but the client’s stated that the side porch is narrower than the front porch and wanted to get as much room as possible and asked that it be moved out. Ms. Wilson stated that it is awkward, because it is a very classic and historic house and it should have a more traditional relationship to the porch. She asked if they looked at doing more of a Rumsford box, because they are not pushing it on to the porch the depth is 40” off of the porch. Mr. Fleming stated that he was concerned with an outdoor fireplace of having more depth in the box so that they do not have an issue with the wind. Ms. Wilson asked about pushing it 12” or more onto the porch so that it is not protruding. Mr. Fleming stated that this was discussed with the clients, but they did not favor this suggestion, because they felt that it was protruding in the porch, from the inside usage area. Ms. Wilson stated that it appears attached in an awkward way and would like to see it pushed back and onto the porch. She suggested moving the stairs to provide more seating towards the back corner of the porch. Ms. Rowe stated that she agrees. Ms. Wilson stated that it needs to be less deep or pushed into the porch by 12”, because it looks attached from the outside, and it needs to be more of a traditional relationship where it is engaged in the porch. She stated that she also believes that it should be pushed past the front façade of the house and does not think it is appropriate on a historic house for it to slip past the front elevation. Mr. Keenan stated that he agrees and must be careful because this is a historic home and there is nothing in the guidelines that discusses brick fireplaces on an exterior porch. Mr. Fleming stated that part of the discussion was they were trying to even it out between the two areas. Mr. Juan asked about the depth of the porch, and if it was 10 feet from the 2nd floor exterior wall. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Fleming stated that they have adequate clearance. He stated that this was not the reason for pushing the box out, because even if they push the box in, they still have the clearance. Ms. Rowe stated that it needs to be moved back so it is not visible from Queen Street. She stated that this is a mar on a historic home. Mr. Keenan asked Mr. Fleming if it is possible to accomplish this. Mr. Fleming stated that he would discuss with his clients. Ms. Dickson stated that it needs to be pushed in towards the house and said that 42” may be too big. Mr. Fleming stated that 36”, 42” and 48” are the three most common sizes, but the depth will not change and is based on the guidelines. He stated that the desire of the client was to build a masonry fireplace that would have been appropriate for the age of the home. Ms. Balzac asked how deep historic porches are. Mr. Fleming stated on this house, it is 8 feet on the side and 9 feet on the front. Mr. Keenan stated that he would have to agree with Ms. Wilson and Ms. Rowe. His concern is the size and placement. He suggested shifting it so that it is out of view from Queen Street and would like to see less depth on the chimney. Mr. Hirshorn asked if it would be possible to shift it onto the porch more, keep the depth and size and bring it in. Mr. Fleming stated that he would look at the isocurve, because he knows what his client’s response will be, which will be not to push into the porch, because it is a narrow depth in that area. He suggested going back to see how much they can bring it down with an isocurve which may be enough to satisfy everyone’s concerns. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to defer the application at 205 Queen Street for the exterior fireplace until the next meeting; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Bob Fleming, Classic Remodeling, representing homeowners, Rob and Margaret Donaldson who are also present this evening. He stated that they took the comments from the February, 2016 meeting and were asked to slide the fireplace further back. After discussions with the clients, they were concerned that if it were moved further back, that the space would be unusable. He stated that the Donaldson’s were adamant that where it was originally proposed is where they would prefer to have it. He stated that the second suggestion was to make the fireplace narrower. He said that there were discussion with two different masons and given the fact that it is outdoors with a breeze, they recommended not narrowing it. He stated that two fireplaces were recommended and would only reduce the size by two inches. Mr. Keenan stated that this is basically the same application as previously submitted. Mr. Fleming responded in the affirmative. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the porch in question is an original historic porch. Mr. Fleming responded in the affirmative. Henry Harden, 220 Queen Street, stated that he came to Mount Pleasant in 1954 and has lived in the same area two houses down Old Village Historic District Commission

from the Donaldson’s home and has known three generations of Donaldson’s and feel that he is a part of the neighborhood. He stated that everything that Margaret and Robbie (Donaldson), have done has been perfect from the interior to the landscaping outside. He stated that they have put a lot of thought into keeping the house attractive with this fireplace. He stated that he has seen the plans for the fireplace and stated that he believes that this would be a nice addition in his opinion. Rob Donaldson, property owner, stated that his great grandfather built this house in 1903 and has been in the family ever since. He stated that he cherishes every piece of old glass and heart pine that it is built of. He stated that he would not do anything to disrupt the historical integrity of the house. He stated that it is not a large house by today’s standards. He stated that the porch is the best room of the house and they are simply looking to add a month on the early side and a month on the late side of the year, where they can continue to enjoy the house and their family as it continues to grow, in different seasons. He stated that they do have an email from the adjoining property owner, Amy Harley, which has been forwarded to Mr. Pohlman. He stated that he trusts his builder and has one of the best interior designers in Charleston and trusts her decision making. Mr. Pohlman stated that for clarification, Mr. Donaldson is referring to the email from Amy Harley, which has been distributed to Commission members. label: 966 Pitt Street
request: 966 Pitt Street – Survey 5976 – Applicant is seeking Final Review on porch roof and window placement alterations from a previously approved new construction

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. John Linton, homeowner, stated that he and his wife are the homeowners. This house was his wife’s great aunt and uncle’s originally and is on a slab. He stated that they had two to four inches of water during Hurricane Matthew and had to rip out all the walls. He stated that it is in the VE flood zone so they are not able to repair it, because the value of it is diminimous. He stated that they are in a situation where they have to demolish and rebuilt, which is one of the basis for the demolition request. He provided photographs of their house in 2015 during the 1,000 year rain, and stated that the home is no longer appropriate for the area, which is an old concrete block house with no historical significance and Old Village Historic District Commission

not compatible with the surrounding homes. He provided plans for a two story home that is board and batten siding, and the size is modest compared to other homes in the area. He stated that they positioned the proposed home more towards the front of the street, similar to the other homes in the area and believe this will provide the view in accordance with the new guidelines for positioning of houses. He stated that this will actually be very similar. He stated that the driveway would be a pervious material. Mr. Hirshorn stated that for the demolition he would be inclined to grant it based on the criteria 1, 2 and 3. He stated that he is still contemplating the design of the new structure. Ms. Dickson stated that she is agreeable to grant demolition as well. Ms. Rowe is also agreeable with demolition. Mr. Keenan stated that he does not have an issue with the demolition based on the three criteria. He stated that he is not following the architectural design, but does like the size of the home. He does not have issue with the board and batten. Ms. Wilson stated that there is a disconnect with the massing pieces. There is a really strong tall gable form and because the other pieces are low, it is reading almost as a tower. She stated that it could be worked to be a little more harmonious. She stated that there is a small entry porch and in the Old Village entry porches are a real front presence and really important. She stated that we really have to fight for those porches and they sometime get undervalued, but especially on Pitt Street, it will be appreciated. She would like for the homeowner to look at the front porch size and its relationship to the building. She stated that it is coming in on the side and sees the access to where the vehicles are going to be, but this house needs to relate to the street a little more. The side gable, the pitches, and the massing is again a disconnect with the strong, very vertical gable facing Pitt Street. The second floor pergola seems unusual for the area. She stated that catching the distant water view and understands that, but struggling with it formally as opposed to having more of a roof or something with a pitch. Visually, from the street, it amounts to a flat roof porch, which is awkward and maybe it is shifted back a little more off the street if it is really important to the homeowner. In general, there is a lot of different massing pieces that are not working together and the house needs more of a front from Pitt Street. Ms. Rowe stated that it comes across looking more like a beach house. She stated that the second floor long rectangular window and the pergola does not seem harmonious. Ms. Dickson stated that she loves porches and is all for it, especially if you have a water view; however, this porch looks stuck on. She does not know how to modify it. She thanked the homeowner for not building another mansion and she loves the idea of a beach house; however, something is not organic about it. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that as a conceptual discussion, he does not mind the asymmetry, but believes it may be too asymmetrical with the very vertical and narrow gable and then the very wide low gable is possibly too much. One thing to consider on the porch, he has seen on similar type structures, where you can have a simple double piazza running along one side and capture some of the views that way, as opposed to the two story box type porch shown, which is awkward. Mr. Linton asked if he is suggesting to have it run the length of the house. Mr. Hirshorn responded in the affirmative. He stated that a very classic double piazza could work better if capturing the views from the second floor is the intent. That could be one idea. He stated that he does not mind the asymmetry if some of the angles were softened. Ms. Wilson stated that she definitely was not going for symmetry and agrees that she does like the asymmetry and quirkiness of it, but needs some balance where those two relate to each other better. Mr. Linton stated that their goal was to design the most efficient house possible and part of that is being a young growing family with budget constraints. He felt that each comment made added several thousand to the budget. Ms. Wilson disagreed and stated that it was really a massing discussion. She stated that Mr. Hirshorn was not increasing the size of the porch, but adjusting the proportions of it so that it felt more anchored to the house and less than something extended from the house. It was not an add, just a scale. She stated that the Commission is here to comment on scale and massing. She stated that it does not have to run the full length nor does it have to be traditional, but needs to engage the form a little better. Mr. Hirshorn stated that there are a number of examples of those two story piazzas on simpler structures both downtown Charleston and in the Old Village and is more tied into the house. He does not believe any additional money will be spent, just a different design. Mr. Linton asked if the Commission is suggesting putting a roof on it as well or is the pergola acceptable. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the pergola would be more of an extension of a porch under one of the gables as a traditional piazza would be. You would lose the openness. Mr. Linton asked about extending the gable roof. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would. Ms. Wilson asked if he means having more of a shed roof; a porch roof that ties in. She stated that she does not want to rule out the pergola, if that is a goal for the homeowner. It is about the form engaging with the house, whether it is slats or a roof is more personal than the massing that is seen from the street. She stated that waterproofing the porch is going to be difficult if the pergola is the homeowner’s decision. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan stated that he would be more in opposition with the pergola. Since he has served on the Commission, very few pergolas have been approved. He stated that he is not in favor of the pergolas. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the comment on waterproofing is significant. He stated that having a fixed roof would help tremendously, as without them they rot quickly. Ms. Wilson moved to approve as submitted, the request for demolition at 966 Pitt Street; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. John and Julia Linton, homeowners and Jody Crosby, designer, were present. He stated that they were here last month for conceptual comment and took all the board’s comments and met with Mr. Pohlman and attempted to address each one. He stated that they believe the finished product is better than the original. He stated that the height, mass, materials are consistent with the neighborhood and a compliment to the street. He reviewed comments from the previous meeting by Commission members. He stated they changed the slope of the left side to make it steeper and reduce the contrast between the gable roof on the right side. Had they made it steeper, there would have been a wall of shingles, so they added a break in the roof and three windows across and there are also windows on the side elevation that match. Those are the changes they made to address the roof differences. He stated that another item is that the porch now has a roof which is consistent with the rest of the home. He provided the Commission members with some examples of homes in and just outside of the Old Village indicating their inspiration for their home. He stated that another comment made was that the house was not engaged with the street, so they have expanded the front porch. The right side where the dining room is located came out and the porch was recessed, but now they have brought it out to the street further to provide room for additional seating and redesigned the entryway and the foyer to accommodate the door facing the street for an Old Village Historic District Commission

inviting feel. They also added a separate pervious walkway from the street to the front stairs of the house, instead of the previous walkway, which was part of the driveway. He said that the windows in the upper portion of the house also provides more of a view from the street. He stated that another comment made was that the porch must have a full roof over the second story; the pergola was not acceptable. He stated that they removed the pergola from the plans and added a full roof. He stated that they attempted to select a roof that would complement the gable roof and the other roof and did not want to do a single roofline that looks like a Charleston single house. They believe the roof selected is consistent and harmonious with the rest of the home. He stated that adding the roof itself addresses the comment that the porch was floating or not as engaged with the rest of the home. He stated that one suggestion was to make the porch longer, which is what they have done. They decreased the depth from 16 feet to 12 feet, because this is a functional porch for them. They increased the length from 14 feet to 19 feet, because of the roofline and the windows. He stated that they will have a narrow view of the water. He stated that another comment made by the Commission was that the windows on the side where there were potential views did not have a grid. He stated that the comment was to be consistent and have grid on all windows which they have done. He stated that staff comment was to highlight or more clearly identify the house on the physical site plan which was also accomplished. He said that a change they personally made was to the garage doors which are louvered, similar to the rest of the house, so it does not look like a garage. They also open outwards. Ms. Wilson stated that the agenda indicates final approval; however, the plans only show conceptual. Mr. Linton stated that the plans were marked incorrectly. It is for final approval. Ms. Pohlman stated that the application was filed as final. Ms. Rowe stated that she applauds all the changes. Mr. Keenan asked if the louvered system on the bottom is a wooden horizontal. Mr. Linton stated that they are two inch louvers with a one inch gap, because there is a 40% air flow requirement. Mr. Keenan asked about the railing system on the right side porches. Mr. Linton stated that it is a grid wire system / wire mesh. Ms. Rowe asked why he is not doing the same grid system on the front porch. Mr. Linton stated that the purpose of this was to make it where there is less obstruction. He stated that it is set back off of the street so you will not see them very well. He stated that the wire grid system was too informal for the front porch. He stated that the wire mesh will disappear into the view. Mr. Keenan stated that he assumes the wire mesh is code, but it does fit the house. He would prefer that the homeowner choose one style of railing for the whole house. He stated that the windows on the front left on the top gable are too small and leaves a lot of solid space on the gable. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Rowe agrees that the railing on the porches need to be consistent. She stated that there seems to be a disconnect. Ms. Wilson stated that she appreciates that a lot of work has been accomplished. She stated that the front and the front right have started to come together. She stated that she likes how they broke up the really wide gable with the porch roof and broke the roof line. Would be great if this could be done on the backside as well and re-center that gable so that you have that relationship of symmetrical gables throughout. There are a few funny conditions. You have aligned your porches with the heated massing of the house and what that does is push your porch roof a foot past the house, so there are dangling rafter conditions. You will be looking at the backside of your roof trim when you are on the porch. If you broke that massing as well and also pushed it in from the primary gable of the house, it would receive that roof and clean up that detail. She said that there is not enough detail in the package to vote on final approval. She said there is no wall section, no elevation details, and they need a large detail of how they are going to case the windows, what the siding is like. On the proposed board and batten, this is especially critical to detail on how this is done. She said they would really like to see the scale of the batten relative to the width of the boards. How are your overhangs? Are you doing open rafter or closing the rafters? She stated that the Commission needs to see all that detail before they are able to evaluate. So far the homeowners and designer have made an excellent effort on the front and right and they could perhaps wrap it around to bring the left side up and knit it together the same way; this would be really helpful. As far as the hard wire for a handrail detail, it is not an approved detail for the Old Village. If the homeowner is worried about transparency, one thing you see people do is a one by four board and then a single cable rail and then another one by four board so you get a bigger spacing in there, but still using approved details. It does not say what the front railing is, but it looks really thin. It shows two by four horizontal flat railing. She stated that there needs to be more information on how you are detailing those railings, the roof, and other areas. She stated that the porch roof is extending past the house. She stated that the whole roof system is slipping into the screened porch. If you are on your screened porch, you are going to see the backside of a foot of roof that is dangling and it will need to be rafted or supported. If the overhang is sixteen inches then you will need to have brackets. Are we going to see the rafters or not, is there a drip edge, corner boards, window casings. The Commission needs to know what that material is and how it is going to work. She stated that it really improved the home a lot when you did the porch as a separate roof line. If you made the gable on the left symmetrical and broke up that roofline on the back, so you could lift that pitch a little on that side and address balancing the two sides of the elevation. Ms. Rowe stated that she agrees that there are not enough specifics. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that she realizes this is frustrating for the homeowner; however, a lot of good progress has been made. Ms. Crosby provided illustrations on the proposed railing system. She said that million dollar homes have this detail. Ms. Wilson asked if she could include this in the final next month, because this is the detail they need to see as it is difficult to understand without detail. Mr. Linton stated that he believes the house on the corner of Pitt Street and Schweers Lane has the same railing on some of their porches. Ms. Wilson stated that a lot of times it is coded; therefore, if this is being proposed, then the more information that is provided the better. Ms. Crosby stated that she was the designer on this home. The questions she has are the kill details for the eaves. She believes that bringing those in is going to be a detriment, especially on a front to symmetry of the house. On the rear, it is going to cause an undue offset in the foundation and in the walls, bedroom walls, etc. Is there another direction the Commission would suggest? Can they hip the front porch roof and do something different there. She would not want to do it on the back, because it would not look right. Ms. Wilson stated that a hip is better for that condition. Ms. Crosby stated that this would help, because they could go past it and bring an eyebrow return in there and execute it a little better. She stated that this is not a very wide house so if they offset the porch in sixteen inches, they will lose wall space. Ms. Wilson stated that you could do this with ten inches on the front with the shed. Ms. Crosby stated that they are really tight on the spacing and bringing that in is going to cause issues with lining up the two story windows and everything below it. Ms. Wilson stated that Ms. Crosby has a good group of houses she has been looking at. She would caution her not to use non-historic homes or houses that were done at the time when things were not being reviewed. She said that a lot of the houses in the Old Village have details that can be referenced, as long as the Commission has more information. Mr. Linton stated that the houses do not have signs on them to distinguish whether they were built when there was little or no review. Ms. Wilson stated that the homes to look at for ideas do not have to be in the Old Village, as there are beautiful historic homes on Sullivan’s Island and just outside the Historic District. Mr. Linton thought he had to look within the district. Ms. Wilson replied, not for detailing or materials. For example, the hardwire railing. If this is not seen very often on historic homes and the homeowner would like to illustrate how it is going to be detailed, if there were pictures of this type of railing on a historic home on Sullivan’s Island that was a great porch Old Village Historic District Commission

with that detail, it would be helpful to the Commission. More information, details, drawings, notes, dimensions. Ms. Wilson moved to defer the final application for 966 Pitt Street until additional information is provided; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. John and Julia Linton, homeowners and Jody Crosby, designer were present. Mr. Linton stated that they had conceptual approval and were deferred, so they are back for the third time. He stated that not all Commission members were present last time and reviewed details with them. He stated that the slope of the roof on the left side was changed as per the Commission’s comments, and added windows. The rear slope will remain the same and they added windows and windows on the side and expanded the front porch out and reconfigured the entryway and the front door to make the front door face the street, so it is more engaging. He stated that a walkway was also added from the street to further engage. He stated that on the two story porch, it used to have more of a pergola type look and it Old Village Historic District Commission

was removed and put in a full roof which was suggested by the Commission. He stated that they also reconfigured the dimensions of the two story porch to make it more grounded into the house and had what was referred to as picture windows, but changed them to a grid to make all the windows consistent. He stated that they have addressed all the comments. He stated that one of the comments was to try and do the same to the back as what was done to the front with the roof, so they have added a similar break in the roof to the rear so there is a changed pitch adding a more symmetrical look. He stated that another comment was to make some of the windows bigger so larger windows were added. He stated that this area will be attic space for them. He stated that the railing details have all been changed to be the normal horizontal railing. He stated that another comment was to add board and batten detail and not to use an inferior detail, so they spent time trying to determine what would be inferior versus superior detail. They looked at St. Andrews Church and that neighborhood is board and batten. Their original idea for board and batten was to do something different from all the other homes in the neighborhood that had recently been built. He stated that the only other change they made is the location of the garage door and match the louvers under the house. Ms. Rowe stated that she applauds the homeowner for all the work they have done, because it looks wonderful. Linda Balzac stated that this has come so far from the first submittal. Mr. Keenan stated that it looks great and has come a long way and appreciate the homeowners working with the Commission. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he loves it and wish they saw a lot more of these, as it is very appealing. He stated that the porches are still not harmonious with the Old Village, as you do not see many of these in the Village. Ms. Wilson stated that if it was in a more traditional row of houses, she may have some push back on the double porch; however, considering the view they have from the top porch, it would be difficult. She does not think it is out of context with the houses as you get closer to the harbor. Ms. Rowe asked if the attic space could one day be added on to. Mr. Linton stated that they have two small children and do not plan on having more. He stated that the ceilings would only be 6 feet there. Ms. Wilson moved to approve the final new construction for 966 Pitt Street; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Ms. Rowe stated that the alterations look much better. Ms. Rowe moved to approve the application for 966 Pitt Street on final review for porch roof and window placement by consent; seconded by Ms. Montgomery. All present voted in favor.

label: 241 Middle Street
request: 241 Middle Street—(HISTORIC 6025) —Final Approval for Enclosing Third Story Rear Porch

events.text:
Ms. Wilson stated that she would remove herself from discussions and voting due to conflict of interest. (Ms. Wilson stepped out at 5:54 p.m.) Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Amber Thomas, 734 Pitt Street, stated that she is the architect working for Heather Wilson, representing the homeowner. Mr. Hirshorn asked if there is an ordinance on enclosing existing porches on historic structures or guidelines. Mr. Pohlman stated that there is not an ordinance; however, there are guidelines. Mr. Hirshorn asked if it is prohibited. Mr. Pohlman stated that it is on a historic home. Ms. Thomas stated that the footprint will not be modified in any way. She showed a panorama of Middle Street showing that you would not see the third floor enclosure, which falls beneath the ridge. She stated that there was a deck where they had a great deal of water, so they would like to mitigate by enclosing it and capitalizing on the square footage. Mr. Pohlman cited Porches and Stoops on historic buildings, and stated that porches, stoops and steps that are original and contribute to the building’s architectural character should not be altered or moved or enclosed on a primary façade or side elevations. Ms. Balzac stated that the deck on the third floor is not original to the home. She did the work on the house approximately fourteen years ago and there was a whole porch put on the back and the deck was always problematic and was put there by the previous owner. She stated that part of the back of the historic home was also renovated. Mr. Hirshorn asked when the third floor deck was added. Ms. Balzac stated that it was done in the 1970’s and is not original. Ms. Dickson stated that it could be removed and not have anything and be closer to the historic original plan. Ms. Thomas stated that what the homeowners really wanted was to enclose that space to utilize the square footage. There is a harbor view that they could capitalize on. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan asked for the dimension of the existing deck. Ms. Thomas said that it is nine feet by thirteen feet. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he is fairly convinced that it is not an original porch and for reasons of preservation of these historic houses, it would be advantageous in the application to have more of a timeline. He stated that this is an issue when the Commission addresses historic homes. He asked to be clear, if a rear porch can be altered, even if historic. Mr. Pohlman stated that it would be up to the Commission. He said the guidelines stated “primary façade or side elevations”. Mr. Hirshorn stated that a rear façade is a primary façade. Ms. Balzac stated there is a house in front of it on the harbor, so it is not visible. A primary façade is when you are on the water. She said the deck is not visible. Mr. Hirshorn stated for reasons of precedence, it is important in dealing with a historic home such as this that it is all documented. He stated that he is swayed that it is not an original porch and is not a primary façade; however, it is obviously a delicate issue. The other question is, with the new structure that is being added, will it be something that you would approve on a historic home. He stated that he likes it better than the porch. Ms. Balzac stated that it is a deck, not a porch. Ms. Rowe stated that it is an improvement. Mr. Keenan stated that enclosing the deck that is not historic, overall, looks better and likes the windows. Ms. Rowe made a motion to approve the plans submitted for 241 Middle Street for the replacement of the deck; seconded by Mr. Hirshorn. All present voted in favor, with Ms. Wilson recusing from voting.

label: 116 Beach Street
request: 116 Beach Street – Applicant is seeking After-the- Fact Final Review for a dock. CORRESPONDENCE

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design Group, representing the homeowner. He stated that they were before the Commission in December and received final approval on these homes which are down on the harbor. He showed the proposed site plan, which has to do with the tree protection and grading. He stated that the lot is sitting at six feet now and in October during Hurricane Matthew, water did come across. He stated that previously they discussed bringing the lot up to nine feet; however, as they worked through the process with Mr. Bernard and Mr. Juan of the Town of Mount Pleasant, they needed to add some low retaining walls. Since they are coming back for approval of the retaining wall, they also have some window and door modifications which can be seen on the proposed plans. Everything that has to do with the parking and front porch are all to control grading and protecting the trees. He reviewed the drainage and grading with Commission members, as well as the retaining walls, which will be 8x8 posts and 3x8 wood slats and a cap, no more than two and a half feet tall. They did the wood retaining walls, in keeping with the seawall and the dock that is going in. The seawall has been approved. From a floorplan standpoint, on the ground floor they previously had the garage door and a set of steps coming straight out. As they worked through the driveway and because of the grade retaining they needed to do, the turn into the garage door was too tight. They have now extended the stairs onto the porch to enter onto this brick ground floor loggia. This is a southern regional use. He stated on the main floor, some revisions to the front porch which is deeper. The doors along the back were previously shown as folding doors, and they have gone back to a traditional French door. In September’s request, the window in the butler’s pantry was on the side and now is moved around to the street side and have added a small window in the back. On the upper floor, there is a matching window in the bathroom that currently was not there in the proposal in September. In September, there were only a few windows in the bathroom along the waterfront, and they have now opened it up so there is now five windows there instead of the previous two. One advantage in changing the front stairs, is that the front porch got deeper and took up a little bit of the space that was there under the dormer windows and the porch roof. He showed the retaining wall and stated that they will have significant plants inside and outside of the retaining. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the loggia was enclosed. Mr. Clarke stated that it is covered, but not fully enclosed. Mr. Keenan asked if the retaining wall was a result of the storm. Mr. Clarke stated that it certainly highlighted it. Ms. Dickson asked if changing the stairs added square footage. Mr. Clarke said that it made the porch two feet deeper in the front, so very minimal. Mr. Clarke stated that they are way under allowable. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan stated that he understands the retaining wall, which is necessary. All the revisions are an enhancement. Ms. Wilson agreed and said she liked the added windows and the deeper porch, as well as the stairs. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it appears there is a network of retaining walls in between the two houses. Mr. Clarke said that there is a large grouping of trees between the two lots. There is a retaining wall on the other lot, which is part of it. They each have their own, so they are able to do their own maintenance. Ms. Wilson asked if Mr. Clarke was creating a large swale. Mr. Clarke stated that it is a swale and because of the critical line setback, he needed to open it up. Zach Bearden, Landscape Designer stated that for these two lots in particular, some existing drains are 4 ½, but they are starting so low. Particularly any design, they try to get above the curve; however, in this case, you really have to bring in a significant amount of fill to make it work. He stated that the retaining walls make it more of a hardline swale and given the natural way for the water to get out. They did not want to pond on the street side. It was very challenging, but works for this particular area. Ms. Rowe made a motion to approve the plans submitted for 116 Beach Street; seconded by Ms. Wilson. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachment 1). Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design Group, reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated the dock was built with all approvals and constructed smaller than originally shown on the approved plans. He stated that he has signatures from several surrounding neighbors in favor of the request.

Mr. Harvey Lemon, 319 Bayview Drive, stated he is not in favor of the dock, particularly the inclusion of a roof structure. He stated that he is in support of Mr. Peter Dodd’s letter. He suggested that having an after-the-fact approval does not allow for comment from the neighbors. He stated that 104 Beach Street had a covered dock, but was removed after requests from Bayview residents. He suggested that covered docks should not be allowed as it impedes the view of the harbor.

Mr. Jenkins Bailey, 311 Bayview Drive, stated he is also not in favor of a roof structure on the dock. He suggested that the covered dock is not good for the harbor or the view from the neighborhood.

There being no further comments, Mr. Hirshorn closed public comment.

Ms. Dovre agreed that every dock should be equally considered.

Ms. Wilson asked when the restriction was put into place. Mr. Rutherford answered that he is not sure the exact date.

Mr. Hirshorn agreed that some of the dock structures pre-date the implementation of the restriction.

Ms. Wilson asked if this issue relates to the historic district. Mr. Rutherford answered that anyone concerned with a dock in the historic district could raise that concern; it does not have to be a concerned raised only from someone that lives in the historic district or in the vicinity of the dock in question.

Ms. Rowe asked if a covered dock is restricted. Mr. Rutherford answered in the affirmative and stated that it is included in the guidelines. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn asked if OCRM has a similar restriction on covered docks. Mr. Rutherford answered in the negative and stated that the OCRM approval would not supersede the Commission’s purview.

Ms. Montgomery stated that the guidelines should be upheld.

Mr. Hirshorn asked what action the Commission can take. Mr. Rutherford answered that the Commission can approve the structure and dock, or the Commission can deny the covered structure and require it to be removed. Mr. Hirshorn asked the applicant if they were aware of the restriction. Mr. Clarke answered that the owners were not aware of the restriction. He stated that the dock was included with the tree removal request, but it was not included on the plans that the Commission reviewed and approved. He stated that the owners had the understanding that the staff approval included approval for the construction of the dock.

Ms. Wilson asked if there is a photograph of both 116 and 112 Beach Street docks. Mr. Rutherford answered in the negative.

Mr. Hirshorn suggested that a deferral might be appropriate to allow the owner to speak to this issue.

Ms. Wilson stated that this is a permitted structure that has the support of the immediate neighbor. She suggested that this should be taken into consideration.

Ms. Montgomery suggested that the guidelines should be upheld regardless of if the structure was constructed with the proper permits, but not approved by the Commission.

Ms. Caroline Johnson, 112 Beach Street, stated that she wanted to make it clear that the dock and structure were constructed with all of the appropriate approvals aside from the Commission. She stated that they were under the impression that they had all of the necessary approvals. She stated that it was not their intention to deceive the Commission.

Mr. Rutherford stated that the dock was not included in the submittal to the Commission. He stated that the dock approval would not have required Old Village Historic District Commission

approval during the tree removal process, so even though included in those plans, the dock would not have been reviewed. He stated that staff would not have been aware of the desire for a dock at the time the application was submitted to the Commission.

Ms. Wilson stated that she was not previously aware that docks required approval from the Commission. She suggested that this was an oversight.

Ms. Lowe suggested that allowing this dock to remain could set a precedent for future requests.

Ms. Wilson moved for approval of the dock with the deviation from the guidelines with the condition that this is a one-time approval and would not set a precedent. Motion failed due to the lack of a second.

Ms. Montgomery moved for denial of the roof structure and that it be removed, with approval of the dock. Ms. Lowe seconded the motion. Motion failed on a 3 to 2 vote with Ms. Montgomery and Ms. Lowe in favor; Mr. Hirshorn, Ms. Dovre, and Ms. Wilson opposed.

Ms. Wilson moved for approval of the dock and roof structure.

As a point of order, Mr. Rutherford suggested that this motion was already stated. Mr. Pagliarini suggested that the proper action would be to have a motion to reconsider the item.

Ms. Dovre moved to reconsider this item. Ms. Wilson seconded the motion. All in favor.

Ms. Wilson moved for approval of the dock and roof structure for 112 and 116 Beach Street with the condition that it does not set a precedent for the historic district. Ms. Dovre seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 3 to 2 vote with Mr. Hirshorn, Ms. Wilson, and Ms. Dovre; Ms. Montgomery and Ms. Rowe opposed. Old Village Historic District Commission

label: 443 Church Street

events.text:

She stated that all the travertine will be a khaki color. The kitchen structure is not seen, as the elevation is shorter than the pool house and the existing home, so it will not be visible from the front of the home and there are also trees on both side on the back end. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it is difficult from the drawings submitted, to grasp the materials and design of the outdoor kitchen structure. She stated that it needs to share more in Old Village Historic District Commission

terms of roof, roof pitch, and column details. She stated that it needs to be more thoughtful if it is going to be modern. She stated that it feels slapped on in terms of the roof. She stated that she believes it will be seen from the street. She is fine with the pool and hardscape, and wonders if the applicant even needs the setback, because going all the way to less than three feet, the Commission would generally like to see more than for the maintenance of the structure on all sides. She asked if the client really feels that they need this relief. Ms. Snell stated that her client really likes the decking in between the pool and the outdoor kitchen; however, she could certainly discuss this with them. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it is included in the guidelines that accessory structures to historical homes, roofs need to mimic. Ms. Snell stated that they did the same type of roofing material, but understands about the structure looking more historic. Ms. Rowe stated that she has an issue seeing this from Church Street. She stated that having an outdoor kitchen that you are able to see, it does not fit with the historic cottage. She stated that the roof’s modern feel does not work, but is not sure she would like to see an outdoor kitchen at all in the historic district. Ms. Wilson stated that if they had a wall and it was not so open and was on the side of the small carriage house or small cottage. She stated that the initial design was to offset the other building, but she will certainly talk to the client about lowering the deck space or put a type of wall, as suggested. label: 104 Friend Street
request: 104 Friend Street – Survey 4227 – Applicant is seeking Final Review for revised driveway from a previously approved plan. [Consent Approval]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design Group, stated that they are under the 5500 square feet with a lot of porch space, front and back. There is a pool deck Old Village Historic District Commission

structure, covered pool, but all open space as well. He stated that this is not a historic home and the only building that is historic close by is the church. There is an existing non historic one story structure. Keeping this one story was important as the surrounding homes were also one story. It is a very large lot that backs up to the church parking lot. He stated that the existing house leaked for so many years that there is mold growing. There is a newer roof to attempt to stop the leaking; however, it is still saturated and stays wet. He stated that a few years ago, there was a drainage issue. He stated that there is a pipe that goes under the church parking lot and goes out to the street on the other side of the church parking lot. He stated that the proposed site is a little overwhelming at first. He stated that the lot does drop down and they will be removing the driveway out from under the 39 inch live oak. It starts going downhill so that you are able to get in under the house. They will be raising the slab approximately one and a half feet so that it does not stay wet. They will have a raised pool deck a few steps down from the porch and will work all the drainage towards the drain pipe. He stated that the house is a one and a half story home. It is brick, but will be a white textured brick. The roof will be slate. He would like to have copper flashing and copper roof on the dormer and turning it down the sides. He reviewed with the Commissioners the site plan for the home, pool and driveway. He stated that they are using high quality natural materials. Ashley Woody, 110 Friend Street, which is next door to the proposed home. She stated that she has lived in her home for a very long time. She provided a survey to the Commission members that was done after the Adams’ built their house and jammed up the drainage on the block. Her question to the architect is: how much soil is going to be put in and what is going to happen. She said that the new pipe that was put in under the church parking lot does not work and has made it worse. When tropical storm Matthew came through, it was the first storm since the pipe was put in. She stated that she has never had water coming up underneath their home. She stated that the dirt under their crawl space had water perking up. She does not believe the pipe worked and is concerned. How will the new homeowners handle the drainage? She stated that on the drawing, the big live oak is not showing, which is in the middle of their backyard. Mr. Clarke stated that he will address this. Ms. Woody stated that she does not want to be left with a mushy backyard. She stated that Mr. Ilderton should never have been allowed to dump all that dirt. She stated that the new homeowners are also cutting it close with the 39.8% of impervious surfaces. Mr. Keenan stated that unfortunately, this Commission has no purview over drainage plans. Ann Muir, 100 Friend Street, stated that after Matthew, it was a flood zone and even when it rains heavily, it floods and is very wet. She stated that the idea of moving the drainage under the church parking lot was Old Village Historic District Commission

smart, but it is not working. She is also concerned about the big oak on the proposed site. She did email the Town regarding the tree and did not get a response. She knows the Town will have property owners compensate when a tree is removed and she would like to know what will be done. Mr. Keenan stated that this Commission does not have purview over trees either, but there is an arborist with the Town and if it is considered a grand tree, you are not able to cut it down. It must be mitigated. Mrs. Muir stated that if the plan is approved without addressing the tree issue, then they will cut it down and say that the OVHDC approved the plan. Mr. Pohlman stated the tree issue would overrule the plan and they would have to come back through for a new approval. The OVHDC is only over the exterior of the building and site plan and has no purview over the trees or vegetation or drainage. He stated that anything that is changed during the permitting process, comes back to the Commission. Jim Muir, 100 Friend Street, stated that the drainage issue is a County project and there was a lot of back and forth getting it completed. He stated that there are two drain areas and it is not in the middle of the field. He said an engineer said that they should have used pumps. He said that he has a picture of the field shortly after they finished the project and sent it to the County and told them that it does not appear to be working. Mr. Clarke stated that the reason why he did not bring up drainage and the oak tree was because it falls on the Town for approval and he did not want to bring this issue to the Commission. He stated that as far as drainage, he was there the day after Matthew and was surprised, because he thought it would be worse. He stated that it was wet. He stated that they are working with a civil engineer and a landscape architect and their sole purpose is to address the drainage and make sure it is done correctly. He stated that on the lot by the hackberry, it is approximately 6 feet 8 inches and they will be bringing in 7 ½ feet of fill where it is sitting at 5 ½ feet. He stated that the Town will not issue a permit until the grading plan and other issues are addressed. He stated that they began their design working around the 39 inch oak; however, an arborist did inspect the tree and it is diseased. It sat so low and will not survive. He stated that they will work through this with the Town Arborist, Eddie Bernard. Mr. Keenan stated that he likes the brick and the description of the paint.
