She asked Mr. Hirshorn if for him, it is at seven feet or could it be a step down and the pool be at twelve feet or somewhere in between Mr. Hirshorn stated that the last design was a partially elevated pool with a retaining wall. He stated that it is great to have a pool, particularly if you are going to invest so much in a home site. He stated that based on the condition of the lot and the surrounding area, it feels as if the property owner is attempting to shoe-horn something in that is not necessarily appropriate or possible on this lot, as it is a unique lot. He stated that he is fully sympathetic to the interest in a pool; however, he would be interested to hear more discussion, particularly from Ms. Wilson on the design element of an elevated pool such as this. He stated that it is not something that the Commission sees very much. He stated that in the center of the Old Village, it would be a bad policy to start seeing an abundant number of raised pools, if this become a new precedent on how to deal with a unique lot. He stated from an architectural standpoint, he would be very interested to hear discussion on this issue. He added that he has not closed his opinion to this issue. Ms. Rowe stated that she believes that where this pool is sitting on that lot, it is better being higher, because it is not being looked down on, Old Village Historic District Commission

particularly by the church. She stated that everything needs to be addressed on a case by case basis. She stated that it is not a historic issue. Ms. Dickson stated that if that is the case, everything sets precedence even if you are looking at them all individually. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his concern is that this will be used as a precedent going forward, as the neighbor’s pool is as well. He understands that this is a very practical solution to the problem. He stated that maybe this means that it is not possible to have a pool there. He said that if this is approved, other property owners will begin to apply for elevated pools, citing this elevated pool. Mr. Clarke stated that they had the pool at over 10 feet on the previous submittal, which was determined to be not appropriate and over the last three or four months, have had it from 10 feet to 15 feet to 17 feet and have gone up and down. He stated that the reason why they brought it up was to condense the mass. He said that he feels the homeowners will do whatever is necessary to get the pool to happen. He stated that he does not know if this is precedent setting or not, because it is a one of a kind lot. He stated that it is the best way to handle the situation and if it were anywhere else in the Village he would not be advocating for this at all, even if it were a raised house in a flood zone. However, in this particular case there is no reason to put it down low. He said the reason they put the porch down the side was to try and condense that mass and the footprint in as tight as possible. He stated that this was the case for raising the pool. Ms. Dickson stated that she believes that Mr. Clarke did a wonderful job of reducing the mass and making a better house. Ms. Wilson stated that she is torn because she does not love a raised pool and does not see them in the Village and although Mr. Clarke has pointed out two of them, it is not in keeping with the character. She stated that the flip side of this is what it does nicely is it allows that porch not to step down and have an awkward rear elevation. She said that the rear elevation is nice and tight and clean. She asked if the pool had an infinity edge. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Clarke stated that it does not have an infinity edge – it is the pool band which is on the edge. Ms. Wilson asked if a rail was needed. Mr. Clarke said that if a rail is needed, they will put one in. He stated that he has done the pools like this before. Ms. Wilson stated that she is still reluctant about the right side section. She said when she looks at the elevation and sketch in what Ms. Woody’s numbers are, where Mr. Clarke is showing the grade nicely going off, the reality is that at that property line, it is dropping six feet. She said if a retaining wall is not there, she does not understand how they are containing their own grading plan. She asked if there is a wall that is not shown that will be there. Mr. Clarke stated that it will not stay consistent from a house out to the side. He said that just as it drops from front to back, it will drop from side to the property line and there is a pipe on his side of the property line which will catch all their water coming from the front and from their side and take it down. He said that this pipe was going to be in a swale to keep Ms. Woody’s water on her side; however, if Ms. Woody would be willing to work with him, they would be willing to design a pipe that could be placed on the property line that could catch both and send the water away. He stated that the pipe would be set where it is needed in order to catch all the water coming down. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would be interested to hear what Ms. Wilson’s thoughts are on the elevated pool issue from a professional prospective. Ms. Wilson stated that in reference to Ms. Rowe’s comments regarding the church, if you look just at Mr. Clarke’s rear elevation, it is really clean and the Commission must consider what it looks at. She stated that he has more rear neighbors that are not present; however, believes the rear elevation is very well done. She stated that it is still big with the porch plus the deck; however, to address Mr. Hirshorn’s concern, she does not have an issue with the raised pool in this very rare situation. Ms. Rowe stated that she does not believe there is another lot similar to this one in the Old Village that drops as this one does. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that he realizes that the Commission does not have purview over the drainage issues; however, the drainage issues are a derivative of the house design. He stated that the initial issue is the house design. He stated that it is very rare that the Commission has this situation where there is a next door neighbor who has substantiated evidence of what could happen if the Commission approves this design and cause flooding to her home. He stated that for this reason, he has a tremendous amount of caution approving, aside from the elevated pool, which there appears to be some consensus. He stated that it feels like the approval of the design of the house as situated on the lot would, as a result, create issues; therefore, he has some reservation in moving forward until there is more clarity. Ms. Wilson stated that Mr. Clarke has done a very wide plan, which is nice and believes it is very attractive, but in doing so, has not provided enough real estate. She stated that it is incumbent upon Mr. Clarke to cut those sections going all the way down and putting Ms. Woody’s grade in their sections and showing the Commission that it can be done. She stated that although she feels Mr. Clarke will do what is necessary to make this work, she is not completely convinced. She stated that she is just referring to the walls. She stated that she believes that this item should be deferred, as it is worth the study. She stated that she believes that this plan, but with the other elevations where Mr. Clarke did nestle the pool in slightly, may make other Commission members more comfortable, who may otherwise have reservations about the raised pool. She stated that she believes the Commission is representing their constituency when they resist the raised pool. Mr. Hirshorn stated that for the record that the issue of the design is in question because of the uniqueness of the lot and there is substantially more mass on this unique lot than originally was there. He stated that in order for him to get comfortable with the new mass under new construction guidelines, he would be more inclined to approve this if he could see more substantiation of what the derivative effects on the lot and the adjacent lot would be of this substantial new mass on the existing lot. He would appreciate clarity. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Clarke stated that he will submit for the September meeting and will have an enhanced grading plan down the side to address the concerns, taking into account that the neighbor’s existing grade. He stated that they will study pulling the pool and pool deck in slightly. He stated that it is where it is and the height it is; however, will try to lose a few feet on the deck. Ms. Wilson asked if Mr. Clarke has considered his design’s relationship to the street and if pushing it back or forward would help. She stated that once the grades are considered, she would be in support of a larger front yard. She stated that perhaps pushing it off Friend Street would provide more dirt in the front to deal with the flooding issues and have a different relationship with Ms. Woody’s property. Mr. Clarke stated that he will study this over the next two weeks. He stated that this is difficult; however, Ms. Woody has an issue that is not of her own keeping and his property owners have an issue that is existing. He said that all they can do is fix their issue and the only way it will affect Ms. Woody is that their lot will no longer be the place that her lot drains to. He stated that they would like to work with her in the installation of the drainage. He said that he will bring back a revised right hand side that shows the Commission that with Ms. Woody’s existing grade what theirs will look like. Ms. Wilson stated that she does appreciate that this is difficult; however, the Commission is not going to prevent Mr. Clarke’s clients from building a home. She thanked Mr. Clarke for his patience. Ms. Wilson moved that the application for 102 Friend Street be deferred; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor. SD/HW AIF III. Staff Approvals [None] IV. Motion to Adjourn Ms. Dickson moved to adjourn; seconded by Ms. Wilson. All present voted in favor. There being no further business, meeting was adjourned at 7:05 p.m. Old Village Historic District Commission

Respectfully submitted, Barbara Ashe

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design Group, stated that last month, they had a good review. He said that they pulled the pool in, brought it up with one step down. He said that the item of discussion was the grading down the right hand side, looking from Friend Street. He said that he had steep fallouts on the grade, from the final grade against the house until it met the neighbor’s property. He indicated the proposed grade along the property line and up against the house. He said currently, the lot does slope as steep as it is shown and there is a concrete driveway. He said that they will be softening the slope so that it matches the neighbors, but will also be removing the concrete driveway and have plantings that will absorb Old Village Historic District Commission

the water. He said the goal is for all the water to be pushed to the rear right and collected to go out the pipe. He said the pipe was designed for a 40 year rain and in the past six months, the Village has had 40 year rains a number of times. He said that the pipe has performed as the Town engineer stated. He said there is no change to the architecture of the house and they spent all their time working on the right side. He said that this was Ms. Wilson’s main concern and believes this addresses her comments. He said that after the last meeting, he also spent time meeting with the neighbor and currently, her yard drains onto their yard and all they are doing will not be draining onto hers and will be collecting the water and sending to the pipe. He said that they will work with her to help with her drainage to go towards the back as well. Ashley Woody, 110 Friend Street, stated that she sees where Mr. Clarke has made the changes on the fill; however, it is still going from 13 feet in the front, which is still two feet higher than it currently is. She stated that all of this has been going on for ten years. She said that she has been dealing with people filling in lots on her block, building houses, and all the flooding. She discussed all the processes over the years, guarantees from other builders that the drainage would work. She said that with this last storm, they now have water coming up underneath their home. She said that once the Commission approves this home, then that homeowner becomes vested in the project and nothing can be done after that point. She said that an earlier applicant was required to have an engineer’s plan for his drainage and asked how she can get the Town to do this for this project. She said that she needs help, because this is her last opportunity. She said that Mr. Clarke spoke briefly with her in the hall after the last meeting, but the new property owners have never come over to her home to speak with her or called to introduce themselves. She said that she does not believe they are being very neighborly in this process. She said that she is not sure what can be done in conjunction with what their plans are to help her, other than cut down her three grand oak trees and fill the lot in. She said that she is asking the Commission for help. Mr. Keenan stated that the Commission appreciates her comments. He stated that this Commission has absolutely no purview over drainage. He reviewed the duties of the OVHDC. He said that water has become a huge Old Village Historic District Commission

issue and the Commission is very sympathetic and are unable to deny an application based on drainage. Ms. Woody stated that this is a process where she is able to attend and asked about the next step at the Town for those that have to approve the building permit. She asked if there is a meeting. Mr. Keenan stated that there are two individuals from the Town present this evening. Mr. Juan stated that he is going to defer the plan with the Town engineer, Mr. Kevin Mitchell, before he issues a permit. He stated that he will defer to Mr. Mitchell to work with the builder. Ms. Woody asked if she would be contacted. Mr. Juan stated that Ms. Woody would have to be in contact with Mr. Mitchell and request to be a part of the process. He said that she may also file a FOIA, as information is available. Mr. Keenan stated that Mr. Linton’s project is also being delayed until a stamped engineering drainage study is provided and added that Mr. Clarke’s project may end up in the same realm; however, he cannot speak to this. Mr. Linton stated that he does believe that the Commission has the ability to approve with conditions. He said downtown Charleston has conditional approval all the time. He said that he believes that this could be approved with the condition that there be an engineering study of the drainage that is approved by the Town. Mr. Keenan stated that he is very sympathetic with Mr. Linton’s situation of any potential efficiencies of any Town employee. Ms. Dickson suggested that Mr. Linton and Ms. Woody work together. Mr. Linton stated that he is at a loss for what to do. He said that everyone else around them has been allowed to build. He said that everyone else’s lots drain onto their property, just as it does with Ms. Woody. He said that he does not believe this is fair and added that this Commission has the ability to condition a permit on that study. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan stated that he does not know anything about this study. He added that Mr. Linton’s is the first he has heard about. He stated that he would have to defer to Town staff, but does not believe the Commission is able to approve on this condition. Mr. Pohlman stated that he would need to inquire further; however, to the best of his knowledge at this time, the Commission is unable to approve on this condition. He stated that he would research further as to what the Commission is able to condition on a COA; however, believes this is outside the scope since it is outside of the guidelines. Ms. Rowe stated that this is part of the Commission’s concern, because this is out of their area of expertise. She stated that she is not knowledgeable about drainage requirements and this is not what this Commission is about. Mr. Clarke stated that he was advised to meet with Mr. Pohlman to go through the proper steps and the first step is to get the design approved or architecture, which is what is currently in front of the Commission. He said that as Mr. Juan stated, during the permitting process, they will have a professional drainage plan done which they have already started. He said that he was not going to bring this to the OVHDC, because this is not the proper venue for this process. He said that Mr. Juan will not approve any building permit until all those items have been completed. Ms. Rowe stated that it appears that Mr. Clarke has completed what he was required to do and it must go through the process. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his comments are consistent with some of the other applications this evening. He said that what Mr. Clarke has created is a nice and tasteful house, but then there is a tendency to add additional elements and coverage on lots that may not be appropriate. He said unfortunately, with many of the lots in the Old Village they are situated in such a way that when you add these large coverages and additional elements, they impact not just the aesthetic of the Old Village, but also neighboring lots. He stated that his reservation from the beginning was the additional element of the pool and realizes why it had to be elevated, and has not been harmonious to him from the beginning. He stated that this is a very specific lot with significant issues and although within the Old Village Historic District Commission

maximum percentage of lot coverage, it is still a large footprint. He said the elevated pool element is a design feature that is not 100% appropriate for this house or as a trend in the low lying lots in the Old Village Historic District. Ms. Dickson stated that she agrees with Mr. Hirshorn’s comments, as the Commission has heard three cases this evening of drainage issues and the situation is not improving. She asked what can be done to prevent building up, which is obviously going to create runoff. She stated that the plan is very well done, but the pool is a problem. She asked about the two feet of fill dirt. Mr. Clarke stated that the two feet of fill is because the current backyard sits at 4 ½ and 5 feet and every single neighbor uses this lot as the drainage pond. He said that they are bringing the grade up in the back, which is still six feet lower than the front. He said there is a seven foot drop from the front to the back. He stated that although it appears to be a raised pool, because some of the others that face Royall Street do have pools at a raised height. He said if you went to the back of the Lutheran Church’s parking lot, you would see the raised pools and driveways, which were also what added to Ms. Woody’s problems. He stated that this lot cannot continue to just be a drainage pond. He said the County installed that storm drain at 5.08 feet and it is meant to have all the lots around it drain to it, so they must bring dirt up in the rear to get that drainage to the pipe. He said that the pool is now more integrated and gives the best example of what it can be, and will be beautiful. Mr. Keenan stated that this is a big improvement from when this began months ago. He said that his concern is the pool and his hope is that once the house is built and engineered properly that the drainage situation is going to improve, not become worse. Mr. Pohlman stated that he would like to reiterate what the Commission may conditionally approve. He said that 156.432 under powers and duties, letter F, “The design review”, which is what the Commission is currently doing, “It shall be a duty of the Commission to review applications regarding moving , demolition, new construction, exterior alteration and building additions in Historic District” and #2, “The review shall follow established criteria in accordance with approved design Old Village Historic District Commission

guidelines.” He stated that the engineered stormwater plans would be well outside both the ordinance and guidelines of the Commission. Ms. Rowe stated that this is such a unique lot. She stated that she attends the Lutheran Church and said that they do not want to be looking at a pool that is low. She said it is a unique situation to have this raised pool. She said she believes that it will look better than a lower pool, because of where the lot is situated. Ms. Dickson said that she cannot make a motion, because she cannot think of a way to do so that seems fair. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the house itself is beautiful, but it is the back decking with the elevated pool. He said that if the pool came out, it would look odd. Mr. Clarke stated that as he understood it from the last meeting, the pool situation had been solved. He stated that it was at varying heights and the Commission did not favor any of them until last month, which is what is shown. He said that he does not want to speak for Ms. Wilson; however, this was her favorite design, because it hid it. He said that this is the best from a water management standpoint. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he feels certain he spoke up against the pool last month; however, he would rather see a terraced green slope that would absorb water. He stated that it seems that a pool is being forced into a situation where it may not be possible. He said the coverage on such a lot becomes an issue. Ms. Rowe stated that Ms. Wilson provided Mr. Clarke with the guidelines regarding the pool, which he has accomplished. She stated that Mr. Clarke has addressed the drainage, so she does not know what else Mr. Clarke is able to do. Ms. Rowe made a motion to accept the application for the plans for 104 Friend Street as submitted. Motion fails due to the lack of a second. Mr. Hirshorn suggested deferring, because the issue of an elevated pool is a significant issue, because if one is accepted, there will be ten more on low lying lots. He said it would be a significant change in the streetscape. Old Village Historic District Commission

He stated that if Commission members are at an impasse, then perhaps Ms. Wilson’s architectural expertise would be helpful. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to defer 104 Friend Street; seconded by Ms. Dickson. Ms. Rowe was opposed. All others present were in favor. Motion passes 3-1. Mr. Pohlman reminded Commission members of the ex parte in the bylaws that no member is allowed to make any comments that would be perceived as a judgment outside of this Commission.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phil Clarke, Clark Design, stated that he will not go over everything again; however, the item that needed discussion was the rear deck pool area. He said he appreciated Mr. Hirshorn’s comments and studied dropping it back down and bringing it back up and what was accomplished differently from last month was the faux waterfall infinity edge and that element has been removed, so the pool is completely within the deck. He stated that he did not want to drop the pool down again, because they want to use the entire rear back yard for water absorption with the lot, directing everything towards the rear storm drain. He said from an elevation standpoint, when you are in the parking lot of the church behind the home, you will no longer see the pool, which is the main difference from last month. Ms. Rowe stated that Mr. Clarke did a great job hiding the pool and it does look like a deck porch. Ms. Wilson stated that she stood on the other side of the church looking back towards Friend Street where the finished floor of the house sits. She said that the perspective of it from the public right of way is not raised and without the infinity edge, Mr. Clarke has done everything he was asked and made the best of a very difficult lot. She stated that she is Old Village Historic District Commission

comfortable with this proposal, as Mr. Clarke has worked very well with the Commission and she appreciates his cooperation. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he is sympathetic to the position Mr. Clarke is in and said it looks much better without the infinity edge. He said that his biggest concern is the precedent of allowing raised pools in an interior lot in the historic village. He understands that based on the topography that this is a difficult circumstance; however, his issue is that it will set a precedent. He stated that for the record, he stands firmly against the addition of raised pools on interior lots in the Old Village as a standard. He added that this is an exceptional lot that is unique. Ms. Wilson stated that she also objects to them categorically, as well; however, this is one where the Commission has their rules and then realizes when they do not make sense. She said relative to the public right of way grade, being across from the church and in front of this house, it is not raised and this is a remarkably odd lot. She does not feel this sets a precedence since Commission members would be approving this as an exception. Ashley Woody, 110 Friend Street, said that she agrees that the back of the house looks better without the infinity pool; however, the pool was never her issue. Her issue is adding all the fill and why they feel it is necessary to add fill to the front yard which is already at street level. She read a letter to Commission members dated March 5, 2007, addressed to Christiane Farrell, who, at the time, was the Deputy Planning Director. She said she has been dealing with the flooding in her backyard for ten years. Ms. Wilson stated that she hears Ms. Woody’s concerns and added that the Commission’s hands are tied because they cannot implement any rules on drainage. She stated that Mr. Clarke has done a really admirable job with coming back to the Commission with reduction in coverage with a new site plan. She said that his grades/drainage are now lower than Ms. Woody’s lot, and he must bring it up in the front in order to drain to the street and not go laterally to the two side adjacent lots. She said that the Commission is extremely sympathetic and is using whatever tools available, which is the house and the hardscape and Mr. Clarke has done absolutely everything that has been requested. She stated that the Old Village Historic District Commission

Commission may ask for surveys along the way to ensure it is implemented as drawn; however, what is being presented is creating a swale between the two lots and will improve the situation from where it is now. Ms. Woody said that this is what Mr. Ilderton said he would do, as well as others and it did not improve things, but got worse. She asked what her recourse is now and where does she go from here. Ms. Wilson stated that all Ms. Woody is able to do is hold the Commission accountable to what is being approved. She said the situation that is facing Royall Avenue is a very extreme situation that no one on this present Commission had anything to do with and unfortunately do not have any purview over. She said there was 6, 8 and 10 feet of fill that went in on those lots and was a tremendous oversight that is impacting Mr. Clarke’s design as well. She said what Mr. Clarke is proposing will improve things for everyone to the best of his ability. She said beyond this, there is nothing the Commission is able to do. Ms. Woody stated that as long as that is on public record so she is able to obtain the minutes and go to someone and say that she did her best. Mr. Keenan stated that he has been dealing with drainage issues for four years and there are other areas in the Village that are going through the same issue. He said that all Ms. Woody is able to do is keep in touch with the Town. He said that Mr. Clarke is a good architect and will work with the engineers to help the drainage system, and hopefully with this house, it will be an improvement. He stated that this agenda item depicts why the Commission is here. He said that the Commission has been dealing with this proposed house for a year or more and what has been proposed as a result is 100% better than when Mr. Clark began. He said the Commission does not have control over drainage; however, what the Commission does have control over is the architectural process. He stated that he appreciates everyone’s effort and Ms. Woody’s input throughout the process and does not know what else the Commission can do. He asked Mr. Clarke to thank the homeowners for their patience and cooperation. He said for him to personally support a raised pool project by no means indicates that he is setting a precedence going forward. He stated that they are not seen; however, this being an exception with the Old Village Historic District Commission

lot, where it is placed and the topography, this was a tough decision. He added that he is a property rights person and is not here to dictate what individuals can and cannot build on their property. He stated that they have done all that is possible for this agenda item and is inclined to approve the changes. Ms. Wilson moved to approve the final design for 104 Friend Street with no changes; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

request: 104 Friend Street – n/a – Hardscaping and fencing

label: 403 Church Street
request: 403 Church Street – (HISTORIC 6200) – Final Review for After-the-Fact installation of Pergola Entry Structure

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Justin Hudd, homeowner, stated that they had some brickwork going to the front door, which is at the back of the house which was confusing to people. So they built a picket fence and other brickwork to try and help guide people to where the front door was and not the back of the house. The Commission did not like this and he was asked to remove it. He stated that they had a gap, so they put a gate up there and chose to put a trellis over the top. He showed a similar trellis also on Church Street. He showed photographs of other trellises throughout the historic district and areas just outside the district. He stated that the guidelines he reviewed did not mention anything to do with pergolas, trellises or arbors. He stated that the fence and the gate fits in with the rest of the Old Village and the trellis is similar to the other one on Church Street, so he did not think he needed to come to the Commission for permission. Mr. Keenan stated that there are thirteen letters from neighbors that have been submitted. Twelve of those letters are in support of and one is not in support. He stated that this is ex post facto and the work has already been done, but was not approved. He stated that there are some Old Village Historic District Commission

pergolas in the village and are examples of pergolas within the neighborhood. Some were built before the Commission was in existence and some were built after. He stated that he has an issue with the appearance of it as it relates to a historical home. The guidelines specifically say, “OVHDC guidelines expressly prohibit pergolas and trestles from being constructed in locations visible from public rights of way.” Mr. Keenan stated that in this case, this is very visible. Mr. Hudd stated that this is the newly updated guidelines after he put in the trellis. Mr. Keenan advised Mr. Hudd that he also did the work without consulting with the OVHDC first. He stated that he does not believe it is the right look for the house. Ms. Wilson stated that she agrees and the examples provided are pushed off the street and in heavily landscaped portions of the house. Mr. Hudd stated that the one on Church is on the street. Ms. Wilson stated that this was also erected without approval from the Commission. She stated that Mr. Hudd’s is much larger. Mr. Hudd showed several other examples of trellises up on the road. He read, “When Pitt Street was to be extended onto Shem Creek, a great arbor stood in the way and the owner defiantly refused its demolition, which is why Pitt Street was never extended and doglegs into Church Street”. He stated that even going back 150 years, the structures were in the Old Village. Ms. Wilson stated that had Mr. Hudd brought the drawings to the OVHDC, she would have suggested a change in scale and several other things. Now there is something installed that is too big and not in keeping with the style of the house. All members present agreed. Ms. Rowe stated that it is just too big. Mr. Hudd stated that his neighbors like the trellis. Ms. Rowe stated that typically if you ask a neighbor for a support letter, unless it directly impacts them, they will oblige. Mr. Pohlman stated that this is under the Commission’s purview. Mr. Hudd stated that trellises are all over the village and it was not in the guidelines at the time it was installed. Mr. Keenan stated that Mr. Hudd should have come to the OVHDC first, rather than putting it up right on the streetscape. Ms. Wilson stated that she would be open to seeing drawings for a revision or landscape that supports what it is going to look like; however, at this time, she cannot approve it. Mr. Keenan stated that it is the height being right up on the sidewalk that he is not in favor of. He stated that this is a clear deviation from what the guidelines state. He understands that it was erected prior to the guideline changes, however, Mr. Hudd did not take the proper steps to get this approved. He asked Mr. Hudd to bring something back for the Old Village Historic District Commission

Commission to review and agree on, otherwise what is there now needs to come down. Commission members agreed. Mr. Hudd stated that the neighbors like it. Mr. Keenan stated that they are more than welcome to attend the next meeting or submit an application to sit on this Commission. He stated that this Commission sets precedence which is why they are here. Mr. Hudd asked if he could take some of the existing examples throughout the Old Village. Ms. Balzac asked what the difference is between a pergola, a trellis and a garden gate. She is going to do some research on these. Mr. Hudd provided the difference between a pergola, trellis and garden gate. Mr. Keenan stated that the home that Mr. Hudd lives in is beautiful and historic and this is the primary concern, which is keeping with that historic nature. Ms. Wilson moved to defer the application for the arbor at 403 Church Street until next month’s meeting; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Justin Hudd, property owner, stated that he apologizes for doing this in the first place. He stated that he received feedback from a number of the neighbors. He stated that he looked at a number of pergolas that are taller, smaller, same width, thinner, different shapes and sizes, some with fans, some without, as well as those located on and off streets, etc. He asked his neighbors what they would do, if they could change anything about the pergola. He stated that they all agreed that they liked it just as it is. He mentioned that one thought was to eliminate the trellises down the side and possibly take the brackets at the top off to reduce the height, or change the shape. He stated that they can reduce the width or height or change the shape altogether. Louis Wright, 409 Church Street, stated that there are two empty lots between them, but he is the neighbor that looks at Mr. Hudd’s pergola every day from his breakfast nook. He has lived at this residence for three years and very appreciative of the Commission. He hopes that a project of this minor nature could be resolved, because their street has been under siege the whole time he has lived at his residence. He stated that they did some visceral changes to his home, which is an 1840’s home. He stated that Mr. Hudd’s home has had some changes, because it has a nicer porch, fence and looks like it is a part of the neighborhood, as opposed to one that is just being fenced two doors away on the other side of the street and suggests that the Commission look at that fence at some point. He stated that he has had discussions with the neighbors and they all share the same view that this pergola is reasonable and not a big issue; it is a pergola. He implored Commission members to consider approving the pergola, because the neighbors like it, as well as the Hudd family. Mr. Pohlman stated that he also received nine emails regarding this item on the agenda. He stated that eight were in favor of the pergola remaining and one was opposed. Old Village Historic District Commission

Linda Balzac’s sister (no sign in), stated that she previously lived on the corner of Pitt and Center Streets and they built a fence. She stated that there was a ten inch gap from the fence to the tree and they planted jasmine and you could not tell. She suggested roses or jasmine. Mr. Keenan stated that he does not believe anyone is offended; however, it is ex post facto and the homeowner did not go through the proper process. He stated that there is a lot of fence line, so it does break up the fence. He said that for the record, as we have revised the guidelines, pergolas are no longer allowed when they are viewed from the street. Ms. Rowe stated that it is simply too big; therefore, something needs to change in the size. Ms. Wilson stated that in one of the photographs provided by Mr. Hudd, the top rafters are much smaller at three inches. She stated instead of the regular lattice, there should be much more of a design open plant bracing which makes it more open. She does think it would be more appealing without the decorative corbeling. Mr. Wright stated that he likes the massing and it is more consistent with his big house. He stated that this is an example of change. Ms. Dickson stated that she also believes a lighter look would be more acceptable and in keeping. Ms. Wilson stated that the historic pergolas are much lighter. Mr. Hirshorn agreed with a lighter look with more landscaping. He asked what the solution would be without completely rebuilding the pergola. He stated that the fact is that the Commission has a guideline on pergolas. He stated that there were weeks of public discussions on the new guidelines and there is a specific guideline on pergolas. Mr. Hudd stated that when he built the pergola, the new guidelines were not in place. Mr. Keenan stated that the project was also not approved. Mr. Hirshorn asked if this specific pergola should be considered under the old guidelines or the new guidelines. Mr. Keenan stated that it was constructed under the old guidelines, but it was also not approved. Mr. Pohlman stated that it would be reviewed under the new guidelines. Mr. Hirshorn stated that there is a guideline that specifies that pergolas must be in the rear of the yard and not in the view of the right of way. He stated that he is going to defer to the guidelines. Mr. Wright stated that it was construction with or without approval and the fact and law is that it was done under the old guidelines, and the neighbors believe it is acceptable. He stated that the Commission must defend going by the new guidelines. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that the guidelines are very clear. He stated that during the weeks of public comment period, residents could have commented on pergolas, but no one did. He stated that the guidelines on pergolas are very specific. Mr. Hudd asked if he should take out the trellises and braces. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it would be an improvement and look less like a pergola. Ms. Wilson asked if the Commission or the Town is 100% sure that he was called in after the guidelines were approved. Mr. Pohlman stated that it is his understanding, yes. Mr. Hirshorn stated that this is very awkward, because at no point, did anyone ever comment on the guidelines during discussions. Mr. Keenan stated that he is in agreement with Mr. Hirshorn that the Commission must adhere to the guidelines. Mr. Hudd stated the pergola was constructed in mid-December and the Commission approved the guidelines on the 9th of January, 2017. Mr. Pohlman stated that at the January 9th meeting, the Commission voted to approve. Mr. Hirshorn asked for the official determination. Mr. Pohlman stated that according to management, that although it was constructed under the previous guidelines, since it never went through the guidelines review process, the new guidelines now apply since that is when the COA was applied for. Ms. Dickson stated that if the homeowner had followed the proper approval process, it would have fallen under the old guidelines; however, it must now fall under the new guidelines. Ms. Rowe stated that it would not have been approved if they had submitted it before the new guidelines, because of the historic home and the size. Mr. Hudd stated that he would ask for suggestions on changes to fit in with the comments made by the Commission about making it lighter in appearance. Ms. Wilson asked what the technical difference between an arbor and a pergola. Mr. Hudd stated that he understands that the guidelines indicate that the pergolas should not be visible for historic reasons; however he has done considerable research as mentioned previously, there is a large great arbor on the corner of Venning and Pitt Streets which is why Pitt Street was never extended which implies that these have been around for a long time. Ms. Wilson stated that this was more of a discussion when the Commission was writing the guidelines and now this Commission must decide what Old Village Historic District Commission

they are evaluating this against. She stated that she can recall one other pergola that was built without approval and asked if there is a statute of limitations. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the Commission would have to apply the same. Ms. Balzac stated that an arbor is an entranceway rather than something that is supporting a roof. Ms. Wilson stated that the definition of a pergola is that it has a roof. Ms. Wilson stated that the discussion is what the Commission’s responsibility is. Mr. Hirshorn stated that if there is a way to view this before the new guidelines and adjust it to make it more like an arbor; however, if it is the determination that this application falls under the new guidelines, then as the first trellis viewed under the new guidelines, the Commission would not be able to approve it. Ms. Wilson stated that this sets a precedence that either the Commission does not uphold their guidelines. Ms. Wilson asked who would be the one to determination that this was completed before the new guidelines. Mr. Pohlman stated that he believes it would be the Town Attorney. Ms. Wilson asked if Mr. Pohlman would send the Town Attorney an email as soon as possible for clarification. Mr. Pohlman stated that he could; however, guidelines are under the Commissions purview. Mr. Hirshorn suggested making a motion that whatever the determination of the Town Attorney is, if it falls within the old guidelines then the Commission may discuss a new design for this and ways to adjust it. If, however, it falls under the new guidelines, then it is not approved. Mr. Pohlman stated that there is too much gray area. Ms. Wilson stated that if Mr. Hudd does come back before the Commission on this item, she would be comfortable providing conceptual comment, but believes the top rafters need to come down. She stated that they are sitting up too tall. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to defer this item until the next meeting; seconded by Ms. Wilson. All present voted in favor. IV. Staff Approvals VI. Motion to Adjourn Ms. Rowe made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Ms. Wilson. Ms. Rowe withdrew her motion; Ms. Wilson withdrew her second. Ms. Wilson stated that she heard discussions that 141 Toomer Lane has significantly reduced its design, details and materials. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Juan stated that he was there today and advised them that they need approval. Mr. Hirshorn stated that there is also the one on Beach Street. Ms. Rowe made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor. There being no further business, meeting adjourned at 8:30 p.m.

Respectfully submitted, Barbara Ashe

Mr. Pohlman stated that the applicant contacted him earlier today and advised that he would not be able to attend the meeting until 6:00 p.m. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he does not have an issue with this request since it is 5:50 p.m., and if Commission members are agreeable, he would like to go to item #6 first and then address #5 thereafter. All Commission members agreed. Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Ms. Wilson asked if this item would have to be evaluated based on the current guidelines, not on the guidelines when it was constructed. Mr. Pohlman responded in the affirmative. He stated that the Town decided that the guidelines to review it are the ones that are currently in place as of now, although it was constructed prior to the adoption of the Old Village Historic District Commission

new guidelines. He stated that because a COA was not issued, it does not have any vesting right. Justin Hudd, homeowner at 403 Church Street stated that he took previous advice to take a look around the Old Village and neighboring places, as well as Sullivan’s Island for other examples of what may be similar to what he has constructed. He stated that while on Sullivan’s Island, he stated that there are some structures that are far larger than his. He showed a current picture of his pergola with the jasmine growing over it. He stated that there are many other structures throughout the Old Village, some larger, some smaller, some narrower and some wider. He stated that as mentioned earlier, precedence can be set, because it is obvious that there are many structures such as his throughout the Old Village. He stated that since they are wide-spread, he assumes that precedence has already been set. He stated that as he mentioned previously, he should have come before the Commission for approval and did not and apologies; however, there is not too much he is able to do at this time. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he agrees with Mr. Hudd that these structures are all over the Old Village; however, unfortunately, there was a movement with the last Chairman to include in the new guidelines, the prohibition of these pergolas from the view of the right of way. He stated that the guidelines went through many different iterations, meetings and public comment and with no opposition, was then added to the guidelines. He stated that unfortunately, we have these guidelines and must stand by them. He stated that this guideline is explicitly stated as being prohibited. He stated that the only recourse he could possibly recommend is if there is a way to delay this until Mr. Hudd could petition to remove this from the guideline. He stated that he has no choice but to follow the current guidelines. Mr. Hudd stated that his confusion is that the Planning Commission has been in existence for a number of years and in the past, the Commission has recommended pergola structures and sees many pergolas in the Old Village which must have received approval. He stated that why historically until now, pergolas were fine and those previously were acceptable, however, now they are not. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that it was the opinion of one of the Commission members and he suggested a revision to the guidelines to prohibit pergolas and there were several meetings and discussions with public input and it was added. Mr. Hudd stated that there are obviously many letters of support and only one or two emails opposing. Ms. Rowe stated that some of the photographs that Mr. Hudd has submitted did not receive approval from this Commission either. She stated that they began showing up all over the Old Village and some were nice and others were not. She stated that the Commission decided that they were no longer going to accept pergolas, and unfortunately, Mr. Hudd came after the guidelines changed. Ms. Wilson asked the Commission members if they are going to go back to those that built without approval. She stated that she knows of a house that she worked on that has a pergola that was not in her design; however, they put it in anyway without approval. Ms. Dickson stated that if a homeowner does in fact, put up a pergola in the time during which it was not approved, then that homeowner is in violation. She asked what recourse does the Commission have, and why do we have these guidelines if no one is going to follow them. Ms. Wilson stated that Mr. Hudd constructed it while pergolas were still allowed, just like his neighbor. Ms. Rowe stated that it was allowed, but property owners were not coming to the Commission for approval. Mr. Hirshorn said that the issue is whether the Commission should bring the neighbor in retroactively, for building a pergola without approval, and they should. Mr. Hudd stated that he has a list of pergolas that were erected that were not approved. Ms. Dickson asked why the Commission bothers to set guidelines that are being ignored. Ms. Wilson stated that she agrees, but feels that in Mr. Hudd’s case, it is slightly different. She stated that there may be an exception, because he Old Village Historic District Commission

constructed it when it was still allowed. She said that if this is the case, then the Commission must deliver ten or more letters to other residents tomorrow to take down their pergolas. She said if not, then she does not feel it is fair for one individual. Mr. Hudd stated that he went through the guidelines prior to constructing and there was no mention of pergolas, arbors, trellises. He said that now it indicates that in the historical context, these did not exist in the Old Village. Ms. Dickson stated that they did. Mr. Hudd stated that this is his issue as well. He stated that he forwarded an email to Mr. Keenan and Mr. Pohlman, because he found that the first recorded instance was listed in a historic gardening book from 1719 and has photographs of trellises all over the area and arbors. He stated that arbors, pergolas and trellises are bundled together in terms of structures. Mr. Hirshorn stated that perhaps the guideline should be refined. Mr. Pohlman stated that the guidelines may be refined at any time; however, it must have a thirty day waiting period for public comment after first being proposed for an alteration. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it appears that the guideline needs more structure. He stated that there are certain pergolas that should not be allowed and some that are historically appropriate. He suggested consideration of refining the guideline, and defer enforcing the removal of Mr. Hudd’s pergola until the Commission is able to refine the guidelines. He stated that it is obvious that these structures do exist and have some historical context. He would recommend accomplishing this in an organized, expedited fashion if this is the course of action. Mr. Hudd stated that it appears fair and his only other suggestion is that in all the guidelines, there is only one place where it says that “this was not present in a historical context” just happens to be a pergola. He suggested removing the word “historical”. Ms. Dickson stated that the language needs to be changed, because it is obviously not correct. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Pohlman stated that the Commission would be required to draft the wording of the guidelines and use input from elsewhere, but it must be stated on record by the Commission and voted on by the Commission after a thirty day review period before the public. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it would be appropriate to accomplish this in an architecturally accurate way. He stated that there are some pergolas that are not appropriate and some that are and many in between. He asked if it were possible to have this drafted in a much more professional way for the next meeting. Ms. Wilson stated that it is. Ms. Rowe asked Ms. Wilson if she has seen language regarding pergolas in historic neighborhoods. Ms. Wilson stated that there has been discussion that there is more new construction than historic, so it does not necessarily need to be steeped in the historic accurate pergola, because the Commission would likely not allow another property owner to do this to a historic house. She said that it is simply gaining back control of when and if a pergola is appropriate. Ms. Rowe stated that we are then back to where we began, because Mr. Hudd’s home is historic. Ms. Wilson stated that it would still be within the Commission’s purview to allow it, but would be recommending against it in the guidelines. She stated that the Commission is able to make exceptions to their own guidelines without setting precedent. She stated that it has been done. Mr. Pohlman stated that this is correct, as the Commission may approve something that goes contrary to their own guidelines as long as the reason is stated, which is the same if a denial is done. Ms. Wilson asked if the Commission is allowed to discuss via email prior to the next meeting or must the discussions take place in a public forum. Mr. Pohlman stated that it should be done in a public forum. Mr. Hirshorn stated that language referring to height and scale. He stated that there are pergolas that are more in context of what the Commission is attempting to avoid. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Pohlman stated that if the Commission is considering altering this guideline, that they state a definition into the guidelines as to the definition of a trellis, arbor, pergola or a decorative entryway. He stated that there needs to be specific wording. Ms. Wilson stated that the Commission could use the word “pergola” and then have a footnote that states that “this refers to any and all gate/entry/archway to include any type of entryway structure. Mr. Pohlman stated that he would recommend the Commission having the language, because there is a definition section within the guidelines that is meant to be referenced by any architectural term to ensure that what is stated is firm. Ms. Rowe asked if Mr. Hudd’s structure could be referred to as a trellis and approve it, and then refine the language. Mr. Hirshorn stated that alternatively to redrafting a new guideline, what could be done is to keep the new guideline that states no pergolas and allow exceptions by the Commission when warranted. Ms. Dickson stated that the language that states “this was not present in a historical context” needs to be removed, because it is incorrect. Ms. Rowe stated that Mr. Hudd’s structure could be defined as a trellis, which would be one with plants growing up. Mr. Hirshorn stated that what he thought the spirit of the guideline was more in the context of the pergola which is similar to the large structure you sit underneath with the heaters and fans. He stated that he was not envisioning that it was going to be referring to an entry gate type structures. Ms. Rowe stated that this is where she believes the Commission got off track. Mr. Pohlman stated that the Commission may approve, with the variation from the guidelines stating that this is acceptable due to (state the reasoning). He stated that the Commission may then revisit the guideline without this being deferred. Ms. Wilson stated that she is fine with defining this as a trellis. Old Village Historic District Commission

Commission members agreed. Ms. Wilson made a motion to define the entry structure at 403 Church Street as a trellis and therefore allow it as an exception to the Commission’s guidelines and consider it approved; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor. Ms. Rowe stated that she believes that a pergola is more of a large structure. Ms. Dickson stated that the terms overlap. Ms. Wilson suggested revisiting and do some redefining. Mr. Pohlman stated that he and Mr. Juan can provide industry standard definitions for the Commission to review at the next meeting and also consider language in order to refine this guideline. He stated that what the Commission views as acceptable in the context of the Old Village will be allowed and those unacceptable would be prohibited. Ms. Rowe suggested setting up a sub-committee to review. Mr. Pohlman recommended that either at the beginning of the agenda or after all agenda items have been addressed, to review and discuss.

request: 403 Church Street- Applicant is seeking final approval new accessory structure (pool)

events.text:
