Mr. Brennan Egan, Archipelago Pools, 222 West Coleman Boulevard, builder, reviewed the request with the Commission.

There being no comments, Ms. Montgomery moved to Commission questions.

Mr. Crosland moved to approve with a conditional on meeting fence guidelines. Ms. Montgomery seconded the motion. All in favor.

label: 739 Pitt Street
request: 739 Pitt Street—(Survey 5907) – Final Review for Alterations to Approved Plans and Approved Accessory Dwelling Unit [Consent Motion Approval]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Jason Fowler, Sea Island Builders, representing Debbie Stocker, property owner. He stated that they began working with the property owner last summer. They evaluated the options early on at 739 Pitt Street as to what could or could not be done with the existing non historic home. The property is subject to a 50% FEMA compliant rule, so they were limited in their design options. He stated that this is a modest renovation, primarily on the inside of the house. The biggest addition that affects the front façade of the home with a front porch, which is approximately ten feet deep and nineteen feet wide, along with a nine foot wide dormer on the front of the house. He stated that he would like to address the existing house first and move on to the ADU. He illustrated the proposed new front porch where there is a small existing porch currently. He stated there is currently a rear deck and they will be bringing the driveway down on the side of the house, demolishing a portion of the existing rear deck. The property line is the edge of the neighbor’s driveway. He stated that these two lots were owned by the same person at one time, so he was not concerned how close he was to the neighbor’s house. He showed the existing front elevation of the house and the glassed in porch which they would like to demolish, add a nine foot dormer and then a porch with a gable. He stated that for the ADU, they attempted a design that is harmonious with the district in terms of the design of the dormers. This is all per the new January 9th passed guidelines. The dormers are four foot wide. They walked Pitt Street and attempted to take in the design elements which they took into consideration for their design. In terms of a massing standpoint, it is obscured from view from the street. He asked Old Village Historic District Commission

for the input on the design of the ADU. He stated that they are working with several large oaks on the property and will be re-siting the ADU to the other corner in order to avoid any damage to the oaks. It is even more obscured from view, but leaves a little less backyard for the homeowner, but are trying to do what is in the best interest of the oak trees. Ms. Wilson asked Mr. Fowler if he or the homeowners have discussed this with the neighbors to the rear, because it is tight in the back. Mr. Fowler stated that he believes that the homeowner has as she has made a concerted effort to discuss the plans with surrounding neighbors. He stated that the neighbors to the rear have a garage which will back up to the ADU. Ms. Wilson asked if it is due to the turning radius of the apron that makes the drive right up on the house and leaving that fifteen feet between the two drives. Mr. Fowler said that it is to stay clear of the oak trees. Ms. Wilson stated that she is referring to the long stretch of the drive. Mr. Fowler stated that they can shift the driveway and create more space. Mr. Juan asked if the entire lot is in a flood zone. Mr. Fowler said that it is an AE12. Mr. Juan stated that the ground floor would need to be redesigned. Being that it is an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) you must treat it as if it were an elevated building in a flood zone and with that, it must be supported with piles/piers, open foundation, not enclosed. Mr. Fowler stated that it is designed as a garage with flood vents. Mr. Juan stated that solid walls are not allowed. It must be supported with piers and 40% open louvers in between each pier support. It is an elevated home in a flood hazard zone. Linda Balzac, stated that the main house is shorter than the ADU by several feet and there has been discussion on the Commission about reducing the height of the structures because it clearly looks like a house behind another house. The height, scale and mass of the ADU is too big. She stated that if the house in the front were much larger, the ADU would not look so large. Mr. Fowler stated that the main house measures twenty-one and a half feet from grade to the top of the ridge which is not very tall and was not built to the current flood code. The ADU is built just below the twenty- five foot threshold and the height is not visible just because it is slightly higher. He does not believe it creates a lot of mass. Ms. Balzac stated that it is visible, because she used to live up the street for a long time. It is visible between the two brick houses that are there now. She stated that what is proposed for the main house is great, because you kept the house and the scale is really nice. It is a one and a half story structure and the structure behind it looks like a two and a half story structure. Mr. Fowler stated that it will not be sited where it is showing now, so when they come back, they will have a new rendering. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Balzac stated that the ADU should be subservient to the main structure. Scott Broadmell, 728 Pitt Street, stated that he lives directly across the street and was concerned about parking. He asked if an ADU can be rented separately and where would the homeowners of the main house park? Ms. Wilson stated that the property owners’ site planning review must show that both units have parking accessible without interrupting the other, which they are not showing at this time. She stated that they need to discuss with the Planning Commission, because parking is an issue, especially for ADU’s. Ms. Balzac stated that she believes that the ADU is very attractive and well designed, just too big for the main house. Mr. Keenan stated that what has been done with the front house is well done and applauds that the homeowner is keeping the house. He stated that his comments are consistent with Ms. Balzac’s that it is way too big and looks like a second house is being built on the lot. He stated that they are in the process of revising the guidelines; however, much of the focus is on ADU’s and bringing the height down. Mr. Pohlman stated that it would be twenty feet for ADU’s and up to twenty feet for accessory structures. Mr. Keenan stated that it is tight in the back and cannot imagine that any of the neighbors to the rear would be in support of this ADU, although they do not base their decisions on this. He stated that it is entirely too big for the project and the parking is also an issue. They would prefer that parking is to the rear. He stated that the ADU is too high and too big. Mr. Fowler stated that it is 680 feet heated and used the 750 square feet footprint allowed for the garage and porch. Mr. Keenan stated that the height, scale and mass is entirely too big for the lot. Ms. Wilson stated that this block does not have full two-story homes, so a full two-story on an ADU is big. She stated that the ADU could easily have clipped vaulted ceilings and bring down the top plate height for the ADU portion. It might also be worth rotating it, especially if you are moving it to that back corner because they are not showing any back out, because now you can back out of the garage and driveway, which is not going to be easy the way it is drawn. If you rotate it, you could pull in and back out to come out. She stated that the driveway needs to come off of the house, because to see the concrete butt up against the foundation of the house is too tight. Ms. Rowe stated that it looks massive. She stated that the ADU looks larger than the original house. There are too many dormers, and if the roof could be dropped down. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Pohlman stated that in reference to parking, given that it is a two car garage, this would actually meet the parking requirements. The ADU requirements only stated that these dedicated spots for the ADU cannot be in tandem with the primary parking spot. So they cannot be side by side. Ms. Wilson stated that the house parking pad must be bigger so that they are actually accommodating the ADU. Mr. Pohlman stated that only one space for each is required. Mr. Keenan stated that this is what they are changing in the guidelines now, because they are trying to get vehicles off of Pitt Street. He stated that they would love to see as much parking as possible to the rear of the home. He stated that this is part of the new revised guidelines. Ms. Wilson stated that it is not realistic. Mr. Fowler stated that he would address this. What he would like to offer for consideration, but the main house may or may not always be there and is not historic at this time. He would like for the Commission to keep this in mind from a massing standpoint. The main house is 1,300 square feet and anything built to code is going to be elevated; therefore, if a new structure was put on this lot, it will be more massive than the existing home. Mr. Keenan stated that is an unfair comment that they cannot base their decision upon. Ms. Wilson stated that even if the main house was a two story, she would argue that it is too big. Mr. Keenan stated that since he has been on this Commission, there have been ADU’s built that turned out to be not what the drawings depicted or they were larger. He asked the designer to review the proposed guidelines which are accessible online, when considering a redraw for the ADU. Mr. Fowler asked for guidance, as they currently meet the height, footprint and heated area requirements of the guidelines. Mr. Keenan stated that it is too tall and there are too many windows. Ms. Rowe stated that they also need to redesign with the piers. Ms. Wilson stated that the design will change when the ADU is put on piers. She stated that the third story dormers are too much and makes it look like a three-story house. She stated that rotating it may help because from the street, what you would see in conjunction with the house is the gable and you do not see a massive structure. She stated that it is all bundled together, but she would be happy to approve the front porch and the plan for the existing house. Mr. Pohlman stated that it is all conceptual, including the main house. Supplemental Animation Old Village Historic District Commission

90% so that it is narrower from the front and re-sited it on the site so there are large oaks that shield any view looking down the side of the property. He presented a 3-D rendering. He stated that they previously had the roof height at 25 feet and have since decreased Old Village Historic District Commission

that to 21 feet, 8 inches which matches the primary structure. In doing this, they reduced the plate height in the 2nd story space to 6 foot 4 inches. Around the perimeter of the room when you are upstairs in the building, the ceiling height is 6 foot 4 inches and they are going to do a vaulted ceiling up from there, but that is as low as they were able to make this and have it still function as a nice living space. Where there are dormers, it vaults up to 8 feet 9 inches and the dormers are to fit in windows. If you look at the elevation of the ADU, to get in these windows which are only 4 feet 8 inches tall, there dormers must be there or there will not be enough room on the wall face. He stated that the scale, mass and height was decreased considerably and the volume of this building was decreased approximately 25% from the original proposal. Mr. Keenan asked for the total square footage on the structure now. Mr. Fowler stated that it is 750 square feet which is allowable and the same on the heated, which is 748 feet which is just under the allowable. Mr. Dickson stated that on the illustration, it appears that it is partially timber. Mr. Fowler stated that it is board and batten. Debbie Stocker, homeowner, stated that she originally purchased the house and wanted to be able to make it handicap accessible, so she could move her mother, who is 89 years old and has Parkinson’s. She wanted something that would work for both of them and also wanted a garage. She said that it was recommended to build a detached garage. She said that she did not want to tear the house down to build something better, but wanted a cottage house. She stated that the two car garage and apartment allows her to keep the cottage house the way it is, with exception of adding a porch. She stated that she did submit packages to her surrounding neighbors and has letters of support. She stated that one of the neighbors, Jim Lee, is here in support of the project. She stated that they have attempted to keep it low profile with lots of grass. She stated that she would like to do the driveway utilizing gravel and not concrete or asphalt. She stated that she would like to make this her home. Ms. Wilson stated that she has a request on the board and batten detail on the primary residence. She stated that a 2 inch batten of the hardie is not a classic board and batten detail. She suggested reducing to 1 or1 ¼ inches. She stated that is her only objection to the main house. She stated for the ADU, she appreciates that they lowered the roof, but still concerned with the massing. She stated that there is a lot going on for such a small building with all the dormers, it does not quite go with the existing house. She stated that it appears like another structure that it tacked on and overwhelms the back. She suggested simplifying some of the dormers. She stated Old Village Historic District Commission

they have done the fig gable on the front with the porch and the triple shed and this is a different vocabulary and they should be more harmonious together since they are part of the one piece of property which do not seem to relate. Mr. Fowler stated that they are not allowed wider than a 4 foot dormer on the ADU, as per the revised guidelines. He asked if the suggestion is to make small dormers on the main house. Ms. Wilson stated that not necessarily, because it limits the footprint and the front house looks good. She stated for the ADU, perhaps two twin dormers. She stated that there are 10 dormers on a small structure. She asked if the stairs were enclosed. Mr. Fowler responded in the affirmative and stated that it is not heated space. He stated that the windows are 4 feet 8 inches tall which is not a tall window and wants to have a space that is light and bright and airy inside. He stated that this was a big design constraint when working with this, because they also have to meet egress in one of the bedroom windows and can only go to a certain size to achieve this. Ms. Rowe stated that she agrees with Ms. Wilson, because if she drove by, she would assume someone built in the back separate from the front. It does not look like the same property. Mr. Fowler asked if this was due to the exterior façade. Ms. Rowe stated that there is the cottage look in the front which looks great, but then the ADU in the back does not match. Ms. Wilson stated that it may just be the four dormers which is really busy. She suggested two twin dormers. She stated on the side elevation, nothing aligns the right side elevation which arguably is the one you see from the street. Ms. Dickson suggested a brick façade which may tie it in. Mr. Fowler stated that the challenge is that the bottom floor (garage) has to be designed as break away walls, as per the Town ordinance, so they cannot use brick. Ms. Dickson asked about the 2nd floor space. Mr. Fowler stated that with this type of structure, it would be a challenge. Jim Lee, stated that no one seems to have looked at the rear view of the home. He stated that the dormer in the back is cedar siding which ties in more to the ADU. He stated that there are some symmetrical looks. Mr. Keenan stated that ADU’s have been a big controversy for many years. He stated that the guidelines have recently been revised. He stated that the purpose of an ADU is supposed to be significantly smaller than the house. On this particular property, it looks as Old Village Historic District Commission

though there are two houses; therefore, he is concerned with the size. He added that he appreciates the effort Mr. Fowler went through; however, the shed is even noticeable from the street and it is only 8 feet tall. He stated that it is a very prominent lot on Pitt Street and is concerned with the mass and scale of it to be an ADU. He does like that the ADU has been turned; however is concerned about the overall size. Mr. Fowler stated that this would be the side that is seen from the streetscape, which is written on page 4 of the guidelines. He stated that when you look at this from the street, what you see is 5% of the building. Ms. Wilson suggested that Mr. Fowler study that elevation look, because it is arguably the least organized elevation of the plan. None of the windows line up, the gable does not relate to the gable of the main house in terms of pitch. There are three different building materials, the porch column is odd in terms of where everything else is going, and the piers. She stated that there is a lot going on in that elevation. She suggested that two larger shed dormers would simplify the elevations and provide better space inside, and to pick up on some of the pitches of the existing structure and the materials. She stated that it does not need to be brick, but possibly lap siding and simplifying. Jim Lee, stated that he does not believe that anyone has given any consideration to the view from Middle Street. He stated that this is very near Alhambra Hall and when you look at the house from Middle Street, everything ties in. If you look at it from Pitt Street, it is different. He stated that in all fairness, both views should be given equal value. Ms. Wilson stated that she agrees and said that the Middle Street view is much more simplified and does not think that the gable needs a different material if you are attempting to tone it down, but that is a simple gable structure and has a more favorable elevation from Middle Street, which is the direction Mr. Fowler should move towards. Ms. Stocker asked if Ms. Wilson is suggesting double gables and thought that they were limited to the width of the gables that they could have on the ADU. Ms. Wilson stated that this is a guideline so the Commission is able to work with the homeowner on. She stated that the house has a steeper pitch to the gable and does have shed dormers. She suggested looking more to the language of the house that currently exists and use this instead of coming up with a whole new style for the ADU. She stated that in this case, having a shed dormer on one side would be appropriate and go with the house, providing better space. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Fowler stated that he agrees and originally had something similar. Ms. Stocker stated that they had larger dormers and were told they were too big. Ms. Wilson stated the last time they appeared before the Commission, there were four dormers. She stated that she would like to see the house and ADU come together. She stated that what she believes the Commission is trying to avoid is where there are two rakes and huge shed dormers on either side. If they are done tastefully and using scale and proportions of the house that is there. She stated that what is being proposed on the main house is great. Ms. Rowe stated that her issue is the size of the ADU compared to the size of the original home. She stated that no matter what is done about the size of the dormers, there is still a big ADU compared to the original home. Mr. Fowler stated that you will not see it from the street. Ms. Rowe and Ms. Wilson stated that it will be seen from the street. Ms. Wilson stated that the way it was rotated helps and if you think about a house that is three times the size of this ADU, which they could build, and think about the massing of how that whole house would be, if the two forms relate better together, it is like one house has been broken apart. She stated that this would be so much better. She stated that it looks like another lot in the back. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he agrees with the comments that have been made. He stated that either the scale of the proposed ADU needs to be reduced, or it needs to tie in more to the house. He stated that a choice has to be made, because currently, it violates both of those guidelines. He stated that this can be accomplished. Ms. Wilson moved to approve the main house renovation at 739 Pitt Street and defer the ADU design for a future meeting; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor. (Ms. Dickson stepped out at 6:09 p.m.)

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Anita King, Swallowtail Architecture, representing Sea Island Builders and the property owner, stated that Jason Fowler presented in the past; however, he is on his honeymoon. She stated that based on the feedback regarding the size of the ADU, as well as the location, they will be keeping the existing screened in porch, update the column trim, but keep the massing the same as it is currently so that it does not feel smaller. She stated that they proposed to put the ADU in the left corner and do a plantation mix driveway in order to save the tree roots. She stated that they have consulted with Town Arborist, Eddie Bernard, on how to Old Village Historic District Commission

accomplish this and to remove the tree in the new proposed plantation mix driveway. She stated that in order to mitigate the height further, they have done a sloping parking court to come down one foot so that the garage doors are actually one foot below the existing grade, which they would drain appropriately and then step back up into the ADU, in order to accomplish the twenty-one feet eight inches. She stated that on the existing house, which was primarily approved previously, most of the comments were related to how the ADU and the main house addressed each other. She stated that they will put an additional porch and dormer. She stated that now the ADU has a matching gable end along with brackets detailing, roof slope and another dormer to relate back to the main house. She stated that they also coordinated the roof slopes and the materials with brick at the base, but also have siding elements and board and batten elements which they will tie together in the design. She stated that they also lowered the plate height. She stated that the height was an issue previously. She stated that it was at 6 feet 4 inches originally and it has since been lowered to 4 feet 8 inches to get the necessary room which is the lowest they could bring it back. She stated that another item they were attempting to keep that is sensitive to the house is they have kept it in the building setbacks in the rear. She stated that they did use the accessory setback on the side in order to have enough room to turn around and stayed away from the trees. She said everything is outside of the tree canopies with the exception of the plantation mix driveway. Ms. Wilson asked if the 31 inch live oak did receive approval for removal. Ms. King responded in the affirmative. Ms. Stocker (homeowner), stated that she is require to replace it with equal number of trees to match the 31 inches and stated that she will plant throughout the property once she has the landscape plan. She has consulted with a landscape architect. Mr. Joe Juan asked for an explanation of the one foot drop in the slab. He asked about the building height. Ms. King stated that this was to achieve the 21 feet 8 inches. She stated that because of the height of the garage and the livable space above, they needed an extra foot so they were trying to bring it down as low as possible. She stated that the plantation mix comes in and slopes and there is pervious brick and would tier back up to come to the front door so they will not have a flooding issue at the door. She stated that they would have a French drain so they will not have an issue drainage-wise. Mr. Juan asked if the enclosure on the left is the entry into the garage. Ms. Kings stated that it would step up slightly. Mr. Juan stated that when referring to the height, what is this referring to. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. King stated that the height is from the existing grade that is going to be maintained on the outside. She said that it is 21 feet 8 inches from the grade. Ms. Wilson asked if she gathered that from the primary residence. Ms. Stocker stated that she bought the house in December and advised the architects and the builder that she did not want to be in a hurry and do what is necessary in keeping with the neighborhood. She stated that it has been a process and believes this is the fourth time before the Commission. She stated that it is a significant expense to her in order to lower the grade so that the unit upstairs is livable. She stated that her mother is disabled and will live with her in the main house and her plan was to have the caregiver stay in the ADU, because her mother must have 24/7 care. She stated that lowering the grade is very expensive, but wanted to ensure it is compliant with what the Commission requested. She stated that another thing that was a consideration when she purchased the property was to get the parking off the road. This home does not have any parking. She would also like that they not be visible, which is why she is requesting a two car garage; one for her vehicle and one for the caregiver. Mr. Juan stated that the property is at grade at the front of the building and thought the building height was being maximized. He stated that his concern is the water going back into the building. Ms. Stocker stated that when she purchased the property, the ADU was an important component for her in order to make this work. Ms. Wilson stated that this is significant improvement and likes that the gable of the garage corresponds with gable on the house, as it now looks like one piece of property. She stated that she is agreeable with the extended shed dormer and may trim the closed shutter on the back to make it more consistent. She stated on the front porch gable is 19 feet wide and garage is 22 feet wide, so there is still a condition where the garage gable façade is bigger than the primary residence. She said it would be great if there were a way to shrink that gable and increase the porch gable on the main house. She stated that she realizes that there is a chimney to work against. She stated that she is conflicted, because she would hate to see a tree cut down, but as an architecture, believe it was a great idea that the driveway was shifted and does a lot of nice things for the rest of the property. She stated that she wonders why the homeowner would like to keep the shed as opposed to pushing the ADU further back and incorporating some storage on the back of the ADU and not have two buildings pressed up side by side. Ms. Stocker stated that it will be done in stages. She stated that the reason she asked to leave the shed, because she is going to need it until the ADU is built, because the house does not have storage; no laundry or utility room. She said the shed is an important storage component. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan stated that he would echo Ms. Wilson’s comments on the gable being larger than the house. He stated that there have been significant improvements from four meetings ago. He stated that the ADU’s have gotten out of hand recently which is why the guidelines have been revised. Ms. King stated that it will be difficult on the garage to bring it in much further and still have the size garage doors and structure needed. She stated that it is possible to enlarge it on the primary residence. Ms. Wilson stated that they typically do not care for one the garage door, but in this case, it is hidden in the louvers; therefore, a single car garage door would be so much better and easier to turn in and out. She stated that it is not infringing on the garage space, but would allow the two outer columns to come in and shrink the gable and make the porch a little bigger. She stated that she is not sure how the other Commission members feel, but she would rather make an exception and give a few inches, rather than make the pit for the garage. She stated that it sounds like a bad idea. Ms. Keenan asked if Ms. Wilson is suggesting giving them the height. Ms. Wilson stated that the homeowner can get a rollup garage door at seven feet six inches, so she is not sure if the eight feet is really critical for the garage headroom, but if the homeowner is agreeable with a lower garage height, there may be a compromise, rather than going below grade with a French drain system. Ms. Stocker stated that if she can get the height without having to scoop down and put in a drainage system, this would save her a $15,000 to $20,000 expense. She stated that she would like to get this approved before ADU’s are possibly banned. She stated that she has been renting a house since December and would like to do this right. Ms. Rowe stated that she agrees that it would be better if the homeowners did not have to dig below the grade. She also agrees that the gable needs to be smaller. Ms. Wilson stated that if there is a sixteen foot wide single garage door, it would be easier to get two vehicles in and out of, but would allow to bring in the column details. Ms. Stocker stated that if she is able to get approved today and this is the condition, she will comply. Ms. Dickson asked if the ceiling of the garage is going to be brought down. Ms. Wilson stated that Ms. Stocker can get a rollup garage door at 7 feet 6 inches or 7 feet 8 inches. Ms. Dickson stated that this will bring the whole roofline down which will be much more attractive. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that in this case, she is suggesting that Ms. Stocker lift her garage floor, but lower the ceiling height in the garage, which would keep the height alignment, so the slab is not a foot below grade. Ms. Dickson asked what the height of the ceiling in the ADU was. Ms. Stocker stated that the living area is at seven feet. Ms. Wilson stated that she is taking the height out of the garage ceiling height, not the living space upstairs. Ms. Stocker stated that she is not an architect, but if it is possible to do this, she would be agreeable. Ms. Hirshorn agrees with raising the garage flooring back up to grade, lowering the height of the garage ceiling, increase the size of the gable so that it appears to be smaller. Ms. Wilson stated that the porch could be a little bigger so that the gable tip of the garage. Ms. Dickson asked how this can be accomplished with so many contingencies. Ms. Wilson stated that in order to do this verbally, she is going to state the motion aggressively and hopes it can be accomplished; however, if it cannot be accomplished, it will need to come back before the Commission. She stated that for her to be comfortable, the gable on the garage needs to actually be smaller. She stated that there would be a single-double garage door so it opens together, but two cars may fit inside; therefore, the outside width of that piece is nineteen feet. She stated that you are basically reversing the dimensions. She said the garage door is hidden by louvers. She stated that the porch increases by two or three feet. She stated that having the slab below grade is only her suggestion; however, if they would prefer to put in the French drain system, that is their preference. She stated that personally for her, she would take it out of her ceiling height. Mr. Juan asked for the overall square footage of the entry area. Ms. King stated that it is only one hundred and fifty. Mr. Keenan asked if this is something the Commission members feel comfortable making a motion on and have the drawing approved at staff level. Mr. Pohlman stated that Commission members would have to provide detailed instructions in order to be approved at staff level. He stated that he would have to comply with conditions imposed on the project. Mr. Keenan stated that he feels it is a large enough change that the Commission would need to see another drawing, through Mr. Pohlman. Ms. Rowe asked if this is doable. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. King stated that instead of taking it out of the ceiling height, would love to just have the grade pushed up. Ms. Wilson stated that for the Commission, the ridges need to align, and the ADU cannot be talker than the primary residence. Ms. Wilson moved to approve 739 Pitt Street under three conditions: (1) the ridges remain the same or the ADU is lower; (2) that the porch gable is four feet wider than the garage gable, and they could go to a single garage door; (3) that the floor frieze board is continuous all the way around to make that consistent, which is the same shown on the right side elevation illustration; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

label: 728 Pitt Street
request: 728 Pitt Street – Historic 5956 – Applicant is seeking Final Review for After-the-Fact revisions to a Historic single-family home

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Scott Broadwell, property owner of 728 Pitt Street stated that they came before the Commission prior and the last time was in November, 2016 and received excellent feedback. He stated that the design by itself may have been a big design, but not felt to be appropriate for the property. He said from the minutes, there were four main points that the Commission had provided for them to work on. One was the existing façade was a craftsman style and was felt that this should be preserved at all costs, so their new design addressed this. Secondly, it was thought to be too big, so it has been scaled down. Third, it was too tall, so there is a one and a half story addition in the back which was brought down from two stories. Last, the setback of the house. He said that the current setback is very generous at forty-two feet and was felt to be historic and important to maintain the jigsaw pattern of the streetscape. He stated that they wanted to incorporate all of this and come up with a design plan that may be more in keeping with what the Commission would like to see. He stated that he feels the new design is a very workable design from a family standpoint, it is something he is pleased with. He stated that he is not a professional, but did learn the CAD program, spent a great deal of time and came up with a design that he hopes to receive positive feedback on. He showed the existing house with the carport off to the side that faces the Wilson’s property. He stated that he proposes to enclose a portion of the porch and the carport, maintaining the tapered column in the front and the overall dominant gable, and also with this addition, the porch roof going around the side. They really wanted to maintain that structure. He indicated where there is a magnolia tree that they are attempting to preserve. He stated that the original house was a fisherman’s cottage and has gone through several evolutions and is what they believe is in the fourth evolution. They are proposing to receive approval to do the fifth. He stated that the most recent structure was on the back of the house, which is a laundry room which is not heated. As far as the overall structure, they would like to preserve all of it, with the exception of the laundry room which would come off with the new design. He stated that the front porch is poured concrete and the railing is two by four and the ceiling is plywood and the tapered are made out of plywood, obviously not historic materials. They would like to bring this all up to historically appropriate materials. He had forensic work done on the roof and the existing structure is quite deficient, all the rafters have been cut and was not tied together very well with the existing structure. He stated that in their renovation work, they would like to properly address the roof structure which is a very important part of preserving the structure long term. He stated that a great deal of the construction work was subpar and rampant with poor workmanship throughout. They would like to bring this up to code and help maintain the structure long term as the home is 100 years old now. He stated that it is fifty-one feet to the Old Village Historic District Commission

main structure and forty-two feet to the existing porch, which would not change. He stated that there is approximately six feet, eleven inches on the side next to the Wilson’s and that setback would be maintained. He stated that they will move in a little on the Duke’s side, but well within the requirements in the guidelines. He showed where Don Bailey resides and where his son resides on the property in the back and they wanted to maintain the site line, so they did not want to cloud that side of the structure, so they will maintain a generous setback on that side so they maintain a site line to Pitt Street. He illustrated the existing and proposed site plan. He stated that the numbers are well within their allowances. He stated that there is a porch on the side of the house that is not covered and is unsure whether that is considered pervious or impervious. They would add a master off of the back, nice covered porch in the back and prefer to open it up in the interior to make it more of a modern layout. It would go from a two bedroom to a three bedroom house. In the front he did redesign it because of the four foot dormer requirement. At the very end, he shows more of a traditional shed dormer for a craftsman house that he prefers, but wanted to show both to receive feedback from the Commission. Any addition on this house is going to trigger FEMA. It is going to be elevated and would point out that the FEMA guidelines are not just to protect insurance companies and the government, but it is potentially to protect the homes from damage. Elevating the home could potentially help to preserve it long term. He stated that the structure would stand approximately twenty-six feet tall and the chimney to code would be two feet taller at twenty-eight feet. He stated that he is not showing railings, but any further rendition would show that detail. He stated that they would like to establish a direction, since their previous efforts were not in keeping with what the Commission felt was a good direction. Ms. Wilson asked where the existing porch ends. Mr. Broadmell stated that you can see where it ends underneath so there would be a little bit of an extension and they did enclose a portion so they wanted to extend it out a little bit to create more balance. He also felt that by adding the little addition off the side, they considered doing a slightly different material so that it looks like an addition and not part of the original structure, but thought extending the porch onto the side would create a more balanced look and be more functional. Mr. Juan asked what the roof material is on the low slope shed dormers and on the left side. Mr. Broadmell stated that it is presented as asphalt shingle, which is what the existing is. He said they could do a separate roof material. Mr. Juan stated that it would have to be, because asphalt shingles will not work on the low pitch and in fact is not allowed. Mr. Broadmell stated that it would possibly be a metal, separate from the original structure. Donald Bale, 724 Pitt Street, asked how high the bottom area is. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Broadmell stated that they are shown at five feet and the lowest grade is 7.2 feet so it would need to be six inches taller than that. Ms. Wilson stated that seven is the lowest point at the rear and in the front you are higher, so it will not seem like it is six feet up. Mr. Broadmell stated that all of the lots there slope from east to west and there is a drainage on the other side of the Duke’s. It is seven feet on one side and nine feet four inches on the other. Ms. Rowe stated that the front elevation has too much going on with a long rectangular window, the windows on the right side that are higher than those on the porch. Ms. Wilson stated that he has the detail like it is part of the porch. Mr. Broadmell stated that it is an enclosed porch, but if you want a more uniformed look. Ms. Wilson stated that he does not have any handrails drawn, but when he does it will start to knit it together, because what he is doing is keeping the look of the porch. Mr. Keenan asked if there is any reason why the wood siding wasn’t extended across. Mr. Broadmell stated that the design has a little bit more of a look of an enclosed structure that was previously open so that it why it was designed that way – almost like a sunroom. He stated that they are enclosing part of the porch and the carport, so they wanted to create that feel, similar to a sunroom. However, if the Commission would like a more uniform front, he will make those changes. Nicholas Popovich, 209 Greenwich Street, stated that one clarification is that from detective work that Mr. Broadmell has undertaken, it shows and evolution of the original structure and that evolution is to continue without masking and turning their backs to what is the history of the house. He is actually attempting to continue the history by showing that there was a porch there, and with many historic structures, to gain living space, those porches have been enclosed and they have not been enclosed to make it look as though they were that way originally. Ms. Wilson stated that she likes the idea of closing in the carport and resolves a lot for the new homeowners. She likes the scale of what is being done on the other side and at the rear. The only thing she struggles with is when you typically enclose porches it is more of one third/two third as opposed to half and half so that one bay to the right of center, and it might benefit from being more open or perhaps it is going back to the original column locations of the porch and doing it slightly more substantial where you have the one shed piece popping out, instead of rebuilding. Keeping the original porch so the addition in fact becomes bigger and the original porch stays more proportionally as it is. But the additional all the way on the left stays. It ties in more in the same way the carport does. Keeping the porch more than half open, make it larger and Old Village Historic District Commission

open that one bay or whether you go back to the original size and do more of an addition on the side. Mr. Broadmell said that he struggled with this and the porch, ideally, would be taken out to the edge; however, the magnolia tree is in that spot. Ms. Wilson stated that she does not have an issue with the shed dormers. Mr. Keenan stated that Mr. Broadmell has a hard assignment and appreciates the efforts. He stated that the streetscape is really important to get right on this house, because it is a historic house. He stated that he is fine with enclosing the carport, but would appreciate a more aesthetically pleasing view from this elevation. Mr. Broadmell stated that he was hoping to get some idea and there is still a lot more work to do. If the overall idea is to maintain the front and simplify it and clean it up, but are getting some traction, he will turn it over to a real professional. Mr. Popovich stated that the omission of the railing certainly effects the façade and perhaps instead of a molding detail under the windows in the enclosed area, if it were embedded railing perhaps to have more continuity and simplify the effect, that may be a route that Mr. Broadmell takes as well. Ms. Rowe stated that the upper window with the eight panes. She stated that the cottage look, but the big expanse of the rectangular window look out of sync. Definitely a window there, but not so big. Mr. Broadmell asked if the one and a half story addition is acceptable. Also the shed style dormer. Commission members agreed. Ms. Wilson stated that it will provide better headroom and she actually likes it for the front as well. Mr. Broadmell stated that he will rework the front, but the overall direction is more appropriate. Mr. Keenan stated that they are going in the right direction and the Commission would like to work with him, but it is a unique structure. Conceptually, it is going in the right direction. Mr. Broadmell stated that he would come back again for conceptual. If they lost that space on the front, would there be a possibility to make it up a little in the back. Commission members replied in the affirmative. Mr. Keenan stated that he would love to see the porch go all the way across. Ms. Wilson stated that even a bonket to push out to the right to get more space, but it might mean shifting where the kitchen is, but there is still a few feet of additional space. Mr. Pohlman stated that this would be encroaching into the setbacks. Ms. Wilson stated that the Commission would be allowed to approve this. Mr. Keenan stated that he would be willing to grant a variance on this. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Broadwell stated that he would work on doing the front porch all the way across. Ms. Wilson stated that she likes the original porch proportions and is okay with enclosing a portion. She said that she likes the porch under that gable, but does not have an issue grabbing that space in the carport and could have French doors onto the porch from what is now closed in at the carport under that roofline. But she would like to see the existing porch that is on the original drawing. IV. Staff Approvals

Mr. Hirshorn stated that there was also a procedural omission on 436 Church Street on the partial demolition of the historic structure. He said although it was approved, there was no discussion on the demolition. Mr. Hirshorn said that we had an application for this previously on the same section of the house and it was approved, because that section was deemed non-historic. He said this is a separate item. Ms. Rowe asked if the demolition was approved previously. Mr. Hirshorn responded in the affirmative and said the homeowner never followed through and re-sold the home. He said that there was lengthy discussion on demolition. He said he feels sure it would have been approved; however it was never addressed. Ms. Wilson said that she was the architect on that project and the prospective buyers decided not to purchase so the contract fell through. Mr. Hirshorn said that they were going to take the back shed portion off and add a new addition. He asked if they would be required to return for the Old Village Historic District Commission

demolition approval. He said that it is procedurally required for the homeowner to stipulate why they are demolishing that section. Ms. Wilson stated that when looking at their application, it does not show that they applied for demolition. Mr. Keenan said that their application stated “final review for addition to historic structure”. Mr. Hirshorn stated that they are going to keep a section of the foundation only and demolish the remaining shed structure. Ms. Wilson said that this is so they can maintain the setback. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the applicant needs to come back before the Commission and make an application for the demolition of historic structure, or is the Commission able to do this for them. Mr. Rutherford said that he will relay this information to Mr. Pohlman. Mr. Keenan said that he believes they may need to come back before the Commission to ensure it is on record and does not believe it will be an issue with Commission members. He said he would like to know why it was not listed on the application. Mr. Hirshorn said that they did request demolition previously; however, it was a conceptual application and the board did not vote on it. He said that nonetheless, a motion needs to be made and the applicant must stipulate under what grounds. Ms. Wilson said that if the homeowners are required to come back before the Board, it should be done in a way that it does not slow them down and is just a formality. 314 Hibben Street – (HISTORIC 6214) TMS 517-15-00-012 – Final Review for Reroofing of Historic Structure. (This item was moved from earlier in the agenda to the end) Ms. Wilson asked if Mr. Pohlman confirmed if they were replacing “in kind”. Mr. Rutherford said that Mr. Pohlman stated that it is the same as the wrapped porch, but different than the second story. He said that it is architectural shingle. He said the existing is asbestos shingle and the property owner would like to remove this. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan said that they have an odd pattern as well. Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Ms. Wilson moved to defer the application for 314 Hibben Street until more detail is provided on the replacement materials. Ms. Dickson seconded the motion. All present voted in favor. VI. Staff Approvals Ms. Wilson made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

There being no further business, meeting adjourned at 7:10 p.m.

request: 728 Pitt St. Preliminary Review for the construction of a new garage addition to an existing primary structure

events.text:

Ms. Kara Reyes reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Gravitt closed public comment.

Mr. Craft suggested that the garage should be moved and the roofline is to “busy”. He suggested having a tandem separated garage would be preferred.

Ms. Gravitt agreed and stated that it does not meet the Town ordinance or guidelines. Ms. Reyes stated that this was the desire of the owners but stated that she would work with the owners to bring it into compliance.

Ms. Gravitt stated that with it being a historic structure, having the garage detached and set back is preferred.

Mr. Foxworth asked if there is a transom above the garage doors. Ms. Reyes answered in the affirmative. Mr. Foxworth suggested a solid garage door would be more historic.

Mr. Craft suggested that separate garage doors would be more appropriate. He also suggested the front porch and eaves be restudied.

Ms. Gravitt asked if the garage could be moved back and include the storage area. Ms. Reyes answered that including the storage in the garage would put them over the 50% allowed.

Ms. Edwards suggested a single tandem garage set back would be preferred. Ms. Edwards asked if the porch would be enclosed. Ms. Reyes answered in the affirmative. Historic District Preservation Commission

Ms. Gravitt asked what additions were added. Ms. Balzac answered that room to the right of the front porch was originally a porte cochere and added the when enclosed, the addition to the back was constructed as well.

Ms. Reyes asked if the garage could have a hyphen.

Mr. Craft suggested that a hyphen might be appropriate if the garage is moved back. He reiterated that a single bay would be preferable.

Ms. Gravitt stated that the ordinance states the garage must be to the rear and detached.

Mr. Foxworth asked how far back the garage would need to be located. The Commission discussed how far back the garage should be located.

Mr. Hankinson clarified that the rear yard typically starts at the rear corners of the house.

Mr. Hankinson reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Ms. Linda Balzac, architect, reviewed the request with the Commission.

There being no comments, Ms. Gravitt closed public comment.

Mr. Craft suggested that it is different from the previous submittal.

Ms. Gravitt asked about the neighboring property. Ms. Balzac answered that there is a long driveway.

Mr. Foxworth asked if there was any comments from the neighbors. Ms. Balzac answered that the neighbor behind them had no objections.

Mr. Craft asked about the porte cochere. Ms. Balzac answered that this was to soften the garage.

Ms. Gravitt asked where they access the home. Ms. Balzac answered through the front door.

Mr. Foxworth asked about the window in the hyphen between the home and the garage. Ms. Balzac answered that the lift is in the garage up to the hallway

Ms. Edwards asked the dimensions of the hallway from the garage. Ms. Balzac answered that the hallway and lift are three feet, six inches wide.

Mr. Craft suggested that the hallway from the garage is small. Ms. Balzac answered that it was designed to be as small as possible and if desired, could be removed without affecting the historic structure.

Mr. Craft suggested that the porte cochere columns should be revisited. Historic District Preservation Commission

Ms. Gravitt asked if all comments were addressed. Ms. Balzac answered that the rear porch is not historic. She stated that the windows were replaced in 2016, the colors would match existing, the garage doors would be noted as wood, and there is fiber cement siding that replaced all of the exterior siding and this would be matched.

Mr. Foxworth asked if the roof color would match existing. Ms. Balzac answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Player suggested that the design looks good.

Ms. Edwards asked about the space between the garage and the house. Ms. Balzac answered that it is four feet, 8 inches

Ms. Gravitt asked the setback from the front porch to the porte cochere. Ms. Balzac answered that porte cochere is 13 feet, 2.5 inches back.

Mr. Craft suggested that wider hyphen should be considered.

Mr. Hankinson cautioned that the stormwater runoff from the roof of the garage should be managed.

Ms. Edwards asked if the home could be moved so it did not encroach into the setback.

Ms. Gravitt suggested that home might be moved back so it is farther from the street and to have the garage farther back on the lot to better meet the guidelines.

label: 443 Church Street
request: 443 Church Street – (HISTORIC 6207) – Final Approval for Alteration to Approved Hardscape and Addition to Existing Accessory Structure

events.text:

Katie Duncan, Duncan Design Studio, stated that she is working with the Holzer Family and was brought into project after pool was previously approved. She stated that the pool will stay the same size, but they would like to switch the spa and the stairs to the other side. She stated that the accessory structure, formerly a pickling house, will serve as the pool house, and the homeowners would like to have a simple shed roof on the side of the structure. Mr. Keenan asked if they will be enlarging the structure. Ms. Duncan stated that the structure will not be altered, only a simple shed roof to the side property line to park a golf cart, which will not be enclosed. Mr. Keenan stated that the homeowners are requesting to swap the stairs and the spa and asked if the other request is for a tin roof on the side of the pickling house. Ms. Duncan stated that when the spa and stairs are moved, they will also move the pool deck to the opposite side. Ms. Rowe asked about the outdoor kitchen previously requested. Ms. Duncan stated that there is no outdoor kitchen, and stated that the fencing was approved with the pool. Mr. Keenan asked if there was an additional fence other than the fence that is currently there. Ms. Duncan stated that there is a four foot fence that will be encircling the property which was approved with the pool and will match what is existing and meet the pool codes. Ms. Rowe asked if the only thing that will be seen from the street is the shed roof. Ms. Duncan responded in the affirmative. She stated that the homeowners will also be putting in landscaping. Mr. Keenan asked about the size of the pool. Ms. Duncan stated that it is approximately 15x30. Mr. Hirshorn asked if it is nine feet from the edge of the shed roof to the property line. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his only issue is when it rains, it will flow from the roof to the neighbor’s property. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Duncan stated that everything under the structure is pervious surface and landscaping, as well as the driveway. This should all help with any runoff. label: 315 Hibben Street
request: 315 Hibben Street – – Final Approval for After- the-Fact alterations to hardscape and pergola location

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Chris and Jane Potts, property owners. Mr. Potts stated that he and his wife Jane are the property owners. He mentioned that his wife is a designer and that he was not involved in this project, but is now attempting to rescue the project. He stated that they made a mistake and should have come back to the board for approval to move the pergola 3 feet and 2 inches. He stated that this did not happen. He said that he has never been in front of the board before. He said they have lived there for four years and love it and want to do everything possible to enhance the value of their property and those around them. He stated that the house is small and when he moved in the front was dirt with an old fence and a huge driveway. He stated that they are not able to extend the size of the home. He stated that his wife wanted to enhance the backyard and hired a draftsman and came before the Commission on August 9th. He stated that the pergola was approved as to the size, color and style. He said the initial plans had pier foundations; however, the Town’s building inspector advised them that they needed a four foot foundation with rebar. He stated that there are two large trees that abut the pergola and his wife and the builders of the pergola were concerned that the pier foundations that big would kill or disturb the trees. He stated that from what he understands, in an effort to save the trees, the pergola structure was moved forward 3 feet and 2 inches. He stated that the problem is that no one came before the Commission for approval and did not know that they were supposed to. He stated that the error was not intentional or malicious. He stated that since that time, his wife has submitted new plans to the Commission. He stated that he paid $55,000 for the improvements to the property. He immediately called the installer and was told that it would be approximately $8,000 to move it back. Mr. Potts read some of the comments made at previous Commission meetings. He stated that there were comments regarding the fans and heaters which they will remove and only use seasonally, whether the Commission has purview or not. He stated that his wife took down her sign. He stated that his wife spoke to all of their surrounding neighbors and none Old Village Historic District Commission

were opposed to it. He stated that everything was done under the old guidelines. He stated that he and his wife take a lot of pride in the neighborhood. Mr. Keenan stated that he appreciates the attention to detail. He stated that his concerns were the heaters, fans and the sign. He stated that there were some complaints from residents on the signs, heaters and fans, which is likely how the process began and subsequently found that the pergola had been moved several feet. He stated that a good compromise may be to clean up the look of it, which has been stated already by removing the heaters and sign. He stated that he is not going to require them to move it back three feet Ms. Rowe stated that she is in agreement with Mr. Keenan, as the complaints she received were due to the sign, heaters and fans. She said that the fence and pergola look great, but she asks that the extra items be cleaned up. Ms. Potts stated that she has planted some flowers which will also help. She stated that she would also like to plant something that grows onto the pergola; however, it takes a number of years to mature. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the 2017 guidelines are controlling this issue or would it be the 2016. Mr. Pohlman stated that since they are coming back, it would be the 2017 guidelines. Mr. Hirshorn stated that they were approved under the 2016 guidelines and there are some technicalities where the homeowner had to come back before the Commission. He stated that the Commission should clarify under the 2017 guidelines, not just for pergolas, but other elements, that they must be out of the view of the right of way. Mr. Hirshorn added that this is important, because there are a number of other items in the process where this is an issue. He stated that it is also important for the record to state that the reason why this guideline was revised as such is because while we do agree that we all want to increase and enhance the value of the village, the Commission also has an obligation. He stated that there is a balancing act of what value-enhancement is and what historical preservation is. He added that he makes every attempt to strictly stick to the guidelines. He stated that the Commission has started changing course due to recent developments, accessory structures and design elements to keep them out of the historic frame of view. He stated that this is an exception, primarily because this was approved under the 2016 guidelines. Mr. Keenan stated that he appreciates Mr. Hirshorn’s comments, which are important for the minutes as well. Ms. Wilson stated that this is not a precedent that the Commission is setting and it is not just pergolas, but any accessory structure. She Old Village Historic District Commission

stated that this pergola came close to competing with that primary elevation, which is what the Commission is battling against. Jim Berg, 402 Patjens Lane, stated that he lives around the corner from the Potts and walks by their property every day. He added that it would be a shame if they had to tear down the pergola. Mr. Keenan stated that what he believes he is hearing from the Commission is for the property owners to clean up the area of all the lights, fans and heaters and everything stays the same with the pergola. Ms. Rowe made a motion to approve the submission for 315 Hibben Street, after the fact, noting Mr. Hirshorn’s language; seconded by Ms. Wilson. All present voted in favor

label: 241 Bennett Street
request: 241 Bennett Street – (HISTORIC 6134) – Final Approval for Replacement of Windows

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Linda Balzac, architect for homeowner, who is also present, George Brewer. She stated that the homeowner has lived in the home for a very long time and had some work done to the home approximately thirty years ago. She stated that the construction workers installed windows from elsewhere and stated that the windows do not open. She stated that many of the windows on the side of the home are original with the wavy glass. She stated that they would like to be able to open the windows to access the breeze as it is hot. She stated that they would like to remove the unsightly metal storm windows and install new simulated divided lights in to match the existing muntin pattern. She stated that they would like it to be clad and the guidelines state that this can be accomplished. Mr. Keenan asked if they were six over six. Ms. Balzac stated that they are eight over eight. Ms. Rowe stated that she applauds removing the storm windows as this will be an improvement. Ms. Wilson stated that it is not in the ordinance, but would prefer if it stipulated that wood would go back into the older homes. Mr. Hirshorn stated that this was brought up before, that even if the original historic windows were replaced and if they retroactively had to be replaced again, that they had to be brought back to the historic design. He stated that these were on other proposals. Mr. Pohlman stated that the approved materials for windows are listed as wood for both historic and non-historic homes; aluminum clad, vinyl or fiberglass could be used on new construction. Ms. Wilson stated that it is wood for historic. Ms. Balzac stated that Anderson has a good looking wood window as well and they have not specifically decided. She stated that it was Old Village Historic District Commission

more ease of maintenance, as this family has been living in the home for a very long time. George Brewer, 421 Bennett Street, stated that it is historic in the sense that the original part, when it was a Charleston side porch house. He stated that the porch portion was filled in, so it is less than historic. He stated that 35 years ago, the contractor thought that the windows were being replaced, but they were not. They reconfigured the windows and attempted to piece them together. He said that they do not fit and are not acceptable. He stated that this is going back to some of the original. He stated that they are not attempting to put modern windows in, but trying to make it more functional so that they can be utilized as opposed to historical windows. Ms. Wilson stated that a wood window would accomplish this. She stated that Anderson or Marvin could do this. She stated that it has been noted that the homeowner would like muntins to match historic and the glazing pattern, especially because it is on the front of the home. She stated that if it was the porch on the side or in the back, but it is a classic, great looking historic house. Mr. Keenan stated that he agrees with Ms. Wilson, because they need to adhere to the guidelines especially because the home is historic. He stated that the guidelines are clear on wood versus clad or vinyl. Ms. Balzac stated that it does not specifically say that they are replacing windows that were replaced; it implies in the guidelines that if you are replacing historic windows on a historic house, it would be wood and you would put the wood back. She stated that there are a number of windows on the house that are not original and there are a few different windows on the house that are not original. She stated that since they are not historic windows that they can get as close as possible to them and using better materials that look like the original, which they have not been in 35 years. Mr. Keenan asked if a wood window from Marvin or Anderson is an issue for the homeowner. Mr. Brewer stated that they have not looked at windows or material or prices or anything else. He stated that it is difficult for him to say what is acceptable and what is not. Mr. Keenan stated that Marvin is making some really nice wood options and with the paint they are virtually maintenance free and will look really nice on a historic home. He stated that this would be his preference as well as the preference of Commission members. He stated that he hears the argument and does not want to dictate what type of windows you can or cannot put on your home, but would rather see a high end wooden window. Ms. Balzac stated that if they state that they will go with wood windows and after looking at options, if the homeowner decides that Old Village Historic District Commission

it is not an option as far as the durability and cost, they will come and address it at that time. She asked if it would be acceptable under the wood if they said yes to that and could come back if they change their minds. Ms. Wilson stated that she would be agreeable to this. She stated that it would be accepted if they are wood windows and if not, the Commission would like to see the options. Ms. Rowe stated that there are only five windows to replace. Mr. Keenan stated that given the research that Ms. Balzac completed, the homeowner may be happier with the wood, especially on the front façade. Ms. Wilson made a motion to accept, as stipulated by the applicant, that they are accepted as wood with no need to come back before the Commission and if they would like to present an alternative, they can come back before the Commission; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.
