label: 415 Church Street
request: 415 Church Street – (HISTORIC 6202) – Final Approval for Fence and Gate

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. (Ms. Dickson stepped out at 5:05 p.m.) James Scott, stated that they have been before the Commission previously and this is the finalization of the hardscape and landscape around the property. He stated that the pool buildings have already been approved and they are proposing to add a little formal garden area, a brick patio with a walkway to get from the driveway, and a brick entrance. He stated that they do not have much coverage to block the pool from the front. He stated that they have planted a significant amount of shrubbery and are proposing a wall in between the row of camellias and hollies, which will match the existing wall out front which is historic. He stated that the proposed wall will be taller. He proposed brick columns and a gate for privacy and security, as well as a pergola that will match the existing pergola. He stated Old Village Historic District Commission

that the driveway will have brick runners and will pull the concrete apron out and replace with a brick apron that will match the brick walk. Ms. Wilson asked if the design of the proposed brick wall is the same as the historic wall out front. Mr. Scott stated that it is. The historic wall is only a few feet high with wrought iron on top and stated that with the proposed wall, rather than having the wrought iron on top, they would like to make it twice the height, but keep the same pattern as the historic wall. He stated that once the shrubbery matures, it will cover the proposed wall. He stated that there are four rows of vegetation and stated that the proposed wall would be tucked between the hollies and camellias. Mr. Keenan asked how tall the proposed fence would be. Mr. Scott stated that they are proposing four feet. Ms. Wilson asked if the existing raised planter is historic. Mr. Scott stated that it was added. He stated that the planter was put in years ago when they renovated the house and stated that they were proposing to do a creeping fig over it so that it will not be seen. Ms. Rowe asked about the wood pergola. Mr. Scott stated that it will be a wood pergola to match the existing pergola that connects the two pool buildings. Ms. Rowe stated that she is concerned about this. Mr. Scott stated that he would be agreeable not to include the second pergola. He stated that the designer put this in. Mr. Hirshorn stated that Mr. Scott has been in front of the Commission previously and stated that he is surprised that more neighbors have not expressed their opinions. He stated that Church Street has undergone a great deal of development and straying away from what was once traditional. He stated that the streetscape is undergoing significant transformation. He stated that recently the guidelines were modified, as well as those that were already in place. He cited “fences and walls” from the guidelines and stated that from his perspective, the proposed wall may not be historically appropriate. He said the formal walls are not typically seen on historic structures and for this reason he has a reservation on the proposed wall as per Fences and Walls, guideline 2. He cited guidelines on “sidewalks, driveways”, #3. He stated that he loves the formal garden and walkways and design; however, struggles with the historic appropriateness, particularly when you look at the older houses. It is much more of a pasture setting and you do not see many formal gardens. He stated that there are some, but he would like to discuss further. Old Village Historic District Commission

(Ms. Dickson returned at 5:17 p.m.) He stated that in reference to the pergola and arbor, he cited the most recent guidelines. He stated that since this is visible, it would not be permitted. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the driveway is an improvement from the cement slab that currently exists, but would like for the Commission to discuss the previous three items in the context of the guidelines that are fairly specific and if there are any counter opinions on what is historic and what is not, he would like to open this to discussion. Ms. Wilson stated that she agrees with Mr. Hirshorn and does have an issue with a brick fence and is peculiar that it shadows what is on the street. She stated that it is heavy-handed and does not seem to go with the house and does not understand the connection to the raised brick planter and cannot assume that creeping fig is going to hide an awkward situation. She stated that a lot has been done and has a formal piece at the back of the pool which she does not have an issue with, but is not in favor of the brick fence. She stated that regarding the arbor between the structures, technically, it is visible from the street and does marry two structures together so she is less opposed to this than the wall. Mr. Keenan stated that he agrees with Mr. Hirshorn, Ms. Rowe and Ms. Wilson, that the brick wall is too much for the historic context of the home. Mr. Scott asked if a wooden wall would work, painted a Charleston green. He said that the idea is not to let people see into the yard. He stated that in a few years, the landscaping will mature enough to hide it. He stated that he is trying to create privacy. He stated that he would feel more comfortable with the wooden fence, but the brick is too much. He stated that the guidelines regarding the pergolas are clear that they are not to be seen from the street or rights or way. He stated that he is fine with the driveway. Mr. Scott asked about brick columns in order to anchor a gate. He is willing to mimic the brick columns on the front wall to anchor a gate and then have wooden fencing off to each side of the columns. Commission members stated that they would have to see the plans first for fencing. Mr. Scott stated that he would like to have a security gate. Mr. Keenan stated that there is a fence along the perimeter of the property. Mr. Scott stated that they would be safer having an added level of security. He stated that the gate would have a key coded lock. He stated that they have found kids playing in the yard. He stated that it Old Village Historic District Commission

is a side yard and the pool is very visible, so having that extra layer of security with the gate for when they go out of town would make them more comfortable. Mr. Keenan asked how it would be closed off on the driveway side. Mr. Scott stated that it is not on the driveway side. He stated that the challenge is the kids coming through the front and are less likely to come down the driveway. Mr. Hirshorn asked if there is a full pool cover. Mr. Scott responded in the affirmative. Ms. Dickson asked about the height of the gate. Mr. Scott said four feet high for privacy and security. Mr. Keenan asked Mr. Scott to review with his design architect other options. Mr. Scott asked if the Commission would move forward with approval of the driveway. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve the landscape plan with the exception of the brick wall and pergola at the street side of the pool; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Carmen and James Scott, homeowners. Mrs. Scott stated that this is an amendment to the former application. She stated that they previously came before the Commission requesting a pierced brick wall that would match the front of the property. She stated that this was declined as it was not “in keeping with the village”, so they are now coming back with a Charleston green four foot fence connected with brick columns that will be identical to the columns that are already on the historic property. She stated that the gate will be joined on either side by a column and on the side of the property to the neighbor side will be a column. She stated on the house side, there is a brick herb planter and the fence will connect there. She stated that they have three rows of significant planting and the fence will be significantly hidden, but it will provide them with privacy from Church Street. She stated that they have a pool in the back and those that may be walking on Church Street would be able to view them. She showed examples from around the Village that they are hoping to accomplish. Mr. Keenan asked if their fence is solid. Ms. Scott responded in the affirmative. Mr. Hirshorn asked if this was a single fence line and does not completely enclose the pool. He stated that at a previous meeting, there was a statement that it was for security purposes. Ms. Scott stated that it is for security purposes in the sense that it takes away the attractive nuisance from other children walking along the street seeing a pool or anyone walking. She stated that it will be completely enclosed when the gate is closed so that you will be able to see anything from the street. Mr. Hirshorn asked if you are able to get around it. Ms. Scott stated that you can get around it by going down the driveway. Mr. Hirshorn asked if there was a wrought iron exterior fence around the whole yard. Ms. Balzac stated that she worked on the house and said the fence is significantly back from the front of the road. She stated that they have an interesting piece of property that they chose to keep as one piece of property. She stated that the privacy fence behind the plantings will blend in nicely. She stated that it is a large lot and they have done everything beautifully so far. Ms. Rowe asked if the planting will become large. Ms. Scott stated that they plan to keep the camellias at a level that will be at the height of the fence and behind it, there are holly trees, so it will be a Old Village Historic District Commission

green wall. She stated that the fence is for additional security and to provide privacy. Ms. Dickson asked why they chose to have the fence solid, rather than spaced. Ms. Scott stated that they wanted a solid surface behind the planting. Ms. Wilson stated that this Commission cannot evaluate landscaping because the house can be sold and the next owner may remove all the planting and all that is left is a painted wood solid fence, behind a wrought iron fence, which she feel is a peculiar arrangement. She stated that if it is a visual thing, then they can plant additional foliage without any concurrence from this Board. She stated that the fence is really not necessary to accomplish security and privacy. Ms. Scott stated that the plantings were put in over a year ago and they still have not grown to their expectations. She stated that they do not have that protection from the attractive nuisance. She stated to address Ms. Wilson’s point on the wood fence, this is why they came before the Commission with a pierced brick fence previously that is at the front of the property and has been there for 130 years. Ms. Wilson stated that the front is an ornate iron fence. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would cite the guidelines on fences and gates to consistency with the other fences and gates and stated that you typically do not see privacy walls. He stated that this would detract from the streetscape. He stated that the Commission has provided significant latitude on many of the other structures that have come before the Commission and to add this extra element is going over, as to the streetscape and altering the historic nature of the property. Ms. Scott stated that each of the pictures provided in the packet are examples of the fences she is referring to and are all throughout the Old Village. Mr. Hirshorn stated that those properties do not have double fences, but a single perimeter fence. Ms. Scott argued that this is not true and is able to provide additional pictures. She stated that what they are looking to do is everywhere in the Old Village. She stated that the pierced brick fence that they came before the Commission for approval is everywhere in the Old Village. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his point is the nature of the double fence where there is one exterior fence and an additional privacy wall. Mr. Scott stated that he takes exception to the statement that they have been given incredible latitude. He stated that they have been before the Commission six times and have followed all the guidelines and have done everything above and beyond what was required. He stated to somehow imply that they have been provided preferential treatment. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that he did not say “preferential treatment”. He stated that originally, the applicants came before the Commission with the ADU, pool houses, golf cart house and the original determination was that it was far too many structures on the property, and then came back, individually for each one. The Scotts stated that they were within zoning laws. Mr. Hirshorn stated that this brings him to his latitude point. Ms. Scott stated that her issue is that she is not sure what the original fence is. She stated that there is nothing in the application that is disallowed by the guidelines, not one thing. Mr. Hirshorn stated that with the exception of guideline 2 on fences and gates, that they should be consistent with the fences and gates on historical properties within the Old Village. Ms. Scott stated that the gate at the back of their property is a solid wooden gate that runs along the entirety of the property that is approximately 6 feet tall. Mr. Hirshorn stated that this is at the rear of the property. Ms. Scott stated that it sounds like we are splitting hairs and is not sure exactly why. Ms. Wilson asked if she was referring to the six inch brick that is seen around the plantings. Ms. Scott stated that she is not sure what was there originally. She stated that the six inch brick with the iron piece are more like twelve inches with the iron pieces above it is what they have at their property. Ms. Wilson stated that if the homeowners are allowed to have their gate and the whole idea is to have a thick hedge where you cannot see your pool through, she asked if they would be happy with the gate and the hedging. She stated that the applicants must understand that the Commission must evaluate the application for when all hedges die and the applicants are no longer interested in maintaining the hedge and then the Commission would be looking at a walled fence that is very different from the rest of the house with another fence in front. She asked if the applicants would be satisfied with the Commission approving the gate and then densely planting up to the gate which would have the same visual effect. Ms. Scott stated that they have densely planted and the plants have not grown quickly enough and 1 ½ years later, they are left with this issue. Ms. Wilson stated that this type of response is exactly why the Commission cannot evaluate this request based on landscaping. Mr. Keenan stated that camellias and hydrangeas are not dense plantings. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Scott stated that there are three layers of plantings with a layer of holly trees behind them. She stated that they would have been satisfied with the pierced brick wall that is identical to the pierced brick wall that underlies the iron at the front of their property that has been there for 130 years; however, the Commission denied this. Mr. Scott stated that this was more in keeping with the property. He stated that there is no wooden wall or fences on the property other than the one at the rear of the property. He stated that they have done everything to try and keep within the original historic element of this property; wood siding, metal roofs, copper, etc. Ms. Scott stated that they have spent a significant amount of money doing this as well. Mr. Scott stated that a pierced brick wall, which matches the front area, which is also similar to the one on Bennett Street that has been in the Old Village for a number of years. He stated that they felt the pierced brick wall was a more appropriate match, but at the previous meeting, they were told that it was not, so they are here again before the Commission for recommendations and their suggested fence. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the pierced brick may be historic; however, the placement would not be, as a second privacy wall in the middle of the yard. Mr. Scott stated that the dividing walls are common throughout the village. He stated that they are simply asking for the same as what has already been approved for others, to have the ability not to see their family in the swimming pool. He stated that he does not want people to walk down Church Street and see his children and all their pool floats. Mr. Hirshorn stated that in his estimation, the open, pastoral setting is more consistent with the Village. He stated that if you live along Bennett Street or near the waterfront, there are no privacy fences or walls and there are a number of pools. Mr. Keenan stated that the OVHDC guidelines clearly explain that just because there are architectural similar situations in the Village, does not mean that they will apply to the application being heard. He stated that this argument can be taken off the table at this point. He stated that the focus needs to be on this specific application. Ms. Scott showed Hibben Street at the end where there is a privacy wall around the entire property. Mr. Hirshorn stated that this is an exterior fence. Ms. Scott stated that it aligns the boundaries of the property. Mr. Scott stated that their next door neighbor has this exact fence on Church Street. He stated that they have a half-acre lot just as they do and in the front of their house, they have a wall that divides their formal front Old Village Historic District Commission

from their more informal back. He stated that this is the exact same thing that they are asking for. He stated that theirs is actually made out of stucco and has a wooden gate. To say there are no such walls, there is one right next door to their home. Mr. Hirshorn stated that to clarify, he believes that the additional structures, which there are many on the property, has significantly altered the streetscape of the historic property to this point and to add an additional Charleston green wall to this would take it past the critical mass of where the Commission would like to go with this particular property. He stated that it also sets a precedent. He stated that there is a limit. Ms. Scott stated that this is not a structure and not on the table for discussion this evening and understand Mr. Hirshorn’s point in looking at the property as a whole. However, what they are asking for is security and aesthetics and other than the point that is being made about double fencing, which she is not familiar with this in reference to the guidelines. Mr. Scott asked if there is anything in the guidelines that specifically states that you cannot have a double fence. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it is more broadly worded. Mr. Scott responded and said that there is not anything that specifically says this. Mr. Hirshorn stated not specifically. Mr. Scott argued that it is then allowed. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it does not allow it either. Mr. Scott argues that it is not disallowed. Mr. Hirshorn asked Mr. Pohlman to display the guidelines. He cited that “design, height and placement, etc., need to be similar to historic fences”. Mr. Scott argued that the Commission should take a look at his next door neighbor’s fence which divides his property in the middle of his yard, which is what they are looking to put in. Ms. Scott cited verbiage in the guidelines, “arrangement of voids to solids are similar to Historic fences in the OVHD,” and stated that she has provided six or seven examples of fences in the OVHD. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the placement of those are on the exterior. Ms. Scott argued that they are not on all of them. She stated that this includes some of very beautiful homes of members on this very board. Mr. Scott stated that they have come with both brick and wood. He stated at the end of the day, they need some sort of privacy screen there and protection so that the pool is off limits and not an attractive nuisance to children coming down the street. Ms. Wilson stated that her personal vote is to build the gate. She stated that there are a number of planting that grow extremely well, so the idea Old Village Historic District Commission

that you cannot get anything to grow is somewhat silly. She stated that there are evergreens that grows very dense and cannot be passed through, and the look the homeowners are discussing can be achieved. She stated that the Commission will not be in a position where they are approving an application where if the homeowners move, there is an odd remnant of a wood wall in the middle of the property. She stated that she is agreeable with the gate and the homeowners can hedge to it, which is outside the purview of the Commission. She stated to approve something that is meant to be hedged, she is not in favor of approving. She is agreeable with the gate as a way to make it a very formal clipped hedge. She stated that the homeowners will achieve the same look and privacy where it will be impassable and the gate can be locked. She suggested cypress, cedar, ligustrum, holly, etc. She stated that there are so many different types that can achieve this in this climate. Mr. Keenan stated that to clarify, Ms. Wilson is agreeable to the gate that the homeowners have drawn on their plans with the brick columns. Ms. Wilson responded in the affirmative. Ms. Scott stated for clarification, what is the specific reason for denying. Ms. Wilson stated that the fence is inappropriate for the home. She stated that she understand what the homeowner is saying about visual protection. She stated as a landscaped item, it makes sense what has been done on the backside in terms of creating a formal garden, left the lawn in the front, but she has to assume that the landscaping all dies and what would be left in the proposal is inappropriate and does not look appropriate with the home or property. She stated that she is stating her best compromise that she would be agreeable to is the gate and then have it hedged to the gate. She stated that this will achieve the same formal look that works great with the gardens on the backside. She stated that you cannot pass through dense hedging and it will provide the order of the gate, the pool will not be visible and will provide what the homeowners are requesting. Ms. Scott asked if there is a fence system, brick or otherwise that the Commission would be comfortable with. She stated that this Commission has approved on historic homes, living fences, which does not meet any of the guidelines. Mr. Keenan stated not in the front. Mr. Scott argued that on the corner of Hibben and Bennett Streets (the old church), there are living fences in the front. Ms. Dickson stated that there is no solid or picket fence, it is just living fence. Ms. Scott stated that there is zero historic value. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Lisi asked if the Commission would consider a picket fence with spacing in between of ¾ or ½ and inch with a square or picket top. He asked if it was just the style of fence that is the concern. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it is the entirety of the project. He stated that the fence adds another layer. Mr. Scott stated that the Commission needs to look at this as a property that could have been subdivided with another house, with an ADU behind it, as well as an ADU behind their home. He stated that they chose not to go that route. He stated that everything else has been approved and they are only asking for this side yard and what is applicable to that side yard. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would be far more supportive of a thick living hedge. Ms. Scott stated that this is not what the application is for; that is landscaping. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he is not in favor of an interior fence. Ms. Scott asked Mr. Hirshorn, for the record, to point her to the guideline. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it would be under Fences & Walls. Ms. Scott asked Mr. Hirshorn for the specific section and sentence. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it would be “placement, arrangement and similar to historic fences in the OVHD”. Ms. Scott asked if the one that they have proposed is not similar to other fences in the OVHD. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it is the placement. Ms. Scott stated that if she were to bring to this Commission, multiple examples of this. Mr. Keenan reiterated that the guidelines explain clearly that the existence of similar architecture does not mean that there are grounds for approval on the application. Ms. Scott stated that except that it is grounds for different treatment for various residents of the Old Village. Ms. Wilson stated that they also must take into account that there were different individuals serving on this Commission at different times. She stated that if Ms. Scott were to bring something that was approved ten years ago, it is not relevant. She stated that this Commission is doing the best they can with the Ordinances and Guidelines provided. She stated that in their estimation, the wood fence appears to create a secondary lot in the front with a solid fence right down the middle. She stated that in the Commission’s opinion, it is not in keeping with the best interest of this house. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would also use the guideline on new construction. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan stated that there are two fairly strong opinions. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would like to include this for the record. “New Construction must be harmonious in size, scale, massing, form, roof type, and location on the lot to the majority of existing buildings on the block in particular, and in the district generally.” Ms. Scott stated that they meet this criteria. She stated that they are proposing exactly what their neighbors have next door in terms of the fence (or secondary fence as stated by the Commission). She stated that there are wood fences up and down their street. Mr. Hirshorn stated that in his opinion, it is not harmonious with the Village in general. Mr. Scott stated that Mr. Keenan’s father-in-law’s house has the exact same thing to block off their pool on Pitt Street. Ms. Wilson stated that it is a totally different lot. Mr. Keenan stated that it is a different lot with a stucco wall. Mr. Scott stated that the concept of having a wall midway into the property. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the house Mr. Scott is referring to do not have an exterior fence as well and that is the only fencing on the property which is around the pool. Ms. Wilson stated that it is also new construction. Ms. Rowe stated that going back to Mr. Lisi’s previous question. Is there anything that would work? Mr. Keenan stated that Ms. Wilson agreed to the gate. Ms. Wilson stated that it is unclear to her why the hedge and gate would not work. Mr. Scott stated that it would take a lot to get the hedge dense enough. Ms. Wilson stated that you can purchase 8, 10 or 12 foot hedging. Mr. Scott stated that they can buy a lot of expensive landscaping; however, it will still take time to thicken up. Mr. Keenan stated that there are strong opinion regarding the nature of the wall versus the historic house and everything else in the yard. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to deny the application for the final approval of fence and gates at 415 Church Street. Motion fails due to the lack of a second. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve a wooden gate with brick piers that they may landscape to, but no fence. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan stated that the motion by Ms. Wilson is to approve the gate, as submitted in drawing, with the brick piers and wooden gate. He stated that landscaping is out of the Commission’s purview. Mr. Keenan asked to see what gate is being considered for approval. Ms. Wilson stated that the previous application had the gate detailed. She stated that she does not know now, because they previously had it drawn in detail. Motion fails due to lack of a second. Ms. Dickson asked if there was consideration to putting up a fence temporarily and taking it down when the landscape fills in. Ms. Wilson stated that it cannot be considered, because landscaping is not part of the Commission’s purview. Mr. Pohlman stated that the Commission cannot do a conditional timeline. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve brick piers and a gate on the location in the application at 415 Church Street; seconded by Mr. Hirshorn. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the piers would be beside the gate. Mr. Keenan stated that they are 4 ½ feet wide. Ms. Wilson stated that they are also 4 ½ feet tall. Ms. Rowe opposed. All others voted in favor. Motion to approve carries.

label: 930 Richter Way
request: 930 Richter Way—(Survey 6042) – Final Approval for Installation of Parking pad

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Katie Duncan, Duncan Design, representing the homeowner, June Thorpe-Galy. She stated that the cul-de-sac is a parking nightmare and the neighbors to the left have a very nice solution. She stated that they turned their front yard into an auto court. She stated that they would like to mimic their idea. She stated that originally this driveway goes all the way back where there was a garage. This was approved to be enclosed and is part of the house so there is no need to carry the driveway all the way to the back. So they will be Old Village Historic District Commission

removing the concrete and adding two parking spaces in the front with a sand set brick, herringbone pattern, it would be a crushed stone parking area with a brick border. She stated that they would be reducing impervious surfaces significantly and would solve a lot of issues. Although the driveway is long, she can only park stacked. She stated that making the auto court in the front will allow two cars side by side, not stacked. She stated that she will also designate an entry walk landing separate from the parking areas. Mr. Keenan asked how far the crushed stone comes out. Ms. Duncan stated that it comes all the way to the road. She stated that where the driveway is now will become plants and landscape. Mr. Keenan asked about the grade and expressed concern about the water runoff. Ms. Duncan stated that all the material will be pervious and will be held in with a brick border so that there is not any runoff of the stone. She stated that using a bigger aggregate piece like the colonial beige stone will help with this. (Ms. Dickson returned at 6:15 p.m.) Ms. Wilson stated that this is a very difficult cul-de-sac and what is proposed is a very nice solution. She stated if the apron or the throat could come down to eighteen. Ms. Duncan stated that she will review this, but wanted to ensure that two cars could get in and out easily. Ms. Balzac stated that she worked on the house and could never find parking. It is an odd area. Ms. Wilson moved to approve the landscape and hardscape at 930 Richter Way; seconded by Mr. Hirshorn. All present voted in favor.

label: 201 Haddrell Street
request: 201 Haddrell Street – Applicant is seeking Final Review for after-the-fact alterations to new single-family construction

events.text: Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design Group, said that from Haddrell there is a small entryway. He stated that the property is low and the neighbors are excited that something is being done, because it does hold water. He stated that there are two home currently that were approved last summer and fall and currently under construction. He stated that it really opens up on Beach Street. He stated that they decided to pull the driveway in off of Haddrell to open the lot up. Still wanted to get a nice elevation to the lot. He stated that the home is 2,580 sf and wanted to make it feel like an old cottage. He stated that it is 1 ½ stories and the second floor walls are 5 feet 6 inches, but has a two story porch roof which opens it up. One story porch everywhere else. He stated that the two gables are not perfectly aligned on the main mass, but are similar in size. He said that it is not a formal house and does not have a formal street front. He said on the side porch it is a hexagonal porch, because he wanted to maximize the space. The lot is more triangular and believes it will look nice, but are open to discussions. Mr. Keenan stated that it is way under the 24.5%. Ms. Rowe stated that it has a lot of character and charm and is not huge. Linda Balzac stated that it is nice to see a house with this height, scale and mass. It is very appropriate for the neighborhood. Mr. Keenan stated that conceptually, the design looks great and fits the street. Ms. Wilson stated that her one comment is that there is a lot of wall with no window. Mr. Clarke stated that it jogs in and out. Ms. Wilson stated that she understands that it does, but suggested a window in the bathroom. Mr. Clarke stated that he would add a window. Mr. Keenan stated on the left elevation, to the left of the hexagon porch. He stated that it is not critical. Mr. Clarke stated that he has a bathroom there which is the main bathroom from downstairs, but will see if he can work something in. Ms. Rowe suggested shuttering it. Ms. Wilson stated that in reference to the size of the mullions on the two side lights on the front, it seems a bit out of character or just too narrow. She stated that she likes that the gables are shifted. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design, representing the homeowners stated that they have been working through getting the permit and the driveway under the 2420 Live Oak that is on the neighbor’s property. He stated that they are still having issues getting this approval. He said they have decided to remove the garage door and the split parking and stay completely out of the tree protection zone having just one garage door with parking off to the sides. He said that this is the only change. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Rowe asked if the new garage door could match the left side with louvers. She stated that the house looks great and this would make it consistent. Ms. Wilson agreed and said she is in favor of anything that removes all of the hardscape and that it is an improvement. Mr. Keenan stated that he agrees with Ms. Wilson and is also in favor of removing the hardscape. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve the proposal for 201 Haddrell Street with a new garage door that matches the louvers of the house; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Mr. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design Group reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Montgomery asked if the “x’s” on the porch railing were removed. Mr. Clarke answered that the two sections previously approved showing one large “x” was changed to two “x’s” to match the other panels. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hackenberg asked if there would be any unfinished wood on additional supports. Mr. Clarke answered, in the negative.

Ms. Dovre stated she is comfortable with the design.

Ms. Rowe stated that she has no issues with the outdoor fans or retaining walls.

There being no further comments, Ms. Rowe closed public comment.

Ms. Montgomery moved to approve with the plans with deviations from guidelines regarding the louvers, fans and wooden retaining wall. Ms. Dovre second. All in favor.

label: 223 Pitt Street
request: 223 Pitt Street – (HISTORIC 5923) – Final Approval for Addition and Hardscape Alteration

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Linda Balzac, architect representing the homeowners. She stated that this is a wonderful historic house and the Lund’s have done a wonderful job with this. She stated that she was unaware that the side porch going down near the driveway was not original. She stated that there is a bump where it was attached. She stated that when they added on they also put a little bump out on the back on the side porch to enclose some space for the first floor bedroom. She stated that they are proposing to bring a piece out and the columns will remain the same so there will be some relief on the pilasters. She stated that they will add a cover and pop out the pieces that are in the back of the house. She stated on the side that is visible from Pitt Street, it was originally a small back porch and there were several additions done in the area. She stated that the family is growing and this area is the family room, so they would like to come out seven feet and simplify the roof. She stated that when reviewing the guidelines, she wanted to effect as little as possible the historic elevation. She proposed to pull a piece out. She stated that there was a shallow hip room and they could not get it to work for the width of the property so she is proposing a lower pitch closer to the house to avoid the three historic windows on that side, and then Old Village Historic District Commission

raise the gable to take the details from the main house. She stated that she would like to make a small interim piece. She would like to pop the roof up and put a fireplace on the back side. She stated that it simplifies the elevations. She stated that it provides a little more space and the windows that are original stay where they are. She stated that all the materials will match existing. She stated that they are slightly above the impervious rule, but are taking some of the impervious space out. Ms. Dickson asked how far over the ratio. Mr. Pohlman stated that when submitted, it was at 42.69% which is 2.69% over maximum allowable. Ms. Balzac stated that existing was at 43.37% and went down to 42.69%. Ms. Wilson asked when the previous additions were done. Ms. Balzac asked which piece. She asked the homeowners to explain the history of the additions previously made. Ms. Wilson stated that she is wondering how historic it is. Craig Lund, property owner stated that he is not certain when the back porch was added, but estimated in the 1960’s or 1970’s. Ms. Wilson asked if he was referring to the small back piece. Ms. Balzac stated that it is enclosed. She stated that it was a back porch and was enclosed. Mr. Lund stated that it was done after Hurricane Hugo. Ms. Wilson stated that she is asking, because there is a lot of work being done to continue the wall and wondering if it needs to be done, and if part of that porch can just become a hyphen and the new family space could be whatever height and what works for the family. She stated that what is being proposed is going to create an off roof condition that is not necessary, because she does not believe that what was enclosed in 1986 warrants the Commission’s protection. Ms. Balzac added that perhaps a hyphen like the one completed at Live Oak, where it was set back very slightly. Ms. Wilson said that set back slightly and the proportions and dimensions of the living room can be whatever the homeowner desires, including ceiling height, because the historic windows on the second floor have been accommodated. She stated that there would be less concern. Ms. Balzac stated that they would need to be concerned about the impervious lot ratio, because they are already over the 40% and have removed what they were able to do so. Ms. Wilson stated that this is not in their purview. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Pohlman stated that the homeowners would have to go before the Board of Zoning Appeals and request a variance. Ms. Dickson asked if they still have to do it even if the 42% sits on the current approved square footage. Mr. Pohlman stated that because the square footage is being reduced, it would be allowable, as they are reducing the non- conformity. Ms. Rowe stated that this will be a big improvement for the homeowners and the streetscape. Ms. Dickson stated that there are three outbuilding on this property. Mr. Lund stated that there is a garage and the original cook cottage. Ms. Balzac stated that the proposed area is attached to the kitchen so it is a family room. She stated that the hyphen would be moving the wall back in slightly. Ms. Wilson stated that she was merely make a suggestion in order to have a larger area; however, the homeowners may want something different. Ms. Balzac stated that this would make more of a definition between historic and new property. She stated that since they are adding on past it, she originally proposed the hyphen with a lower roof in order not to affect the windows upstairs. However, there are a number of ways to define it. Ms. Wilson suggested that if the interior walls are where the homeowner would like them, she would do the roof all the way the same. Mr. Lund stated that the walls are the same, they are just going out seven feet. Ms. Balzac stated that she would have done this, except the three windows on the second floor are historic windows. She stated that the middle window could be shortened. Ms. Wilson asked Ms. Balzac if she could keep the hip roof that has the same ridge that it has now and just extend it. She asked if there was enough ceiling height. Ms. Balzac stated that it is really shallow. Sam Lisi, stated that he is not in favor of the pitch and the room itself is very small so they were hoping to achieve a vaulted ceiling. He stated that this is when they decided to shorten up the middle window. This was their solution. It stated that it is certainly not easy. Carol Lund, homeowner stated that this will be the only fireplace in the house. Ms. Wilson stated that she is not opposed to what is being proposed. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Lund stated that the original fireplace was taken out by the previous homeowners. Ms. Wilson stated that what is being proposed is great, but was suggesting that if needed for interior space, but does not think that this is something that needs to be protected. She stated that she would do what works for the homeowners. She stated that she felt it was a great deal of work on something that was not historic. She asked if it was the same pitch. Ms. Balzac responded in the affirmative and stated that the one behind it is lower. She did match the wrap around porch pitch. Ms. Wilson asked about the stairs and if they go on the back. Ms. Balzac stated that they will be on the driveway side, but it will be a stoop and two stairs. She stated that there is a small overhang with nice detail. She stated that there is a door that leads to Mrs. Lund’s office space and they wanted to put small overhang which is over concrete so they are not increasing the impervious surface. Mr. Hirshorn asked about the porch bump out and if it was the original porch. Ms. Balzac indicated where the porch originally stopped and stated that it never went around the corner of the house. Ms. Wilson stated that her final comment is that it should be one roof form and does not know if that means that the middle window needs to stay and understands and supports taking the walls taller, adding a fireplace, making the room bigger, but would like to see a simplified roof form. She stated that it is such a classic house on the street and it just needs to be simple and elegant. Ms. Rowe stated that she does not mind the bump down and believes it provides some character. She stated that she would rather see the roof kept as is and not touch the windows. Ms. Balzac stated that the homeowners do not wish to touch the windows. She stated that the hyphen below will help a little, but complicates the wall. Ms. Wilson and Ms. Balzac discussed various options. Ms. Balzac stated that the window openings are original; however, the windows are not original. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve the addition with the exception that the upper portion of the central window will be maintained and the lower portion will be shuttered or enclosed in order to accommodate a higher ridge and a uniform roof line; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor. Ms. Wilson amended her motion to include the stoop overhang over the studio; Ms. Rowe amended her second. All present voted in favor. Old Village Historic District Commission

label: 304 Morrison Street
request: 304 Morrison Street – Survey 6162.00/ Historic – Screen mechanical equipment in rear of house

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Ms. Wilson stated that she would be recusing herself. Lauren Giovingo-Wiley and Jake Wiley, stated that they are in the process of purchasing this home and would like to come before the Commission prior to finalizing the purchase to make sure that they are able to make this home fit their family. She stated that they went from two to four children very quickly with twins. Prior to purchasing the home, they would like to ensure they are able to do the renovations. She stated that the current homeowner is present to support the purchase and renovations and he was able to locate a picture that his father drew of the home prior to renovations. She stated that the dormer on the front, which is considered a non- conforming dormer that they are proposing to take down, and put back the three dormers, will take the house back to its original structure. She stated that they started with the Sanborn maps to try and figure out what the original structure was. She stated that what they are proposing to take down is the front dormer to the original three dormers, remove the tower which is a bathroom over a bathroom which was an addition. She stated that the reason they are requesting this is the way the structure was built was subpar from where it should be now. She stated that she has a letter from the engineer that provides the information. She stated that the addition that is off to the side, they are proposing to take it down and rebuild it, due to the structural nature of the building. Ms. Dickson asked if she is referring to the green garage. Ms. Wiley stated that she is not referring to the green garage, but it is in their future plans to remove it at a different time. She stated that looking at the existing house, there is an addition with a breezeway, indicating on the illustration the portion they would like to demolish and rebuilt in a different nature to accommodate the twin girls with a playroom space, as well as master suite that is connected to the house. Mr. Keenan asked if the only demolition would be behind the iron staircase. Ms. Wiley responded in the affirmative, but added that the large non-conforming dormer would also be taken out and replaced with the original three dormers. She stated that the other proposal is since they are removing the big dormer, which houses three nice rooms upstairs, they lose a lot of the space on the second floor. She stated that they would like to propose taking a shed dormer off of the back of the house that would mirror the front dormer so they will have room to have bedrooms upstairs. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Rowe clarified that it is a shed dormer. Mr. Wiley stated that it is a little bit of a different dormer. He stated that you want shed instead of gable in the front, which is more historically accurate. Ms. Wiley stated that on the Pitt Street side view of the house, there is an existing porch that wraps around to approximately the middle of the house and then it is enclosed. She stated that it is believed that it was an old kitchen. Mr. Lewis stated that it was an old kitchen and a breakfast nook. Ms. Wiley stated that it was enclosed over a porch space and was not built to hold that type of space. She stated that they are proposing to take that back down and open it up in to a side porch and wrap that side porch around to the back slightly to allow for a door. She stated that this would all be open porches and believe that this is what it was originally prior to closing it in for the kitchen and breakfast nook area. Ms. Wiley stated that looking at the back of the house, it sits on an alley. She showed where the new shed dormer would be located on the back of the house with the windows. She stated that it would be bumped down so it does not overwhelm the original historic structure where it connects to the master down below and a play space above. Ms. Dickson asked if it was right up to the lot line. Ms. Wiley responded in the affirmative. Ms. Rowe stated that according to the Sanborn map it has been that way. Mr. Keenan asked about the total heated square footage. Ms. Wiley stated that it is 3,390 with all the additions. Ms. Dickson asked why the teardown of the green garage were not presented at the same time. Mr. Pohlman stated that this is conceptual. Ms. Wiley stated that it is a matter of time Mr. Keenan stated that he appreciates the conservation aspects. He stated that it is a prominent street location on Pitt and Morrison Streets and stated that the plan looks really good. Ms. Dickson stated that she loves the idea of taking it back to the proper historic look. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it all looks and sounds great; however, on a historic structure, there is an extensive amount of altering of the historic structure and adding on and changes porches, dormers and more. He appreciates that the proposed plan is to bring it back to what it was, but he does not see any documentation. He stated that Old Village Historic District Commission

when a massive alteration of a historic structure is proposed, it needs more of a real historic documentation. Mr. Lewis stated that he can likely answer those questions with the documentation he has. Mr. Hirshorn stated that all of the elements need to be treated with a sensitivity and documentation so that the Commission is comfortable that it is being restored back to what it was. Ms. Wiley stated that if they are not able to produce photographs of what the house originally looked like, they would like to give the house a more conforming look to the neighborhood with the front dormer, which is much different than anything else you would see in the neighborhood. Mr. Hirshorn stated that this would not be acceptable. He stated that the fact that it is more conforming would not supersede the fact that it is historic. He stated that the portion that is proposed to be demolished and replaced with a nice new addition, there is a way that builders can document that it is not historic. Jake Wiley stated that he prides himself on being somewhat of an architectural archeologist, because he loves old building, which is what brought him to Charleston. He stated that he works with Ms. Wilson. He stated that when he was studying this particular building, taking pictures and measurements, it is easy to see on a timeline basis, what new materials were added. The previous homeowner built it himself and you can see that the old foundation is fantastic with old brick piers. He stated that all the way downstairs is exposed so you can see the old barn wood next to pressure treated lumber on CMU. Mr. Hirshorn suggest that when the final presentation is made, to document and take pictures of newer additions/renovations. He asked for the potential homeowners to research what they can on the dormers so that from a preservation standpoint the Commissioners will be more comfortable. He stated that Mr. Lewis must have some old pictures. Mr. Lewis stated that he would look through his paperwork. He added that if you go back to the drawing that indicates where the potential homeowners are proposing to take down, this was built in the 1960’s because there is a bomb shelter underneath. He stated that his father built the bomb shelter for the Cuban missile crisis. He stated that his dad built the bomb shelter. Above it, there is currently a structure that is an auxiliary unit that was built for an aunt to live out her life. He stated that the way the house is laid out the way it is, is because his parent rented our portions as apartments to military. He said that all of this was put in 1963. He said that portion is the most recent of the house. He stated that everything on the main portion of the house is historic. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that it appears that the Commission is relatively comfortable and asked that the additional documentation be presented when they come before the Commission for approval of their plans, to ensure that the historic structure is not being altered. Mr. Wiley stated that he believes this can be put together. Ms. Dickson stated that it would be great to write the history of the house. Mr. Lewis stated that he has the hand written deed from 1887 when it was originally in the Morrison’s name and then it passed down into his family in 1923. He stated that it has been in his family since that time. Ms. Dickson stated that if you write the history of the house, subsequent generations would appreciate it. Ms. Rowe stated that in order for the Commission to defend its position, the more documentation that is presented the better. Mr. Keenan stated that it is obvious that the architect that they hired knows what the Commission desires and conceptually, as long as the Commission is comfortable with the historic nature and fabric of the house, the conceptual plans are great. Mr. Hirshorn stated that reopening the porch is great and has been documented. IV. Staff Approvals

Ms. Wilson stated that she would like to recuse herself from this item. Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Lauren Giovingo, stated that she is one of the buyers of the property. She stated that her husband, James Wiley is also present, as well as Collin Cope, one of the architects, and Mr. Don Lewis, the current owner. She stated that when she was before the Commission last month, she was asked to provide documentation. She stated that she started off at the South Carolina Research Room at the library downtown Charleston and they did not have any pictures or specific information on this property. She stated that she went to the local Village library and they also did not have anything, but advised her to go to the Pitt Street Pharmacy. She stated that she met Mr. Richardson; however, he did not have any information. She stated that the current owner, Mr. Lewis was able to contact his cousin who found that it is available, and was put in the Commission’s packet. She stated that these are the only two pictures that were found. She said the first picture (exhibit A), is the original house. The second picture (exhibit B- 1) is the first phase of renovations that were added onto the side of the house. Mr. Keenan asked if they knew the date of Exhibit A. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Giovingo stated that there is a letter that Mr. Lewis (current owner), wrote which discusses Exhibit A, which would have been around 1870 which is what the house looked like at that time. She stated that there is the first phase edition, which is estimated to be between 1952 and 1957, which is the Exhibit B-1 photograph. She stated that Mr. Lewis also wrote out the series of how the house turned from family to family, why the home has a bomb shelter and when that was built. Mr. Pohlman stated that the letter was not included in the Commission’s packets. He stated that the letter was emailed after the packets were put together. Ms. Giovingo provided a copy to Commission members. Ms. Dickson asked if Ms. Giovingo was one of the owners of the property. Ms. Giovingo stated that they are potential buyers. Ms. Dickson asked who the other potential buyers were. Ms. Giovingo stated that her husband is the other investor. She stated that the home is for their family. She stated that it is been a learning experience doing the research on the home. She stated Exhibit B-2 is a survey that was done on the house dated 1952 which indicates how the house sat on the lot in 1952. She stated the 1952 photograph mirrors the first edition phase. She stated that they also did some architectural investigative work, where they went under the house and took photographs of where the structure physically changes from the original building to the first phase edition and second phase edition, including the bomb shelter structure. She stated that these are all estimated dates. She stated that they have also included the letter from the Civil and Structural Engineer, a professional, who has documented much of the same information. Mr. Hirshorn asked if they were able to determine when the dormers were switched to a shed dormer. Ms. Giovingo stated that from the second picture (exhibit B-1), you can see the shed dormer; however, she is unable to answer the approximate date. She stated that when you look at the proposed elevation from street side elevation, she pointed out where they made a change. She stated that they are attempting to pull vehicles off the street to where they will not be visible in the yard. She stated that they created another parking space underneath with a deck over it. She stated that they do not need the living space; however, what they originally proposed was only wide enough for one vehicle and she drives a big utility vehicle. She stated that this was the only modification there in order to get the vehicles off of the street. She stated that they took the side stairs off the front and moved them underneath since the vehicles are underneath. Mr. Keenan asked if the plans were different from what the Commission reviewed last month. Mr. Giovingo stated it is, only on the right side. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Collin Cope, architecture, stated that this comes from being respectful. He stated that part of why they did not want increase that area to make it a two car garage was to be respectful of the basic scale and proportion of the original home. He stated that they want it to be thinner volume and that way the ridge does not come up above the existing home and trying to make it a little smaller and attach a porch on the other side, so you have a wrap in porch that works its way around façade of the house. Ms. Giovingo stated that with this addition, the interior side elevation changes slightly because of the deck. She stated on the back elevation, other than the open air porches, it is essentially what was brought before the Commission last month. Mr. Hirshorn stated that there is a portion of the porch facing Pitt Street that is going to be reopened and asked if this was addressed historically as to when it was enclosed. Ms. Giovingo stated that she did not find anything specific on this portion of the home or even a picture of that side of the home. She stated that from the photograph of the front of the home, it is not clear because of the shrubbery. She stated that on the structural engineer’s report, it indicates that the structure under this was originally porch and is not structurally sound enough to be able to hold that piece, which was a kitchen. Mr. Cope stated that in the conversation he had with the engineer, they both independently came to the same conclusion that the language of the structure underneath that area that had been enclosed was 100% for a porch, the same as the rest of the porch. He stated that it changed dramatically when you get to the inside. He said that the inside structure, similar to the main gable, has its own language of structure. He stated that the outside of the piers are placed sporadically. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it is not “if” it was originally a porch, but when it was no longer a porch. He stated that for purposes of a partial demolition on a historic structure, trying to determine the timeframe of when they enclosed it, is it historic or an add-on, was it part of the 1950 renovation or prior. Mr. Lewis stated that the porch addition has been there for as long as he has been alive. He stated that it was definitely prior to 1955. He stated that in 1952, his father took full possession of the property from the rest of the heirs. He stated that between 1952, 1957 and 1958 was when his father made many of the other changes. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the porch enclosure, specifically, was it done during the 1952 renovation. Mr. Lewis stated that it is possible, because he was born in 1955; however, for the entirety of his life, it was a kitchen area. Ms. Dickson asked how much of the lot will this be taking up. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Pohlman stated that sizing for both the Board of Architectural Review (BAR) and impervious. Mr. Cope stated that what they are taking out and adding back is compliant with the under 40% once the large accessory structure is removed. Ms. Dickson asked if he was referring to the garage. Mr. Cope responded in the affirmative. Ms. Dickson stated that it looks so large on the drawings and said that there does not appears to have any lot remaining. Ms. Giovingo stated that there is still quite a bit in the front. Mr. Keenan stated that the total heated square footage of the house is 3,960. Mr. Pohlman stated that porches would add another 1,225 square feet. Mr. Rowe stated that she applauds the photographs and the research. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his only concern has nothing to do with how it is design. He stated that when a partial demolition on a historic structure is being requested, which the Commission does review, convincing evidence of areas being demolished needs to be illustrated as not being historic and not worthy of preservation. He stated that his only two reservations are on the porch enclosure, which clearly was an addition; it is a matter of when. He stated that sometimes these additions become part of the historic structure, even if they are added on later. He stated that on the dormers, it is clear that originally the photograph indicates what is a preferably design. However, when was the shed dormer added and is that a part of the historic structure. Mr. Cope stated that it is really a very large gable. Mr. Hirshorn asked when the large gable was added and is it incorporated into the historic structure, although it was not original, and is it worthy of preservation. He stated that these are reservations that should be discussed. Ms. Rowe stated that if you have the first photograph of the house, estimated to be 1870, it should supersede anything that was done after that, because it is the original home. Mr. Dickson stated that this is a constant battle with preservation societies. Linda Balzac, stated that the additions are clearly 1950’s as it was a big thing to put the big dormers with terrible pitches on the front of houses. She stated that it is clearly not original to the house. She stated on that the left side is a fill in and poor one at that. She stated that what is being proposed is an exceptional job of renovating a historical house. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan stated that the most important element is the main historic structure and stated that he does not have an issue with the architecture and stated that the homeowner and potential homeowners have done a good job presenting the case and providing sufficient information on a timetable. Mr. Hirshorn stated that for a point of order, do the prospective homeowners need to apply for both the demolition and approval of the plan. He stated that it would be a two part process, where the applicant would provide grounds for demolition, which the Commission would consider for approval, and then consideration of the plans. Mr. Pohlman stated that there would have to be two motions. Mr. Hirshorn stated that there are specific grounds for demolition for historic structures and the application would be based on one or more of those grounds. Mr. Keenan stated that the application shows that it is for Final Review for Additions and Alterations. Mr. Pohlman stated that he neglected to state that it was for demolition as well. He stated that this was part of the staff review, which was for demolition as well. Ms. Rowe stated that it appears that the evidence for underneath the house is in order, as to what may be demolished. She mentioned that there are zoomed in photographs clearly indicating different eras. Mr. Hirshorn stated that one of the recent projects similar to this is the St. Andrews Church where the partial demolition of a historic structure was approved based on the nature of the non-historic section that was added on and not essential to the historic structure. He stated that it is clearly available, but requires a separate motion. Mr. Pohlman stated that it may be two separate motions under the same application. Mr. Keenan stated that this would be final. Mr. Hirshorn stated that this should be stated for the record. Ms. Rowe made a motion to approve the demolition at 304 Morrison Street as it has shown to be contemporary. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the burden must fall on the applicant to present the ground of demolition. Mr. Pohlman stated that first and foremost, there is a motion on the floor. A second is required prior to discussion. Motion fails due to lack of a second. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he is still not clear on which grounds as there are specific grounds for demolition that are denoted in the guidelines. He Old Village Historic District Commission

stated that the applicant must actually state what those grounds are. Mr. Hirshorn suggested looking at the Ordinance for demolition. Mr. Cope stated that according to the letter from the engineer, he states that it could potentially be a dangerous structure. Mr. Keenan stated that on the application, this item is up for final review for addition and alterations; however, there is no demolition on the application. He stated that additionally, the reasons are not cited. Mr. Pohlman stated that there are two demolition requests within the submitted packet at this time. One is for the accessory structure and the partial demolition on a historic structure. Mr. Keenan asked if those requests were made last month. Ms. Giovingo responded in the affirmative. Mr. Pohlman stated that it was part of the conceptual. There was a formal notice that the applicant’s intention was for demolition. Mr. Keenan stated that this would make the application incomplete. Ms. Giovingo asked if the application could be approved tonight and they would provide a more complete application with a few days. She asked for it to be approved with the language that they could bring back in the application. Mr. Pohlman stated that item #1 would be for the addition, as well as the porch bump out; #2 the carport area; and (3) the metal shed. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he is agreeable with the carport and the new construction; the addition that is going to be remodeled. He stated that the dormers and the porch would fall under #1 and is it A, B, or C. Mr. Cope stated that “A” for the dormers. He stated that having examined them, you are able to tell that that floor is framed in the large gable. He stated that the additional dormer was not built as solid as the other, and this is the same conclusion that the engineer had in his findings. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to approve the partial demolition of 304 Morrison Street on the main structure under demolition ordinance 1.A. and on the accessory structure and addition under 3.A.; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor, with Ms. Wilson recusing. Mr. Hirshorn stated that in reference to the hyphen, it appears that it is a two story. Mr. Cope stated that it is an open stair hall that is flanked by a porch on one side and an enclosed porch on the other side to minimize the connection. He stated that it is purely transportation to make the master suite away from the main house to pay homage to the main structure. Mr. Keenan stated that under the three bay windows on the right, is that the actual roll up garage or will the owners be driving up under the porch. Mr. Giovingo stated that there is a garage under. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan asked if they are double doors. Mr. Cope stated that it will be a garage door that is completely set and custom built to match all the louvers and you will not be able to distinguish that it is a door. Mr. Keenan asked if there was anything under the porch and if it was just open. Ms. Giovingo responded in the affirmative. Mr. Keenan asked what the small space to the left is – the one that is open. Mr. Cope stated that it is to distinguish that it is an entrance. Ms. Rowe made a motion to approve 304 Morrison Street as submitted for final additions and alterations; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor with Ms. Wilson recusing. Motion carries.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Mr. Jake Whiley and Ms. Lauren Whiley, owners, reviewed the application with the Commission.

Ms. Robin Colman, 118 Pitt Street, expressed concern with the raised HVAC system at 304 Morrison Street, as it is extremely noisy and an eyesore. She shared video of the HVAC unit with the Commission. She expressed concern with the use of a chain link fence and brick walkway to the rear of the Morrison Street property. Mr. Chris Coleman, 118 Pitt Street, expressed concerns with the HVAC unit at 304 Morrison. He suggested that the HVAC unit can be viewed from Morrison Street. suggested that the request involves a zoning variance that the Commission does not have purview to review and approve. He asked that the request be denied.

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman stated that the applicant is requesting the extension of the COA (Certificate of Occupancy Application), which is listed under 156.433(A4) indicating that they are allowed to request such. Lisa Thomas, 204 Venning Street – stated that she is the owner and it was first approved when she purchased the property. addition so that he is able to move in with her. She stated that it is a garage, but it is 2 stories and her father would stay upstairs. Mr. Keenan stated that there are now new guidelines on ADU’s (accessory dwelling units). Ms. Thomas stated that there is no plumbing in it; only an open room for her father to sleep. She stated that there is a bathroom in the main house that he would use. Ms. Wilson asked if it was a connected unit. Ms. Thomas responded in the affirmative. Ms. Wilson asked Ms. Thomas if she remembers the height on the unit. Mr. Sam Lisi (contractor) stated that it is under the main house. Ms. Thomas stated that it is set back. Ms. Linda Balzac stated that it is attached to the main house and not higher that the house. Mr. Lisi stated that it actually falls under the eave.
