label: 108 Carr Street
request: 108 Carr Street – Survey 6269 – Final Review for Accessory Structure and Addition [Consent Motion]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Michael Taliercio, stated that he is a residential builder and designer with Charleston Drafting Company and is representing the homeowners, Stephen and Charlette Zacharkiw. He stated that they requested his services to resolve some issues on their site. He stated that the first issue is storage. He stated that this home is not historic and was built in 2011. He stated that it does not have a garage or storage shed. He stated that they have two small children and do not have an area to put bicycles, toys, beach items, tools, etc. He stated that they would like to request having a storage shed on the property and would only be accessible from the outside. He stated that it would encroach into the setback. He stated that it does not encroach into the accessory setback. He stated that they do not have another area on the lot to put the storage shed, and stated that they would keep it as minimal as possible so as not to encroach into the side setback and also to have a path to get to the backyard. The property to the left is the confederate cemetery. He stated that it is wide open at this time and the homeowners would like to put a pool in the back, but would also like to have a covered seating area. He stated that since it is wide open, they would like to put up some screening, but not so much as they would like to have some airflow. He stated that there are two grand trees, which the homeowners discussed with the Town arborist last year. The Town arborist suggested that the homeowners hire a licensed arborist to dig around the area to check for roots. The arborist did not find roots in that area. Preliminary, the Town arborist stated that he did want to see on the final site plan how all the utilities were connected to the pool house in the back. He felt that they would not be able to accomplish this, because originally they wanted to do an ADU (accessory dwelling unit) with an apartment above it; however, it was too big for the side. He stated that they reduced it considerably; therefore, they do not have a bathroom, Old Village Historic District Commission

kitchen and stated that the grand trees will not be harmed. He stated that regarding the pervious coverage, it could be reduced by taking out the very nice brick lined bluestone walkway in the front. He stated that they are trying to avoid the 2 ½% overage of pervious coverage. He stated that if they have to remove it, they will, and would then install permeable pavers instead. He stated that they will be removing the concrete area in the backyard and put in permeable pavers. Ms. Rowe asked if Mr. Taliercio has the elevation of what the proposed storage shed will look like. Mr. Taliercio stated that he has a conceptual drawing. He stated that the main massing of the home is brick and stated that he believes that the living room in the back is done with wood lap siding and they would be matching the lap sidings. He stated that this is also a bump out and not part of the main massing of the home. He stated that they would still like to use the brick as part of the project. He stated that the pool deck will be a brick wall with brick row lock, and will have bluestone pavers on top of that. He stated that they will take some of the brick elements from the main house. He stated that the chimney on the main house is stucco and they will be matching that and do brick detailing. Mr. Keenan asked how many inches the pool is raised. Mr. Taliercio stated that the lot is hilly and said that it drops down. He stated that the pool is at level ground on the left side of the property and then comes up a little over two feet. He stated that they are not going to put a fence on the main pool deck itself, but will be along the property lines. Ms. Dickson asked what they will do if the Zoning Board does not allow more square footage. Mr. Taliercio stated that this is 40% on this lot compared to other lots in the neighborhood and does not feel it would be too significant. He stated that if they found it necessary to tear out the front walkway, it would be enough square footage to meet the 40%. Ms. Dickson stated that she has looked at it and it appears that the entire lot will be used up. Mr. Taliercio stated that he was careful with all the calculations to include everything and is confident in his numbers. He stated that the home is over 25% of the lot. He stated that it will be right at the maximum. Mr. Keenan asked if Mr. Taliercio has the elevation of the proposed fence. Mr. Taliercio stated that the homeowners have not yet decided; however, it will be a four foot fence. He stated that they would like to do a privacy fence. Ms. Wilson stated that although the house is not historic, it faces a historic cemetery so the elevation is very sensitive. She stated that the Commission Old Village Historic District Commission

will want to see different details in the elevation, but also thinking about how the pool elevation reads is going to be really important. She stated that if it were a different lot, she would not have an issue with the accessory setback; however, because of the historic nature of the cemetery, it is extra sensitive. She stated that even tying in the way Mr. Taliercio has to the brick, he must strip that brick and wag into the side and said it will be difficult. She said for the cabana, she would like to see it relate more to the house. She stated that the pitch should be the same. Mr. Taliercio stated that he matched it more with the front porch, which has a lower pitch. Ms. Wilson stated that it is a gable. She stated that if Mr. Taliercio were bringing a porch roof off of it, but it is a structure, so it needs to match the main rooflines. She stated that there are closed gables and Queen Anne returns and then it goes to a chunkier rafter detail with more of a timber detail. She stated that this is something that the Commission has been struggling against where the ADU’s and Accessory Structures are popping up and do not relate to the house. She stated that whether the house is historic or not, she would like for this to look like one property. She stated that she appreciates the use of the brick and bluestone, tying it together that way; however, she would want to see some of these connections in the elevations and architecture, as well. She stated that on the chimney, the shoulders need to come down and be classic shoulders or do a straight run; however, it is difficult to screen against those. She stated that another way to do this is to do straight up, which is similar to what the main house does, although angled, still a more contemporary straight chimney. Mr. Keenan stated that this is a very unique lot and where it sits, with heavy visibility from Royall Avenue. He stated that the accessory structure it too large for the yard. He asked Mr. Taliercio for the dimensions of the pool. Mr. Taliercio stated that it is 14 ½ x 8 feet. Mr. Keenan stated that he would like to see a much smaller accessory structure. He mentioned that they need to be more sensitive to the surroundings. He also agrees with Ms. Wilson on the chimney design and does not feel that the structure is not in keeping with the house. He stated that if it were not visible from Royall to the cemetery, he may feel a little differently; however, that area has prominent visibility. He stated that he would like to see everything scaled back on the accessory structure. He stated that the Commission will need more information on the fence and in reference to the storage shed, he is okay with it. He stated that the Commission needs to see more detail. Ms. Rowe echoes the comments regarding the storage shed, as it looks like it is stuck on the side of the house. She stated that she would need to see a more detailed drawing. She stated that the pool cabana appears very large to her and said it is too big for this lot. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Taliercio stated that he previously had an ADU that was too large, and kept on scaling it down. He stated that they felt this met the minimum needs to start. He stated that they attempted to take some of the elements from the main home; however, they can make the whole structure smaller. He stated that he is a little concerned that if they make the roof steeper, they may not be below the 15 foot. Ms. Wilson stated that perhaps a portion could go towards the equipment so you are able to get the extra things out of sight and clean it up. Ms. Dickson stated that there will still be a big structure in the backyard. Ms. Dickson stated that she is more concerned with the pool equipment screenings things that stand out when you are driving down the street. She stated that she would be more inclined to allow the size of the structure, if they would eliminate the pop on items. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he echoes the comments on the size. Ms. Wilson stated that it would be good to obtain and picture from Royall Avenue of the house as it is, and whether it is 3D or cut out, to show the Commission what it would look like. Mr. Keenan stated that he believes Mr. Taliercio has been provided with good feedback and stated that the Commission feels that this is too big for the yard.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Michael Tuliercio, Charleston Drafting Company, representing property owners, Stefan and Charlotte Zacharkiw. He said that at the conceptual review in June, the main consensus was that the pool structure was too big and the mechanical pad next to the pool was too much. He said that the lot coverage at that time exceeded 40% and they were asking for two and a half percent, which they would have had to go before BOZA prior to final approval from OVHDC. He said that they did take the footprint of the pool house and shed on the side of the house down, it made the lot coverage less, just over 1% of the 40%. He said that they then changed the front walk from brick to a permeable brick walk. He said this way they will not need to go before BOZA as they are no longer exceeding the 40%. He said that in the back of the house, there is a large section to the left of the home that is open. He said they are proposing to put the shed there. He said that the encroachment into the side setback is because the shed is attached to the building so it is considered part of the main structure. He stated that the shed footprint is not exceeding the accessory setback. He said he understands it must be approved as part of the main house. He said that the pool house was considered too large, so they lowered it 14% less. He said the roof pitch was also a concern, so they took comments from the Commission to make it match the main house. He said they also changed the eave return to more closely resemble the main house. He said that the fireplace in the rear was also considered too large, so they made it smaller to match the existing chimney on the main Old Village Historic District Commission

house. He said that they also removed the pool equipment pad and moved it to where the air conditioning equipment is currently located next to the main house, so it would not be in view. Ms. Rowe asked why the chimney is slanted. Mr. Tuliercio said that it is to match the chimney on the main home, which is also slanted. Ms. Rowe stated that she had an issue with the shed, because it is facing the historic cemetery and looks like it is stuck onto the house. Mr. Tuliercio stated that it is a small area site, and with the blank area on the side of the house, it would be a nice area to fill in so it does not look like something is missing. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his issue is the shed. He said if it was the same material as the existing house, it may blend in a little better. Mr. Tuliercio said it is the same material as the back wing of the house Mr. Keenan stated that the shed is attached to the brick section of the house and believes Mr. Hirshorn is saying it would look better if it were brick. Tom Gressette, attorney representing John Henderson, who owns 302 Bank Street, the home behind Mr. Zacharkiw’s home. He stated that he has provided the Commission with a photograph of the backyard, which is a view from Royall Street, through the backyard to the Carr Street backyard, where the project is proposed. He said that this Commission is allowed to/required to protect the welfare, harmony, design and balance of the Old Village. He said that looking at this picture through what used to be the backyard of this lot. He provided Commission members with some history on this lot. He said that no one has ever reviewed this plan as it currently exists, meaning this house on this small lot. He said that no one has even asked if this house fits on this lot. He said that there is no presumption that this house has ever been approved or is, in fact, harmonious. He said that the project does not begin with any assumption that it has been as a parcel subjected to appropriate review. He said when the other portion was severed off, the current owners purchased it and have continued to live there and now the request is to erect a 20 foot A- Old Village Historic District Commission

Frame bathing house/cabana and a swimming pool; thereby interfering with not only the direct view through this area to the historic cemetery. He said that the cabana is going to be six feet from the cemetery and is not harmonious with the Old Village. He said that this backyard has a six foot difference within the backyard where they are proposing to construct. He said that not only is the lot very small, but it is higher than everything around it and is going to be built up with a large structure, increasing impervious surface and the rate of runoff directly into the yard behind it. He said that it is not in the general welfare of the village to have drainage issues. He said that the impervious surface limitation of 40% is not a guarantee or a right to 40% unless it is appropriate with size, scale, streetscape and other considerations. He said that covering half of the lot that sits up on the hill is not appropriate. He said taking out an area in the front to be at 40% does nothing for the backyard and is only a numbers game. He said that the yard is just too small for a pool and a cabana house to exist and is going to block the view and streetscape site to the confederate cemetery. He said that it is also not harmonious with the surrounding properties because it will create a drainage issue. He stated that this will all be directed to the back lot that Dr. Henderson owns. He stated that this cannot be constructed on this property, because the lot is just too small for a pool and a pool house. He stated that in order for the Commission to approve this, they would have to grant certain encroachments. He added that encroachments are special and there is no need for the Commission to grant special encroachments, because the lot is too small. He asked the Commission to review the design, as he feels there is no real design elements or sound protection or drainage protection. He added that, most importantly, there is no relation to the design of the house. He said that he is not aware of any other place in the Old Village with a cabana house that is exposed in this area. He said that if the Commission does not take a step back regarding the 40% impervious surfaces, which is not a guarantee, as well as drainage issues, he said there will continue to be issues. He added that they are friends and neighbors; however, this parcel is too small for a pool, a house, a cabana, a shed, a screened porch, two driveways, and two grand oak trees. He requested that the application be denied. Old Village Historic District Commission

Stephan Zacharkiw, property owner, stated that they did not design the house, but only purchased the home. He said that if they had designed it, many things would have been different. He said that he has two small children and the picture that was provided earlier on the side of the house, is a cleaned up version of the side yard. He said that requesting the storage unit is not out of greed, but necessary as they do not have any storage. He said that this is not about maximizing the footprint. He said in reference to a special encroachment, this would be the only encroachment they would be asking. He said that he is not an attorney, but Mr. Gressette is, by profession, and is also his neighbor. He said that from the first day, he has involved all the neighbors and has gone out of his way to let the neighbors know what they were proposing for well over a year. He said that Mr. Gressette was also talking about putting in a pool and another structure. He said that it is incredibly frustrating, because a sign has been outside of his home for a number of months and discussions have been ongoing for well over a year. He said that it disappoints him that Mr. Gressette wants to appear as an attorney, not a neighbor, and take this tact. He stated that Mr. Gressette resides at the residence of Mr. John Hunter Henderson. He said in reference to Ms. Dickson’s comments earlier, people were building up and creating a new issue of draining down. He said that they are at high ground and are not trying to create a runoff that is not already naturally there. He said that he cannot help the angle of his property. He stated that the direct impact of anything flowing down is another neighbor, not Mr. Gressette behind him. He said that it is very interesting that the neighbors when directly facing their house to the right, flowing downward, they do not have an issue. He said that this is the only issue, in the final hour, and not brought up in advance. He said from what he has learned this evening, this is all about approving the design aspects. He said that he is happy to work with any engineering suggestions. He said that he would like to point out some of the comments that Mr. Gressette mentioned of how their view of the cemetery is no longer going to be intact. He said that between Mr. Gressette’s garage, the trees and their fence line, he does not believe this is a worthy impact. He said that Mr. Gressette mentioned that he, too, was planning on putting in a pool and cabana. He said that Richter Way Old Village Historic District Commission

has an example of a standing outdoor cabana living space such as what he is proposing. Mr. Gressette stated that he has no legal ownership of Mr. John Hunter Henderson’s home and has been retained by Mr. Henderson to make this presentation. Mr. Gressette stated that in reference to the fencing on the backyard, it would be appropriate if that fencing was staggered down the hill and a rear elevation showing that, with coping underneath to help with drainage. Ms. Rowe stated that since this was initially brought to the Commission, she believed it was too much for such a small lot. She said that going down Royall Avenue, it is very visible. She stated that she is opposed to the shed on the side. (Ms. Wilson returned to the meeting at 7:09 p.m.) Mr. Hirshorn stated that he has less of a problem with a shed as long as it was more incorporated with the existing brick home, both in material and in attempting to match the roof height with some of the porch heights. He said that this would not be a significant change to the streetscape. He said that the Commission has a tendency to avoid pool constructions that are in view of the right-of-way and attempt to have them somewhat hidden from the streets. He said that they do, in fact, alter the streetscape. He said that this case, in particular, the fact that there is a cemetery adjacent to it, some sensitivity should be considered. He said that he would like to hear discussions on how to address the pool and cabana and if the new construction would have any impact on the existing streetscape. Mr. Keenan stated that he has served on this board for four years and is in favor of property rights and does not want to dictate what property owners would like to do with their property. He said that his thoughts are that the cabana is out of place and possibly too large. He said he would like to work with Mr. Zacharkiw on the shed, but feels that it should be brick coming off that side of the house. He understands there is siding off the back; however, that section is not attached to the siding portion of the home. He said that it does not even look appropriate in the drawing. He said if there is a way to create something different, he would be in Old Village Historic District Commission

favor. He said that he is struggling with the shed being in plain view, because the view corridor is significant from both Bank Street and Royall Avenue. Ms. Dickson said that she is trying to determine if there is some other way to move the storage shed somewhere else. She asked about the height of the shed. Mr. Taliercio said that it is eight feet. Ms. Dickson asked if it could go under the windows, on another side of the house. Mr. Taliercio stated that in the front there is no room and may be possible to move the HVAC equipment that is on the backside of the house, but then it would be in the side setback. Ms. Dickson stated that she agrees with the comments from other Commission members, as space is limited; however, sympathizes with the homeowner. Mr. Taliercio stated that since it is a small lot, 40% is much different from other projects that have larger lots. He stated that they are attempting to shrink everything down as much as possible, while still trying to meet the homeowner’s needs. He said the pool house looks a little bigger although it is smaller, because they did raise the roof pitch. Ms. Dickson asked about only having the pool without the cabana. Mr. Taliercio said this is ideal for his client’s request. He said originally it was an ADU with living space above. He asked if it was possible to have the cabana and the pool, or is there no size that is small enough. He asked if the Commission could provide input on whether the pool house/cabana is acceptable at all in any type of design or if the Commission feels it is just not appropriate. Ms. Wilson stated that she has a bigger issue with the shed than the cabana. She stated that it should be taller and look more like it is part of the house. She stated that if they go with siding, she would suggest a window. She stated that there is no drawing of the front porch on the left side elevation and if it were present, you could see how it is out of relationship with the first floor of the house. She stated that there is a Old Village Historic District Commission

way to make it look like it is part of the house. She said that they are working around a vent and they could duck that through the storage area and end up with more storage. She stated that storage such as kayaks could be lifted high. She stated that brick would be great if they could match the exact brick, and since it is not a historic house, the brick should not be too hard to locate. She said if they are not able to match the brick and kept the siding, a window with a shutter or fixed shutter, so that it does not look like a shed, but an extension of the house, would be more appropriate. She stated that in reference to the cabana, she asked if the homeowner would be more open to doing louvered or paneled shutters to dress it up, because it is on the thoroughfare and the entrance to the Village. She stated that instead of the three quarter fencing wall, something that has the louvered ventilation. She stated that they are also going to want the privacy. She said that she feels that they should be able to have a pool and the cabana, but take a few feet off. She said perhaps a 12 or 13 x 18, taking it away from the tree and relate it to the pool and not the stairs, and have a slightly smaller landscape folly element character with all those trees and cemetery. She said it seems like it would be more in place with the amount of land in the back. She stated that those are her concerns. Mr. Taliercio stated that he would discuss this with the homeowners; however, believes they will be open to making the shed taller, because they would like to have as much storage as possible. He said in reference to the slats on the cabana itself, they assumed that the privacy issue would be addressed with the perimeter privacy fence so that it would be blocked from Royall Avenue as far as seeing anyone in the cabana or at the pool. Mr. Keenan asked if the example of the fence is shown. Mr. Pohlman stated that it is. He stated that the fence would be around the rear and side yard. Ms. Wilson stated that the architect has gone through the effort to make the roof and the fascia relate to the house and the house is a traditional house, so she would argue that the louvering and/or screening should continue in that vein. However, because this is someone else’s front yard, it needs to be more respectful and keep it more in concert with the Old Village Historic District Commission

existing house. She said that continuing with the vocabulary of the house, like it was done with the roof, is more appropriate, because it really is a front yard and is perceived that way. Mr. Taliercio stated that it is the type of detail in the Old Village, but not in the historic district. Ms. Wilson stated that she realizes that it is their backyard, but it does have a very front presence on Whilden Street and they must also be respectful of the cemetery and make sure that the facades that are facing it are harmonious so that the whole composition and elevation all works together. Mr. Taliercio stated that on the fence detail, he has a note on the site plan saying that putting that fence along the rear property line is contingent upon approval from the neighbor in the back. He said that the issue with the existing fence is that it would not be appropriate for a pool enclosure, so they would need to work with the neighbor. Mr. Gressette stated that he understood that a fence on a corner lot could not be higher than a specified height. He said that he does not believe there is an issue working out the details of a staggered fence that would be suitable. He said the question would be whether the landowner is able to put the fence all the way around the back of Bank Street or have a staggered 5 ½ foot fence and then go to a 42” picket fence. Mr. Keenan stated that the Commission would have to look at the fence more in detail when they come back. He stated that he believes the homeowner received positive feedback. Mr. Zacharkiw stated that the feedback is very helpful and is very much amenable to what has been said. He said that it is currently an eyesore for the neighborhood and just wants to finish the backyard. Ms. Wilson made a motion to defer 108 Carr Street, pending further study, with the request to draw the full left side elevation as seen from the cemetery so the front porch, storage, cabana, pool ledge and fence are seen; seconded by Mr. Hirshorn. All present voted in favor. (Mr. Hirshorn departed at 7:24 p.m.) Old Village Historic District Commission
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Ms. Wilson made a motion to move this item to the end of the list; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

label: 909 Royall Avenue
request: 909 Royall Avenue – (Survey 5983) – Final Review for Alterations and Additions

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Linda Balzac, architect representing the homeowners, stated that the home was built in the 1970’s and stated that the height, scale and mass is similar to the other houses on that street. She stated that the homeowner wishes to make the four foot deep front porch, ten feet deep as they spend a great deal of time in the front. She stated that they have an exceptionally small lot at 7,500 square feet and they are proposing to enlarge the home to 2,160 square feet. She stated that they are getting very close to the 40% rule and they will be matching existing details as far as the siding on the dormer. She stated that they will be replacing most of the windows with two over two instead of the six over six and it will be a carriage style door that will be a composite just to provide a little detail to where the garage is. She stated that they need a little family room and kitchen, and will be moving the laundry room from the garage to the first floor. Ms. Dickson asked if the tree in the front yard will be affected. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Balzac stated that it would not. She said that she change the direction of the stairs instead of coming straight off the porch. She wanted to have a sense of a staircase. Ms. Wilson stated that she is not able to figure out how Ms. Balzac is going to accomplish this, because the porch roof is now going to come out in front of the gable and lap over the return. Ms. Balzac stated that it is going to lap over the return and come straight out past it. She stated that she did not draw it correctly on the front elevation. It should be covered. Ms. Wilson asked about the size of the windows over the dormers, relative to all the other ones, the elevations are taller and narrower and she would like to have them the same as the other windows. She stated that she likes the two over two for this house, because it is such a small house. Ms. Dickson asked if the addition would violate the ratio. Ms. Balzac stated that it would not. She said that it is currently 28.8% and with the additions, will go up to 38.9% and BAR is at 32.26%. She stated that was 1,600 square feet and going to 2,160 square foot house. Ms. Wilson stated that the homeowners also get allowances on this home. Ms. Balzac stated that they do, but the homeowners did not want to take any at this time. Mr. Hirshorn stated that on the left and right side elevations, the roofline appears to be off. He stated that it is difficult for him to see it on a one dimensional drawing, as well as the three windows that appear to be out of context. Ms. Balzac stated that those three windows are over a bed. She stated that she is attempting to keep some privacy on that side, because the house next door is close. She said if you look at the rear elevation, it goes to a gable. She stated that there is the 6 and 12 pitch that matches the existing gable roof and she did not want it to be one long shed, so she popped the gable up to tie into the main house with a 6 and 12 pitch at the family room and brought the shed dormers down at 3 and 12, because they are normally a shallower pitch so all the soffits can tie together and not go over the ridge that is existing. Ms. Wilson asked if the two were coplanar and if there was really a corner there. Ms. Balzac stated that it currently does not have a corner, but there can be a little bit of an indent. She stated that the house is a box currently and they will continue the lines of the existing walls out. She stated that when she has done this before, put a corner board so that the siding just doesn’t continue as a mass so that it looks like a corner, but it is a single piece. Mr. Keenan stated that there is a thirteen foot addition across the back, replacement windows at all existing windows that will remain, new ten Old Village Historic District Commission

foot deep front porch with stairs, new carriage style garage door at existing opening and a new dormer over the garage door, where the windows will match the regular windows. Ms. Wilson stated that in reference to the false corner, she stated that it will lose the whole rake and will go and bend out. Ms. Balzac stated that it will be the same depth, but it is a little wider than the rest of the house currently. Ms. Wilson asked if the shed piece could be pushed in at least four inches. Ms. Balzac stated that she would prefer to push it in six inches. She stated that she would do that on both sides of the house. Ms. Wilson stated that the main front would stay intact when the additions go in. She stated that although not in the Commission’s purview, the tree is very close. Ms. Balzac stated that it is, but it is a River Birch that is nearing the end of its life cycle. Ms. Wilson moved to approve 909 Royall Avenue, as long as the addition is inset six inches on both sides on the primary gable and the windows are consistent and proportioned; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

label: 106 Center Street
request: 106 Center Street – (HISTORIC 6046.00/ 6046.01) – Final Review for Alteration to Hardscape and Accessory Structure

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Linda Balzac, architect representing the homeowners, stated that they extended the roof on the existing accessory structure after she did the calculation and she will amend this. She stated that they will still be in a good space. Ms. Balzac stated that this is her family homestead and her parents resided here and currently, her sister resides here. She stated that the terrace has always been small for the six grandchildren and now that the coping of the bluestone is failing at the waterside of the bluestone, she would like to put a deck level with the side of the pool and take the bluestone out and step out with terracing in the yard. She stated that there is significant drop that is visible, which is a hill. She stated that the retaining wall is still in great shape and then it goes down to the yard. She stated that they would like to keep the accessory structure. She stated that there are holes in the roof. The kayaks and paddle boards are tucked under. She stated that they would like to put in a seating area which is right next to the deck and would like to tier the deck down in seating stairs. It will be done in epay wood. She stated that they wanted to tie it to the dock, which has been there many years. She stated that their afterthought was a cantilever roof for kayak storage. She stated that they would also like to screen the accessory structure, which has concrete pavers and would like to extend the epay in there and have almost full height screening with just a door so there is minimal amount of screening Old Village Historic District Commission

as possible (Tru-Screen) to keep it simple and not block the view from the house. She showed the top of the shed which is rotting plywood. It will eventually match the existing roof. She stated that the shed roof does not have a very large pitch so it is not very visible. She stated that they will keep the posts just the way they are. She stated that there is a great deal of growth all around, so the back area is almost invisible from all angles. Mr. Keenan asked if the accessory structure is the same size. Ms. Balzac stated that it is, but they are shifting it over to the left of it three feet to put a rack for the kayaks. Ms. Wilson asked if anyone is able to see the backside where the overhang is being proposed. Ms. Balzac stated that there is one neighbor that is able to see it, but it is more attractive than what is presently there. She stated she walked down the impervious surfaces and only a small section of the bluestone has been moved. Ms. Rowe asked if the screening was existing. Ms. Balzac stated that it is. Ms. Wilson stated that she likes the deck and the terrace and going to epay. She stated that the shed is more of a repair. She stated that her concern about the overhang is that too many items will get stacked up on the back side. She asked if Ms. Balzac really needs the bracket. She stated that it is not that big of an overhang if you allow the flat roof to slip over. She stated that the corbel draws attention to the Asymmetry and understand why they want to cover it up. Commission members stated that she really likes the terraced steps. Ms. Wilson moved to approve the hardscape and repair of the shed at 106 Center Street, minus the corbels; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

events.text:

She stated that it was her error. She was unable to submit the application; therefore, the homeowner submitted it herself. before. She stated that the parking pad moved over. She stated that this was approved at the last meeting with a brick line concrete driveway. label: 110 Morrison Street
request: 110 Morrison Street – (HISTORIC 6163) – Final Review for Replacement of Front Porch [Consent Motion]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. William Sparkman Witte “Sparky”, stated that he is a lifetime resident of Mount Pleasant and grew up at 208 Venning Street, therefore, he is very familiar with the Old Village. He stated that he loves the Old Village and does not want anything to harm it. He said that the porch the homeowner has is wood and has been replaced time and time again, even with treated lumber. He presented the Commission with samples of a newer product and stated that he understands the Commission has approved synthetic materials in the past. He stated that they would like to present this product, because when assembled, there are no gaps. He stated that it would be a gray color and the project would take approximately one week to complete. Mr. Keenan asked if this would be installed on the first floor porch. Mr. Witte responded in the affirmative. Ms. Rowe asked if this is an approved material. Mr. Witte stated that the OVHDC has approved other synthetic materials. Ms. Rowe asked if it has been approved by the National Register in 48 states. Mr. Witte responded in the affirmative. Ms. Dickson asked if the house is historic. Mr. Witte replied in the affirmative. Beatrice Weston, homeowner stated that she has lived in her home for 67 years and is not changing the appearance at all. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that if the 48 states have approved this product for National Register and Historic Places replacement, asked if Mr. Witte had any additional information or paperwork, because this is a broad statement. He stated that this Commission has a strict policy on materials for historic porches, casings and windows and this product is not listed. Mr. Witte stated that it has not yet been approved by this Commission, because no one has applied for it yet. He stated that there are other synthetic products that are on the approved list and believes this should be added. Mr. Dickson stated that Mr. Witte would be asking for a variation rather than change of guidelines. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he does not know enough about this material and it is rare for the Commission to receive applications for synthetic porches, particularly on historic homes. Mr. Keenan stated that the flooring on the porch is not historic. Ms. Weston stated that it has been replaced a number of times. Mr. Witte stated that this is the latest and greatest synthetic material. Mr. Keenan stated that the Commission is conflicted, because it is not on the Commission’s approved materials list. He understands what Mr. Witte is attempting to accomplish; however, he does not know anything about the product. Ms. Weston stated that her daughter works for a building supply company and has researched this material. She has assured her that this would last many years. She stated that she has replaced the treated wood porch many, many times and it is a nuisance to have to continue to do so. She stated that this new material will look exactly like wood. Sam Lisi, stated that he is a builder in the Old Village and believes this is something that the Commission should begin to look at. He stated that he is pro-historic and keeping the authenticity of a home; however, this has been an ongoing nightmare for many residents. He added that manufacturers over the years, have created a wonderful replacement plank boarding that looks just like wood, and this homeowner is fighting Old Village Historic District Commission

a maintenance nightmare. He believes the Commission is going to need to overcome some of these issues, similar to Hardie plank versus wood. He stated that the porch has minimal exposure. He stated that this is a really good product. Mr. Keenan stated that the artisan Hardie plank is difficult to distinguish from the real wood plank. Mr. Lisi stated that this will help salvage the homeowner’s pocketbook by not having to replace the porch over and over again, and will not disrupt the character of the home. Mr. Hirshorn asked if there were other materials that are on the approved list that have some of the similar features. Mr. Lisi stated that there are some similar; however, the one that Mr. Witte displayed is one of the better materials, because it has the full thickness with a character grain and does not look synthetic. He stated that epay would be the alternate wood product, but the manufacturer recommends that you not paint it, because the oil in the epay is dense and does not hold paint. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the solution is to get this material approved, but does not know how to move forward with this process. He stated that the Commission could look into the approval in the other 48 states and add it to the approved materials list. He stated that currently, there is guideline #5, which must be adhered to. Ms. Dickson asked to refer to Ms. Wilson’s notes. Mr. Hirshorn stated that Ms. Wilson believes that on historical features, approved materials should be utilized. Ms. Dickson asked Mr. Pohlman what the procedure is for getting this new material approved. Mr. Keenan read the guidelines on page 14 relating to porches and stoops. He stated that he would like to work with the homeowner; however, to approve this tonight would be a deviation from the guidelines. Mr. Pohlman read the section in the guidelines under Overall Design, and stated that it indicates that new materials must be approved by the Old Village Historic District Commission

Commission before the application is submitted for COA, with the two applications being separate. He stated that if the Commission approves this material for porches on historic homes, then at the next meeting the COA would be able to be approved. He stated that the material must be approved first and added to the list. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it would take a minimum of two more months. Mr. Pohlman stated that the material could be approved this month and next month, the application could come back for review. Linda Balzac, stated that she would specifically name this PVC, because there are many lower quality PVC materials on the market that are not good. Mr. Keenan stated that anything that would be a lesser quality than this would absolutely not be considered. Ms. Dickson stated the Commission needs to use care in the wording. Mr. Keenan stated that the consensus is that this is for a historic property and the Commission must tread very lightly with this. He stated that the guidelines must be adhered to which is not typically with a historic property. He stated that he would be willing to hold a Special Commission meeting in order to put this material on the table for approval. Ms. Dickson moved to defer 110 Morrison Street until the board has a chance to research the material further; seconded by Mr. Hirshorn. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Old Village Historic District Commission

Sparky Witte, 784 Post Oak Drive, stated that he has been a resident of Mount Pleasant since 1951 and used to live on Venning Street. He stated that he came before the Commission last month to seek approval to replace a porch on a historic home with a new material. He stated that it was deferred in order for the Commission to review the material. Ms. Wilson stated that she does not believe the Commission should approve this material. She stated that the ordinance as written requires that the Commission protect the historic structures with like material. She stated that Mr. Pohlman provided the information citing the Secretary of Interior’s rationale. Mr. Witte stated that he believes in the beginning of what Mr. Pohlman read, it stated that the Commission could vote on changes of different species. Mr. Pohlman stated that this is correct, as this portion of the guidelines does allow for the presentation and election of new material. Mr. Witte stated that this is the latest and greatest material available. He stated that the property owner is simply attempting to protect her porch from having to go through the expense of replacing it every five years. Ms. Rowe stated that she understands as her home has a large wrap around porch, which requires a great deal of maintenance. She stated that her feeling is that the Commission does not know enough about the material and there are too many of these synthetic materials. She stated that the Commission must go with what the Secretary of Interior’s standards are, because it is not an approved material. Ms. Wilson stated that additions and new construction is different. She stated that there are only a small number of historic houses left that do have original material and it is part of the OVHDC’s guidelines and ordinance to protect those homes. Mr. Witte stated that he grew up in this Town and is in favor of preservation; however, he also sees what goes on behind this Commission’s back. Ms. Dickson stated that although it does state that another material may be accepted, currently this material is not accepted. She stated that this Old Village Historic District Commission

Commission does attempt to be vigilant about as many of the historic homes that are left in the Old Village as possible; however, things do happen behind the Commission’s back. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would concur that the original historic wood material be utilized for porches. He stated that he realizes this does require maintenance; however, the long term value of historic structures in the village has increased by maintaining the historic integrity of the original materials. He stated that porches and windows are likely the two main features of these old historic homes in the Old Village. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to deny the synthetic wood for the use on the historic porch; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present were in favor.

label: 141 Toomer Lane
request: 141 Toomer Lane – Historic 4244 – Applicant is seeking Final Review for replacing fencing. [Consent Motion Approval]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Old Village Historic District Commission

Scott McCormack, said he does not believe any of the changes are major and when they originally went through this process, they were attempting to get the size, scale and massing approved. He said there were details that they did not necessarily show and now that they have gone through the process with the builder, they would like to clarify those. He asked if some of the items could be approved in concept, and then final approval be made at the staff level, rather than come back before the Commission each time they make a change to the roof or soffit. He said they would like to make a general proposal. Mr. Keenan stated for clarification that whatever is being presented to the Commission today is what will be approved. He stated that this Commission will not approve this plan based on the fact that the property owner may want to change their mind moving forward. Mr. McCormack asked if they will need to come back before the Commission each time they decide they want a metal roof versus a shingle roof. Mr. Keenan responded in the affirmative. Mr. McCormack asked if they will need to come back month after month as they go through this process. Mr. Keenan stated that if they are changing the application, yes. Mr. McCormack asked if the decisions could be made at the staff level since everything is within the guidelines for the Old Village Historic District. Mr. Pohlman stated that because it is an approved application and has not received CO (Certificate of Occupancy), it would have to come back to the Commission, because it is an alteration to a set approved plan that staff is unable to overrule. He stated that until it is a finalized structure, has received a CO, and meets all the qualifications as a new construction, the application would have to come before the Commission. Mr. Keenan stated that the roof can be considered today for approval; however, if the applicant prefers to change roof materials, they must come back before the Commission. He stated that if the Commission approves anything today, then this is what must be built. He said if there Old Village Historic District Commission

are any changes, Mr. McCormack must come back before the Commission. Mr. McCormack asked if some of the changes are able to be approved today. Mr. Keenan responded in the affirmative. Mr. McCormack stated that there are elevation changes that they would like to make at one of the windows. He presented photographs of a home on Royall Avenue and Pitt Street to show the detail that they would like to include. Mr. Keenan asked if the only change to the front elevation was the window. Mr. McCormack stated that he would also like to change the railing. He said some of their elevations showed railing and some did not and they are attempting to make it more consistent across all the elevations. Ms. Wilson asked if the overhang detail/soffit was also being changed. Mr. McCormack responded in the affirmative and said it would go from open rafter tail to an enclosed rafter tail, but would keep the same open rafter tail angle, unlike a boxed in soffit. He said that the detail is shown on A6. He said the rafter tail is getting a piece of hardy trim on the two sides and this is an example of the type of soffit that they are looking to do. He stated that they are also proposing that the foundation be changed from stucco to brick. He said in reference to the railing, one drawing shows the front porch with the railing and one without, which is the same with the side elevations. He reviewed other details with the Commission and added that windows were left off in the basement. He said they discovered that the foundation had to be stepped, because it is on a grade and they do not build walls at an angle. Mr. Pohlman stated that this is the subgrade mentioned in the staff report. Mr. McCormack said another thing they had to change is at the proposed elevation; there are no louvers shown where the chimney is located. He stated that the chimney is recessed, so they needed some way to keep the dirt from falling down under the porch. He said they would like to add Old Village Historic District Commission

stairs off the porch for access down into the backyard, and on the rear elevation, they are proposing to add an outdoor fireplace at the bottom of the chimney, which will be a see through box at the base of the chimney. Mr. Keenan asked if it is a dual sided fireplace. Mr. McCormack responded in the affirmative and said it would be more like a firebox and vented into the existing chimney. Ms. Wilson stated that the pitches on the porches will not accommodate shingle because they are too shallow; therefore, they would have to be metal. She stated that without any rendering she is unsure whether the homeowner is proposing some shingle and some metal. Mr. McCormack stated that he was proposing all shingle. Ms. Wilson stated that under a 4/12, you are not able to accomplish this. She said any roof with a pitch less than a 4/12 cannot handle a shingle and will need to be metal. She said there is a situation on the dormers and the rear porch, as well. She stated that she has an issue with a mixed medium viewed from the street and believes the streetscape should have one continuous roof material; therefore, she would like to see the change happen behind the gable. She is fine with the closed rafter detail behind the street front; however, for the cottage look, the one that was referenced on Royall Avenue had a much tighter overhang and a flat soffit, which would be a good look, and to keep it closed. However, the 16 or 18 inch overhang is not compatible with the other changes that have been made, which she does like. She stated that the bay window pop out is a nice touch; however, the wrapped soffit does not work with a hip roof, which is on the garage. She said her suggestion would be that if Mr. McCormack really does not want all the rafter tails for cost, look or maintenance, to bring in all the overhangs and go to a flat soffit and take cues from the house that was included in the packet. She said to consider the metal for the front, because otherwise, there is an issue with the porch roofs. Mr. McCormack stated that it was their intention to have one material on the roof and added that this is exactly the information he is looking for in order to prevent any additional delays in the process. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that on the front elevation, there was mention of brick; however, the Commission would need to see the detail. She said the issue with brick is many times, it is framed to the CMU and then the brick is applied. She said it then flashes out four inches, because the brick is not structural. She said if they are truly using brick, the Commission will need to see the detail on top of the structural section. She said with as little as what will show on the front, she would prefer to see the stucco. Mr. McCormack illustrated what he is attempting to accomplish in a photograph at 630 Pitt Street, which shows more detail. Ms. Wilson stated that what was done at the 630 Pitt Street residence is a brick water table, which is nice; however, without seeing this detail drawn, it would be a large piece of flashing instead of the brick water table that is sitting on top of the foundation wall. She stated that lastly, she prefers no railing; however, the issue with the illustration is the columns and posts have nothing tying them together. She said that she would have some concern about that, and perhaps the stair should go all the way from the right hand gable to the first column, then pick up the hand rail, otherwise there are too many verticals with nothing horizontally tying them in together. She said without a rail, the newel posts are not structurally sound. Mr. Keenan said he feels the railing looks better. Mr. McCormack stated that on the original drawing, one elevation shows the railing and one does not. Ms. Wilson stated that a railing is not necessary on the side porch. Mr. McCormack said they were attempting to have consistent drawings from one elevation to the next. Ms. Wilson asked Mr. McCormack what they wanted to do. Mr. McCormack stated that they opted for no railings. Ms. Wilson stated that in this case, the stairs need to change to go from rail into house if that is the proposal. She stated that what is being proposed now does not work. Mr. Keenan stated that the Commission would need to see a new drawing to determine if the metal roof needs to stay. He added that he prefers the Old Village Historic District Commission

railing, but if that is not what they want, then the Commission will also need to see new drawings on this. He added that if Mr. McCormack would like to do the brick, the Commission will also need to see that detail. Ms. Rowe stated that without the railings, it changes the entire look of the house and looks unfinished. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his question is regarding the new proposed stair that is external on the side-rear of the home. He said he has an issue with the design and asked if there was an alternative. Mr. McCormack said because there is a tree in the back, they looked at running it straight across the rear elevation; however, it would encroach into the tree zone more so than constructing it the way it is shown in the illustration. Ms. Wilson stated that she also has an issue with this the way it is drawn, because it looks like a 6x6 post. She said she would like to see it cut into the porch or around the back or screened in a way that does not look similar to a beach house; however, without a plan, she is unable to determine where the tree line is. Ms. Rowe suggested running it down from inside the porch underneath the house so you do not see it. Mr. McCormack stated that they did discuss doing a spiral staircase inside behind the louvers as an option; however, it cuts into the porch space considerably. Mr. Keenan said he agrees with the comments by the Commission members and if there is a solution to hiding the staircase, this would be preferable. Ms. Wilson suggested coming out, leaving the porch headed towards the front, but use the foundation as a generous step down into the yard, which would help with the stepping for the grade. She stated that structurally, the builder will step it; however, the mason can slope and stucco the top. She said with the multiple steps and a different louver at every height, it will need to get cleaned up even if the last step becomes a seat wall or something that allows the bulk of the louvers to be Old Village Historic District Commission

consistent. She said this would clean up this elevation. She also addressed some issues on the back hip porch on A6 illustration. She said that the whole soffit is flat above the doors off the master, and is not the detail that is shown where you are tracing the underside of the rafter. She said it goes back 90 degrees to the porch. She said this is a detail that could be carried around to the front, in order to alleviate the rafter tails, but would make more sense with the hip roofs and lower pitches. Mr. Keenan stated that the application is for final approval; however, the Commission is not able to provide final approval. Mr. McCormack asked about approval for the trim around the water tables and the windows in the basement. Ms. Wilson stated that she does not have an issue with the windows; however, the wood water table would change if the brick is done. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve two windows in the ground floor level and defer the decision on all the details relating to overhang and foundation details on the application for 141 Toomer Lane; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Ms. Wilson said this item was approved; however, the Commission needed to review the type of window being installed. Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Mr. Keenan stated there was a consent motion earlier to approve this item as submitted; however, Mr. McCormack advised the Commission that the windows they were proposing to install are vinyl. Scott McCormack, stated that their original drawings that were approved and submitted did not have a window detail associated. He said they are proposing a vinyl window and said the approved materials does not specify. Mr. Keenan asked if the windows were originally wood. Mr. McCormack stated that wood clad was put on the application, but it was not indicated on the drawings. He said when he spoke with staff, he was advised that they had to use a wood window. Ms. Wilson stated that Anderson is a vinyl clad wood window. Mr. McCormack stated that this window is vinyl on both sides. Ms. Wilson asked if it would be an SDL. Rob Burke, stated that this is the pattern one vertical zero horizontal. Ms. Wilson stated that the window has large plastic flanges and things that would not be seen on a vinyl clad window. Mr. Keenan stated that he is not sure if all vinyl windows are allowed in the Old Village. Mr. McCormack said that on the approved building materials list, it indicates that they are. Mr. Keenan asked why all vinyl. Mr. McCormack stated that it is a superior window as far as durability. He said on the inside they would be covered with plantation shutters. Ms. Wilson asked if they have installed these windows in historic neighborhoods. Jeremy Rathft, stated that they have in many of the barrier islands and all throughout Florida. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that her concern is the way it is angled and does not see how it is trimmed or cased on the exterior. She asked how they would case the windows. Mr. Burke stated that it would be cased just as you would a wood clad window, right up to the flange. Ms. Wilson stated that they would have to angle cut the casing material or it will have a huge revealer on the outside. Mr. Keenan stated that it is difficult for him to base his decision off the window being shown, because there are a number of big windows on this home and a feature of the house. He said their concern as a Commission is that they do not see many all vinyl requests. He stated that the guidelines only indicate “high quality” vinyl. Mr. Hirshorn asked about the actual guideline on windows, not the materials, but the guideline itself. Mr. Keenan asked if Commission members are comfortable with how the windows will be cased. Ms. Wilson said that she does not see how it can be accomplished. She said if the Commission approves the windows, then there will be another revisit on how the exterior trim will be done, because you would have to angle cut the side of all the casing around. Mr. McCormack said that his builder has been able to come up with ways to tie things together. He said they are putting artisan siding on the side of the house and are not trying to come up with a cheap way. He said that there have been issues with aluminum in coastal environments. Ms. Wilson stated that her concern is the hanging flange and how it is actually going to be installed and trimmed. Mr. McCormack stated that if it is vinyl wood, the wood is on the inside. Ms. Wilson stated that the window is inset, so you have the flange that is going on the cased opening, but then it is set back in the opening so there is a different shadow line and it looks like a window that is more historic, although it is clad and vinyl. She stated that the vinyl window that is being proposed is surface mounted, picture frame and it is an entirely different installation that is going to look different. She said that Anderson is vinyl Old Village Historic District Commission

clad wood and even their 400 has a historic application/installation setup, which is their vinyl window. She said the Commission has approved this. Mr. McCormack said that this is what would have been helpful to the homeowner when looking at the materials list. Ms. Wilson said that she agrees that it is vague. Mr. McCormack said that the issue from the beginning is that it just said wood clad and stemmed from staff saying that a wood window needed to be installed. Ms. Wilson stated that if you look at all the new construction, they are Anderson or Marvin windows; one is aluminum and one is vinyl. She stated that it is not the vinyl material, but the installation tectonics that will be an issue. She said that the labor for the siding and casing will be challenging for this. Mr. McCormack said that if they can find a vinyl window that allows the casing detail to continue as drawn, will this be acceptable. Ms. Wilson said it would be to her. She said that if they would like vinyl inside, it is up to them, but it is the way it is being shown and detailed. She said there is a sill and casing, and going to the expense of hardy, so a thick wood casing would be used to receive the hardy. She said that they have gone through all the effort and expense to obtain all the great details and the window will sit significantly far forward. Mr. McCormack asked if they can receive approval to change to a vinyl and have the actual model approved at the staff level. Ms. Wilson said that it is a reasonable request to her, but she is only one Commission member. She said if Mr. McCormack sent a cut-sheet with the model and information on the window being installed. Mr. Keenan stated that he appreciates Mr. McCormack bringing up the window issue, because he could have avoided issues with this window from a construction standpoint with casement. Mr. McCormack said that he is out of time, as this will stop the build where they are if he has to wait another month. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson asked if Mr. McCormack is willing to provide cut-sheets this week. Mr. McCormack responded in the affirmative. Mr. Keenan stated that the Commission members could review the cut- sheet for the window and if acceptable, have Mr. Pohlman approve it at staff level. Ms. Rowe stated that she is fine with that option, as long as she is able to review the cut-sheet. Mr. McCormack stated that going forward for others, it would be helpful to have a list of recommended products. Mr. Keenan said that this is a good point to be more specific with the windows. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design, stated that he has used this window on some other projects prior and found it to be a great window; however, does not believe this window should be used in the Old Village. He said it alters the original character. He said the difference between a wood clad window, whether it is clad with vinyl or aluminum is that it still has the wood frame so the shape and size and proportions of the frame of a wood window are still there with a clad window. He said that a vinyl window does not have the strength in the same areas and you end up with the wider flanges. He said it is a great window, but not appropriate for the Old Village. He said when he read “vinyl high quality”, the only one he could compare it to would be a Hensel Stone window, which are extremely expensive which is a steel and fiberglass window. Mr. Keenan thanked Mr. McCormack again for bringing this to the Commission’s attention. Mr. Keenan asked for a new motion for 141 Toomer Lane, regarding all else on the application, excluding the windows. Ms. Wilson moved to amend the approval for 141 Toomer Lane to approve all changes to all elevations and plans, but to exclude the all vinyl Shoreline window and request alternatives to be approved at the staff level. Mr. Keenan reiterated that the Commission is approving the elevations and everything else submitted at 141 Toomer Lane, with the exception of the Old Village Historic District Commission

vinyl windows. He said the applicant is to go back and research this, resubmit to the Commission cut-sheets for staff level approval. Seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

label: 135 Toomer Lane
request: 135 Toomer Lane – Final Review for Hardscape Alterations. [Consent Motion]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Losse Knight, architect, reviewed the original approved site plan where they had one spot footing at the newel post for the stairs. He stated that functionally, aligning the door in option A, makes for a more favorable furniture configuration on the back porch. He stated that they have established this rhythm of having equal bays with the three columns coming across the rear. He said that there are not too many views to the back of the house, so their preference would be to obtain more usability inside the porch floor plan, given that it is not highly visible. Mr. Keenan asked if their preference is Option A over Option B. Ms. Wilson asked if there has been discussion with the Town’s arborist, Eddie Bernard. Mr. Knight stated that they have been attempting to communicate with Mr. Bernard; however, originally they were approved with having the one spot pier which is more of a fencepost without rebar and a small amount of concrete. He said that if Mr. Bernard advises that he is unable to approve Option A, he said that given the structure of the remaining posts to support this and the fact that it hangs on the band Old Village Historic District Commission

board of the porch itself, it could potentially be floated and not encroach into the tree area at all from a structural standpoint, if necessary. Ms. Dickson stated that her only concern is the tree and would like to ensure that the tree is not going to be harmed. She said there were so many beautiful trees on that lane and many have been lost to development. Mr. Knight stated that the nice feature of this landing, is it is an open air where rain and breezes are able to come through. He said that the owners wish to maintain and protect the tree and would not propose this if it were going to be detrimental to the tree. Mr. Keenan stated that he does not see an issue and agrees with Ms. Dickson on ensuring the tree is protected; however, it is out of the purview of the Commission. He said that he does not have an issue with either option A or B. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would defer to Mr. Bernard; however, if Mr. Bernard is agreeable, he would not have an issue. He said that he would like to see some type of clarification from Mr. Bernard. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve Option A at 135 Toomer Lane, as submitted, and have Mr. Bernard make the determination on the tree; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor. Mr. Martschink asked if he could revert to Option B, if Mr. Eddie Bernard made the decision not to approve Option A, in order not to come back before the Commission. Mr. Pohlman responded in the affirmative and stated that the property owner would need to re-apply and request approval for Option B. He said that the property owner may only build what is approved by the Commission. Ms. Rowe asked if another motion may be made to approve both options. Mr. Pohlman said that he would not recommend it. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Martschink asked if the column spacing could be approved in order for them to finish the porch. Ms. Wilson stated that this is part of both Option A and B and they can finish the porch and come back before the Commission for the stair. Ms. Wilson amended her motion to approve these items independently; Option A, porch column spacing, stair alignment and shutters at 135 Toomer Lane; Ms. Dickson amended her second. All present voted in favor.
