label: 202 Pitt Bank Street
request: 202 Pitt Bank Street – HISTORIC 5940 Survey 6110 – Final Review for Installation of Retaining Wall. Rev. 03/29/2018 [Consent Motion]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Linda Balzac, architect for homeowner and Sam Lisi, contractor. She stated that the homeowner who recently purchased the property would Old Village Historic District Commission

like to rotate the home so that the long side is facing the road and the short side is now the deck. She stated that the property owners have two smaller vehicles and would like to be able pull them off the street and straight into the garage. She stated that this was already approved approximately two months ago. She stated that when turning the house, it moves three feet back off the street and is intrusive on the property line. She stated that she called this “conceptual” because she thought the guidelines were in effect for the checklist, but everything has already been approved and the homeowner would just like to rotate the home. She stated that she moved one retaining wall over so it is straight for the vehicles, and all materials will match existing and the brick retaining wall will be the same height as it is now. Mr. Keenan asked if the right side elevation is what was originally seen from Bank Street. Ms. Balzac stated that the house is almost a square. She stated that the paperwork towards the back portion of the application is the one that was approved and it has a 19 foot side, which is the front seen from Bank Street. Mr. Keenan asked if this was what was originally approved. Ms. Balzac responded in the affirmative. Ms. Rowe asked if the Bank Street view was still the same. Ms. Balzac stated that it would be two feet wider. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he is still a little confused about what the Commission is approving. Ms. Balzac stated that it is the same footprint; however, the house is being rotated. She stated that they previously had a 14 foot wide garage and would like to rotate the house in order to create more room and pull the cars straight into the garage and off the street. She stated that the current house is being demolished, but the footprint will remain the same; they are just rotating it slightly. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the Bank Street view is a wider view. Mr. Keenan stated that he really likes what is there, but it is being demolished and a new house is being built. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn asked if Ms. Balzac has the elevation for the new proposed garage that is three feet wider, as well as the gable, in relation to the main house. Ms. Balzac stated that she does not. She said the house is 16 feet in one direction and then there are stairs to a second story structure. She stated that there are three or four roof pitches on the house to keep it at 18 feet. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it appears wider and lower to him. Ms. Balzac stated that it is wider and lower. She stated that it is really close to the 10 and 12 pitch that is on the house. She stated that if she went up slightly to get it to the last pitch, she would be fine with that. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it would be difficult to say unless he saw it next to the main house. Mr. Keenan stated that it is lower than what was previously approved. Ms. Balzac stated that it is the same height, but she lessened the pitch. Mr. Hirshorn confirmed that what Ms. Balzac intends to do is rotate the home so that the long side is now the front. Ms. Balzac responded in the affirmative and said that it is only three more feet. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it would be a totally altered streetscape than it currently exists. Mr. Balzac stated that it will definitely look much different than it does currently. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the Commission has been very particular about the accessory structures taking cues from the main residence. Ms. Balzac stated that it does take its cues from the main house, as she did the main house originally, and said that this is the second time working on it. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would have liked to see a new elevation with the new proposed structure in relation to the house. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan stated that it would be helpful. He stated that he prefers the pitch taller and narrower. Mr. Hirshorn stated that everything is shoe-horned in the back area of Bank Street. Ms. Balzac stated that to achieve a taller and narrower pitch, it will need to be slightly higher than 20 feet. Mr. Hirshorn understands the practicality; however, it is difficult to make a decision without seeing it. He stated that the Commission has gone back and forth on many of the applications for this very reason; to ensure the pitches match. Mr. Keenan stated that the ADU is not a pleasant discussion. Ms. Balzac stated that this is not an ADU, but simply a garage for two vehicles and a small loft in the back for their three sons’ swim items. She stated that she has kept the pitch as low as possible on the sides so that it did not go up any higher. She stated that she may need an additional three to six inches to get the pitch at the original pitch. Mr. Hirshorn stated that with the application, he would like Ms. Balzac to provide a drawing where the height and pitch are increased and the streetscape. Ms. Rowe asked how long the original building was from Bank Street. Ms. Balzac stated that it is the same width as the original building, which is 19 feet.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Linda Balzac, architect for the homeowner, stated that one garage was approved at a previous meeting and the homeowner wishes to turn the existing accessory structure, which will remain the same size, so that the wider length is facing the street to allow for a double door. She stated that the structure is actually three feet further off of Bank Street and will allow more parking in a garage and in the driveway, as Bank Street has parking challenges. She stated that one of the requests at the last meeting was to show the proposed garage in relationship to the elevation which is a right side elevation from the harbor which is the front of the garage. She stated that everything is to match existing as per the last Old Village Historic District Commission

submittal that was approved, adding the extra detail for the eave which matches the existing house with all details in place to match the existing structure. She added that the homeowners wish to change out the doors and windows of the main house on the harbor side. She said there are two doors and three sets of windows which are broken up, and because of the view, they wanted to make it more open and simplified, so they proposed three sets of sliders versus five windows and two sets of doors. She stated that they wanted to reduce the muntins, so she kept some at the top to have a proportional light with the same proportion as the windows for detail. Ms. Wilson asked if there was anything in that elevation that is historic or original. Ms. Balzac stated that the home is only ten years old. Ms. Wilson said now that the width of the garage is the same as the gables on the side, she asked why not close the gable and do what was done on the house. Ms. Balzac stated that this is an accessory structure and felt it was too detailed and the eyebrow should not be there. She wanted it to be a little simpler, because it is an accessory structure. Ms. Wilson stated that it is just a very wide gable in relation to the house. Ms. Balzac stated that she feels quite sure the homeowners would be amenable to this if the Commission feels strongly about it. Mr. Pohlman stated that there was an approval and what the homeowners were requesting originally was to rotate the structure 90 degrees for the square footage and keep the detailing the same. He said that the Commission decided that the roof pitch was no longer steep enough and to tighten up the roof pitch, which is why this is before the Commission this evening. Mr. Keenan stated that he likes Ms. Wilson’s suggestion, but feels it is more of a personal preference. John Gaskins, 131 Chicco Lane, stated that looking at the overall appearance, it blends in nicely, because of the left side of the house which flows in with the accessory building. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that his only issue is the proposed sliders on the harbor view, as opposed to the existing doors and windows. He stated that he feels this is a very modern look and an important elevation. He stated that he understands the homeowner wanting a panoramic view; however, feels it is inconsistent with the rest of the house when putting a modern detail on a very traditional looking home. Ms. Rowe stated that she agrees with Mr. Hirshorn’s comments. Ms. Balzac stated that these are Anderson French wood sliders, A series. Ms. Wilson asked if they were clad or wood. Ms. Balzac stated that they are clad with a ten inch toe kick. She provided Commission members with photographs. Ms. Wilson stated that this would be continuous and consistent and she does not have an issue with these sliders. Mr. Keenan added that since Ms. Balzac has provided illustrations of the sliders, he is fine with it and believes the doors will look fine. Ms. Wilson stated that in reference to the accessory building, she feels it should be a closed gable. Ms. Balzac stated that she would be fine with Ms. Wilson’s suggestion. Ms. Wilson said that if it had more of an accessory structure relationship to the house, it would be different, but it is in line with the streetscape so it has a significant relationship with the house. Mr. Keenan stated that it improves the look and asked if the applicant would be agreeable to this. Ms. Balzac stated that the applicant would be agreeable. Ms. Rowe made a motion to approve 202 Bank Street, Final Review for Exterior Alterations and Alterations to Accessory Structure, and changing the gable; seconded by Mr. Hirshorn. All present voted in favor.

label: 436 Church Street
request: 436 Church Street – (HISTORIC 6191) – Final Review for Reroofing of Addition to Historic Structure. (revised 12/4/2017)

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Kate Campbell, Beau Clowney Architects, stated that the house is circa 1850’s and she is doing research on the evolution. She stated that they pulled up the Sanborn maps, which show it has been added on to. She stated that the 1912 Sanborn maps show this home as a gable structure that is more of a t-shape with one story casings on the front and back, with a two-story porch. She stated that at some point the two corners were infilled and the large gable on the side elevation was put in. She said there were significant alterations to that side, but has really remained this core block of a house until the mid-1990’s when the carport structure and one story piece on the backside of the project were added. She showed illustrations to the Commission of the home. She stated that what they are proposing is to add to the rear of the structure with a link, revealing the historic corner which was obscured with the 1990’s addition, alter the kitchen area and pull it back from the main corner, alter the roof slightly, and do a one story living room addition. She stated that they are attempting to follow more preservation minded concepts. She said that landscape and paving plans were received from the owner 24 hours prior to submittal of the application, so they put it on there for reference and are still working with Sheila Wertimer’s office on what the layout will be. She stated that conceptually, she wanted to provide the framework. She stated that one of the owners is an artist and would like an art studio to paint off the living room. She added that they are not in a flood zone. She said that the side setback that they are requesting, the survey shows one corner 2.4 feet off the property line, so they will be encroaching 8.2 feet into the existing required setback. She said that they are stepping the new addition in so they are not going any further into that setback from that corner and will be about 3 feet off. Mr. Keenan stated that the middle section, where the former roof is, will be removed, that is not changing. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Campbell said that the roof will come off and the wall will move back and the other wall becomes the separation between the new kitchen and the old. She says it will feel like a link and then the new building. Batton Kennon, of Beau Clowney Architects added that Ms. Campbell mentioned that the original house has since been altered throughout the years. He stated that there was a t-shaped gable and the backside was one story up until after 1938, when it was changed. Ms. Dickson asked if they would be proposing some type of new gable. Mr. Kennon responded in the negative, as it has since been changed. He stated that the hyphen will have a new roof, because the shed will slope into the new addition. Mr. Keenan stated that it is massive, but the lot is also massive. He stated that he likes the addition and what was done with the porch, extending it out. Ms. Dickson asked if the fireplace is an inside/outside fireplace. Ms. Campbell stated that it is an outside fireplace downstairs, but not on the porch. Mr. Keenan stated that he is fine with the pool and stated that Ms. Wertimer’s landscape plan is out of the Commission’s purview. Ms. Rowe stated that she loves what has been done to take it back to what it should have been. Mr. Hirshorn stated that in reference to the proposed demolition of the addition, he would need more documentation on when it was built and that it is not historic. He stated that although it is an addition, it may still be old. Mr. Kennon stated that their research shows it was done in the mid 1990’s and any request on how this should be done, they would need some direction. Mr. Hirshorn said that how it has been accomplished in the past is documentation with slides on the interior foundations and materials so you can date it through this process. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Campbell stated that the kitchen cabinets are definitely late 1980’s to early 1990’s as well as the appliances. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would refer back to how Ms. Campbell documented the St. Andrews Church demolition of that one section from the historic structure. He stated that he would mimic this process. Mr. Keenan stated that it could also be accomplished through old surveys. Ms. Campbell stated that she could check with the Town on the permit for that time period, and she will submit this with their final request. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it looks great, but it is a substantial increase in the structure, not necessarily from the streetscape, but it is a historic structure that the applicant is proposing to add a very large new section. He added that as a precedent he is not 100% on board with such large additions to historically preserved homes. Mr. Keenan asked for the square footage of the original structure. Ms. Campbell said that the addition is approximately 480 square feet. She stated that what may be difficult to read is that there are a great deal of porches, which are open. She stated that the addition steps backs in order to be subordinate to the main structure. Mr. Keenan stated that it is deceiving on the drawings, but most of what is being added are porches. Ms. Campbell stated that it is all open underneath, as well. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he cannot recall many examples of historic houses where there has been such a large scale addition. Ms. Campbell stated that an example would be the Boatwright’s home, which was done a few years ago. She stated that this was a historic house and a two and a half story addition was added to the back side, and the lot is smaller. She said there is also the house on Morrison. Mr. Hirshorn stated that in many cases the addition mimics the historic structure, even if they are hyphenated or the gable height is lowered. He stated that in this case, an entirely new structure is being added to a historic house and he has not seen too much of this. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Campbell stated that it happens frequently downtown where there is a kitchen house that may or may not have not been connected, and there is a variation of materials, which tells a story of how something has been added on. She stated that you have the main volume of the historic piece, then a link and another building. Ms. Keenan stated that the exception for this lot is the overall size of it. He stated that the logic really applies when there is a smaller lot and a large historic home on it and then the homeowner attempts to max out the ratio. He stated that he is not aware of a lot larger than this one in the Old Village. Ms. Dickson stated that when this is complete, it will likely exceed the 50% ratio. Ms. Campbell stated that they are only at 32% impervious. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he struggles with the idea of leaving the historical structure as it is, as opposed to adding on a beautiful addition, as it does alter the historic nature of the entirety of the home and lot. He stated that from a preservation standpoint, he is unsure what the implications would be. He added that although there is room to do the addition, it is not the same house it once was. Ms. Rowe stated that it helps that the house is sitting sideways, so it is not facing the street. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the applicant could add to the application some concrete examples of where these large new additions have been added on to the back of historically preserved homes. Mr. Keenan stated that he would like to go on record to say that he really appreciates the architects’ elevations. He stated that this Commission sees all scales and believes this is a good one to use as far as what the Commission is expecting to see, especially on conceptual. He stated that it makes it much easier for the Commission.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Kate Campbell, architect, stated that this was before the Commission in July. She stated that they researched the Sanborn maps, and this house used to be a two story house and on the back was one story. She said at some point, they added the piece in the front and back and a large gable on the side elevation. She said what they are proposing is to demolish a portion of the kitchen and maintain the area along the side, renovate the kitchen and add a living room on the back side that is one story. She stated that they would also have a wrap-around porch on the back side opening onto the garden. She said the property is large and the homeowner would like to add to it and follow the traditional development patterns of a single house that you would see downtown or in the Old Village, where they are adding and stepping back along the length of the property. She said the homeowners are working with Sheila Wortimer on the landscape design and added some parking. She said that they are not in a flood zone so they would like to utilize the space underneath as an open area with a fireplace on the ground floor. She said that there will be a small enclosed artist studio as a portion of the porch. She said that one other thing they would like to do is change out the wood rails that are not historic and go back with a rectangular shoebox style picket with a round rail on both porches and bring it back to what is more historically appropriate. She said that the property does slope down as it goes to the rear of the property and the stair will be internal on the porch. She said they are maintaining the existing kitchen wall and not going any further into the setback and are slightly less. She said at the closest point, they are just under three feet to the property line, so this will also be a request of the Commission to allow them to continue this, because setting it in ten feet would not make sense in terms of the development on that property line. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that the staff notes indicated that the property owners were at 40%; however, it appears they are only at 30%. She said they are well under the lot coverage. She said she appreciates that the stairs are enclosed and believes the plans look great. She asked if the columns are also going to be improved when the pickets are replaced. Ms. Campbell added that the property owners want to do a historically sensitive porch renovation. Mr. Hirshorn asked how many additional feet of encroachment is on the new addition. Ms. Campbell stated that it is approximately 33 additional feet along the length. Ross Evans, 430 Church Street next door, said the only concern he has is on the additional 33 feet. He said that this house is right on the property line and his driveway goes right next to it and when it rains, they get water. He said with the 30 additional feet, what is the property owner going to do to drain water off of the roof and where will it go. He said they currently get water and with the additional 30 feet of house, where will the water go, other than in his yard. Mr. Rutherford stated that drainage is not in the purview of the Commission and would be handled with the Town’s Building Permit division. Mr. Keenan stated that this is an accurate statement; however, it is a good question. He said that both the applicant and architect are both present. Ms. Campbell said that they would gutter that side and try to mitigate that roof slope coming off on Mr. Evan’s side. She said that they are not legally allowed to drain on any other property, but will work with Mr. Evans and their client on this. Mr. Evans stated that this would normally not be an issue; however, they have a basement that previously did not get water and when 424 Church street was renovated, they began getting water in their basement. He said that they also said they would try to keep the water off his property, but now they get water in the basement. He said when 424 Church did their renovations and built an addition on, it is 10 feet away from his home and now drains into his yard. He said he met the homeowner of 436 Church Old Village Historic District Commission

Street and does not want to create issues, but wants to know where the water will go. Ms. Wilson said that when you look at the roof plan, not a tremendous amount of the roof pitches towards Mr. Evans home and could be handled with gutters and French drains along the side of the property. Mr. Evans stated that there are gutters on the front portion of the home, but they drain into his yard. Ms. Campbell said that they will need to change the direction of the gutters. She said they could do a sub-surface pipe that the gutters tie into that will stay on the property. She said they can explore ways to mitigate, but attempting to control it with gutters would be the most effective. Mr. Keenan said that all this Commission is able to do is ask that the architect and landscape planner work with Mr. Evans to come up with a plan that is adequate. He said that both the architect and landscape planners are reputable. He asked Ms. Campbell to continue the communication with Mr. Evans and advise Ms. Wortimer that there is some concern as well. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would reiterate for the record that with an additional 30 feet of encroachment, the Commission would like to make certain that those stipulations are followed through. He said that this is an extensive amount of additional encroachment and realizes that they are allowed to follow the house line, which is already encroaching on the property line. He said that this is a large amount of addition and the water will go somewhere, and although there are ways to mitigate this to some extent, the likelihood is that there will be some runoff. He said he would like to make sure that there is follow through and everything is handled satisfactorily. Ms. Rowe stated that they are doing the historic portion of the house a huge favor and taking it back to what it looked like with integrity. Mr. Keenan said that he would like to reiterate Mr. Hirshorn’s concerns and added that every month, this Commission has drainage issues that arise in these meetings and technically it is not in the Commission’s purview; however, wishes that the Commission did have some input in this regard. He said that it is up to individual property owners to be good stewards and Old Village Historic District Commission

be considerate of their neighbors. He said that the project as a whole, looks good. Ms. Rowe made a motion to accept the application for final review for 436 Church Street as presented; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

label: 641 Royall Avenue
request: 641 Royall Avenue – (Survey 5991) – Final Review for New Accessory Structure [Consent Motion]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Rush Dixon, Rush Dixon Architects, representing the homeowners, Jon and Ansara Piebenga, stated that the discussion last month was to simplify the design. He stated that they did simplify in every way possible. He stated that one of the main discussions was the exterior spiral stair. He added that they attempted a square stair; however, they were not able to make it work. In order to solve this issue, they took the original spiral stair and brought it into the building, which hopefully solved this issue. He mentioned that they also removed the front dormer that was requested, which originally mimicked the main house and replaced it with a simple gable, which was a recommendation of the Commission. He stated that they still have the side dormer, but it is a very simplified version of the previous dormer and is a simple shed dormer in lieu of the hip dormer. He said that the back covered porch, they reduced the size of the roof and took it off of the back porch and are keeping a deck there for someone not using the upstairs and giving the opportunity to sit outside. Old Village Historic District Commission

He said there is a nice view of the backyard and pool. He stated that they would like to maintain that element. He stated that they removed the flower box and simplified the fence; therefore, compared to last month, he believes they have done everything that was requested. He stated that in reference to the positioning of the structure, he stated that where they would like to place the garage is right at the edge of the driveway, where the fence currently sits. He stated that this would allow them to use the existing concrete driveway. He stated that the position of this structure would put the building just past the breakfast area, which the homeowners use on a daily basis, so this would not obstruct the natural light in that area. He stated that they have nicely responded to the terracing of the house itself. He said they have the front porch element, the main house corner, the one story element then another ten feet back is the garage. He stated that if it is moved back further, it creates dead space of extra driveway area that is not necessary. He stated that it is a nice opportunity for landscaping to create the corridor/gateway to the backyard. He said that if they moved the assessor structure further back, he believes it would be detrimental to neighboring properties, because it would be structure and more structure and it would be nice to keep it all together and have an openness from one neighbor’s backyard to the other. Mr. Juan asked if the property is located in a flood zone. Mr. Dixon stated that they are. Mr. Juan asked what the elevation of the slab is. Mr. Dixon stated that it would be below. Mr. Juan stated that the Town’s ordinance does not allow for an enclosed structure when there are habitable rooms or spaces above the garage. He stated that it is treated as if it were an elevated structure; open foundation, piers. Ms. Wilson stated that his slab is a 12 and asked if he needed a plus one. Mr. Juan responded in the affirmative. Ms. Rowe asked if the upstairs was going to be a habitable space and thought it was a playroom. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Dixon stated that it is not intended to be an ADU (accessory dwelling unit), as there is no plumbing, but a playroom for the children. Mr. Juan stated that it is still a habitable space. He stated that if it were only a garage, the structure could be enclosed and limited to parking and storage. He stated that anything beyond this is habitable space and condition and would have to meet the open foundation system. He stated that he did not see a floor plan, but asked about the spiral staircase that goes up into the upstairs. Mr. Dixon stated that it used to be outside and brought it inside to remove it as an element on the exterior. Mr. Juan asked if it is enclosed on the ground floor. Mr. Dixon stated that it is open on the ground floor and it is not until you get to the top that you open the door to heated space. Mr. Juan stated that it needs to maintain a separation between that space upstairs and the garage for fire separation. He stated that having it open and having a means of egress to grade through the garage is a code violation. Mr. Dixon asked if the use of the upper level for storage change. Mr. Juan stated that if it is storage and unheated, it would not come into play, if just for storage. Ms. Wilson asked if the height requires that it have a kitchen. She asked if it is because it is over 18 feet even with the matching roof. Mr. Pohlman stated that the way the ordinance was restructured for the Old Village is all accessory structures, whether garages or ADU’s are allowed to go up to 20 feet now. He stated that this being at 19 ft. 11 in. is below. Ms. Wilson stated that she likes the location of the structure and it does not need to be pushed back any further. She stated that she knows there is some complexity on how to vent the lower level. She stated that aside from this, she does not have an issue with the massing and or location of the structure. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Rowe added that she applauds what has been done to make it more a part of the historic looking home. Ms. Dickson stated that this is a big improvement over the last design. She asked about the distance of the proposed structure to the property line. Mr. Dixon stated that it is set at the six foot line. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his only reservation is the balcony on a garage, particularly if it is not an ADU. He stated that it is not something you would normally see on a garage. Mr. Dixon stated that they do have two doors; one from the stairs to step out onto the balcony and another from the heated space. He stated that they are going to want furniture there, because it is a play room and smaller windows were not going to work. He stated that this is their way of getting things up to the playroom. Ms. Rowe asked if it was possible to turn this into a dwelling unit. Mr. Juan stated that they may; however, the ground floor walls would have to be redesigned. Mr. Dixon stated that on the ground, they would need to raise the stair and have direct access to the outside. Mr. Juan responded in the affirmative and said that the walls would also have to be changed to an open foundation system with louvers and lattice. He stated that solid walls would not be allowed on the ground floor unless the slab is elevated to one foot above the BFE (base flood elevation). Ms. Wilson stated that she believes it is going down one foot in the new flood maps, which may help. Ms. Wilson stated that before taking away the balcony, it is a possible location for the stairs, as it came directly onto the balcony, it would solve a lot of issues. Mr. Juan stated that it could, as it would be the means of egress. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Dixon stated that he would like to revisit the spiral stair being visible as an element in the back, given the fact that it would not be visible from the public right of way. Ms. Wilson stated that she believes it would be visible from along the side. She stated that this would be more difficult for her to get comfortable with. She stated that if the structure is going to a louvered screen system on the lower lever, it seems like it could be considered an exterior spiral stair that has some sort of screening. She stated that she believes there is a way to screen or install it in a clever way that gets you in an exterior entry into the second floor space. Ms. Rowe stated that she agrees that if the stairs can be screened and get it back outside, then it may resolve the issue. Ms. Wilson stated that the homeowner wants the balcony in order to hoist furniture up in through the doors. Mr. Dixon responded in the affirmative. Mr. Pohlman stated that this is conceptual; therefore, no motions are necessary. Ms. Rowe stated that she hopes that the Commission has provided some good feedback.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Rush Dixon, architect for the property owners, stated that the drawings they are proposing have very minor changes from the last presentation. He stated that Mr. Juan indicated at the last meeting that if the upper level is to be occupied, the lower level would need to be treated differently by accounting for floodwaters. He said when discussing with Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Rogerson, this is a Mount Pleasant requirement, above and beyond what FEMA requires. He said the owner was interested in keeping the aesthetic the same and plan to use the upper level as storage and the garage as the garage. He said that there is still the component of the garden shed on the back. He said that the homeowner has larger items that they would like to be able to store in the upper level, which is why they kept a flat area on top of the storage shed in order to lift and get items in through the double doors on the backside. He said with moveable or removable balusters, they would be able to do so. He said other than this, he believes the positioning of the accessory structure was agreed to, all the materials were replicating the novelty siding that is already on the existing building, the copper flashing at the base, and incorporated brick at the bottom. Mr. Keenan said that this is a significant improvement. He said Ms. Wilson was concerned about the balcony in the rear. He asked if the balcony was necessary for the applicant. Mr. Dixon stated that the owners would still like to have access to the two doors. He said there is a pull down stair inside of the garage portion to get smaller items out; however, they would still like access through the double doors to hoist more sizeable items up. He said the homeowners are aware they are not able to occupy the upstairs portion of the accessory structure. He said they would like some sort of flat element at the double doors for easier access. Ms. Rowe stated that she applauds what has been accomplished to make this work. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the balcony was the reservation he had at the last meeting and said he still has reservations, because it is not consistent with other garages and accessory buildings. He said a balcony element is not consistent. Ms. Dickson stated that she understands having the balcony to hoist the larger item up for storage. Mr. Keenan stated that this Commission is somewhat under a microscope on ADU’s and accessory structures. He said that the Commission just updated the guidelines. He said that this sets the precedent that the Old Village Historic District Commission

Commission is not looking for. He said that the design of the structure is fine and he would prefer to see the balcony eliminated. He stated that the Commission is seeing an increase in requests for ADU’s and are becoming more outlandish. He stated that by allowing one balcony, it would open the door for more requests such as this. He said he understands that it is not in the view of the street; however, the neighbor directly behind will view it. Ms. Dickson asked if the accessory structure has plumbing. Mr. Dixon stated that there is no plumbing. He stated that it was never intended to be any type of living area. Mr. Pohlman reminded Commission members that this is not an ADU (accessory dwelling unit), but an accessory garage. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he can either defer or conditionally approve with the removable of the balcony. Mr. Dixon asked if the back garden shed portion of the structure was in danger of being denied. He stated that it is a simple shed roof going up to double doors that had a baluster in front of it and asked if that would be more palatable for Commission members. He said that the homeowners would like to have the garden shed for garden tools. He stated that starting at the bottom of the doors, have a modest slope roof down towards the back. Ms. Rowe asked if Mr. Dixon would like to leave the double doors and eliminate the balcony. She said it would look like two hanging doors. Mr. Dixon said that it could be treated like a Juliet balcony with some type of railing in front of it. He said that the railing could be removed so that the doors could still be used. He said they would have to stand on the metal room, but would still have reasonable access, which is what the homeowners were requesting. Mr. Juan stated that in reference to a hand or guard rail in front of the double doors, if it were not a walking surface and a roof, it is more of an access and not habitable space. Mr. Keenan stated that he would be amenable to this, but would have to see more details. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Rowe stated that she thinks that the current design looks better, but still sets the precedent of having a balcony. She stated that she does not understand why the homeowner needs two doors. Mr. Dixon stated that he will suggest a wider 36 to 42 inch door to his client. Mr. Hirshorn stated that if the homeowner is going to eliminate a nice balcony, he would be hesitant to approve a compromised balcony. He stated that he would prefer to approve the balcony as it is presented or eliminate the balcony and replace the double doors with windows and a roof. Mr. Dixon stated that if they are able to keep the back portion, put a simple roof on it and replace the double doors with windows, if this is an acceptable direction, he will try to work with this. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to defer the application at 641 Royall Avenue until further design is presented on the back side of the structure; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

label: 641 Royall Ave
request: 641 Royall Ave. Approved for the installation of a new roof

label: 728 Pitt Street
request: 728 Pitt Street – (HISTORIC 5956) – Final Review for Additions and Alterations to Historic Structure

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Scott Broadwell, homeowner stated that he is here with this father, Russ Broadwell. He stated that they received a lot of positive feedback in March when they presented and at that time, the design was enclosure of the carport and an “L” shaped addition on the back. He stated that the application indicates a two story addition; however, it is a one and a half story addition. He stated that the upper level has a five foot knee wall. He illustrated the street rendering of what the street level would look like with the addition in the back with the enclosure of the carport. He stated that there is mention of demolition and what is being demolished is a small section, which is an unheated laundry room. He stated that they were able to preserve the porch and the craftsman look of the porch. He stated that looking from the front, there are two Old Village Historic District Commission

bays that are open and one will be enclosed. He stated that they are extended slightly back from that and making it into an L shape. He stated that the porch in the back is open. He stated that they reduced the scale from the March conceptual and will maintain the historic corner on the house. He reviewed with the Commission the two side elevations. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his only initial question is if the proposed demolition of the old laundry room section is historic. Mr. Broadwell stated that it is built on cinder block with separate materials from the original structure. He stated that it was the most recent addition to the property; however, they do not have anything in the permitting office that is able to date this. He stated that it was built with non-historic components. Mr. Hirshorn asked if there is an illustration of that area on an existing elevation. Mr. Broadwell stated that the structure went through several different evolutions and looking at the types of material in the piers, and the original structure was a Fisherman’s cottage and the front gable structure was then brought out as the second element and the third element was what enclosed the front porch and created the carport and then the last evolution was the added laundry room. He stated that it is constructed of different materials, has different siding and piers, and is not heated. Mr. Hirshorn asked Mr. Broadwell what year he believes this was added. Mr. Broadwell stated that based on the materials, he would estimate the 1970’s. He stated that the flooring is 1970’s Formica and it has butylene plumbing. Mr. Keenan asked if this would be the only section demolished. Mr. Broadwell stated that when they presented in March for conceptual review, this was the same component discussed that the Commission indicated was acceptable. Mr. Keenan asked if the pool was added. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Broadwell stated that this was not present in March and said that it is a plunge pool for his children and is not visible from the street. Mr. Keenan stated that he knows the homeowner has been working very hard on this project and he appreciates the effort. He said that he likes the design in the front, the enclosure on the carport, but a little nervous about the height in the back and hopes conceptually, that it does not dwarfing the historic structure. Mr. Broadwell stated that the flood code requires them to come up sixteen inches, so the front of the house obscures more of the back by coming up slightly. He stated that the total height is just under 26 feet and well within regulation. He stated that it is shorter than the one that was presented in March, coming down two feet. Colin Cope, with Heather Wilson office, stated that this is next to Heather Wilson’s home and this is a very familiar situation where you have a small cottage on the front and slightly pushed back from the street and then there is a small section, they refer to as hyphens to the one and a half story. He stated that when you are in the front of Ms. Wilson’s house, you do not even know the other structure is back there and it is larger than Mr. Broadwell’s. Ms. Rowe stated that the homeowner has done a remarkable job and loves what was accomplished in the front. Mr. Hirshorn stated that where the new addition is there is not a big height differential; however, from another angle, the roof is much lower. Mr. Broadwell stated that it does not build perspective whereas the other angle does. He stated that from the street, the lower part of the windows are obscured. He said from the street, the lower half of the window should not be visible. Mr. Cope explained the different perspectives and added that the tree shown is massive. He stated that you are not able to see the new structure, because of the tree. He stated that it leans out over the house in between the carport and what is being shown in the back. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan asked what the total square footage of the proposed addition. Mr. Broadwell stated that it is 2,500 total square feet. Mr. Keenan stated that he looking for the square footage of the addition. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the addition is 1,100 square feet. Mr. Keenan stated that it is a challenging lot and believes that it looks very good. Ms. Rowe stated that they have done a great job keeping the Craftsman look together. Mr. Cope said that what they are doing is filling in a carport which are not traditional and filling it in will provide a more traditional look. Ms. Dickson stated that it is a shame to take a small house and put a large addition in the back. She stated that she does; however, likes it much better than the initial design, because the character of the Fisherman’s Cottage was kept. Mr. Broadwell stated that they attempted to try and do the addition as discreetly and appropriately as possible without losing the character. Ms. Dickson asked how far the pool was from the lot line. Mr. Colin stated that it is currently just a placeholder and could be moved around. Mr. Keenan stated that the application does not include the pool. He stated that the Commission is addressing the house. Mr. Hirshorn stated that unfortunately he was not at the conceptual meeting; however, if he had been there, he would have recommended creating the square footage that is less visible from the street. He stated that this is his only reservation. He stated that when these additions are added on to historic structures, at what point is preservation being compromised and how important is this. He said that this is clearly visible from the street and alters the streetscape of a historical structure. He stated that he does not have an issue with demolishing the Old Village Historic District Commission

utility room; however the streetscape of a historic structure is being altered. Mr. Broadwell stated that since the March conceptual, they have scaled back the size and height considerably. He stated that the structure has already gone through several evolutions and this is just part of the evolution. He stated that this helps this structure evolve in to the future and hope this is the last evolution. Mr. Keenan stated that there are not many of these Fisherman’s cottages left and all that can be done is to be good stewards and protect historical structures. Mr. Hirshorn asked if any other one story designs were considered. Mr. Broadwell stated that it would encroach on the rear neighbor, which was not acceptable to the Commission. Mr. Hirshorn asked what the grounds were for the demolition for the utility section. Mr. Broadwell stated that the concrete block would not be able to support the new addition. Mr. Cope stated that that he would certainly say A, which is poor construction and obviously has safety issues. Mr. Broadwell stated that he would select “A” for demolition. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to approve the demolition of the utility shed section to the rear of the property based on guideline “A” under partial demolition of historic structures, public safety; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor. Ms. Rowe made a motion to approve the application for 728 Pitt Street, final review for additions and alterations; seconded by Mr. Hirshorn. All present voted in favor. III. Staff Approvals Mr. Pohlman stated that there were no staff approvals. Old Village Historic District Commission

VI. Motion to Adjourn Ms. Dickson motioned to adjourn; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor. There being no further business, meeting adjourned at 7:06 p.m.

Respectfully submitted, Barbara Ashe

label: 402 Patjens Lane
request: 402 Patjens Lane – Survey 6212 – Applicant is seeking Final Review for further additions to previously approved additions

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Mr. Pohlman stated that the address should read 402 Patjens “LANE” and not Court. Linda Balzac, stated that she is the architect on the project and stated that the homeowner is requesting for a wrap-around porch with materials to match existing, including wood flooring on the porch, with a small addition on the back of the home to enlarge the kitchen. She stated that the lot is an odd shape which is why they are requesting the six foot encroachment to the rear yard setback. She stated that one of the reasons for the impervious surface reduction is because they will be removing the existing concrete driveway and replacing with a pervious paver at a future date. She stated that the request is for a wrap-around porch, the rear one story addition to enlarge the kitchen and a new privacy fence with a gate that is not visible from public purview. She stated that they would like to simplify to make it a solid fence with detailing to match the existing neighbor’s fences and instead of stucco columns, to ask for brick. Mr. Pohlman stated that this should be submitted for the next review meeting. Ms. Balzac stated that since this is conceptual, she would like to advise the Commission what the homeowners would like to do, which is to make Old Village Historic District Commission

the brick columns in the back corner of the house and the fence to match the neighbor’s fence in a Charleston green. She stated that they have signatures from all the surrounding neighbors approving the proposed work. Ms. Wilson asked if this is submitted as conceptual because of the fence. Ms. Balzac stated that with the new list that was approved, she believed that there would have to be significantly more detail in order to request approval. She stated that they would certainly entertain the idea to ask for final because there is a great deal of detail, because the homeowner did the drawings and did an excellent job. She stated that all the details will match existing and Village Restoration will be doing the work. She stated that if they need to return for final on the fence and gate, since it is not as submitted, they would be happy to come back for those two things if the Commission can consider final on this tonight. Mr. Pohlman stated that it is under the Commission’s purview to elevate it from conceptual to final if the Commission so desires. Ms. Wilson stated that she likes everything that has been proposed. Ms. Rowe agreed. Ms. Dickson stated that she is unsure how everything can be put on this lot. She stated that it looks tight up against the neighbors in the back of the house. Ms. Balzac stated that the encroachment would only happen at the right corner, but gets greater after that point. She said that the house is still on the property at a diagonal and is still under the 40% rule, but it is a very odd lot and the house is placed oddly. She stated that they are asking for a very small addition and a wrap-around porch which will significantly improve the house. Ms. Rowe stated that there is also a lot of room in the front of the property. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he likes everything and is happy to do final approval with the exception of the gate and fence. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to approve 402 Patjens Court for final approval, as submitted, with the exception of the picket fence and gate; seconded by Ms. Wilson. Mr. Pohlman requested that the motion be amended to reflect the correct address of 402 Patjens Lane. Mr. Hirshorn amended his motion and Ms. Wilson amended her second. All present voted in favor. Ms. Wilson asked if Ms. Balzac was referring to the fence on Whilden. Ms. Balzac responded in the affirmative and showed an illustration of the brick columns the homeowners would like, instead of the stucco. She also showed a photograph of the proposed fence. Ms. Wilson asked if the whole property line will be fenced. Ms. Balzac indicated on the illustration where the fence would be installed. Ms. Wilson stated that she did not have an issue with the conceptual.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed the application with the Commission.

Ms. Linda Balzac reviewed the application with Commission.

Ms. Montgomery asked about the window Ms. Balzac showed the proposed window in closet addition.

Mr. Hackenberg asked about the entrance and exit behind the home, the number of cars allowed in driveway, and the location of front door of home. Ms. Balzac answered that the front door is in back right corner. She stated that the driveway has space for the two required parking spaces.

Ms. Rowe stated she is concerned with look of the window in the front and that it is not in harmony with home.

Mr. Jim Byrd, 402 Patjens Lane, stated that 401 Patjens Lane has the same type of addition as the proposed addition, so these additions already exist. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Montgomery moved to approve previously approved setbacks and agree to window in the proposed closet with the idea it is to match the previously approved windows. Second by Mr. Hackenberg; all in favor.

events.text:

She stated that the homeowners would like to change the existing sunroom that has some interior plexiglass into a traditional wall to match the windows at the front of the house. She stated that she will put three windows across to make it more traditional. She said they would like to add a fence along Pitt Street where the elevation is for the work that is occurring and to keep it at 42 inches high, extend it along Pitt Street and return slightly down Bank Street. She stated that this is listed as conceptual; however, if the Commission has enough detailing, she would ask for consideration for final. Old Village Historic District Commission
