label: 959 Pitt Street
request: 959 Pitt Street – Survey 5890 – Final Review for After-the-Fact Alterations [Consent Motion]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Cindy Cline, Wertimer and Cline Landscape Architects, stated that her clients are the Moore’s and the initial site plans were submitted by the architects and they allocated placeholders for many of the paved surfaces on the site. She said there was a general area indicated for the driveway and stair landings. She stated that they have developed with the client more definitive areas, such as entry into the garage, guest parking and circulation around the site. She stated that the materials are traditional materials seen throughout the Old Village, and they are proposing a tabby concrete driveway with old Carolina brick detail, bluestone stepping stones and the combination of bluestone with either lawn or ground cover between the pavers. She stated that it is a straight forward site plan. Ms. Dickson asked how the Commission will know it is just under 40% once all the hardscape is installed, because it does not appear that it is. She stated that 40% is four fifths. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Cline stated that the oyster shell pathways and the guest parking area will all be a pervious oyster shell paving. She stated that the stepping stones that are shown are not set on a solid base and are pervious. She stated that they are definitely up against their lot coverage limit. She stated that where they were able, they designed for the paved surfaces to be pervious. Ms. Wilson asked if the pavers in the back, the opposite side of Pitt Street that are set in ground cover have a function or intended use. Ms. Cline said that the owners did not want the lawn maintenance, but did want some useable space in the back. Ms. Wilson stated that there is some general neighborhood concern, which is what Ms. Dickson is alluding to, in terms of impervious surfaces, which is still not greenspace. She stated that the Commission is struggling with how to best direct and respond to this. She asked if there is anything compelling about this space when they have so much other outdoor space. Ms. Cline said that they did want to have the opportunity to be able to use some of their lot at the ground level. She stated that the property owner is a gardener. Richard Ouzts, 957 Pitt Street, said that he has lived in his home for approximately 43 years and his biggest concern with this particular situation is that he has never had flooding until the last heavy rains. He said that he is getting flooding from 959 Pitt Street, which has already ruined an air conditioning unit and duct work. He said that another issue is 955 Pitt Street, which created a tremendous amount of flooding on that side. He stated that he has lost all his hydrangeas, roses and now his trees are dying due to flooding on both sides of his residence. He said that he has been there for 43 years and feels he should see something that is going to cure these problems. He stated that he has a formal complaint with the Town of Mount Pleasant building inspector, which lists all his concerns. He said that the Town did come out and he also spoke to Mr. Mitchell at the Town. He said that no one appears to be able to help him or tell him anything. He said that he has a mosquito issue now and it is a shame that he has to deal with this situation. He said that he is not Old Village Historic District Commission

against the houses being built on both sides of his home. He said that he is not 20 or 12 feet up in the air, but is grandfathered in and they pay a premium for insurance to live in that area. He said that he is concerned about the flooding. He said that he turned in a claim to FEMA to replace the air conditioning unit and duct work, as well as contents in his workshop and feels they may help him. John Linton, 966 Pitt Street, stated that their residence is across the street and their existing driveway is directly across from 959 Pitt Street. He said that his concern is the same as Mr. Ouzts, which is the drainage. He added that 40% is not a right to 40% lot coverage and it is the Commission’s guideline for the maximum. He said there was an approval for 28% and now this one is for 39.95%. He said that the house that was there previously was substantially less than 28% lot coverage. He said that he came before the board in January, 2017 and it took until May to receive approval. He said that the Town is holding their building permit until they complete an engineered drainage study that has a comparative analysis of existing and proposed conditions, with calculations for the runoff. He said that it must show no adverse impacts on any neighbor. He said no other property owner in the history of the Old Village has ever been required to do this, which was admitted by the Town staff. He said that his plans have a 10% lot coverage and it is completely beyond him why his plans are being held up. He said that 959 Pitt Street’s elevations on the driveway are at 7.9 feet in places and the road is at 7.5 feet. He believes that part of 959 Pitt Street’s plan is to run this onto their property, and they are not able to do anything without a certified engineer’s stamp. He said that at the beginning of his process, the Town told him that he had to submit the engineers’ insurance certificate to the Town. He stated that the plan and landscape architecture work looks great at 959 Pitt Street and should be approved with the condition that a certified engineer does a plan with calculations showing how it ties to the stormwater infrastructure and that it show that there will be no adverse impact on any of the surrounding neighbors. He said that this could be one condition and the other could be that it be deferred until 959 Pitt Street’s plan is completed or a drawing done by an engineer showing that it will not have adverse impacts. He said, lastly, to add a condition that a new building permit must be obtained. He said that what they currently Old Village Historic District Commission

have is a building permit that was based on placeholders for the impervious surface and believes it is fundamentally unfair to let the applicant operate under this permit and come back to the Commission, doubling what the impervious coverage is on the outside of the home, and not have to do the same type of study that one neighbor is being required to do. He said that he would like to make these requests to the Commission. Mr. Keenan said that the drainage issue is unfortunately one of the most important issues that comes before the Commission and it is completely out of the purview of the Commission. He said that the Commission is unable to enforce drainage issues. He said that he was unaware of the request for stamped engineering drawings of the drainage. He said that it has been done in the Old Village before and it has not solved the issue. He said there are major drainage issues in the Old Village and a stamped set of drawings is not going to correct these issues. He stated that the Commission may provide advice and hope that the applicants will be good stewards towards this. He asked Ms. Cline if she is able to speak to the issue on drainage or if the property owner has reviewed it. Ms. Cline stated that given recent events, they are witnessing unprecedented flooding events in downtown Charleston, on Kiawah, James Island, as well as the Old Village. She said that recent events are not the norm. She said that the street is actually higher than the garage slab on the proposed driveway area. She said this was dictated by the architect in the very beginning. She said they are having to hold this existing grade in the front yard and are proposing to create a channel drain which takes the water coming down into their lot from the street and putting it into some type of drywell on the side of the driveway. Mr. Keenan asked if this would run down both the north and south sides of the property. He said that Mr. Ouzts’ property is to the north. Ms. Cline stated that they are holding grade almost all the way across the corners of the house and meet existing grade well in advance of any of the property lines. She said where they saw the biggest issue in dealing with the water coming into the garage was at the point where the brick pattern ends and the apron coming from the street meets. She said in a storm, what they are hoping is that any runoff that may come from the Old Village Historic District Commission

street they could catch at an intermediate point before it goes towards the garage slab. She said they are tied to existing elevations and are trying to mitigate the existing circumstances without adversely affecting any other properties. Ms. Wilson stated that while the Commission does not have purview over drainage, the Commission does have purview over what is approved in terms of the house and hardscape. She said what Ms. Cline is describing is essentially a condition that the Commission created by approving a house with a slab at a certain elevation. She said that the Commission cannot tell the property owner to put in drainage, but the Commission can deny slabs, hardscape and all the conditions that create a drainage problem that the Commission has no ability to help remediate. She said when this plan was presented, she was not on the Commission, but stated that she did not believe that a motor court in front of a house was in keeping with the Old Village. She said it was approved and now this Commission’s hands are bound. She said that this Commission has no option but to approve a motor court, otherwise they are not able to park their vehicles. She said that she that she does not wish to approve more hardscape that is creating more conditions. She believes that there is too much stonework and hardscape at the grade, and the house is already enormous by Old Village standards and has a very large and very generous motor court out front. She stated that it is a beautiful house, but believes it is asking for too much. She said that even when it is pervious, there is still too much hardscape with pervious material in between. She mentioned that there is still a lot of water shedding off the site that was not previously shedding. Mr. Keenan stated that he agrees that it is a beautiful plan and said that Ms. Cline’s answer regarding drainage was that they do not have a plan for drainage. He said that with all the recent storms and rains, the Commission needs to look at drainage, because it is a major issue. He said that there is too much hardscaping, which creates an issue for next door and across the street. He said that rather than all the intricate pervious pavers, he would prefer to see a French drain plan. He stated that he agrees with Ms. Wilson. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Cline stated that if they were able to keep the intent of the general design plan. She stated that the motor court is as it is, because they are not able to get into the garage any other way. She said that she does not want to presume anything until she discusses this with her clients, however, the areas where they are showing stepping stones, could become greener, maintaining those same spaces as outdoor rooms in order for the homeowner to engage with the landscape, but not so much stone. Ms. Wilson stated that she would go one step further if it helps with construction and making progress, to go ahead and approve the drive court, because they need to keep moving forward. She asked that Ms. Cline study the ancillary paths and stone rooms at the back, she would be agreeable with this conditional approval. Ms. Wilson moved to conditionally approve the front portion of the plan at 959 Pitt Street for the driveway, drive court and guest parking and defer the stone paths and rear of the landscape; second by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Julie O’Conner, designer representing the homeowner, stated that this is a vacant lot on the harbor. She said she studied what little there is of a streetscape in the area, which is a four house street. She said that all of the homes are set back from Chicco Lane and her proposal mimics this in her design. She said that all the homes are drive under homes, with parking on the Chicco Lane side due to their harbor frontage. She stated that she is proposing the same. She said that the other homes are primarily two story homes on top of drive unders and she is proposing a slightly modified story and a half on top of a drive under for her project. She stated that this lot has one of the most beautiful views and the house is designed to take advantage of those views. She said that it will read very well from a streetscape perspective due to the location of the other houses and where they sit, set back. She provided photographs from the dock owned by homeowners at the corner of Chicco Lane and McCants Drive. She said there are a number of great trees, particularly in front of their neighboring property. She said the materials proposed are all approved materials and took the architectural voice of the village with metal roofs, exposed rafters, a lot of windows in order to take advantage of the views. She said one of the things on the site plan that she liked considerably was to come in with a little less of an entrance. She said that some of the other properties have wide driveways that come off of Old Village Historic District Commission

Chicco Lane and she thought it would be attractive to have a single driveway that cut through the middle of the lot so when you did see the house, you would see the front stairs and the front door and landscape at the street. She said once you come into the property, the driveway would curve around to the two garage doors so the vista from the street would be the front door and not the garage doors. She stated that the only guideline she is varying from slightly is the guideline to have all the parking behind the house; however, this is a harbor front property and all the neighbors also have their parking in the front on the Chicco Lane side, which is indicative of the neighborhood and harbor front property. She stated that they are proposing a small amount of fill in the back as the lot goes from an elevation 10 ½ at the street down to a five when they hit the OCRM line. She said the neighboring properties are higher than they are at 6 ½ or 7 so they want to raise up just to 6 at the back section so they are not significantly lower than their neighboring properties. She said other than this one request, they are not proposing any fill on the property and it will continue to drain as it has done, naturally. Ms. Rowe stated that there appears to be a great deal going on with the plan and when she first viewed it, she thought they were townhomes. She loves symmetry; however, there is a great deal going on, on a simple smaller lot and added that it is very busy. Ms. O’Conner said there could be some simplification with regards to the materials. She stated that the broken massing on the front was purposeful in order to break it up and provide more manageable pieces to work with and did not want it to be a big box on the street, although there are a few boxes on the street. She said she wanted it to read symmetrically and wanted to minimize the front load garage and some of the detailing was meant to do so. She said she can see potentially limiting the amount of materials and not doing the material change from clapboard to shingle could clean it up slightly. She stated that the broken massing was important from a design perspective. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he agrees with Ms. Rowe and said that the streetscape on Chicco Lane is fairly eclectic so he would categorize this design as well. He said that the areas he has issue with are the windows, especially on the front façade, which are fairly aggressive window Old Village Historic District Commission

configurations and a number of various types of roofing. He said that it is not very consistent with the Old Village, in general, having that many different types of roofing on one structure. He said that it appears very eclectic. Ms. Wilson stated that her concern is, that while it is broken with details and applied material, it is a fifty foot wide mass with a uniform height, which you do not see here. She said there is no protruding porch, no single story roof and the porch roof that is there is tucked in and will be hidden. She said it is too massive on the front for Chicco Lane. She said the houses that are adjacent have half the width or less coming forward to Chicco Lane and have more of a Charleston single type of massing. She said that it is a wall of two story and too much. She said where the closest neighbor is located, this house has gone with the most massing. She said the left side setback is less of a problem, because the rear is pushed back on the other side of the pool and does have a porch roof, but the next side elevation is a tremendous wall and she cannot support it next to a property or house that is half the depth. She stated that this house is coming 30 feet beyond the corner of an existing house. She said on the back, there is the critical which is typically 25 or 30 foot setback. Ms. O’Conner said there is no setback because of the plat date. She said the other houses had to have the critical line setback, but this one does not. She said the reason why some of the other homes are setback further is because of the very large live oak trees and this lot does not have any trees at all. She said the plat date on all of those lots pre dates the OCRM setback. Ms. Wilson said that the Town used to require that the streetscape be drawn in plan and poché as well as elevation. Mr. Pohlman said that it is not a requirement; however, it can be requested. Ms. Wilson stated that this is something she would definitely need to see, because as she reads this and then goes out to see what the houses look like, but it looks like twice as much house going twice as deep as the neighbors. She stated that typically the Commission requires a site of the whole block showing where the massing of all the houses are. She stated Old Village Historic District Commission

that the piece going beyond the Gaskins’ house being two stories, it looks like a seventy or eighty foot two story wall. Keith Jones, 121 Chicco Lane which is the house on the left side. He stated that he has an issue with the massive house that is being proposed and that it extends all the way to the critical line. He said that house in that lot now floods back almost thirty or forty feet into that lot past the critical line and to build this house on the critical line and block a view all the way out to Ft. Sumter and a third of their view of the harbor after they have been there 21 years. He said they live on their back porch and always knew something would be built there, but to stare into someone’s swimming pool and porch, he does not think this is right for the Old Village and does not believe it is befitting the harbor scape which all the houses are set back from the critical line on Chicco Lane. He stated that the house needs to move towards Pitt Street 25 or 30 feet. He said that it is a huge mass. He stated that his wife is Ruth Brennan who is listed on the plat. John Gaskins, 131 Chicco Lane, stated that the lot being discussed is a smaller lot than his by approximately ten feet. He stated that it is a massive structure he and does not want to dictate to anyone how to build a house, but believes it is important for the Village to not only maintain the hardscape and streetscape, but the harborscape. He stated that precedence has been established and it may be 100 years before you see a house come down on that harborscape, and a new one go up. He said that homeowners over the years have all tried to be in line with each other in order to maintain a beautiful harborscape. He said he understands the streetscape is a little more difficult to work with and the hardscape will be easier, but the harborscape is critical and the beauty of the Village with all the beautiful homes lining the marsh. He said that the tides do come way up into these properties and cannot imagine trying to build something right down to where a street used to be, which was engulfed by Mother Nature. He said that it is the legacy that we leave that is important and the Village is not just any place, it is hundreds of years old and thinks we should all do our best to keep it as original as possible. He said it means a great deal to him and his family, as well as all the neighbors. He said that we can compromise on other things. He said Old Village Historic District Commission

personally, he does not care for the design of the house and said if someone is going to purchase that great of a lot, which is considered one of the five best locations in the tri county area, to be more creative with the house. Janice Gaskins, 131 Chicco Lane, stated that she has an issue with the flooding they have and feels that this house is going so far into the marsh grass, where is the water going to go. She said that if this massive structure is allowed to be built, their homes will really flood. She said it is too much house for the lot and not in character with the other houses in the Village. Mr. Keenan stated that Ms. O’Connor described the street as a four house little street and he agrees with this description and stated that he is in agreement with the rest of the Commission members. He said there is concern about the height and mass, scale and positioning. He said that the harborscape is significant and the homes that grace them, it must be protected. He said many are hidden behind big oaks. He said that this proposed house is unlike anything along the front and thinks this needs to go through the creative process. He does not wish for it to look like every house in the Old Village; however, does not believe it is designed for this location. Ms. Wilson stated that there are not many lots on the harbor, so the Commission does not have specific guidelines for this; however, in other oceanfront towns, especially historic ones, you would have the average, within two blocks, of everyone’s house, which is what is neighborly. She said you do not come in because you have the right with the unique plat date to build out an additional forty feet. She said the setbacks and massing on the site are within the Commission’s purview and this is what she has the most issue with. She said that there are residents who have lived there for up to thirty years and this is not fair to them. She said she would like to see a more comprehensive study of what is on the harbor within two blocks of this lot. She said the historic houses on the harbor front is what faces the harbor, and this house is being designed as a two fronted house or possibly what faces the harbor is more important than this, because Chicco Lane is a unique area. She stated that this is a difficult lot, but the mass must get broken up as she does not see a Old Village Historic District Commission

situation where she would support a fully two story house on this lot. She said that it is insensitive to the adjacent structures that do have a varied height with one and two story broken forms and the step down to face the water and have porches that address the water. She said that the biggest issue is an 81 foot two story wall which does not exist anywhere in the Village. Ms. O’Conner stated that what it sounds like is that the property rights of one or two are considered more important than the property rights of her client and believes this is a slippery slope and something that needs to be considered carefully. She said that the three houses to the left of this property are all full two story houses on drive unders and the house to the right does have one story sections, but the others do not. She said that none of the houses are historic and this is not a historic streetscape. She said there is a very contemporary house two doors over. She believes something needs to be said with regards to the architecture and style. She said that this harborscape is not pristine or a planned unit development, but one that has been developed over time. She said that the house is not an eighty foot wall and does not stand out forty feet past that house, but fifteen feet past the house. She said that this property is extremely expensive and the client has desires and that is what she has accomplished. She agrees that it can be broken up and things that can be done to simplify the massing and the elevation to make it less busy. She agrees that there are certainly always things than can be done, but takes exception to the idea that the other houses on this street do not have full two story masses, because they do. Ms. Wilson stated that they also have one story components and this proposed house does not. She asked Ms. O’Connor to show that it is fifteen feet, because when she looks at where the Gaskins’ house ends, according to the survey which is the only document she has to review in the submittal, it is clearly more than fifteen feet beyond the end of the Gaskins’ house. She said in reference to the value of the property, this is not the concern of the Commission, nor does the Commission intend to respond. She asked Ms. O’Connor to leave the value of the property outside of the discussion. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. O’Connor stated that her client’s property rights are equally as important as the neighbors. Mr. Keenan stated that this does not need to be combative. He stated that there is constructive criticism that Ms. O’Connor is hearing from the Commission and the neighbors, and added that it is her job to discuss those with her client and address what is being heard. He stated that the Commission wants to work with Ms. O’Connor and her client; however, it must go through the process. He stated that what Ms. O’Connor is currently proposing is not going to work on this lot. Ms. Rowe stated that in reference to property rights, this had nothing to do with her looking at this and thinking this did not fit in the Old Village, on Chicco Lane or from the harbor. Mr. Keenan stated that there have been a number of comments. John Gaskins, stated that he respects Ms. O’Connor defending her design; however, his comments are his alone. IV. Staff Approvals [None]

label: 131 Live Oak Drive
request: 131 Live Oak Drive – Survey 6246/6246.01 – Applicant is seeking Final Review to install artificial turf in the front yard

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Jennifer Dickerson, stated that she purchased the property a few months ago; however, did not build it. She stated that the current material that is around the garage is a loose gravel and dirt and the rocks sling out into Toomer Lane and into the garage. She said what they would like to have is a more attractive aesthetic and a material that is just as permeable as the dirt and gravel that is currently there so that runoff issues are not created. She said there is an additional issue she is hoping the Commission will also hear this evening and both of her neighbors who would be affected by this are present this evening. She said on the side of the garage that borders Mr. Martschink’s property (south), they discovered that the fence which was supposed to run on the property line is actually encroaching onto Mr. Martschink’s property. She stated that they would like to move the fence so that it is in line with the drawings Old Village Historic District Commission

submitted and put a gate in the front so that the golf cart can go behind the gate. Ms. Wilson stated that she would need to see a drawing of the gate and fence. She said behind the existing cast iron plants, a double gate is shown, but this is not there. Ms. Dickerson stated that in the picture the golf cart is blocking it. Mr. Keenan asked if it would match the fence on the other side of the garage. Ms. Dickerson stated that it would. Ms. Wilson stated that the pervious artificial turf and swimming pool is there and not part of this request. Ms. Dickerson stated that everything behind the fence remains the same. Ms. Wilson stated that it is difficult to determine what is existing and what is being proposed. Ms. Dickerson stated that what is being proposed is the fence and gate to hide the golf cart and the bricks and walk in front of the garage would be removed and the pavers would cover all of this. Ms. Dickson asked if the pavers were pervious. Ms. Dickerson stated that they are pervious so water permeates. She said that nothing will runoff. She stated that they do not have a drainage issue in that area. Ms. Wilson stated that they cause the drainage problem for others below. She said that she does not see any calculations and has no idea what the current lot coverage is. She said that it is still stone and although some water flows, there is still water that sheds off. She said she needs calculations. She said there is no survey and was not here when the house was approved. She said she sees a lot of lot coverage and where the property line is, there is not much lawn and would need to see calculations in order to approve more drive and pavers. Ms. Dickerson stated that they are already at the maximum of 39.5% impervious coverage, but what is there now is rocks and they are only replacing the rocks with pavers, which sit on rocks. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that it is adding twice the amount. She said she would personally like to defer and request more calculations. She said that it is unclear what is new and what is being proposed. She also suggested reviewing a sample of the material. Ms. Rowe said that it would look better replacing with the proposed pavers versus what is currently there; however, they may be at the maximum and not able to add anything additional. Ms. Wilson stated that historically, the Commission asks property owners to maintain at least three feet of green between their neighbors so they are not running driveway or rock right up against the property line, but that would be for the neighbors to comment on. She stated that it is not typically a condition the Commission allows. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the house is already shoe-horned into the lot and they are at the maximum impervious percentage. He said that if additional is added, he would be leaning against approval. Ms. Dickerson stated that if they do not add stone and must keep it green, they will not be able to put the golf cart there, which means that instead of being tucked away, it will be visible as there is nowhere to park it. Miles Martschink, stated that he owns the property on the left side and has met with Jennifer and Jack Dickerson and what was discussed was extending the fence from the rear corner of the garage to the front property line to park the golf cart. He said that he supports the pervious pavers, because they are on an incline and the gravel comes out onto Toomer Lane and is not attractive. He added that this is assuming they are not exceeding the lot coverage ratio. He stated that the fence needs to be moved two feet over and extending it all the way to the front of the garage with the same stucco column that is existing and a gate at the edge of the garage. He said that he is fine with it. Ms. Wilson departed at 5:42 p.m.) Mr. Keenan stated that he understands what the homeowner is attempting to accomplish; however, the application is incomplete and it is difficult for the Commission to make assumptions. He said that Mr. Martschink’s drawing is helpful, but needs to be submitted with the Old Village Historic District Commission

application. He stated that he is okay with the pervious pavers, but wants to understand the lot coverage ratio and would like to see a better illustration on what the Commission is considering. Ms. Rowe stated that she agrees, but would like to see the calculations as well. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he is more akin to the last application where the house is already encompassing the maximum of the lot coverage and then going back to add more, whether pervious or impervious surfaces. He said he would be more inclined not to add additional. He added that he is fine with changing the current rocks to pervious pavers, but less agreeable to adding more hard surfaces to what could be a green buffer. Ms. Dickson asked where the second vehicle is parked. Ms. Dickerson stated that the other vehicle parks in the area marked 12 foot wide where her husband backs in his truck. She said that it is difficult to read the drawings as presented. She stated that the rains and storms have not been the norm, but the Commission needs to be careful. She said that it would be nice to see more specifically what is being requested so that the Commission may make a more informed decision. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to defer the application at 131 Live Oak Drive; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor. Mr. Keenan requested more defined drawings, materials and lot coverage ratio.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Jennifer Dickerson, property owner, said that she did come before the Commission in September. She said that the original proposal was to extend the driveway to the fence line and after listening to the Commission’s comments, she decided that they would not change the footprint of the driveway at all. She said that there are brick pavers bordering the entire driveway and will leave those in place and take out the gravel that is currently there and proposes to replace them with pervious pavers. She said their driveway sits on a hill and the gravel spills out onto Toomer Lane. She said that the pervious pavers accomplish the same permeability for water and are much more attractive. She said the other reason why they were originally requesting to extend the pavers to the fence line to the back of the house was because they believed they could park their golf cart in that area. She said Mr. Martschink, who owns the property behind theirs, pointed out that their fence along the back of the property followed the wrong fixed point and built the fence two feet over onto Mr. Martshink’s property. She said that they bought the home Old Village Historic District Commission

when it was less than one year old and did not get a survey. She said that they must now move the fence off of Mr. Martshink’s property. She said the original proposal from the architect shows what they would like to accomplish. She said she would like to put the fence and the gate exactly how it was drawn by the architect. Ms. Wilson asked if it is a stucco column with vertical wood. Ms. Wilson moved to approve the new pavers on the driveway and fencing at 131 Live Oak Drive, as submitted; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. (Attachment 1).

Ms. Jennifer Dickerson, 131 Live Oak Drive, reviewed request with the Commission.

Mr. Mike Tinkey, 208 Venning Street, stated he is opposed to turf and suggested that it does not fit within the historic district

Ms. Dickerson stated that he originally had the same concerns with using turf for the front yard and wanted to make sure that it close to the neighboring yards. She stated that they have been battling fungus and pet issues over the years. She suggested that it would be a vast improvement with the aesthetics of the yard. There being no comments, Ms. Rowe closed public comment.

Mr. Hackenberg has no issue with the turf and stated that the yard does not receive a lot of sunlight which is a problem. He asked if it could also be placed on the side of the house. Ms. Dickerson answered in the negative and stated that they had concerns with how it would look over the exposed roots.

Ms. Dovre asked how the turf is would be cleaned. Ms. Dickerson answered that it can be cleaned with a cleaning solution administered through a garden hose attachment.

Ms. Montgomery expressed concern with the use of artificial grass in this area as it is a historic street. She suggested that the turf would not be appropriate for this area.

Mr. Gallogly expressed concern with setting a precedent

Ms. Rowe agreed that turf would not be appropriate for the historic district. She also suggested that it would be difficult to determine which types of turf would be allowed.

Mr. Gallogly moved to deny the request for installation of turf. Ms. Dovre second the motion. Ms. Rowe, Ms. Montgomery and Mr. Gallogly in favor. Mr. Hackenberg and Ms. Dovre Opposed.

118 Live Oak Drive – Survey 6239/6239.01 – (TMS 517-15-00-05 Applicant is seeking Preliminary Comment for a new pool.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed the application with the Commission (Attachment 1).

Mr. Ben Prillaman, Aquatica Pools & Spas, reviewed the request with the Commission.

There being no comments, Ms. Rowe closed public comment.

Ms. Montgomery asked about the privacy and if a buffer is required. Mr. Prillaman answered that it is up to the homeowner.

Mr. Gallogly suggested that the fence should be at least eight feet. Mr. Rutherford answered that fences cannot exceed six feet in height. Ms. Rowe asked about the length of pool. Mr. Prillaman stated it is approximately twenty-four feet long.

Ms. Montgomery moved to approve preliminary approval. Mr. Gallogly second the motion. All in favor.

F.237 Middle Street – Survey 6045 – (TMS 532-09-00-022) Applicant is seeking Final Review for extensive alterations to a single-family home.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. (Attachment 1).

Charlie Miraziz, Herlong Architects, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. Bob Burns, 9 Pierates Cruz expressed concern with the possibility of two home renovations at the same time and the protection of the historic trees on these lots. He also expressed concern with the parking of contractor vehicles during construction.

Mr. Sam Lisi, Village Restoration, stated he potentially could be the contractor for this project and he as well as the homeowners are aware of the tight area and will make adjustments for the parking as well as the care of the trees.

Ms. Montgomery moved to approve the design deviation for horizontal lattice, stoop and step moved over out of TPZ and setback for parking. Ms. Dovre second the motion. All in favor.

G.102 Live Oak Drive – Survey 6242 – (TMS 517-15-00-057) Applicant is seeking Final Review of a not-in-kind window replacement.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. (Attachment 1).

Ms. Parker Best, Patty Wilbourne Designs, 107 Pitt Street reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Montgomery asked about the curtains currently on window. Ms. Best responded that there are curtains but they most likely will be replaced. Ms. Rowe suggested a casement window. Mr. Gallogly recommended that all the windows match.

There being no comments, Ms. Rowe closed public comment.

Ms. Montgomery moved to deny since it does not match the design guidelines or other windows on home. Mr. Gallogly second the motion. All in favor.

VII.Staff Approvals – None

There were no staff approvals for May.

VIII.Review and Approval of Design Guideline Alterations Concerning Porch Fans

Mr. Rutherford reviewed the guideline changes with the Commission.

The Commission did not move to change the Design Guidelines having noted needed text changes to those proposed.

IX.Election of Chair and Vice-Chair

The Commission elected Ms. Rowe as chair and Ms. Montgomery as vice- chair by secret ballot.

X.Motion to Adjourn

Ms. Rowe moved to adjourn at 7:40 pm. Mr. Gallogly second the motion. All in favor.

Submitted by Jane Yager-Baumrind

label: 212 Live Oak Drive
request: 212 Live Oak Drive – (HISTORIC 6233) – Final Review for New Addition and Exterior Alterations. [Consent Approval]

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Neil Stevenson, Neil Stevenson Architects, stated that the existing building is a combination of an existing building with an addition on the rear. He said the front building is a one story cottage on a large piece of property, located at the bottom of the pond on the edge of the marsh. He said that he hopes drainage will not be an issue as far as pushing any water on to any other resident. He said the water during the last storm almost came up to the homes, but nowhere near entering the footprint of the home. He said that the family is a growing family and purchased this home and needed to build an addition to accommodate their family. He said that they looked at the potential of going vertical, but felt that it was awkward as far as being respectful to the historical house in the front. He said that there is an existing awkward garage that was built at the skew so they began to explore the possibility of removing the non-historical garage that was built in the 1980’s and build a one story addition that would not compete with the historical home and keep in the design nature of the neighborhood by keeping it low. He said that they would like to straighten it out as it relates to the main house more and not pull it any closer to the property line than the existing garage was, which is where there were some setback issues where there is an existing building that is already over the setbacks. He said that this would be improving the situation in that respect, and creating a connection between the main building and the addition that is lightly touching the buildings and have it set as all glass so you can see through the two additions and see the marsh beyond, which is the intention. He said at the same time, keeping the addition low enough so it is a few steps down from the main house in order to keep the height a profile of the house, but high enough so there are no flooding issues. He said that the addition is also set back from the main house so it recedes into the background. He stated that for the Old Village Historic District Commission

driveway, they are staying with the materials that are used on the existing house to make it all work together. Ms. Dickson asked if three bedrooms were going to be added. Mr. Stevenson stated that in the main house, there are three bedrooms, and the addition would be the master bedroom. Ms. Dickson asked if the footprint on the historical home would be changed. Mr. Stevenson stated that there will be interior alterations and minor structural work in the piers and the roof; however, no changes to the footprint or windows. Ms. Wilson asked what the idea was behind keeping the scale of a garage for the master when there is no garage function. She stated that it is a wide addition so it is asking for a large relief on the side yard. She stated that it is showing a two car garage, but there is no garage function. Mr. Stevenson stated that there is a covered carport in the front, so there will be cars parked in front of it. He said that it was more for relief than anything. He said that it does not have to show as a garage door, and there are other ways to make that wall more interesting. Ms. Wilson stated that the size of the addition is too wide relative to the existing house. She said that it is slightly competitive and the master does not need to be that wide. She said that it is no longer a garage. She stated that a lot of historic neighborhoods have carriage houses and there is a vernacular that is established, but that is not here, so in general, the Commission attempts to encourage homeowners to do away with the garage aesthetic. She stated that there is an opportunity to eliminate it, because the homeowners are not asking for a garage. She would be in support of some relief, not seven feet, and the addition be explored more as residential vernacular and windows, possibly shuttered, to address the street rather than a faux garage door. She said she would be more in support of that relief if it was to get wider connection. She stated that the idea of a hyphen is really rich and to have the ability to see through to the marsh is even more appealing. She stated that if the car proportion was no longer the concern and could get narrower with the glassy connection Old Village Historic District Commission

being more prominent, she would be more in favor of the side yard relief; however, not for two garage doors. Mr. Stevenson asked if the Commission would be acceptable with three feet off the property line. Ms. Wilsons stated that not as it is drawn, but possibly for a different reason. She said that she generally does not have an issue with side yard relief; however, she would suggest pulling off the side yard slightly. She said if it was for a more compelling reason, such as more view to the marsh, more sunlight passing between the two pieces, etc., she would be more agreeable. Ms. Rowe stated that the flat roof carport coming off of the front appears to just be stuck on. She stated that if the addition did not look like a carport garage, it would fit in much nicer. Mr. Keenan stated that he is agreeable with Ms. Wilson and Ms. Rowe’s comments regarding the carport, as he had similar concerns. He said that the additional elevations are major improvements and are nice. He stated that if the width of the addition could be tightened up, it would look really nice. Ms. Dickson stated that she does have an issue with encroachments and does not see a need for it. She stated that there is ample room for a master bedroom. Ms. Wilson stated that she agrees that the master bedroom does not need to be that large. She stated that it is not parallel to the property lines. She stated that if you look at the front of the house to the right, they have given away a lot of side yard setback, so giving back the trapezoid and inverse on the other side is something she could get comfortable with. She stated that something needs to be given back to the neighborhood if the Commission is going to provide that type of relief and asked for more detail. She stated that she would like to see that area stronger and cleaner and not the garage doors. Ms. Rowe asked if the entrance closest to the street was necessary. She said that there is too much going on in the small corridor. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Stevenson stated that this is an existing stair and could be eliminated. He said that the owners asked for it in order to put in a mud room; however, they did not have this as part of their design. He agreed that it would clean up that area. Mr. Keenan stated that conceptually, the Commission has provided good direction.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Neil Stevenson, architect for the homeowner, stated that at the last meeting, he presented this project and there were a few things he was asked to review. He stated that one was to increase the distance of the connection piece, which highlights a design feature that would be more attractive. He stated in doing so, it reduced the width of the addition and pulled it in a foot off of the property line. He said that he was also asked to rethink the design of the structure over the vehicles so that it integrated better with the design of the house. He said another change, which was more of a budgetary change was, instead of restructuring the entire roof from the existing house, non-historical roof, they kept this so they are able to work with what they have, because it was too expensive. He stated that the homeowners decided to leave it as is. He said another proposed change was to simplify the entry at the connection, because there were side stairs. He said that they reversed the side stairs and created a patio to step up, which simplifies the path and cleaned up the entrance. He said they added windows to the addition, making it look less like a garage and more of an addition. Ms. Rowe said she has a difficult time with the carport which looks stuck on to a historic cottage. She stated that the glass in the connection looks great, as well as removing the steps. She added that the carport does not work for her. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the roof in the hyphen is flat. Mr. Stevenson stated that there is a slight slope which they have to gutter in the rear; however, it is not completely flat. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the roof on the addition runs in front of the hyphen. Mr. Stevenson said that it connects and the intention was to minimize the impact of the connection. Ms. Wilson stated that the patio does not have a roof; it is just over the glass connection. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Stevenson said that the roof extends approximately three feet in front of it. Ms. Wilson stated that it is subordinate to the main roof and she appreciates the changes. She stated that she lives across from a carport and said that it is not contained and is tacked on as an addition to a historic house, which is unfortunate. She said that it detracts from the roof that has been done on the addition, which goes back to the cottage original house, which is very attractive. She said then there is the carport with a hip roof that detracts from all the other beautiful work that is being proposed. She said this is a difficult situation, because she realizes the homeowners want the carport, but does not see a solution for it. She stated that she is in support of everything else, except the carport. Mr. Keenan said he appreciates the glass connection and what was done everywhere else; however, he does have a concern with the carport. Mr. Stevenson asked if it were designed as a garage and was enclosed. Ms. Wilson stated that she would prefer to see a garage move forward on the lot and put a greenspace between the garage and the house and alleviate some of the driveway. Mr. Keenan stated that typically the Commission is not in favor of additional structures; however, in this case, there could be some compromise. Mr. Stevenson stated that this provides him with good direction.

label: 720 Pitt Street
request: 720 Pitt Street – HISTORIC 5954 – Final Review for Shutters and Handle Rails [Consent Motion] Old Village Historic District Commission

events.text:
Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. He stated in the applicant’s original application there was an error and she considered the BAR to include a pool and an unenclosed deck. He said that she has the revised numbers and is below the BAR, but it was an error in their calculations. Elizabeth Drake, architect for the homeowner, stated that they are actually at 30%. She said that what the Dukes would like is remove the screen porch on the back of their home, keep the front covered porch, add a deck, a pool and a covered cabana on the back, which will not be screened in. She said they would like to enclose the cabana. She said that the Dukes have a long narrow lot and the back of their lot runs into Ben Tatum Lake. She said where there is flooding or the gates are closed, the water comes up into their yard and under their basement. She said they want to have a pool, but do not want it down at the ground level, but would also like to maintain some greenspace in the backyard. She said if they remove the screened porch off the back, terracing down slightly to a raised pool, it would get them out of the flood plain. She said putting the pool directly behind takes away the visuals, so it is not seen from the street. She said the cabana pulls off to the side where the driveway comes down, so it is more of a functional Old Village Historic District Commission

part of the house where the entrance is to the back. She said they would also like to enlarge their laundry / mud room and increase the entry into that space. Ms. Wilson asked if Ms. Drake knew how far it is from the back property line. She said it is at least 60 feet. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the screened in porch proposed for removal is historic. Ms. Drake said that their historic home is the front piece and all else has been added on. Mr. Hirshorn asked when the screened porch was added. Ms. Wilson stated that it was in the late 1990’s. Mr. Hirshorn asked if there was any way to put a ground level pool in the back. Ms. Drake said that the survey does not have elevations, but the property does slope down and the water from the lake does creep up. She said the backyard is wet and the owners thought if they took the back porch off, it would become their deck, as they would like to preserve some greenspace. She said that having an elevated pool would be a nice option. Ms. Wilson stated that she is not sure a ground pool is possible. She said her property is approximately three feet higher than their property as she lives 2 properties down. She said her backyard is likely three feet higher and her pool floods during a heavy rain. Ms. Dickson asked about restrictions on elevated pools. Ms. Wilson added that there are no restrictions. She stated that the issue was that once they approved the elevated pool there, everyone else would want to request an above ground pool. Ms. Rowe said that here in the village, we must consider the lots such as the Dukes where an in ground pool is not possible. Ms. Dickson said that the question then becomes whether they have to have a pool or not. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that there were specific stipulations regarding the above ground pool. He said part of the concessions was that the specific lot was hidden from the view of any right of way and significant adjustments were made to soften it to make the deck area smaller. There was a significant reduction in deck space and amenity space. He said that they are allowed only under very specific circumstances. Ms. Drake stated that the pool and back yard area are visually isolated and not infringing on any neighbors. She said they would buffer it with the terracing. Mr. Keenan asked about the height of the actual pool deck. Ms. Drake said it is approximately six feet six inches. Mr. Keenan said that his concern is the height of the pool and does not want to get into a situation where it is visible from the street or surrounding neighbors and wondering if the pool house could be moved directly behind the pool. Ms. Drake said that it would infringe on the yard and take away from the play space. Mr. Keenan asked if the cabana is screened. Ms. Drake said the cabana would have operable louvers with wood siding to match the house. Ms. Wilson stated that the lower you go with the pool, the further away it gets pushed from the house. She said the homeowners may want to consider not dropping it down and could get rid of six feet of deck and hug it into the house. She appreciates the fact that it is getting tucked into the house. She said that the hip roof does not fit, because on one hand, it is going to be sided and dressed it like the house so that from the street, it does not read as a cabana. She said cabanas are becoming prevalent, but are not in keeping with the Old Village. She said if it were more of a gable similar to the house and then continued the effort in refining it and tying it into the house, then from the street, it is not coming out any more than it is now. She said it is an improvement. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Drake said she did a gable from this direction, but it became tall, as she was trying to put a good pitch on there. She said she will explore it once again. Ms. Wilson said that the height is not an issue with her. She said what she has the most trouble with is the over width of it from the house. Ms. Drake said that the terracing was to keep the railings down. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would like to stipulate that the Commission would like all this to work out. He said that this new construction faces the lake, so it is very visible from Royall Avenue. He said that it needs to be treated as sensitively as the last approved construction of a raised pool on Friend Street, where the Commission met in the middle and significantly reduced the elevation. Ms. Wilson said that the pool was the same level as the house on Friend Street. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it was originally a stepped infinity look in the front. Ms. Wilson stated that Ms. Drake is not proposing infinity. She said they are planters. Ms. Drake responded in the affirmative and said that the Commission is drifting away from stepping down to the pool. She said you do not want it to look too big, but want to soften it. Mr. Hirshorn said he likes the idea of tying it closer to the historic structure so that it does not come out so much particularly from the Royall Street elevation. Ms. Drake said she would like it to engage the yard slightly. Mr. Hirshorn said that he would like to figure out a way to reduce the scale and keep it less visible from the surrounding area. Ms. Drake said that they were contemplating putting in a small bathroom. Ms. Wilson asked where the finished floor would be. Ms. Drake said it would be the same level as the deck. She said the homeowners would like to have some type of outdoor bathroom amenity. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson said that she would not add anything else at this point and work on the cabana and pool. She added that the bathroom would have to be at the finished floor of the house and it would take away from the primary deck. Mr. Keenan asked if the wall is stucco. Ms. Drake said that it is not and said she was contemplating having it open similar to a porch. She said they were discussing doing brick. Ms. Wilson said that if Ms. Drake is able to shrink the footprint slightly and make the cabana look like a cabana on the inside, and all primary house on the outside and tie them together. She suggested toning it down slightly from the street. Mr. Keenan stated that this is conceptual and asked Ms. Drake to provide a list of materials at the next meeting. Ms. Wilson stated that from the other side of Royall Avenue, it is an improvement and the stepping down grounds the house and it does not look like a raised generic house. Mr. Keenan stated that more detail needs to be provided to the Commission. Mr. Hirshorn stated that from his perspective, the initial gambit is to stick to the stipulations that were made after long and hard discussion on the raised pool. He said from his prospective, to change from that compromise, detailed presentation will be necessary on the way it is being stepped down. Ms. Drake said that she can get the surveyor to get some spot elevations on there; however, when a pool is raised, the material is going to be difficult. She said it will be exposed to the weather and you do not want it to get run- down in a short period of time, so any input would be welcome. Ms. Wilson stated that the way it is wrapped, it will never be seen because it is under the deck. She said there will still be piers for the deck. Ms. Drake asked how to treat under the railing. Ms. Wilson said the same way you would treat any deck or porch. She said that the whole pool is being wrapped and there is not a big exposed stucco wall, which is to Ms. Drake’s advantage and can match the existing house or Old Village Historic District Commission

make another proposal. She said there is no massive weeping pool wall to contend with, which is good.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Elizabeth Drake, architect for the homeowners, stated that she listened to Commission members at the last meeting. She said they are removing the screened porch and the clients would like to have a cabana separate from the main house, as well as a raised pool. She said they did get the spot elevations which are shown. She said the lot is low and backs up onto the Ben Tatum pond. They originally had the deck surrounding the pool at the height of the house. She said they have the whole raised deck dropped approximately 15 inches and made the pool narrower by approximately 12 inches. She said by having you step directly out of the house, it reduced the amount of decking that was needed, so she pulled the structure closer to the house by approximately 42 inches. She went to a gable, as opposed to the hip and was trying to keep the roof low with the hip, but it was not in keeping with the house. She said they designed the fireplace, so you are not able to see it when looking down the driveway. She said they put it at the back of the property. She said on the left side, she had the stairs at the edge of the setback; however, she pulled the stairs away from the setback and will have some planting as you step down. She said the terraces are trying to keep the appearance of railing to a minimum and will need to be worked out more. She said she would like to look more at the massing because they are limited as to the size of the deck, but not make a raised pool with a lot of railings, which is what the terracing and landscaping is. She said in the last presentation, she was not clear that the owners were requesting privacy; therefore, they are requesting that the cabana have louvered shutters that are operable. She said this would provide privacy. She also cleaned up the golf cart and garage storage as well. Ms. Montgomery stated that when she previously served on this Commission, there were negative feelings towards Bermuda shutters. She asked if there is an alternate shutter or has there been a change in the Commission’s position. Ms. Wilson asked if the shutters tilted out or hinge open. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Drake stated that that they tilt out which would provide the most privacy; however, there are those that pivot. She said that they are open to comments on this. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the last iteration of the Commission on Bermuda shutters was they would be acceptable if they were fixed. Ms. Wilson asked why they would use a louvered shutter with the hinging at the top. She said if they are hinged, you would have just as much privacy when closed, but would also have the ability to open them. She said the look is the same when closed. Ms. Rowe stated that Ms. Drake did everything that the Commission requested, and it looks very nice. Mr. Pohlman stated that in the guidelines, under Doors and Windows, it states, “do not install new shutters that are clearly out of keeping with the building’s character. This includes shutters of the wrong size or architectural style for the house. When closed, shutter should cover the window completely, without overlapping each other on the wall surfaces. On historic buildings, window shutters must be operational rather than fixed.” He stated that this would be the only guideline regarding Bermuda shutters, which would be if the Commission felt that it was the wrong size or architectural style for the house. Ms. Wilson said a louvered shutter goes more with the house, as well as the ability to open it. She asked if there was a reason why Ms. Drake did not match the soffit and detail of the house. She said that it is the only thing with a traditional gable open rafter, whereas everything else has the Queen Ann return on the house and there are a lot of them, so it is a very strong vocabulary for the house. She asked if Ms. Drake was going to screen under the cabana, so whatever is put under will be screened. Ms. Drake said that there will not be any screening. Ms. Wilson said under the house, what is put in between the piers, is there going to be wood. Ms. Drake said she has not intended to do so. She said that they have not considered that portion yet and thought they would louver around the pool but leave underneath the house open. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson said that the massing looks good and the relationship with the house is much better, which is why she is looking at the smaller details. She said she feels very good about the massing. She asked Ms. Drake to put the dimension from the rear property line when she returns. She said that the eave detail should match as it is a house with a really strong gable vocabulary and the only gable that would stand out. She said Ms. Drake has done everything else to knit it together. Ms. Drake asked if Ms. Wilson would like for her to take the siding horizontal as well. Ms. Wilson responded in the negative. She said under the house should be concealed so at the very least, the area that faces Pitt Street should be screened. Mr. Hirshorn said that the view from Royall Avenue is also prominent and suggested that Ms. Drake screen the entire area under the house. Ms. Drake said that she likes the elevation looking back from there. She said she was trying to design the cabana differently without the return; however, understands it is needed. She said on the backside, she changed the overhang. Originally where the screened porch is, it came down to a slope, she was making the eaves line up between the two and bringing it down to a more severe facia soffit to give it an edge, but it is not something that goes with the rest of the house. Ms. Wilson stated that if Ms. Drake does this, it will require a column on the outside corner where it turns, because it is a massive overhang to wrap the house. She said she is not sure how it is totally going to get attached to the house. Ms. Dovre said that she was also thinking of a column for the connection, but other than that, she believes Ms. Drake has done everything in compliance. Ms. Drake said that she would review this, because it is open, so she may change it up, but it does need a column. Ms. Wilson asked if Ms. Drake was trying to get it covered into the entry. Ms. Drake said she liked the way it wrapped and brought the house around. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson said that she likes it on the back covering the exit out to the pool more. Mr. Hirshorn asked if there is any comment on the subject of elevated pool decks. He said the application for an elevated pool, a concession was made because it was secluded and not in view of the right of way. Mr. Pohlman added that it was also because the slope of the lot decreased significantly. Mr. Hirshorn stated that this is a similar lot situation; however, the exception is that the pool deck is clearly visible from Royall Avenue across the lake. Ms. Wilson stated that the Commission is not able to comment on landscaping; however, when landscaped it will be more buffered and the pool will be screened. She said that she is advocating for this project, because she is in favor of the greenspace being preserved. She said it is a deep lot and there is a large greenspace area in the rear that backs up to Ben Tatum pond. She lives two lots away so she understands how wet it is in the back. She said at the very least, it would have to be a partially raised pool. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he understands that landscaping is not the purview of the Commission, but he would still like to see some preliminary landscaping. Mr. Pohlman stated that this is outside the Commission’s purview and would not be advisable to request. Ms. Montgomery stated that the homeowner will no doubt use some type of landscaping, because it will be very visible. Mr. Pohlman stated that the homeowners are proposing planters and asked if Mr. Juan would provide building code guidance on how far the planters must be for height to get around the railing. Mr. Juan stated that it is 30 inches. Mr. Pohlman said that if the homeowners install 30-inch planter beds, they will be able to get around the railing restriction around the pool. He said they would be planter beds, which is a structure. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Drake stated that she has one planter bed and there is still some work to be done. She stated that she is attempting to wrap the lower bed all the way, which reduces the height of the cabana. She said once it is constructed, she believes the homeowners will plant some landscaping at the back of the property. John Dukes, homeowner, stated that they absolutely want to landscape the back for privacy, as well as the fence. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the elevated pools/decks are not something the Commission wants to see all around unless there were specific reasons. He said he would like to know if the pool is going to be shielded. Ms. Wilson stated that she believes these requests can be handled on a case by case basis. She said they are fortunate that their lot is deep and are able to provide screened space to buffer it. Ms. Montgomery said the area underneath the pool would be a great place for bicycles and other items. Ms. Drake said that on one side, there will be some type of opening. Mr. Dukes anticipated it being enclosed to hide any pool equipment. Ms. Drake said there is storage elsewhere and under the cabana. Mr. Hirshorn said he believes the architect and homeowner have received good comments.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Elizabeth Drake, architect for the homeowners, stated that she apologizes that there are no details. She said that the clients would like a pool and wanted to push off of their existing kitchen and add a new laundry and mud room entrance. She said they proposed to remove the existing screened porch off the back and the side porch as well and will be rebuilding them. They propose to pull out from the kitchen area and pull off a gable with all the details to match existing. She said they need to relocate the HVAC and will use the picket style at the front of the house around the unit. She said in the back in the cabana area, they would like to make it transparent and less heavy and thought the cable railing would be more appropriate. With the new rule, they thought they were set with the gable, but when they learned they would have to do 20 feet, they explored lowering the pool deck and it did not work. She said they decided to try and work with the hip roof, and if you look at the front, there is a hip on the Pitt Street side, and she pulled that slope and moved it back to the cabana. She said the clients favor the Bahama shutter look, so they have come back with that proposal and will provide more detail and photographs of what the homeowners want. The fireplace was moved over to the property line, which was previously on the pond side, which will be brick. She said they are attempting to tie it into the ground using brick and coming up with louvers that would match the rest of the house. She said at the bench area, there is the one by four vertical tongue and groove, that the first step down on the terrace would be the bench where the children could gather, and the landscaping would be on the lower terrace. She wrapped it around to the side and is pulling Old Village Historic District Commission

it around and doing two planters to soften it. She said there is a full drop and the railings would be along that side. She said the idea of the walls at the pool deck is for privacy and the materials were going to be similar to the cabana and have a wall over at the banquette which is close to the house. She said in the site plans, she did address the distance from the rear property line, which is 59.5 feet to the edge of the cabana from the rear property line. She said that the six-foot grade is in the middle and comes closer to the cabana. She got rid of the wrap around shed and changed the roof off the backside of the house. Ms. Wilson stated that the front of the house is historic, but the back is not. She said in terms of materials on the cabana, she asked if the columns would be wood. Ms. Drake said it is wood. Ms. Montgomery asked if stucco was considered in order to lessen the brick look. Ms. Drake said that there are brick piers there currently and the clients like brick. Ms. Wilson said that this backyard floods which is why they need the lower level of masonry. Mr. Hirshorn feels that Ms. Drake has addressed a number of the issues. He asked if there were any feelings on the new hip roof on the cabana. Ms. Rowe said that she likes it. Ms. Wilson said the change was based on the maximum ridge height they were allowed. She said that Ms. Drake has done a good job tying the height to the overhang. Mr. Hirshorn said that he would like to see more of a finished design where the materials are showcased and what type of bricks are being used, because it does not appear complete. He said particularly the brick and he would be comfortable if Ms. Drake stipulates that it is Savannah or Old Charleston. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Rowe asked if that could be done at staff level if the brick was designated. John Dukes, homeowner, said they would absolutely match what is existing, which is the Savannah Grey on the chimney. Ms. Wilson stated that the cabana could be approved with the stipulation that all the details match the house. She said what she would personally like to see, is that the railings come back, but that it would not preclude them from permitting the cabana and working with the pool company and getting things moving. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the Commission members were agreeable with the Bermuda shutters. Mr. Pohlman said the guidelines only state that inharmonious shutter styles should not be installed. Ms. Wilson stated she believes the Commission can approve the project but ask for a railing detail and an example of a shutter at a future date that would not slow the homeowners down from engineering and permitting. Mr. Hirshorn said that he would be happy to hear a motion with stipulations on materials for the brick, shutters and the railing. Ms. Wilson stated that if there is existing brick on the house, the brick should match the house, and this can be stipulated. She said they should only return on this item if the brick cannot be matched or they want to do something different. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve the cabana, pool and deck of the project at 720 Pitt Street, with the stipulation that the facia and roof details match the house, the brick matches the house, the columns are to be wood and the applicant will bring back railing details and a sample or picture of a shutter at a future date; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.
