label: 6 William Street
request: 6 William Street – (Survey 6030) – Final Review for Installation of On-Street Parking pad. [Consent Motion]

events.text:
Guideline Discussion regarding Garages & Accessory Buildings #6 (Moved earlier in the agenda) Mr. Keenan stated that from the Guidelines, under Garages & Accessory Buildings, #6 reads: Pergolas and trellises, being absent in historical context, should be placed in rear yards and not visible from public rights of way. Mr. Keenan stated that this is what the guidelines state; however, there is no definition. Ms. Wilson stated that the issue came before the Commission when Mr. Keenan was absent. She stated that Commission members were looking for a way that would not implicate the Commission or violate the ordinance, but also not feel compelled to request that the owner(s) deconstruct what is currently there. She said that Commission members agreed on a definition or clarification between a pergola, trellis and an arbor. She said that they are all utilized interchangeably and clarified what the Commission will not allow. Mr. Keenan stated that Mr. Pohlman has provided definitions for the Commissions review. Mr. Keenan read the definitions for each structure. Ms. Wilson stated that the concern appears to be how to eliminate these structures over people’s gates onto their property and believes the Commission needs to state that none of them are allowed in the front. Mr. Keenan read further, “Pergolas and trellises, being absent in the historical context should be placed in rear yards and not visible from public rights of way”. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Dickson stated that pergolas, trellises and arbors were all present in historic context, so this sentence needs to be eliminated from the guidelines. Ms. Wilson stated that the question is if the Commission will allow this at their discretion. Mr. Keenan stated that he would be agreeable to a case by case request. He stated that he does not believe you can eliminate them permanently. Ms. Dickson stated that how this was first addressed, was due to the home on Hibben Street, which is not a pergola, but an arbor. She stated that it is a complete outdoor room. She stated that the Commission does not want any additional structures of this type. Ms. Wilson stated that if the Town does not issue permits for these structures, does this mean that they do not come under the purview of the OVHDC either. Mr. Pohlman stated that there is language in the guidelines regarding driveways, sidewalks, decks, etc. which do not go through the permitting process. He stated that the question comes up often about how something was put in without the OVHDC’s approval. He said this is why, because they do not come to the Town for a permit and are not familiar with the guidelines of the OVHDC. Mr. Keenan stated that he is agreeable with the definitions provided by Mr. Pohlman; however, the Commission should have the leeway or the right to make a decision based on the application. Ms. Rowe agreed and said that there are so many factors involved. Ms. Wilson asked who did the diagrams for the guidelines. Mr. Pohlman stated that the images were obtained from Beaufort, SC and Beaufort, NC. He stated that they are in the resources and not the guidelines. Ms. Wilson asked what would be the best way to have images put in, because this is still not clear, and images would help. She said that there should be an example of what an acceptable pergola looks like. She stated that it would still be done on a case by case basis and the location would still need to be placed in the backyard. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Pohlman asked if Commission members were contemplating the elimination of the large shade structures in view of the right of way. He said that placing specific language into item #6 with sizes and dimension. Ms. Wilson expressed that all these types of structures should be within the OVHDC’s purview and have the Commission evaluate them on a case by case basis. She stated that they should not be seen by the public right of way, in general. Mr. Pohlman stated that this language could be specific to state this, and that it must be reviewed by the OVHDC. Ms. Dickson stated that the definitions need to be included. Ms. Wilson stated that if one is mentioned, all three should be mentioned, because they are somewhat the same. Mr. Pohlman stated that if Commission members would like to reword this item now, he would insert the three definitions from Webster’s dictionary into the definition section of the guidelines. He asked how the Commission would like the new section to read; pergolas, trellises and arbors should be placed in the rear yards and not visible from the public right of way. Ms. Wilson requested to add, “And are under the purview of the Old Village Historic District Commission, regardless of the cost of the structure”. Mr. Pohlman stated that it is mentioned in the guidelines. Ms. Rowe suggested adding, “And should not be inharmonious with the surroundings”. Ms. Rowe asked where “cabana” is included. Ms. Wilson stated that a cabana has a roof, so this is a permitted item. Mr. Pohlman stated that if a resident attempted to build a cabana, it would not only be against the OVHDC guidelines, but it is against Town ordinance to build this structure without a permit. Ms. Wilson stated that a cabana may not be approved without Mr. Keenan; however, the pergola, trellis or arbor can. Mr. Pohlman stated that there are two other matters regarding the guidelines that he would like to address with the Commission. He said the first would be under “Sidewalks, Driveways and Streets, #7, which states a Old Village Historic District Commission

minimum of one off street parking should be provided on all resident’s lots. A standard parking space should be 9x18”. He said that this is actually underneath what Town Ordinance now requires in the Old Village. He said that he would recommend striking this, because it will lead to confusion. Ms. Wilson asked what the Ordinance states. Mr. Pohlman stated that it was recently revised to state that the 9x18 is a Town standard in normal parking ordinance and in addition, in the Old Village, “#5 Parking Requirements. A minimum of two off street spaces are required per residence and additional space for homes over 2,500 sf of gross floor area are required at the rate of one space per ever 1,000 sf over 2,500 sf. Ms. Wilson stated that this will now cause more pavement. Mr. Pohlman stated that this is Town Ordinance and requested by the previous chairman, Mr. Bennett, to be put into the Town Ordinance. He asked the Commission if it would be acceptable to eliminate #7 from the guidelines. Ms. Wilson asked if an item could be added to the guidelines. She stated that Sullivan’s Island has enacted the 50% green rule, because there are so many pervious surfaces. She stated that the impervious on Sullivan’s Island is 30% and there are no variances for this. She stated that you can add as much impervious; however, the lot must stay 50% green. She stated that you are only allowed to cover landscaping material on 50% of the lot. She stated that this makes a huge difference. Mr. Pohlman reiterated that landscaping is outside the purview of the Commission. Ms. Wilson stated that hardscape is not and suggested changing the guidelines to state: “Hardscape can only additionally cover 10% above and beyond the 40% allowable impervious”. Mr. Pohlman stated that he will have to address this with Administration, because the ordinance for the Old Village states that up to 40% of the lot can be impervious. He stated that this is what the law states and wants to ensure the guidelines do not go outside of the law. He stated that he would have to discuss with Legal Counsel as well. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that if Legal Counsel is not in favor, to provide suggestion on how it can be stated. Ms. Dickson stated that Sullivan’s Island will also request residents to demonstrate that it covers the square footage as presented. Ms. Wilson stated that Sullivan’s Island requires a foundation survey before the framing is allowed to begin. Ms. Dickson stated that if you drive through the Village, there are houses that were approved by the OVHDC; however, what was approved and what was built are not the same. Mr. Juan stated that he would go back and review this project. Mr. Pohlman stated that he would like clarification on another item in the guidelines, because it is being addressed, which is the model. He said in the guidelines, as one of the required submittal items, require a 3D computer model if a structure is being improved over 50% or new construction. He said that he has been asked if it can be a physical model that the applicant has taken images of, as opposed to a computer model. Commission member disagreed. Ms. Wilson asked why designers/architects cannot bring in a hand built model, to scale and accurate. Mr. Keenan stated that he personally prefers the CAD. Mr. Pohlman stated that several architects have asked to present hand built models due to the cost to the client, for both conceptual and final. He stated that as it is written, “Applicants for new construction, and or renovations, and or additions of 50% or greater, require a three dimensional computer rendering of the project”. Ms. Wilson stated that she would be agreeable to eliminate this for the 50% rule, because it could be cumbersome. She stated that for new construction it should be a 3D model. She asked if someone comes before the Commission and would like to build a two scale paper model, is it something within staff’s purview to ask Commission members to have them bring it to the meeting. She said that it is not what the Commission encourages; however, there will be cases where it is appropriate. Old Village Historic District Commission

IV. Staff Approvals (None)

request: 6 William St. Approved for alterations to a driveway and construction of a rear yard pool

request: 215 Pitt Street – (HISTORIC 5925) – Final Review for Reroofing [Consent Motion]

request: 127 Chicco Lane – n/a – Generator

events.text: Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Ms. Wilson made a motion to move #3, 127 Chicco Lane to the end; seconded by Mr. Hirshorn. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Julie O’Connor, designer on the project, stated that they were here last month for conceptual comment and with those comments they have made changes to the design. She stated that they moved the house away from the marsh approximately five or six feet, but at the same time, added an 11 foot deep one story porch on the back that was not there previously. She said that they also reduced the entire rear mass to one story. She said previously they had a two story mass that was closer to the marsh and there was no porch on the back, so they reduced the entire section to a one story element. She said the only two story section is the square section that is forward on Chicco Lane. She said they deepened the front porch to give a better entry statement and slightly modify the bays on the front. She said they added piers under them to make more of a statement. She said they also modified the siding materials which were initially shingle on the Chicco Lane side and lap siding underneath. This has been changed Old Village Historic District Commission

to board and batten on the top. She said the comments made were that it was too busy. She added that everything will be the same color so it will be more of a textural change. She said that the amount of heated and cooled square footage has been reduced and increased the amount of the porch square footage. She said it went from 12% of porches on the original submittal to 15%. She said the BAR remained somewhat the same, although slightly reduced. She said they are now at 4,081 heated and cooled square feet. She did a quick survey of the adjacent properties to the left and right of their square footage and averaged those together. She mentioned that the house at 121 Chicco Lane was the smallest of them all, but their proposed home is at the average size of heated and cooled square footage and exceed the amount of porches necessary. She said they are happy with the amount of porch gained on the marsh side. She submitted drone photographs electronically from the marsh in order to show how their proposed home will relate to their adjacent neighbors. She said the impact that the fencing around their neighboring properties has on the marsh front, was particularly of interest to her. She said their closest neighbors have large trees on the marsh side and their property does not. She said you are able to see just how much more forward the lots on the right are. She said that while their proposed home is approximately 15 feet forward of their neighbor, she does not believe it is a significant impact given the amount of fencing and grade that has been added to that property and the trees that make such an impact. She feels that they have done a good job at responding to the Commission’s comments and one of the great benefits of going down to one story is now they have a beautiful vaulted space for the living room and the amount of porch is beautiful making it a see through structure. She stated that the drone photograph also shows that all of the adjacent homes, with the exception of 121 Chicco Lane, are full two stories and have a large presence on the marsh and fill up the width of their lots. She said in terms of the harborscape, their home is consistent with this. She said they have responded well to the Commission’s comments. Ruth Brennan, 121 Chicco Lane, property owner, stated that she has a handout for the Commission and she and her husband have been living there for over 21 years. She said she would like to address the culture of Old Village Historic District Commission

the Old Village and stated that to own this type of property and enjoy the marsh, ecology and everything present is appreciated, and the value of this property is very high. She said when they moved into their home, they knew what they were getting and understood the respect they had to have for all their neighbors. She said that the designer failed to show any example of how the house would sit out on the marsh, which is very imposing and using the critical line to get the mass of the house that they want. She said that they all have the critical line, but no one she knows on the waterfront has done this. She said the proposed home is out of the norm for the Old Village and the harborscape. She said that there is also a pool that is 30 feet out into the marsh past their front metal gate corner and said what they will be looking at is a pool, which is not inconspicuous. She said the house and piers will sit out into the line of the actual land mass and will be built into the marsh. She said the second page is their rendition, and added that this is a 70 foot wide lot, and there is a 5,400 square foot home on it and it is entirely too big for the lot. She said it goes all the way down the entire lot on both sides so the neighbors on either side see a wall of a house, especially on the Gaskin’s side. She said that on page three is the biggest issue, which is the flooding. She said that they have a very strong flooding issue along the marsh area and have always had issues. She said that any high tide that is 8 feet, it is on the property. She said that this is not going away. She said this is an Army Corps of Engineers issue that is going to have to be addressed; however a pool and piers do not need to be approved, which would be a potential issue for drainage and for their land that is adjacent. She stated that this is a very significant concern for them. She said the next page is the Gaskin’s home, which is 131 Chicco Street and it indicates how much water goes into their yard. She said if the proposed home builds up with the two feet requirement, which is allowed, from where their pier sits, which is four feet, this is now a total of six feet. She said an eight foot tide would go into the proposed pool and into the subfloor area. She said there is going to be an issue with moisture and controlled moisture, which is not going to work. She provided additional photographs that indicate how many occasions the water line goes back. She also added an article from September, 2017 that discusses the new restrictions on property and the Old Village Historic District Commission

way homeowners are addressing their properties for flooding purposes, because the water table is rising. She said there are other articles regarding the Old Village and lot coverage. She said just because a critical line is used to increase the massing of a house, it does not mean that you also push it into the marsh. She added that it is so negligent, stripping the neighbors of their wonderful experience on the water. She said none of the houses are without green space, which brings to the culture a sense of respect. She said on the proposed plans, they do not have any green space and said that the house is ten feet off both sides. She said it is only six feet from the front of her home, because there is a thirty foot pool proposed. She said that it is completely disrespectful to the culture, the environment and the neighbors are very concerned. She said that they are setback fifty feet, when the requirement is twenty-five. She said she is asking that the Commission look at this, because they could easily move their house up towards the driveway and the twenty five feet forward and still have the twenty five foot setback. She said all that is out there is concrete. She said what they are really there for is the water front and all the neighbors sit on their porches. She said it would be simple for the homeowners to push their house up twenty five feet forward and still be setback twenty five feet and respect that the adjacent properties are also back. They should not be an exception. She said what sticks out to her is the appropriate and the inappropriate plan shown on the guidelines and said the proposed home falls into the category of the inappropriate plan presented. She said that new construction should be harmonious in size, scale, massing, form, etc. She does not feel the house is attractive and other things could have been done to make it attractive. She said the property owners have every right to build their home and they welcome them. She asked if this was a spec home or if there are real homeowners. She read the guidelines that state, “new construction should adhere to the underlying setbacks required of the lot”, which according to the Town ordinance, it does adhere; however, for the Old Village, it does not apply. She further indicated that the setbacks should respect the structures of the adjacent properties, which is on page 28. She said in closing, she would like to ask that the pool not be approved, as more work needs to be accomplished in order to consider a pool and it should be inconspicuous to the neighbors. Old Village Historic District Commission

She said that she has a pool that sits in the middle of their property. She said she has the right to do things on her property, but does not do them, because it is the right thing to do. She said if a precedence is set, it will cause a landslide effect and the Old Village and the marsh will cease to exist. Keith Jones, 121 Chicco Lane, said that he always knew that a house would be built on that lot one day. He said his concerns are very similar to his wife’s and all her comments were from the Old Village Historic District Commission guidelines. He said there is streetscape, harborscape and how buildings are subject to the Commission’s design. He said that the home does not follow the harborscape of the Village. He said that in reference to the proposed pool, the shallow end of the pool is at six feet and the deep end is at five feet and this is the elevation on the property. He said that on a seven foot tide, he does not see how this can be done. He said the pool goes six feet past the corner of the fence of their property in front of the old sewer, not where their house comes to. He said he does not understand the engineering of this or any of their retaining walls. He said with the amount of water that comes onto this lot, they must look at what is going to happen when the water comes in on both sides. Janice Gaskins, 131 Chicco, stated that she is here to speak on behalf of her neighbor, Fred Crawford who lives next door to her. She said he was unable to attend this evening. She read Mr. Crawford’s note: My name is Fred Crawford and we have lived for 37 years in the house we built at 135 Chicco Lane, in 1985. At that time, our neighbors’ homes on either side were set back to the exact same distance from the water. We saw no reason to be any closer to the water and we also wanted to be a good neighbor, so we set our home back at the same distance as theirs. There were no oak trees on our lot and we still have no oak trees on our lot that would have prevented us from building closer to the water. In 1989, hurricane Hugo pretty much destroyed both neighbors’ homes. After the lots were sold, the new owners chose to also be good neighbors and set their houses back at the same exact line with us, as to the distances as previous houses and made the same choice as ours. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Gaskins said that what Mr. Crawford is saying is when he built his house at that time, there were no exact setback rules and he could have put his house all the way to the water, but he didn’t, because he had neighbors on either side and wanted to be a good neighbor. She said that his house was built first, her house was destroyed by hurricane Hugo and was setback exactly with Mr. Crawford’s. She said the neighbor on the corner of Chicco and McCants were the last to build and they also chose to set back. She said they are all set in a row and the proposed home is going to come out and sit 25 feet, which was previously 40 feet. She said it will stick out way in front of them and this is not what any of the neighbors have done, trying to be good neighbors. She would like to ask them to think about pushing it more towards the road and be a good neighbor. Joanne Cooke, 631 Pitt Street, said they are on two lots and have a cottage on the back lot, which is at 130 Chicco Lane. She has lived there for 52 years. She said her husband’s office was in the cottage in the back yard. She said he was in the shipping business. She said he also took care of the maintenance of the lot at 127 Chicco Lane. She said they lived through hurricane Hugo and added that her lot is the highest lot in the village, so they did not have any flooding or damage. She said the lot at 127 Chicco is always flooding and whatever debris floats into the river during the storm come onto 127 Chicco. She said she has neighbors on the front on Pitt Street and neighbors in the back on Chicco Lane and said it is all one little village. She said in regards to water runoff, there is only ten feet on either side of the proposed house on this lot and asked where the water will run off. She said the water will need to go somewhere which means all the houses in that area are going to flood. Mr. Pohlman reminded the Commission that water and storm runoff is not reviewed by the Commission, but accomplished during the building permit phase. Ms. Cooke said everyone was using Mr. Robert Broome’s lot (127 Chicco Lane) as a garbage disposal, even the Town. She said he (or his attorney), wrote letters to everyone and asked them not to do anything on this property, because “someone should question whether there was toxic waste on this lot, as it appears that there are a lot of people who are not Old Village Historic District Commission

going to be able to escape liability”. Ms. Cooke stated that the Town’s Public Services Department was using this lot, so there is a lot more to it than building a big house. She said that people are on their porches and look to the left and right and see Fort Sumter and downtown and if a house is built too far out, it spoils the view for many of the neighbors. Ms. O’Connor stated that she would like to thank the neighbors for their information regarding the flooding and this something they will take under advisement. She said they do have their pool raised up two feet. Mr. Keenan asked if there was any fill dirt coming in. Ms. O’Connor said the properties on either side are higher than this lot so it is something they need to consider. She said in terms of drainage, the lot slopes severely from Chicco Lane down towards the marsh. She said the idea of moving the pool back is potentially on the table. She said she appreciates the information regarding the flooding from the neighbors. She said that at the last meeting 40 feet was mentioned and was incorrect. She said the house was forward of the neighbor by 25 feet at the last meeting and now it is at 16 feet. She said in reference to the graphic provided by Ms. Brennan, on the first page it shows that the house is all the way out to the fence line of the neighbor. In fact, the proposed house is 20 feet back from the fence line of the neighbor, so the graphic is incorrect. She stated if the Commission looks at her sheet #2002, it will indicate where their fence line is and it is 20 feet in front. Ms. Wilson stated that what Ms. O’Connor is referring to is the riprap wall. Ms. O’Connor stated that she is not familiar with what a riprap wall is. Ms. Wilson stated that it is the seawall. She said on the drone photographs, you are able to see the seawall. Ms. O’Connor said that she is 20 feet back from that. Ms. Wilson stated that she is not. Ms. O’Connor stated that she is talking about the Gaskin’s property and the image shown from the drone photograph is indicating the fence line, which is the riprap wall and reiterated that she is 20 feet back from there. She said the porch is 11 feet deep. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Rowe asked Ms. O’Connor if she indicated that she was 25 feet back at the last meeting. Ms. O’Connor stated that she was 25 feet forward of the Gaskins’ house and now she is 16 feet forward of the Gaskins’ house. Mr. Hirshorn asked if Ms. O’Connor was measuring from the end of the house or the porch. Ms. O’Connor said from the porch. She said that her porch corner is now 16 feet in front of the Gaskins’ corner. Mr. Keenan stated that there appears to be some discrepancies. Ms. O’Connor stated that she would like to point out the drawings are to scale and have dimensions on them. She said the front of the Gaskins’ house is 75 feet from their property line which is in the marsh and is an odd way to measure it, but the only fixed point she has. She said that the Gaskins’ house is 75 feet from their rear property line which is in the marsh. She said that her house is 59 feet from their property line which lines up with theirs, so their property is now 16 feet in front. Mr. Jones said that their porch takes up the whole view. Ms. O’Connor said that she is not debating this, but advising what the numbers are. She said that on Ms. Brennan’s first photograph with their proposed house noted on it is not correct. She said it is the same as the next image. She said the next few images regarding the flooding are very helpful and she appreciates those very much. She said that she would also like to respond to the statement that Ms. Brennan made that no one goes up as close as they can get to the critical line. She said that this is not the case. She said the 101, 105 and 107 Middle Street homes are built as close as possible to the critical line, so this is not an unusual circumstance in the Old Village. She said in terms of setting back from Chicco Lane, all of the homes on Chicco Lane are setback more than 50 feet from Chicco lane. She said she wanted to clear up some of the misinformation that was provided. She said in terms of toxic waste on the property, she said this is something they definitely would like to know. She thanked the neighbors for this information. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that she understands that Ms. O’Connor feels there is some discrepancy and said that the neighbors are not the professionals and have done the best they were able to do. She said that their drawing was actually closer to scale with regards to the house than the drawing that Ms. O’Conner did with the appendix where the CAD drawing was done on the photographs. She said because this is a significant request, this item was important. Ms. O’Conner said that she was unsure which drawing Ms. Wilson was referring to. Ms. Wilson said that it does not have a label on it, but was towards the back. She said it has Ms. O’Connor CAD drawing on it, not to scale with the photographs. Ms. O’Connor said that she did scale the photographs and said that it is to scale. She said those houses are taller than their proposed house. Ms. Wilson said that she went to the site and measured the width of the Gaskins on the front, which was approximately 20 feet – the piece that comes to the forward of the street and Ms. O’Connor’s is 50 feet. She said that it could be to scale, but it does not read that way. She said that the addresses on Middle Street are not relevant. She said that it is the two blocks on Chicco Lane. She said that she stood out there and felt there was no reason for this house to go even one foot past the houses to the left. She said she would personally add that it should split the difference between the house on the right and the left. She said that the proposed house is 30 feet in front of the Brennan’s and 16 feet in front of the Gaskins and it should be behind the Gaskins and somewhere in the average between the two properties set. She said that this would be the compatible neighborhood thing to do. Ms. Pohlman asked Ms. Wilson to clarify “in front”. Ms. Wilson stated marsh side. She said that the proposed house is already pretty far in front of them on Chicco Lane already as well and while she appreciates that the change was made to drop to a one story on the back, there was a discussion at the last meeting about the massing on the front which is tremendous at 50 feet wide and over 40 feet tall and just not in Old Village Historic District Commission

keeping with what is there now. She said it is a thorough set and has a great deal of detail which she appreciates, but said she was hoping the Commission was going to have the opportunity to have another conceptual review of this, because she feels the front massing needs to be broken up and needs to come back off the critical significantly. Ms. Rowe stated that she agrees with Ms. Wilson’s comments and going in front of the neighbors’ homes is not something she will support. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he concurs and ties this to the guidelines on new construction on massing and scale and location on the lot, as well as in conjunction with the street in general, which is crucial and something the Commission reviews closely. He said the house that Ms. O’Connor designed on Middle Street has a similar issue. He said that there are a number of issues with the front façade of this proposed home, the extension of the rear façade, the materials and windows, and to echo Ms. Wilson’s comments, another conceptual review would be necessary. Ms. Dickson stated that she agrees with the comments of Commission members and added that it is too big of a house for the lot. Mr. Keenan stated that his concerns are fairly consistent, and believes it needs to come back off of the marsh. He said there is ample room on Chicco lane. He said that he is also concerned with the front elevation as far as the scaling. He said that typically, there are up to three rounds of conceptual review and believed it was premature after the comments Ms. O’Connor received last month. He said the Commission would like to work with the property owners on this project, and the neighbors would also like to work with them. He said that he would like to see both existing and proposed side by side at the next meeting in order to understand what was drawn and what is being proposed. He said that the pool is also a concern and the flooding is a great point and he would like for the pool to shift back as well. John Frick, stated that he is the owner of 127 Chicco Lane and is also curious about the flooding issues and appreciates what the neighbors have experienced through their years of living there. He said if he pulls the house back substantially, approximately 15 or 16 feet, or however far they are past the Gaskins’ now and brings in fill to work on the elevation with Old Village Historic District Commission

the flooding, they are still lower than the neighbors. He said that there was discussion about bringing in fill; however, they did not want to create an issue for the neighbors with flooding. He said with a small amount of fill and mindful planning, the runoff can be controlled, because the lot is sloped and the water is going to flow towards the harbor. He said there have been a number of comments regarding the home being too big for the neighborhood. He said that he does not believe this is true. He said that he is a family of six and needs a big home and asked Commission members if he should not purchase the lot because he cannot build the home he needs for his family. He said he would like for this to be taken into consideration. Ms. Wilson moved to deny the application for final approval at 127 Chicco Lane; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Kate Campbell & Beau Clowney, Beau Clowney Architects, representing the homeowner. Ms. Campbell said most Commission members are familiar with this property along the harbor, which is the last vacant lot. She hopes that the Commission and neighbors will provide comments and that their design addresses some of the concerns read from the last submittal. She said it is a sloped site from grade 11 feet to approximately 3 feet. She said there is a critical line that impedes in the property; however, due to the plat date, this property is not subject to a 30-foot critical line setback. They have attempted to create more of a one-story volume that addresses Chicco Lane along with the front porch, utilizing the slope on the lot similar to most of the adjacent waterfront lots that have a park-under concept, where the house is more embedded into the hill, which will help mitigate the height from Chicco Lane and the harbor. She said they have a flood zone issue to address where they are required to build the house up off the lowest adjacent grade, which is where their overall height restriction is based from, which is at the rear of the lot. She said they are matching the 7-foot grade line that runs along the property. She said there would be a small amount of fill on the back- side tapering down towards the critical line. She indicated the one and two-story portions of the home. They set the rear heated portion of the house approximately 30 feet off the critical. She said there is a one-story porch that wraps around and a one-story porch off the master bedroom and indicated where the porch is all open and not a solid heated space. She said there is a tight turnaround and they are exploring the possibility of a guest parking space, but also function as a turnaround space. She said that they will be required to do a stormwater management plan and a drainage management plan. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Dovre said that the parking is tight; therefore, for permanent residents living there, what will be an easy come-around. Ms. Campbell described how the property owners would enter and exit their garage and driveways. She said they may design a larger turnout as they are navigating and turning around in terms of property owners within their own property. She continued with the design of the house and said the property will be at Chicco Lane grade and they may have to install a retaining wall in order to get some type of slope back slightly in order to prevent any water from going underneath the house. Ms. Dovre asked if the house that is proposed will be similar to building on a hill. Ms. Campbell said it is more similar to cutting into a hill. She said there will be some type of low retaining wall and/or swales along the side as they cannot shed water onto any other properties. She said the grades she is showing are the existing grades and have not worked out the proposed grades. Ms. Rowe said that she is happy that the house is moved back off the critical line. Mr. Hirshorn asked if there is an illustration that shows the proposed new structure relative to the critical line and the neighbors and asked if the porches extend beyond the neighbors. Ms. Campbell responded in the affirmative. Mr. Hirshorn stated that this was a hot discussion during the previous submittal. Keith Jones, 121 Chicco Lane, said this is a 5,300 square foot house, but he does like it much better than the previous submittal, and it is set back. He said that both the pool and porches are way beyond his porch. He said the 127 Chicco Lane porches will extend way beyond theirs and into their view. He said the lot is open and the pool is very conspicuous and only 10 feet from their fence and 20 feet in front of Old Village Historic District Commission

their porch. His main concern is the pool specifically in that location, which is not inconspicuous and almost out into the marsh, and the proposed porches being so far forward of his porch. He said the lot floods half way up during a storm and if they put the pool where it is being proposed, it will be flooded, even with a 6-foot retaining wall. Janice Gaskins, 131 Chicco Lane, said she lives on the other side of the proposed house and her only complaint is the porch that is jetting out way past all the neighbors’ structures. She thought the idea was to try and build it all in a row so that no one interferes with anyone else’s view, which the porch will obviously do. She said it is not a deck, but an enclosed structure with a roof. She said this will block Shem Creek, Patriots Point and the Ravenel Bridge, because it will be obscured by the proposed roofed structure. Mr. Hirshorn asked about the depth of the porch. Ms. Campbell said it is 12 feet deep. Ms. Gaskins said this would be 13 feet beyond all the other houses. She asked how far the porch juts out into the flood line, not the critical line. Mr. Pohlman stated that for clarification regarding the flood line, this is from FEMA and is not exactly a straight line. He showed the flood area that would dictate the height that the building would have to meet, plus one foot, in order for the Town to comply with FEMA flood grants. He said it has nothing to do with the critical line or the marsh and is judged from aerial imagery on how high flood waters could rise during a catastrophic event, such as a hurricane. Joanne Cooke, 631 Pitt Street, said her lot goes all the way back to 130 Chicco Lane. She said one of her concerns is flooding, which the homeowners seem to be addressing. She said her second concern is the porch. She has no doubt that it will be enclosed, which will block the view of all the other properties. She said that it should not jut out as it blocks the views of the neighbors. She said other than those concerns, she believes it is beautiful. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Dovre said that she is also concerned about the porch being too far forward and blocking the neighbors’ views, who have resided there for many years. Ms. Wilson said that the proposed plans are exponentially more sensitive than the previous application. She appreciates the stepping down in scale and the first story pieces do help both in addressing Chicco Lane and the harbor. She said that Ms. Campbell has done a great job of having two fronts which is needed on this lot. She said this will also be the same comment that you must take the three houses into consideration and not go past them with a porch or anything else. Her opinion is that it is the average of the four houses. She appreciates that Ms. Campbell is using the 30-foot setback; however, it is simply neighborhood capability. She said many of the residents have lived in their home on Chicco Lane for 20, 25, and 30 years and it is inconceivable to her that the Commission would allow anything with a foundation to go beyond the average of the four houses that this property is in between. She said the Commission would be more flexible on Chicco Lane because it is a unique street and has some ability to absorb some different relationships. She said other than those points, she believes that Ms. Campbell has done a great job. Mr. Hirshorn asked if Ms. Wilson had any issue with the pool Ms. Wilson said that the pool in the proposed location is not suitable, because it will flood. She said it would have to be raised and the Commission will need to see the site section and how it will be handled. She added that with the precedence that has been set, they cannot deny a pool on a harbor lot. While she respects what Mr. Jones said earlier about it being an open lot, it is also very narrow. She said that she does not know if it can be pulled back to be more parallel to the back. She believes an inground pool can go past the build-to line of the diagonal between the neighbors and if they wish to keep the location, the Commission would like to see a compelling buffer for the neighbors; however, the Commission is not able to comment on Old Village Historic District Commission

landscaping. She suggested that when they come back before the Commission, to show how sensitive they can be. Ms. Rowe agrees with Ms. Wilson that the porches and/or decks cannot block the neighbor’s view but believes everything else looks so much better. She asked if Ms. Campbell could simply square off across the back. Ms. Campbell stated that shifting it forward works, but with the turnaround, it may compress everything on the front and this is what they were balancing everything with, trying to ensure they were creating one story pieces on the front while also navigating to the second garage without having two driveways. She said this is part of the reason they were attempting to match everything with the heated footprint and having the porches be out, because the porches are inherently more transparent than a solid wall with windows. She said they will study this further. Ms. Rowe stated that they have the space and as far as the pool is concerned, it is tricky. Ms. Wilson believes Chicco Lane can absorb a little more two-story than what is being proposed. She said this is a unique lot, but believes Ms. Campbell is on the right track. Ms. Montgomery said that the portion of the porch that juts out the farthest, she asked if it can be removed and the porch where stairs are coming out from, she asked if the stairs could be put on the exterior and the porch moved over closer to where the pool would be, so there would be a nice front porch, and instead of it going across, it would come down the side. Ms. Campbell said that is a possibility, but believes it is a balance of spaces that have direct light and those that have indirect light. Ms. Montgomery said this would help with the view. She said they have had homes cut across the site lines before and it is a difficult situation, but it will be a beautiful house. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson said that she likes how the stairs are now because what she likes so much is the formality and the way it addresses the harbor. Mr. Hirshorn said it appears that the main issues are the porch and the pool. He added that this is a difficult lot.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Ryan Smith and Beau Clowney, Beau Clowney Architects representing the homeowners. Mr. Smith stated that the BAR calculation increases approximately 159 square feet, which was due to the reconfiguring of the porches due to staff’s comments in the initial meeting. He stated that other than this, the massing as a whole remains unchanged. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Clowney stated that listening to the Commission’s comments at the previous meeting, their clients elected to rethink the porches on the harbor side and have pulled everything back so that all neighbors line up. He said that they did pull the guest bedroom on the street side closer to the street and the whole main porch on the main level changed orientation, once they began thinking about the pool and house to accommodate the concerns of the neighbor, pulling the pool over and changing the orientation of the porch. Ruth Brennan, 121 Chicco Lane, is the homeowner on the right side facing the waterfront. She has been there for 21 years and said that her biggest concern is that this house is 5,400 square feet as opposed to her and her neighbor’s house at 3,500 square feet. She feels it is too massive for that location. She stated that using the Critical line in order to get and achieve these numbers with this size of a house is not appropriate because the waterfront has marsh that comes up on that particular land mass and there is a flooding issue. She said the flooding issue extends almost 50 feet back beyond where the pool is actually proposed to go. She said there is a change in height from her house to the Gaskins’ house and it decreases. She stated that the Gaskins’ already experience a tremendous amount of flooding and there are pictures to demonstrate this. She stated that if you pull up the sketch on A.0.1 that indicates where the pool is going to be located, the pool will only be eight feet back from the corner of her house, so she will be looking at her neighbor’s pool all the time, which will devalue her house tremendously and becomes an eyesore for the community. She said it is absolutely inappropriate and they could have put the pool anywhere where she was not looking at it. She said there are a number of design elements, but the persistence is remarkable, because the neighbors were trying to impress upon the new homeowner that the flooding is the biggest issue and it would be an engineering feat to even put in an inground pool. She added that all the pools in this community are inconspicuous along the waterfront. She said that there are a number of trees that go all along the side which create a buffer for the massing of this house and is concerned as they are Old Village Historic District Commission

discussing only keeping one when there is another oak up front that should remain and a black gum tree in the middle that is on the property line, which she does not want removed. She said she has not seen any landscaping either. Janice Gaskins, 131 Chicco Lane, stated that she is interested in the slide 11-24 because it indicates that the deck is going to be equal to the other houses on the other side, but on #12, there is clearly a porch out front. She asked if what is sticking out is an eight-foot porch. She said she is concerned with the flooding as well. She asked when this large home is built, where is all the water going to go. Dr. Gaskins, 131 Chicco Lane stated that he grew up in North Charleston and has been around for a number of years. He said that he has some concern about the potential for two feet of fill, because if you look at the lots, most of them are level; however, if you bring in two feet of fill, the water will go on his lot. Mr. Hirshorn stated that drainage does not fall under the purview of the Commission; however, the overall design is. Ms. Brennan asked if there was consideration of a bulkhead that is not drawn in. Ms. Wilson stated that this would be a decision made by DHEC (Department of Health and Environmental Control). Ms. Dovre asked if the pool is being repositioned and if it is still visible to the neighbor; however, behind that area is a crucial flooding area, because the land slants. She asked if the elevation on the pool changed in height. Mr. Clowney stated that the pool will be at a certain level and as it moves out, the ground would taper off. Ms. Dovre said that there is already low ground critical flooding in that area, so was anything added. Mr. Clowney stated that they know they have to take care of the drainage and by law, cannot drain to neighboring properties. He said Old Village Historic District Commission

with Sheila Wertimer and the landscape architect, they would be doing a complete drainage plan for the entire site. He said in regard to the trees and the privacy along the edge, there are trees there already, but there is a pool and a hot tub on the adjacent property already, so they want privacy as well. Ms. Wilson said there is a discrepancy in terms of whether it is the porch or the heated house. Mr. Smith stated that everyone will be lined up. Ms. Wilson asked about taking the pool out and submit with the landscape plan. She said there are pools on the harbor and while compliant with the 40% lot coverage, what they see people come back with is a great deal of pervious paving and there is still the loss of greenspace. She said without seeing the decking and how they are going to handle the landscape, she is unable to support the pool as submitted. She stated that the neighbors have a legitimate concern and she is unsure if the homeowners will do an infinity edge where there must be at least 18 inches of fall as the pool tapers out, or where the decking or the path to the pool are located. She stated that there are still a number of unanswered questions that she is certain Ms. Wertimer will address; however, not knowing what those are, she is not comfortable approving the pool. Mr. Clowney stated that he would like to discuss this with his client; however, he would like to note that the house north is an “L” shaped house and has a great deal of open space between the bulk of their house and this proposed house. He said he knows that his clients would like to have a pool and if they were to remove the pool and submit it with a supplement application, he would like to ensure that they are not giving up the opportunity to have a pool. Ms. Wilson stated that she is not saying “no” but needs to understand it more. She said while she respects the applicant’s concerns, she would be more comfortable with the pool once she sees how it will be Old Village Historic District Commission

handled. She added that the Commission is not technically allowed to vote on the landscaping. Ms. Montgomery asked about the possibility of turning the pool 90 degrees so that it is not protruding out as far into the harbor. Mr. Clowney stated that they have looked at several different options and one of the nice things they like about the one being proposed is that they pulled the edge of the pool all the way to the house so that it creates a nice shaded area. He said they hear the concerns and are taking into consideration the drainage, landscaping and all the obstacles; however, the homeowners do want a pool and have moved the house back considerably. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it appears that the pool will be separate from the home application. He asked if there was any further discussion from Commission members regarding the scale and massing of the home relative to the rest of the homes. Mr. Hirshorn stated that 5,500 square feet versus the other 3,000 square foot neighbors’ homes. Mr. Clowney stated that the home is not 5,500 square feet and stated that it is 4,700 square feet. The 5,500 square feet includes the porches. Ms. Wilson stated that there is a precedent for a larger home on the harbor and said a great deal of progress has been made from the previous submittals. She stated that the applicants have been sensitive to both Chicco Lane and the harbor and feels much effort and compromise have been made. She stated that she does not believe it is within the Commission’s rights to mandate a smaller house. She stated that the Commission is not excited to see applicants push the limit and then come back again with pervious surfaces. She said it is maintaining the greenspace that is the base of the Old Village poché. She is hopeful this is in the landscape plan and stated that she is not voting against the pool but would like to see how it will be handled sensitively. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson moved to approve the house at 127 Chicco Lane, with the provision that sheet A 0.1 is correct and honored and that no portion of the house or porch exceeds past 121 Chicco Lane and that the pool is excluded from approval until the Commission sees a complete drainage and landscape plan; seconded by Ms. Montgomery. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with Commission (attachment 1).

Ms. Cheryl Cave, Wertimer and Cline, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Janice Gaskins, 131 Chicco Lane, asked the about the height of the bulkhead. She stated that their bulkhead is two feet in height and suggested that this was sufficient.

Mr. Keith Jones, 121 Chicco Lane, distributed a copy of previous houses surrounding this property. He expressed concern with the height of the proposed bulkhead. He also expressed concern that pool would create noise pollution as well as cause additional flooding in the area.

Ms. Wilson explained that the height of the bulkhead is seven feet from sea level. She stated that the bulkhead is proposed to be the same height as the grass would be once the two feet of fill is put in.

Ms. Ruth Brennan 121 Chicco Lane, expressed concern with the pool and that is not in inconspicuous location. She suggested that the neighbors have not been contacted regarding this request. She also expressed concern with the proposed wall and suggested that there should be more greenspace. She expressed concern that the live oak on the property would be compromised with the addition of the pool. She asked that the Commission deny the request for the pool. Old Village Historic District Commission

Dr. John Gaskins, 131 Chicco Lane, suggested that the bulkhead should be two feet and should be in line with his lot to avoid any flooding issues.

There being no further comments, Mr. Hirshorn closed public comment.

Ms. Dovre expressed concern with the addition of the pool because of area flooding.

Ms. Rowe stated that she has no issue with pool.

Ms. Wilson suggested that there are other pools on neighboring properties.

Mr. Jeff McCall, 127 Chicco Lane, suggested that it is disingenuous to deny the pool given that there are pools on neighboring properties. He stated that some properties have a pool and hot tub.

Mr. Hirshorn stated that the nature of the historic district is that you could be overlooking your neighbor’s pool.

Ms. Wilson pointed out that the Commission asked for restudy of the pool but gave previous approval for the house. She stated that the pool has been moved and are proposing extensive landscaping to screen the pool. She asked about the tabby drive. Ms. Cave answered that it is for additional space to maneuver and for additional parking. Ms. Wilson suggested that there should be more greenspace.

Ms. Montgomery asked if the tabby driveway can be broken up with more greenspace. Ms. Cave stated that this could be reviewed and consider some design features.

Ms. Wilson asked if a second curb cut could be added. Mr. Rutherford answered that there may be limitations on more than one entry way, but it is something the applicant can discuss with the Transportation Department. Mr. McCall stated they would be willing to have that discussion.

Ms. Wilson moved for approval with final review by a committee of the Commission with members of Ms. Wilson and Ms. Rowe for the second curb cut in lieu of the tabby drive in the front. Ms. Rowe seconded the motion. Motion Old Village Historic District Commission

passed on a 3 to 1 vote with Ms. Wilson, Ms. Rowe, and Ms. Montgomery in favor; Ms. Dovre opposed and Mr. Hirshorn abstaining.

XIII. Staff Approvals

No staff approvals this month.

There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 7:06 pm.
