events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Carl McCants, architect for the homeowners, stated that his clients were living in North Carolina during the construction of this project. He was not hired on for construction administration and many of the changes were made by the contractor without approval. He added that the contractor is no longer involved with this project, and he would like to go through all the items that were revised on the house. He said that in reference to the steps, they received the CO and final, and then the Commission came back to request revisions and he is not sure how this can be accomplished. He said the front door went from a double to a single door, and the size of the window adjacent to that, reduced in size due to a revision on the interior for a bathroom. The larger window would not work. He said the front steps are the most significant revision. He said it now is all stucco and per building code, there must be a handrail. He said they tried to nestle it into the berm behind it and due to the large oak tree, they were not able to bring in enough soil to produce what was approved through the Commission. He said the Town’s arborist stated that it would damage the tree. He said they had to install a handrail which made the stairs look larger. He said another revision was the chimney cap, which changed, and there were brackets around the house and all of the brackets were never installed by the contractor. He said that the windows on the left front façade were mulled together and now they are not. There is a wood separation between them. He said that the stucco revision, all the brick was taken off and there were areas that were breaking up the massing Old Village Historic District Commission

showing bricks in portions of it and stucco in other areas. He said that it is now monochromatic on the whole lower elevation of stucco. He said if you look through the other elevations, he has highlighted the revisions. Ms. Dickson asked again why this is ex post-facto. Mr. McCants stated that he was not involved in the construction administration, and the homeowners assumed that the contractor was doing what was required of him. Ms. Wilson stated that Mr. McCants was not involved in the construction process and is now coming in to rectify the situation. Mr. McCants said that the house is built and the Town of Mount Pleasant issued the CO (Certificate of Occupancy), so the family is now residing in the home. Ms. Wilson asked if the homeowners have the interest or desire to add the brackets that were originally designed. Mr. McCants said that they do; however, now they are in a financial issue with the contractor. He said that it may be a struggle for them at this time. Ms. Wilson asked if it would be fair to say that they are working on trying to get their costs refunded or obtain the brackets. Mr. McCants stated that they are trying to resolve it. He said that the homeowners are present if the Commission has specific questions for them. Ms. Wilson said that she is more in favor of what Mr. McCants designed than what was actually built. She said the overhangs are big, so the brackets would be favorable. She said that the Commission could allow time and leeway to allow the homeowner to work through this with the builder. She said that regarding the other three sides, she does not have an issue with any of those changes. She is struggling with the cable rail, because it has a very commercial look. Mr. McCants said the cable rail was approved on the porch, but was not approved for the handrail. He said they were going to nestle the stairs behind the parapet brick wall. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that it is very different when it is in the shadow of the porch and then there is the stepped brick knee walls that are handling the landscape and give it a much more refined look, as opposed to all the cable on diagonal and stepping and changing elevation. She said she would like to see the corbels come back, but is not in favor of the cable rail; she has an issue with it. Ms. Rowe said that she feels the same way about the cable rails, but is not sure what else can be done, because there must be a rail. Mr. Keenan asked if there was a brick wall on the approved front elevation. Mr. McCants stated that there is a brick wall behind at the porch level and there was a parapet wall that was set in front of it towards the streetside and the stairs were hidden inside where they were not seen. Ms. Wilson stated that with railing, you would not have any of the diagonal runs of railing, but three straight runs stepping down. Mr. McCants said that the large oak is almost right in front of the area being discussed so it is somewhat screened. He said if he fills in the hand rails with pickets or something else, it will look more massive, but the cable rail is somewhat transparent and not noticeable. Ms. Wilson asked about putting the knee walls back so there are three straight runs of cable rails, part of the original design. Mr. McCants stated that the issue with this is they are not able to bring the fill in that they needed to berm it up to code. Ms. Wilson said to do rail, but keep the stepped foundation wall so that there are three simple horizontal sections of cable rail, so you get back to the parapet walls on streetside. Mr. McCants asked if Ms. Wilson is asking to add more of the stucco up higher. Ms. Wilson responded in the affirmative. Mr. McCants said that it would be counter to what they are looking to accomplish, because it would look more monolithic and make it appear like a large concrete wall. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that his issue is, if this had been presented as it has already been built, he would have personally not accepted it. He said what to do with it now is a difficult question. He said that this design, as built, is an issue with him. Mr. McCants asked about using shiplap to make a shiplap parapet wall. Ms. Rowe stated that it is transparent the way it is so she is unable to envision seeing another texture. Mr. Keenan said that all the other changes are inconsequential; however, he agrees with Mr. Hirshorn. He said he would like to see the corbels come back. He feels that the homeowner has a significant amount of funding tied up in the railing which puts the Commission in a very tough position. He said that adding another element of siding will not remedy the situation. He said this situation puts the Commission in a very difficult situation, because they do not want to tell the homeowners that they must demolish what has been done and start over, because they have a significant financial investment. Ms. Wilson asked if the homeowners would be willing to do something else such as stepped planters or something that brings it back to where the design was headed originally. Mr. McCants said that their first approach was to wrap the lower portion of the stairs in shiplap and leave the handrails where they were, which would soften it. They were also discussing planting fig to grow over the whole section and let the handrails rest above the fig. He said there are already plants in place that will mature and cover up the majority of that area. He said that he does not have an issue studying other solutions, but would like more of a definition about what the Commission would like to see. He said that they are at the mercy of the Commission. Mr. Keenan suggested tall vegetation. Mr. McCants stated that Ms. Wilson’s suggestion of staggered planters are doable, which would also change the grade without getting into the root system of the oak tree. Ms. Wilson stated that she is in favor of what was approved initially and would like for Mr. McCants to come back with ideas. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. McCants asked if this could be handled at staff level. Mr. Keenan stated that he would like for it to come back. Ms. Wilson moved to approve all items, with the exception of the cable rail, which will be deferred only for a study of the front façade of the house; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Carl McCants, architect for the homeowners, stated that they went back and attempted to soften the contemporary feel of the front stairs on the house. He said one option is using 1x4 epay hand rails running horizontal and following the rake of the stairs. The other option would be to enclose the whole staircase with 1x6 treated shiplap and have it stained to match the garage door. He said they brought in landscape architect, Jody Furman to help with landscape screening of this area. He said that the combination of what he and Mr. Furman are creating will help satisfy the Commission with reducing the contemporary elements. He said that his client would prefer the first option. Ms. Wilson asked why the same size is not being used all the way across. She said it is too stepped. Jody Furman, Furman Land Design, stated that he installed five 15 gallon podocarpus, which are 4 to 5 feet tall and three 7 gallon podocarpus. He did not want everything to be uniform and wanted it to follow the contours of the stairs. Ms. Wilson stated that going back to Mr. McCants’ original design, all the stepping was eliminated with the garden or retaining walls, which were more flat. She said that if all the podocarpus were the same height, it breaks up all the stepping. Mr. McCants stated what Mr. Furman has done with it is allow the stairs and handrails be transparent and not cover it up coming all the way down. He thinks that it is an easy change if the Commission prefers the podocarpus to be the same height. Ms. Wilson stated that she does not prefer either option and would prefer that it remain as it is now. She said the corbels and brackets were removed and thought that it was agreed that the homeowners would attempt to get Old Village Historic District Commission

them back from the builder. She said that a timeline was not set, but would like the record to reflect that at some point the big overhangs will have the brackets. Mr. McCants stated that the information he received from Mr. Pohlman was that he only needed to address the staircase and leave the plan as it was and the staircase was the only item that needed to come back before the Commission. He said he may have misunderstood, so he did not address this. Ms. Rowe stated that the motion from last month reflected what Ms. Wilson just stated. Ms. Wilson stated that the stairs are what they are and at least with the cable, it is less of an element. She said for the record going forward, this Commission is not setting a precedent for cable railings on the front of homes, because it is not appropriate. Ms. Rowe asked if there is already landscaping installed. Mr. Furman stated that there are four exfolias there now and will keep one and relocate the other three. He said they will put the Japanese yew in place of the exfolias. He stated that they were worried about the exfolias taking too long to cover up the wall. He stated that he was attempting to cover up the white wall with a bigger size pot. Mr. Keenan stated that he does not know how the epay is going to look. He said that he agrees with Ms. Wilson and would rather keep it as it is now with the cable railing. Ms. Rowe agreed with keeping the railing that is there now. Ms. Wilson stated that she would like the brackets put back. Mr. McCants responded in the affirmative. Ms. Dickson said she prefers the second option, because if it were all covered with plants it would be less busy. Mr. McCants stated that keeping it with the cable railing would be less busy, because the cable railing is transparent and you do not notice it as much. Ms. Dickson said she disagrees and the eye just sees all these lines and feels it is disturbing. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson made a motion to deny changing the railing at 129 Live Oak and remain as they are now, and deny the elevations without the brackets. She said basically the Commission is denying everything brought this evening. She said the brackets come back and the railings stay. Mr. McCants stated that in the original plan, they had the bracket, but also had brackets on the columns, as well, that were almost like fins. He asked if Ms. Wilson was referring to all the brackets or only those on the overhangs. Ms. Wilson said that the house has larger overhangs and they should have a bracket. She said where the overhangs are two feet or greater, it should have a bracket. Seconded by Ms. Rowe. Mr. Hirshorn, Ms. Rowe, Mr. Keenan and Ms. Wilson were in favor. Ms. Dickson was opposed. Motion carries 4-1.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Carl McCants, architect representing homeowners, stated that his clients recently purchased this property and are a young growing family. He said the house is small and they felt the need to put the ADU up to achieve one more bedroom for the house. He said they studied the house trying to determine how to add another bedroom and it was difficult. He said the ADU is not going to be a rental property, but for guests and family members that visit. He said it will also be in conjunction with the pool that they would like to have put in. He said it would be for this young family trying to create outdoor space for the children and typical lowcountry living. He said there is some concern with the house directly behind his clients’ feeling as if they are towering over and looking down on his clients and is one reason that the ADU is anchored on that side. He said what they are proposing is to heavily plan the space between the pool, ADU and the neighbor directly behind them to create more of a buffer for privacy. He said looking at the site plan, there is a 47” oak and a 36” oak which present a problem with the initial design of the house, as well as the location of the ADU and proposed pool. He said they are requesting the 3½ foot setback on the rear to get more distance away from the main house. He said with the 3½ foot setback, it is only keeping them ten feet off the main structure. He said they are also trying to address grade issues and are studying the water runoff. He said there is a grate inlet on the far back left corner and they are attempting to capture all their water off of the proposed ADU, so it does not go into Mr. Martschink’s property or the adjacent property on the left and can be contained in that area. Mr. Hirshorn stated that two letters were heard earlier regarding this property. Jack Dickerson, 131 Live Oak Drive, stated that they reside in the house on the left side. He spoke to the owners of this property who are very nice and Old Village Historic District Commission

appear to be willing to work with the neighbors. He said their concern is the actual size of the proposed project. He said what is being proposed is right on top of everything and should be within tolerance. He said they do not agree with the setback which is there for a reason. He said they are right at their 40% impervious and were not able to put in anything else, so keeping everything to within the Old Village standards is what they are looking to achieve. Losse Knight, with LFK Architects,1360 Old Brickyard Road, said he is here on Mr. Miles Martschink’s behalf and believes that the letter Mr. Martschink wrote is fairly detailed and what the ordinance does and does not allow. He said he is here to elaborate if there are any questions relative to Mr. Martschink’s letter. He said that the diagram provided in the letter speaks to how the accessory dwelling unit is somewhat encroaching on the south portion of the property line. He said outside of the Old Village guidelines there are other things to be considered. He said when looking at the International Residential Code (IRC), there is fire safety that should be considered. Also, when looking at the IRC 302.1, there are some requirements where you are not able to have projections or roof overhangs within two feet of the property line; the code does not allow it. Ms. Wilson asked about the rule where the taller ADU’s pitch matches the primary home. Mr. Rutherford stated that there is a 20-foot rule. He said the pitch is in the main ordinance when it is a non ADU. Ms. Montgomery stated that after reading Mr. Martschink’s letter, she agrees with everything stated. She could not in good conscious approve the project the way it is shown. Ms. Wilson stated that it would be difficult for this Commission to approve any sort of setback encroachment without having worked through it with the neighbors, as it is impacting them the most. She said that it is also too wide in its design relative to the pitch and scale of all the pieces of the original design of the house. She said if you take the three feet off and comply with the side yard setback, they would be able to achieve pitch and massing of the gables that were designed originally, which would do better justice to the design. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that the Commission members are all likely in agreement that the setback encroachment, particularly in the context of this lot, which historically has been a very difficult parcel of land. He said they would have a very difficult time approving an encroachment on a setback, as well as a large ADU and pool. He said if this is something the homeowners would like to follow through on, there would be no setback encroachment and as minimal of a structure as possible, because that area is very tight. He said this area of the Old Village is particularly challenging with all the new buildings that have gone up in the Toomer Lane and Live Oak area. He feels that each individual homeowner is interested in maximizing the properties, but this area is at the limit for structures. He said he would use this as very strong guidance when coming up with a plan. Mr. McCants stated that what he finds puzzling is that there are a set of guidelines that they are able to come to the Commission for on lots such as this. He understands if this lot was not subdivided, which is something the Town should review in the future with subdividing lots in the Old Village which is special. He said once you let someone develop a piece of property like this and allow the set guidelines, then people such as his clients are looking at the guidelines, and talking to Town staff, who advises them what they can and cannot do with the approval of the Old Village Historic District Commission. Ms. Wilson said, “yes and no”, because the homeowners are asking for relief on the setback, which is above and beyond. She said there is no subdivision taking place any longer and this was done many years ago. She said Commission members may not like it, but it was done so long ago, that it is what it is. She said the Commission is not attempting to limit the homeowners from doing some type of outdoor space; however, it is a reduced side yard setback, an ADU, and a pool, which is a big request for someone who just purchased a house. Mr. McCants asked if the Commission has the purview to provide relief on the side setbacks. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that the Commission does have the purview when there is a condition where there is a hardship and a need for it; however, does not believe that a 21-foot-wide pool cabana meets that criteria, nor does the pool. Jack Dickerson asked if the side setback must apply to the pool as well. Ms. Wilson responded in the affirmative; however, she is only one vote and is not sure what her fellow Commission members think. Mr. McCants stated that the large trees have made it very difficult and back to what Mr. Dickerson stated, they are still under all their pervious coverage. He said the trees have forced their hand to try and combine everything into this one side corner of the lot. He said if the trees were not there, then the whole presentation would be completely different. He said the original house design would probably be different as well. Ms. Wilson stated that if Mr. McCants were designing this from the start for this client, it would be entirely different; however, the clients purchased an existing house and Mr. McCants has a challenging job, which will be difficult.
This item was withdrawn by the applicant.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachment 1).

Mr. Carl McCants reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. Zuckerman, 129 Live Oak, stated his family loves his home and just need more space for an office and guests.

Mr. Miles Martschink, 135 Toomer lane, stated he has no issue with the concept, but suggested it is too massive. He stated that he did some calculations on the recently approved ADUs and distributed this to the Commission to review. He suggested that the total size is approximately 900 Old Village Historic District Commission

square feet. He suggested that this is too massive when being added to an existing 2,600 square foot home.

Mr. Hirshorn questioned the square footage calculation. Ms. Wilson stated that the applicant indicated that the structure was 639 square feet. Mr. McCants stated that the 639 square feet is the heated square footage, with a footprint of 678 square feet.

Mr. Martschink suggested that lowering the roof portion over the open area and reducing the dormers would bring the massing down. He expressed concern with the proximity of the ADU to the main structure. He also expressed concern that there is not enough parking for this request.

There being no further comments, Mr. Hirshorn closed public comments.

Mr. Rutherford stated the application meets parking requirements.

Ms. Dovre suggested that the structure is “too tight”.

Ms. Rowe suggested that the ADU is “too big”.

Ms. Montgomery asked how the rear yard would be accessed for construction of the pool.

Ms. Wilson stated that there are other homes in the area that are much larger and commended the applicant for using the same style as the existing home. She suggested that the size is not an issue. She stated that she is in favor of the request.

Ms. Montgomery expressed concern with the massing of the chimney. Mr. McCants stated that the chimney could be reduced.

Mr. Hirshorn stated that there is some concern with the massing of the ADU. He stated that he is conflicted with the request as it does meet the guidelines and is consistent with the surrounding streetscape; however, he suggested that the applicant restudy the massing to determine if some adjustments can be made. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that an ADU was recently approved that was larger and was the same proximity to the main structure and side setback. She stated that the main structure was larger than with this application.

Mr. McCants agreed and stated that there are structures on the same street that were recently approved.

Mr. Hirshorn suggested that the concern is with these homes are unique. He stated that this has been a concern with this area of the historic district. He asked the applicant to review the request and consider where some adjustments could be made.

Ms. Rowe suggested that it looks “top heavy”. Mr. McCants disagreed and showed the home on Live Oak that is similarly “top heavy”. He stated that historically, there were multiple structures on a lot, that were cobbled together over time. He suggested that this is better than having a larger, mansion type home. He suggested that the rooflines would help in reducing the massing of the structure.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachment 1).

Mr. Dotan Zuckerman reviewed the project to the Commission.

There being no comments, Ms. Rowe closed pubic comments.

Mr. Rowe moved for approval as presented. Ms. Montgomery second the motion. All in favor.

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phill Rosenbaum, representing the homeowners, stated that if you look at the elevation drawing, the homeowners would like to install a kitchen window directly below the two windows on the 2nd floor. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson said that it is a kitchen window, which is why it is shorter than the rest. She asked if the homeowners would be open to a casement so that it does not look like a smaller version of the other windows on the same elevation. Mr. Rosenbaum said that they went through a great deal of effort to duplicate what was there. Ms. Wilson said that the window does not duplicate. Mr. Rosenbaum said that in style and design it does. Ms. Wilson said it would be more appropriate not to try and duplicate it, because the others truly are historic. She said that a nine light could still be accomplished, but it would be in a casement or single sash, as opposed to having the two sashes that are shorter versions. She added that she appreciates that they are using all wood windows and matching all the detail. Mr. Rosenbaum asked if the Commission would be amenable to either a single sash or a casement. Ms. Wilson said it would be easier to use across the kitchen counter. Mr. Rosenbaum said it is going to be difficult to reach to open it no matter how it is installed. He said they even considered doing a single fixed window. Ms. Wilson said she would prefer a nine light fixed window, then all the lights line up and are the same size. Ms. Wilson moved to approve the new window at 321 King Street as a single sash nine light window; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

label: 310 King Street
request: 310 King Street – – Final Review for Alterations to Hardscape

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Katie Dunan, Duncan Design Studio, representing homeowners, stated that the house was constructed in 2013 and one of the primary goals of the residents is that it is an age-in-place, which means that if there is ever Old Village Historic District Commission

a time that the home requires handicap accessibility, it would be. She said in the original design, the drive goes uphill to meet the elevation at the side door and because it was designed with the crushed stone, it has caused rutting and is falling down the slope. She said the crushed stone is not working well. She added that the residence already has the concrete pavers on the right and other places on the property and they would like to continue this down the driveway so that it all matches. She stated that the pavers are pervious; however, she has counted it towards the lot coverage just as a precaution. She said that the pavers are actually pervious. She said the concrete pavers for the entry walk are poured in place concrete pavers with green joints and are already existing. She said to tie the driveway and entry walk together, she is proposing a poured in place concrete band that cuts the driveway so as you come up the drive, there is a place to open the car door to access the front door. She said that they would like to leave the crushed stone on the circular portion of the drive. She said that it already has existing concrete paver boarders and although more crushed stone needs to be added, it does not rut, because that piece is more level versus the side driveway, which is steep. She said on the second portion, they are requesting a design for the back courtyard. She said that existing now there is a freestanding garage, the residence and a small screened in porch area, with a large oak tree. She said there is a wonderful courtyard space in the back and she would like to put a deck on the whole piece so that it is all at one level so it is handicap accessible for the entire yard in order to come out of all of the doors and be on one level and enjoy the backyard without having to step down. She said that there is already an existing back deck and a breezeway deck existing between the screened in porch and they would like to run the boards the same way with the same material and details. She said they would like to expand the deck in order to have an indoor and outdoor living space. She added that there is an HVAC unit that is an eyesore for the space, so she is proposing to have a dry stack stone backdrop to a barbeque that would be in that area in order to cover and hide the HVAC unit. Mr. Keenan asked about the sliding barn doors. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Duncan stated that currently there is one single at the screened in porch door that opens to the space and she would like to propose barn doors in order to open up the screened in porch and enjoy the space as one outdoor space. Ms. Wilson asked about the six foot stack wall. Ms. Duncan said that there are courtyards formed with existing oak trees and when you are sitting on the screened porch, you see the beautiful oak tree and nothing else. She would like to create the same theme of the stack stone wall that is behind the barbeque have a backdrop. She said this is within the setbacks and it is not fencing it off and there is still open circulation. Mr. Hirshorn asked about the barbeque space. Ms. Duncan said that the barbeque is not visible at all from anywhere, as it is in the very back of the property. Mr. Keenan asked about the type of wood for the decking. Mr. Duncan said that it is pressure treated pine, which will match the existing. Mr. Keenan said that his concern was the front. He said there is so much topography with this lot. He said that his concern was the water runoff; however a neighbor said that he was not concerned. Ms. Duncan said her clients are very interested in having as much pervious material as possible for everything that is being proposed. She said they are attempting to use all environmentally sensitive products and are not contributing to runoff. Ms. Wilson said that her one concern is the stack wall that would be seen from the street. She said that with a stack wall, a footer will be required and the oak tree already has footers on all four sides. She said it is a tall stone wall and she worries about the tree. She added that she loves all the other designs that Ms. Duncan has done, as well as the driveway. Ms. Duncan asked about reducing the height of the wall. Ms. Wilson said that her concern is the footer limiting the growth of the tree and the trees are one of the best features of the house. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan asked about the purpose of the stack stone wall. Ms. Duncan said the idea is when you are on the screened in porch sitting, the space is beautiful, but it does not have a backdrop for the tree. Ms. Dickson asked if this could be accomplished with plants instead of a stone wall. Ms. Duncan said that this could certainly be considered. Ms. Wilson said that the stone wall is the only thing she has a concern with, and everything else is wonderful. Mr. Keenan said that he agrees, because stone is not typically found in the Old Village. He said it appears the applicant may be agreeable to some tall planting which he would be in favor of. He said everything else in the design looks great. Commission members all agreed. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve the plans for 310 King Street with the exception of the six foot forward garden stone wall; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

label: 701 Royall Avenue
request: 701 Royall Avenue – – Final Review for Alterations to Hardscape and Fencing

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Charles Claus, said that the goal is to create a fenced in border for the home. He said they have a new seventeen week old puppy that they would like to have a yard area so the puppy does not get out. He said there is podocarpus that borders, and the fence will not be visible from the street and will be behind the podocarpus, and the fence will go all the way to the garage area with a small gate. He said the only element that will be visible from the street is the new gate. Ms. Rowe said that she likes the hedge and gate. Ms. Dickson appreciates that the fence is going behind the podocarpus. Mr. Keenan stated that his only question was the living fence which is typically not what is seen in the front of the house. He said since there is going to be a hedge, he is not opposed; however, believes it is in the Old Village Historic District Commission

guidelines, so the Commission would be making a motion for this. He asked if the homeowner is proposing to install a living fence. Katie Duncan, Duncan Design Studio, stated that the property is on a corner lot and the front façade is on Royall Avenue. She said that this is the side street and it is really the backyard where the fence will be installed. Mr. Clause stated that they enter in and out on McCormick Street by design. He said although the address is technically on Royall Avenue, it is an inaccessible entrance. Ms. Wilson said that it is helpful that there are mature podocarpus foliage on site. Ms. Duncan said that they will reuse any existing hedge are able to obtain podocarpus that size to match. Ms. Rowe made a motion to accept the application at 701 Royall Avenue, final review for alterations to hardscape and landscaping; seconded by Ms. Wilson. All present voted in favor.

label: 108 Carr Street
request: 108 Carr Street – (Survey 6269) – Final Review for New Accessory Structure, Pool, Addition, and Fencing

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Michael Taliercio, Charleston Drafting Company representing the homeowners, Stephen and Charlette Zacharkiw. He said that he would like to review some of the changes from the last meeting. He said one of the main changes was the rear fence/pool enclosure. He said originally there was a privacy fence; however, the neighbors to rear facing Royall Avenue, decided that they would prefer the fence to match theirs. He said that it slopes, so the fence was terraced down. He said that it is five feet on the right side; however, because of the grade, it puts it just over four feet to meet the pool enclosure standards. He said they would like to keep the same design of the fence and use it on the side property lines as well. He said the width of the pool cabana was reduced by another three feet to bring it away from the oak tree and reduced the scale and coverage of impervious surfaces. He said they changed the guardrail on the front porch to match the guardrail on the rear porch of the home. He said currently, they are not showing any shutters for more privacy on the pool cabana until it is built and potentially put up curtains or hang shutters. He said at this time, they are not proposing to show anything there. He said water runoff was another concern of the rear neighbors, so they will have Old Village Historic District Commission

gutters on the pool cabana, which will run towards the front of the property instead of the rear. He said in reference to the proposed shed, one of the comments at the last meeting was the materials, which were previously lap siding and it is currently showing as brick. He said Ms. Wilson’s comment was to try and study to see if the height of the shed could be raised in order to relate more to the house. He said they did study this and showed it to his clients. He said they did not feel it was appropriate because with the doors on the front and back of the shed, it would relate to the ground level and not to the first floor level which is the raised crawl space. He said while a window could be installed on the side so it appears to relate to the inside, with the doors on it, it was still awkward. He said they would like to keep it at the height it is now, but change the cladding to brick instead of lap siding. Mr. Keenan said that it is basically a brick enclosure. He asked if the pool was always raised. Mr. Taliercio said that on one side, it is a few inches above grade, and said that because the site slopes considerably, it is less than thirty inches on the other end. Ms. Wilson asked if the Town’s arborist has provided his comments. Mr. Taliercio stated that prior to his involvement last year, Mr. Zacharkiw met with Mr. Bernard and he required Mr. Zacharkiw to hire a certified arborist to see if the roots would be an issue and the certified arborist found that they would not be. He said that the plans on how the main conduits from the house to the pool cabana for electricity still need to be reviewed by Mr. Bernard to ensure it does not interfere with the root system. Ms. Dickson asked if the pool would cause issues with the root system. Mr. Taliercio said that was the main concern and the arborist said that it would not. He said the main trunk line roots do not go under that footprint. Bobby Byrd, said he and his wife live at 304 Bank Street on the corner of Bank and Carr Streets. He said that his backyard is the property that is next to the Zacharkiw’s. He said when Mrs. Zacharkiw came in this evening, he Old Village Historic District Commission

advised her that he was not here to speak against the application and does not have an issue with the Zacharkiw’s building a pool or the aesthetics. He said that he did have a concern about the large oak tree in the back; however, he is confident it will be remedied by the experts. He said the minutes from the last meeting eluded to the fact that he consented to what was going on and he does not. He said that his biggest concern is the water drainage. He said they have lived in their home for 22 years and have never had any water drainage from their property, even after the house was built. He said they have not had any standing water in the yard. He said that this is his only real concern. He said the neighbor on the other side on the corner of Bank Street and Royall Avenue spoke at the last meeting, he has hired an engineer and advised him that he should be concerned about the water runoff. He said that he heard earlier that it is beyond the purview of this Commission. He said that he does not know how this can be. He said that of the three properties, his is the only one that is historic, having been built in the 1900’s. He said his concern would be the standing water draining into his property. Mr. Keenan stated that the Commission does not have any purview over the drainage plan. He said that it is up to the engineers. Ms. Wilson stated that she is still having an issue with the shed. She said because of the historic cemetery on the left side, she has concerns. She said if this means a floor needs to go in and have steps to lift the stair, then this is something that could be done. She said she appreciates the brick, because it is an added expense; however, it still looks like a shed tacked on to a house. She said that her recollection from the previous meeting was the back side of the pool cabana was going to be shuttered. She said that this cabana is backing up to a major thoroughfare entering into the Old Village and other people do not need to view this. She said that this is an unusual situation, because what is being entertained is a backyard accessory structure, in what is someone else’s front yard. She said the cabana should not be open air and seen from Whilden, Royall or any other road. She recalled the discussions of louvered shutters in order to obscure it on the backside. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Rowe stated that she has had concerns about the shed from the first application, because of the scale and it appears to be stuck on the side of the home. Mr. Hirshorn stated that could support a utility shed structure and would defer to the professional, Ms. Wilson, from an architectural standpoint. He stated that being situated next to the historic cemetery, all of the proposed changes are being taken into context. He said it is very difficult for him to see an appropriate way to build a pool cabana so close to the cemetery. He said that this again falls into the guidelines on new construction. He said he is willing to hear other comments on this. He said from a historical preservation standpoint, it is difficult to consider. Ms. Dickson said that she agrees with Commission members’ comments; however, her main concern are the trees and prior to her consideration, she would like to have something concrete from the arborist. She asked if one of the trees was being removed. Mr. Taliercio stated that none of the grand trees were being removed; however, there is a 16 inch oak that they requested to be removed. Mr. Pohlman stated that Mr. Bernard is aware of all that has been stated and will review thoroughly prior to permitting. He stated that the Zacharkiw’s have received an email from Mr. Bernard, the Town’s arborist. Mrs. Zacharkiw stated that she appreciates all the feedback as this is their 5th time coming back before the Commission. She said that they did meet with Mr. Eddie Bernard, from the Town and also had an arborist come and dig trenches to examine the roots. She said they care very deeply for their oak trees, so much so that they would not have proposed the pool if it meant harming the trees. She said Mr. Bernard was appalled that their home was built to the tree. She said it was not their design, but they purchased the house already constructed. She said that when the arborist dug the trench, he found that the tree roots are growing into the cemetery and not their property. She said there is a letter of approval. Mr. Pohlman stated that when the plans are submitted for building permits, Mr. Bernard will re-review to ensure all the data is still appropriate. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Taliercio said that at the last meeting, he was under the impression that the pool cabana and the pool were acceptable if they brought it down in scale. He said he feels like things are regressing. He said other details are not as important until there is clarity on the pool and pool cabana. He said the size of the cabana is fairly small. Mr. Keenan stated that he is fine with the utility shed and understands the need for storage. He is having some concerns with the pool and the pool cabana, based on the location of the backyard and the visible viewpoint from everything around it. He said that louvered shutters would be helpful on the pool house from the Royall Avenue viewpoint. Mr. Hirshorn said that it is the pool house and its location that has been the issue, adjacent to the cemetery. Ms. Rowe said that a pergola that is seen from the road is not allowed to be built. Mr. Pohlman responded in the affirmative. Ms. Rowe asked what the difference is between the pergola and the pool cabana being seen from the road. Mr. Taliercio stated that it is being defined as an accessory building and not a pergola. Mr. Pohlman said that the proposed cabana would have a solid roof structure. He stated that pergolas, arbors and trellises are typically open air structures. Mr. Keenan stated that the fence and chimney help hide this. Ms. Wilson stated that Mr. Hirshorn’s concern is this being visible from the cemetery. Mrs. Zacharkiw asked if the Commission would consider voting on the fencing this evening, so they are able to move forward one aspect of the project. She said that they would love to make their home and yard beautiful for the neighborhood, and added that they have received positive feedback on their front yard. She said that they are willing to do whatever the Commission is requesting and if the Commission does not want the pool house/cabana, then they will not build it. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson said that she does not totally disagree with the cemetery view; however, she is in favor of an accessory structure, because it anchors their property. She said with the appropriate façade facing Whilden, the accessory structure would be acceptable. She said she would be amenable to the louvers being operable on Whilden and on the cemetery side, they should be fixed. She said if some type of louvered system, or fence or landscaping of the whole panel on the gable end of the accessory structure and pool became something that was screened, she would be in favor. She asked the homeowner if they considered rotating the pool, because then the back of the cabana would be facing the cemetery. She said that she has more concern with the cemetery than the view on Royall Avenue. Mr. Taliercio stated that it would be pushing it closer to the grand oak and would be an issue. Mr. Keenan stated that he believes the Commission is at a point where they are able to make a motion on the fence. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to approve the fence at 108 Carr Street, as submitted and defer the pool, pool house and shed until the December meeting. Ms. Wilson said she would second the motion if the Commission is actually telling them that with the revisions they are going to be able to move forward on their project. Mr. Pohlman stated that before there can be discussion, a second must be made. Mr. Hirshorn withdrew his motion. Ms. Wilson stated that regarding the pool house, the pool house should not be viewed from the cemetery. Mr. Hirshorn stated that in order to approve the pool house, there would have to be significant elements of privacy, particularly on the historical elements where the cemetery sits. He said with reference to the shed, he is open to an appropriate design and is very close to approving that element. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson said that it should be lifted and tied into the elevation of the house with a window or a fixed shutter, as it has shed proportions instead of house proportions, but seen as an extension of the house. She stated that the roof should lift up and be in line with the porch roofs on both sides. She said she does not have an issue with the back being solid, because it is currently blank; however, if they would like to install a window or fixed shutter, it may provide some detail, but it would be up to the homeowner. She said that the shed needs to look like it belongs with the floor plates of the house. Mr. Taliercio stated that the door on the front would have to be eliminated on the front side of the shed and only put in a door on the rear side with steps going up. He said, otherwise, he is not sure about having a high window and a low door on the same bump out. Ms. Wilson said that there will be stand up paddle boards and other equipment. Mr. Taliercio said that there will also by bicycles and toys. Ms. Wilson said that they could float a floor in there with pressure treated wood, with a few steps to go into the door and everything is raised. Mr. Taliercio stated that if it is going to relate to the house by raising the roofline, he feels that the doors going into the shed from the outside also need to be at that level. He said that they would likely eliminate the one on the front side of the house. Ms. Wilson stated that she was suggesting a few steps on the front to step up. Mr. Taliercio asked if this would be for the back side as well. Ms. Wilson said if they want both doors; she does not have an issue with the doors. Ms. Rowe suggested just a window on the front. Ms. Wilson stated that it is the left side elevation because of the cemetery that is more of a concern to her than the doors. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that if the storage is important, she would approve the storage, assuming that Mr. Taliercio will line the top plate up with the porch and the drawings could be submitted to Mr. Pohlman. Commission members agreed. Ms. Wilson moved to approve the fence and the storage shed, with the top plate of the storage shed to align with the top plate to align with porches at 108 Carr Street, and conceptually accept the pool and cabana, pending enclosure details at the next Commission meeting; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

(Mr. Hirshorn departed the meeting at 7:26 p.m.

label: 315 Bennett Street
request: 315 Bennett Street – Survey 6130– Final Review for Alterations to Fencing and Installation of Parking pad

events.text: Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. David Shuford, homeowner, stated that their solution to much of the drainage issues were catch basins throughout the front and back yards, which are included in the plans, as well as French drains going along the property line. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve 315 Bennett Street plan as presented; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Austin Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. David Shuford, homeowner stated that he is not sure who was involved in the Phase 1 of the landscape project; however, they originally put the fence in the backyard and were not sure if grass would grow in the side yard. He said before they fenced it in, they were treating it as a side yard. He said the grass is doing well there, so they will have more room for the children and the dog. He said along the front they also did not know originally what parking would be required. He said they moved into the house in January and now realize they need more than anticipated. He said the back is too tight for their SUV’s. He said it was suggested by the landscape architect to run the parking area along the road; however, they are open to any comments or recommendations by the Commission. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his experience is that many homes in the Old Village have the street-side gravel parking spaces. He understands the need; however, the material that works best is the plantation mix. He said it is loose material, but when wet, it bonds and does not run into the street. He said the proposed river pebble is not recommended. Ms. Montgomery agreed with Mr. Hirshorn’s comments. Ms. Rowe stated that the plantation mix is more subtle looking, as well. She said that Mr. Shuford has done a wonderful job with the property and she does not have any issue, as long as it is not the bigger pebbles. Ms. Wilson stated that she would actually like to see the parking area reduced. She said it is a huge run of gravel and she is personally not in favor of plantation mix. She said she would like to see the material bordered and contained in some way. She stated that this is a massive run of gravel in a high visibility historic street. She stated that she is not agreeable with a large parking area, without it being broken out with some thought in the landscaping and how to buffer it. She said it is going to be so easy that there Old Village Historic District Commission

will be vehicles in front of their house all the time. She is agreeable with the fence, but not the parking strip. Mr. Hirshorn asked if Ms. Wilson would recommend a brick border or a reduction of the surface area or both. Ms. Wilson said both. She said she would prefer that it not be located on Bennett. She said the homeowner has accomplished a significant amount of work on the front of the home to restore. She said she lives across the street from a neighbor who did the same thing and the whole block parks in front of their home, because it is not landscaped. She said you end up with a parking lot in front of your home. She said at the very least, she would like to see it bordered and defined as a single space with landscaping breaking it up. Mr. Shuford stated that it was the recommendation from the architect; however, he is in favor of what the Commission recommends, as well as the type of mix used. He said as far as the border on the house side, it would be the steel border. Ms. Dovre stated that she has seen the house and it is beautiful. She personally would like pavers as opposed to pebble. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it appears that the consensus is to contain the material to one area with a plantation mix rather than the river stone with some type of confining border. Ms. Rowe asked if Mr. Shuford has looked into the grass that you are able to park on. Mr. Shuford stated that he has not. He said there was mention of an installation you are able to park on, where grass is able to grow. Ms. Wilson made a motion to approve the fence and defer the parking for the project at 315 Bennett Street; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor. Mr. Hirshorn asked Mr. Shuford to come back next month with another alternative for parking.

label: 625 Royall Avenue
request: 625 Royall Avenue – n/a – Hardscaping and fencing

events.text:
Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design Group, said that he also has Meredith Bearden present who will be the landscape architect, as well as the owner on the property. He said that this is right next to Ben Tatum pond, and the Tatum property. He said that it is wet all the time and sits at approximately five to seven feet grade with seven being the highest point. He said the finished floor is sitting at 9’3” at an AE12 flood. He said everything sits under flood. He said the lot was re-platted in 1964 to set aside this as a lot and the house was built in 1965. He said it does sit below flood and there are four conditions for the demolition and feels that they meet the financial condition. He said it would be very costly to raise the house and it is not worth the value of the property. He said there are also no historical redeeming qualities. He said this would be the reasoning for the demolition. He said the property is behind the previous submittal’s property and are in the historic district. He said that across the street is not in the historic district, but still in the village with newer homes. He said the road drops considerably heading toward the pond, with the pond being the low spot. He said that drainage affects many of the decisions that they have made. He said all of the neighbors currently drain to a shared drainage ditch which goes to the pipe that drops into the pond. He said that while they are doing a larger home, they would like to use less of the property. He said that they will not be bringing in too much dirt and a raised home, similar to the one directly across the street. He said there will be a driveway coming in, with the main entrance on the side of the driveway and one straight ahead. He said they will be putting in a small piece that is being classified as an ADU, but is integral to the home and made it small and subservient to the main house. He provided an overall map of the area surrounding the property and said they are a similar size in footprint to some of the other homes in the surrounding area. He said to the BAR, they have to include the portion of the underneath space they are using as a garage and have that defined. He said the BAR seems higher than it would be if they did not have to Old Village Historic District Commission

include the section underneath. He said they will be bringing the grade up slightly in the front to encourage draining both towards the street and the pond and setting the house as low as possible back behind the raised grade in the front to minimize the height of the raised home. He said that the lot begins to drop off towards the back and in the back it appears higher, because the grade in the back is higher, with everything falling into the drainage ditch. He said that they are not proposing a pool at this time. Mr. Hirshorn said that the biggest conceptual issue is which was the elevation that was juxtaposed next to the house next door, where Mr. Clarke mentioned wanting to keep the height. He said the scale and mass when you look at it from the streetscape on Royall, there is a difference. He said he would like to hear from other Commission members to see if this is within the parameters of some of the guidelines. Ms. Wilson stated that she has an issue with a raised house on this block. She said this is a tough area, because it is on Royall Avenue, which is half subject to the OVHDC and across the street is not. She said there are no raised houses on that side of Royall Avenue. She said that the ridge on this home is going to be at least five feet taller than the one on the left. She said it is significantly taller than anything else on that block. She cannot think of any raised houses for more than a block or two. Mr. Clarke stated that there is one on the other side of the pond. Ms. Wilson stated that the one in the woods is raised, but has a very low second story. She said she understands that they are able to get the FEMA boost for the ridge height; however, no one uses this and everyone is held to the 35 foot ridge height in the village. She said she needs to understand this more, because it is very tall and does not see a real advantage to it being raised, since this property is able to get some parking on the wing to the left. Mr. Rutherford stated that Town-wide, if you are in a flood zone, you are allowed an additional five feet, because those located in floor areas must raise their house. Ms. Wilson stated that the rest of the Town adheres to this; however, those on Toomer Lane had to obtain a variance. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Rutherford stated that he is unsure of the current elevation of the property; however, if it is an AE12, the first floor would have to be at 13 feet. Ms. Wilson stated that this proposed home is at 17 feet. Mr. Clarke stated that he did the design on the homes on Beach Street and the one on Haddrell, and they all went to 40 feet. Ms. Wilson stated that those are different to her. Ms. Dickson stated that they are on the water. Ms. Wilson said that when you drive around the village, you do not see many houses that go bumper to bumper on their side yard setbacks, but try and stay tighter so that people have views, light, and breezes through their side yards. She said when they are blocking it side to side, the secondary element is detached and towards the back and the mass is more broken up. She said that her two comments are, really tall and really wide for this lot. Mr. Clarke said that the piece on the left, they did try to push it back as far as possible, and although it shows up on the front elevation, he does not know how much it would be seen. He said it is wetlands in the back area. He said they are attempting to keep everything as far forward as possible to alleviate any flooding or drainage issues. He said that this is why they attempted to break it up in mass and have the taller piece in the middle and the one story wings on the side. Mr. Keenan said that it is a great looking house, but has a difficult time envisioning it on Royall Avenue. He said he would like to see the height come down and have more of a front porch as a focal point, as opposed to the two porches there now against the two-story section, since Royall Avenue is such a prominent street. He asked if there are any additional drive-in bays under the house. Mr. Clarke said that there is one under the kitchen and one under the ADU (accessory dwelling unit). Mr. Keenan said that he is not as concerned about side elevations. Ms. Rowe said that she agrees with what has been said about the size, mass and scale. She said it looks too massive, although the design is beautiful. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson said that Mr. Clarke typically has his 3D renderings which is very helpful to the Commission members. She said when you add the topography it would help as well. Mr. Dickson asked about the square footage of the home. Mr. Clarke said that it is approximately 4,000 heated square footage. He said that it is a unique lot that is the beginning of the drop to the pond. He said the reason they did the park under is if they did the crawl, they would have a large detached garage, but he did not want to take up as much square footage on the absorption of the soil and it is tough to get it too far back. He said they studied both and went for the raised. Mr. Dickson asked if the drainage ditch actually drains to the lake. Mr. Clarke responded in the affirmative.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Phil Clarke, Clarke Design, stated that last month, the main objection was doing a drive under and bringing the grade up in order to ensure the ground floor was not too wet. He said as it was compared to the house next, it was too massive. He said the main comment was to bring the height down as much as possible, still being above flood. He said that he has accomplished this. He said that they have brought the grade up out of flood and raised it slightly around the front and let it drain off and took away the drive under element and the ADU, and detached a garage in the back. He said there are dormers, in order to use the upper floor as storage or a small room; however, it will not be a finished room. He said that it is a similar architectural style, as most of the comments last month were favorable with the style, brackets and the simple coastal farmhouse look. He said by losing the ground floor space which counted towards the BAR, he was able to increase the rear porch slightly and the right side elevation which will be seen across the pond also looks nice. He said the pool is shown for location only and not planned on at this time. Ms. Rowe stated that when you look at the garage it makes a significant difference, because it sets back. She believes it looks great. Ms. Dickson asked about the square footage. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Clarke stated that the BAR (building area ratio), is 4,975 which is heated space plus porches. He said that the actual heated space is 3,586. He said the porch in the rear is large and has a nice porch on the front as well. Ms. Wilson said that the style is more classic and is appropriate in the historic district. She said that on the side elevations, the gables are not complete. She said she would like to see Mr. Clarke follow through with what has been done on the front, on the side elevations, especially the left side which is exposed. She said that the gable on the exposed side needs to have as much integrity as the front of the house, where there are clean forms and the corners are expressed. She side on the right side, the gable could be expressed so that there is a true primary mass to the house, making it stronger. She said that it is misleading on the front elevation, because with the garage, it makes it look wider than it really is. She said she appreciates forgoing the drive under. She said that she really likes the back elevation, because the forms and gables are knitted together in a more fluid manner than the front. She said she is not sure if the front porch wraps around and ties into that piece (mud room). Mr. Clarke said that he has considered taking the mud room and sliding it forward and letting the porch wrap around. Ms. Wilson said that this is what she is referring to. She said since Mr. Clarke has to submit the garage separately, perhaps take it out of the house so it does not show so wide. She said that it is a great improvement. Mr. Keenan said that he also likes the rear elevation, primarily because of the porch. He said that his comments last month were to enlarge the porch slightly. Mr. Pohlman stated that just prior to final approval, demolition will need to be approved. He stated that the structure cannot be demolished until a final COA has been issued. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson moved to propose the demolition at 625 Royall Avenue based on the structure not being eligible for renovation to current code and compliance; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Rutherford reviewed the staff report with the Commission (attachment 1).

Mr. Phil Clark, Clark Design Group, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Montgomery moved for final approval. Mr. Gallogly second the motion. All in favor. Old Village Historic District Commission

label: 200 Queen Street
request: 200 Queen Street – Survey 6091 – Applicant is seeking Final Review for revisions from previously approved plans to install a solar tile roof and, also, to install a dock to the harbor

events.text:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Kenneth and Patricia Spicer, potential homeowners, said that his architect is not present at this time. He read a letter that his architect sent to the Commission. Mr. Hirshorn stated that for a harbor front home, some of the design details do not mimic some of the historic homes seen in the Old Village harbor front. He said that he is not referring to the new construction, but the general detailed themes of windows, rooflines and porches, which could be better honed to mimic some of the historic homes on the water front. Ms. Rowe stated that the proposed additions do not fit the feel of the harbor front. Ms. Dickson stated that she would like to see it simplified. Mr. Spicer said that the lot size is a constraint and their attempt was to mimic the existing house that is there. He said the floor plan for the first floor will remain unchanged; however, the second floor is where the change takes place. He said that the main reason is because they feel strongly about their grandchildren and their carbon footprint. He said they both drive electric cars and would like to have solar panels. He said that he learned from Town staff that the Commission is not enthusiastic about solar panes and tried to make the roof solar panel compatible. He said that there is no slope on it, it is flat. He said that he has done a great deal of research on other sites in Hilton Head, Kiawah and Isle of Palms, where they have flat solar panels, which are Old Village Historic District Commission

not as efficient. He said they put dormers up to break-up the roofline, but are still faced with trying to hide the solar panels. Ms. Wilson asked if it is a hard rule not to allow solar panels. Mr. Pohlman stated that in the guidelines under Roofs, #7: If solar panels are desired on a building, they should be placed on a rear elevation or in a valley area of the roof that is not visible from the public right of way. Mr. Spicer stated that this property has 2 ½ views from the public right of way, depending on how wide the Commission considers public right of way on the harbor and Queen Street. He said that there is no rear elevation that is out of the public right of way for this property. Mr. Keenan stated that the solar panels are in the middle of the house on the flat section of the roof, so they will not be visible. He said there have not been too many applications for solar panels in the past several years. He said that he echoes Mr. Hirshorn’s comments, as the whole application is difficult to understand and is not certain if this is due to the fact that there is an existing home there already. He said that typically the architects that come before the Commission display both existing elevations and a proposed elevations, which is very helpful. He said that it is difficult for him to decipher what is there and what is being proposed, and has some concern with the additional height, but primarily, it is the harbor view. Mr. Spicer said that the harbor is approximately 800 feet from the front of the lawn. Ms. Wilson said that it is important for the Commission to see existing and proposed elevations on the same page, which helps to evaluate the impact on the neighborhood. She said this is difficult, because the neighbor on the right is a large tall house, but Queen Street is not a large street with very small houses. She said what is being proposed is too tall for Queen Street, when you consider the Old Village Historic District Commission

streetscape. She said that there are nine foot flat ceilings with a lot of attic space so more could be done with the existing rooflines, utilizing dormers or vaulting some of the space. She said that the height needs to come down. She said that she appreciates the discussion of a front door; however, it is not really a front that is addressing the street. She said that the elevation that faces Queen Street needs to be considered for neighborhood capability. She said that this is the tallest elevation of all the elevations, because that ridge is raised the highest. She said it needs to be stepped down towards Queen Street. She said on many of the old homes, the front is the harbor. She said that the front door and front porches are all harbor-side, so they could put a garden entry onto the front porch on the harbor. She said that she would not go to the expense of a grand entrance. She suggested spending additional time studying the elevation along Queen Street. She said where you see the gable that brings the eave down and looks low on Queen Street although it rises up higher in the middle. She said the overall flow of the current house is better than what is being proposed in terms of how it relates to its neighbors in scale. She added that the homes on Queen Street are not big, but there is a very large house on either side so the Commission is sympathetic to this, but are also concerned with existing streetscapes and neighbors and who is being impacted. She stated that this is where the existing versus proposed is very important, so that the Commission is able to understand what the impact is. She stated that she would rather see a solar panel than a house get 10 feet taller. Mr. Spicer said that it would be easier for them, because the southern exposure is where the solar panels are more efficient. Mr. Pohlman said that this is a guideline, so it is at the Commission’s discretion whether they would like to provide some leniency. He said when discussing with the property owners prior to coming before the Commission, that they must attempt to abide by the guidelines first and then request any leniency. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that on the other pitches she would rather see a solar panel. Mr. Spicer stated that they researched the solar singles, which are not commercially available and there is some concern as to how soon they will be available. Ms. Wilson stated that she understands why the flat roof helps the solar panels, but this is causing a host of other issues with the large flat roof in terms of drainage. Mr. Spicer said that the builders have mentioned TPO roof (Thermoplastic Polyolefin) and have guaranteed 25 years. Ms. Wilson said that she would not encourage this, not just technically, but aesthetically, as it is not what is typically seen in combination with pitches. She said if a modern askew were being presented, this would be one thing; however, she would ask to have the architect re-study the roof forms. She said that personally, she would be open to seeing solar panels from the side and rear. Mr. Spicer asked if this would be on Queen Street and the harbor- side. Ms. Dickson said that if the front of the house is declared to be the harbor-side, then why not put solar panels on the rear of the home. Mr. Spicer stated that unfortunately, the panels must be south and west in order for the panels to be effective. Ms. Wilson said that the second gable that is back, would face that direction and panels that tilt up could be installed, which would not be seen from the water, but would be above the primary ridge. Mr. Spicer said that the efficiencies of solar panels is 18% to 21% and for their needs, they would need 36 to 38 panels which are approximately four feet by six feet. Ms. Wilson suggested geothermal which works great when heating and cooling the home. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Spicer said that they had geothermal on Sullivan’s Island and because of the mineral content in the pipes, it was a disaster. He said it was not just the pipes coming into the house, but the ones in the ground which must be dug up every three to five years. Ms. Dickson stated that she has had geothermal in her home for twelve years and has not had a single issue. Mr. Spicer asked if it was from a well and if he would be allowed to put in a well. Ms. Dickson responded in the affirmative. Mr. Keenan responded in the affirmative. He said that he believes the solar panels will be an issue if that many are going to be required. He said he would advise against the TPO roof, as the Commission would likely not consider this as it is a commercial application. Mr. Spicer stated that they would be completely covered by the panels in this design. Mr. Keenan stated that he believes the potential property owners have some good feedback for their conceptual application. Ms. Rowe stated that she would likely not support the solar panels if they were to be seen on the harbor side. Mr. Hirshorn stated that there would have to be a way for the panels not to been seen in the right of way.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Old Village Historic District Commission

Hans Altenbach, architect for the homeowners, the Spicer’s, would like to present the plans. He said that there are eight houses in that section of Queen Street, five two-story homes and three one and a half story houses. 200 Queen Street is one of the one and a half story houses and the Spicer’s would like to take it to a full two-story house. He said the houses are all AE13, with the exception of 200 Queen Street and the one adjacent to it facing the harbor. He said 200 Queen is the only house that has eight-foot parking underneath.
